sessions.title: “Make Me a Map”: Building a GIS Agent with AgentBricks, MCP, and Lakebase
sessions.body:
Geospatial workflows are complex—querying spatial databases and generating visualizations requires specialized expertise. We built an AI agent that takes a Slack message and returns a fully functional map application.

 

What started as an internal tool for Solution Architects—replacing hours of manual data prep—is now used by customers too.

 

The architecture: Lakebase serves as the spatial backend (Postgres-compatible with PostGIS), while our MCP server exposes Felt's mapping capabilities to AgentBricks. Users ask for a map in Slack, the agent queries Lakebase, connects to Felt, and posts back a working map.

 

This talk covers:

  • Lakebase as a geospatial engine—Postgres compatibility in a serverless lakehouse
  • MCP tools for live connections—wiring Lakebase → Felt directly
  • AgentBricks orchestration—multi-step GIS workflows from Slack

 

Attendees leave with a pattern for building agents that produce working applications, not just answers.

sessions.title: 0 to 100 AI/BI Apps in 120 Days: Building an Enterprise Data and AI Platform From Scratch @ Alpura
sessions.body:
In early 2025, Alpura faced fragmented data, multiple BI tools, weak governance and no scalable AI foundation. In just 120 days, we rebuilt the entire data platform on Databricks. Using the Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold), Unity Catalog for enterprise governance and Databricks Metrics for a centralized semantic layer, we created a governed, scalable lakehouse foundation.

 

We consolidated more than five legacy platforms without disrupting operations and eliminated KPI inconsistencies by standardizing business logic. On top of this foundation, we rapidly delivered 100+ AI/BI assets, including 10+ production-grade applications such as a Walmart Scintilla analytics app and an Ambassador Program app — built in days, not months. Leveraging Genie AI, we enabled conversational BI to accelerate adoption.

 

This session shares a practical blueprint for building an AI/BI factory at enterprise speed.

speakers.name: Javier Hauss
speakers.bio: Javier Hauss is Director of Data & AI at Alpura, leading a company-wide transformation centered on a modern lakehouse architecture. He deploys scalable AI products to drive value across commercial, operational, and supply chain functions. Previously, he built the data and AI capabilities for a new bank from scratch and worked at Uber and McKinsey. His focus is on operationalizing data and AI to build competitive, agile businesses.

speakers.name: Marvin Nahmias
speakers.bio: From leading global engineering teams at corporate giants like Verizon and Coca-Cola to being a serial startup founder in the world of Fintech, Marvin Nahmias has built a 25+ year career architecting rapid, Tech & AI-driven value. His latest feat is testament to this philosophy: a radical 120-day transformation at Alpura. He led the charge to unify all fragmented enterprise data— into a single, cohesive data & semantic layer, creating the ultimate source of truth for the business. With this powerful foundation set, his focus and his team has now pivoted to the next frontier: deploying a suite of powerful, people-first GenAI/AI/ML solutions designed to optimize operations, unlock new revenue streams, and double the value of Alpura in 2030.

sessions.title: 10 Gigawatts of Renewables = 3.2 Billion Events a Day in the Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: Industrial AI's real bottleneck isn't the model — it's the data foundation. Operational data has the classic 3 V's at extreme scale: Variety (hundreds of OEM protocols and naming conventions), Velocity (1-second sensor streams), and Volume — 3.2 billion events a day from a 10 GW renewable fleet.Nexalis is the cloud-native industrial data infrastructure layer for the AI era. A zero-copy architecture makes OT data available in your Databricks environment — cleansed, shaped, and AI-ready in under 4 seconds — unlocking the full analytics ladder: descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive.Three production deployments: EDF Power Solutions on Maverick6 (solar + battery); Clenera (1.6 GW today → 5+ GW); Calpine with Accure (predictive battery degradation deep inside the BESS).Same architecture, same pattern — heading next into conventional generation and nuclear. Anyone can dump events into a bucket. Cleansed, shaped, and AI-ready in less than 4 seconds is data engineering.

sessions.title: 1000× Faster Retrieval: Indexed and Full-Text Search in the Lakehouse
sessions.body:
Delta Lake and Iceberg excel at large-scale analytics, but they are not optimized for sub-second point lookups or full-text search. In operational workloads — such as security analytics, log investigation and telemetry — retrieval queries that require full scans or high-cardinality filtering can take minutes to hours, when seconds or milliseconds are required.

 

I built IndexTables, an embedded, Tantivy-based indexing layer that runs directly inside Spark executors, enabling up to 1000× faster query performance while preserving the Lakehouse model. This session explores the architecture: object-storage-hosted indexes with ACID transactions, millisecond-latency aggregations over billions of rows, native time-series bucketing for efficient GROUP BY analytics and NVMe-backed caching with proactive pre-warming.

 

Attendees will learn how Capital One is using IndexTables to complement Delta and Iceberg, creating lakehouse architectures that support both analytical and retrieval-heavy workloads.

speakers.name: Scott Schenkein
speakers.bio: Scott Schenkein is the lead engineer for Capital One’s cybersecurity practice.  He has experience leading engineering organizations across retail, finance, and cyber security.  His specializations include data engineering, cloud, cryptography, devops, mentoring, and enterprise collaboration best practices.  Outside of work, Scott enjoys time with family, is an avid musician, and enjoys cycling and hiking.

sessions.title: 3 Steps to Red Team Your LLMs on Databricks (Using Tools You Didn't Know You Had)
sessions.body: You added guardrails, PII filters, and safety controls. Then someone Base64-encodes a prompt injection and your model hands over data like it was asked nicely.This session is a live walkthrough of how to red team your LLMs on Databricks using BlackIce, Databricks' own open-source containerised toolkit. 14 security tools. One Docker image. Five minutes to deploy.In 3 steps we will spin up a model serving endpoint with AI Gateway guardrails, launch BlackIce on a single-node cluster with NVIDIA's Garak, Microsoft's PyRIT, Meta's CyberSecEval and 11 more tools ready to go, then point Garak at the endpoint and run attack probes, encoding attacks, jailbreaks, prompt injection, and system prompt extraction — to get an Attack Success Rate in minutes.You'll leave fully understanding how to use BlackIce to secure your LLMs, whilst feeling slightly more paranoid about just how easy they are to break. Better you find out here than in production.

speakers.name: Gavita Regunath
speakers.bio: Gavita Regunath is Chief AI Officer at Advancing Analytics, a data and AI consultancy and Databricks Gold Partner. She leads the AI practice, helping organisations move from AI experimentation to production grade systems that deliver measurable value. Her work spans Generative AI, agentic systems, machine learning, MLOps, governance and evaluation, with a strong focus on building scalable AI solutions on Databricks. Gavi works closely with technical teams and business leaders to turn strategy into practical delivery, particularly across financial services, insurance and retail. She is a Microsoft AI MVP and Databricks Champion, and regularly speaks on making AI useful, trusted and ready for the real world.

sessions.title: 800TB, Zero Pipelines: How Ensemble Health Partners Built an AI-Ready Revenue Cycle on Lakebase
sessions.body:
Ensemble Health Partners manages revenue cycle operations for 30+ health systems, processing 25 billion+ transactions across 800TB of healthcare financial data. Legacy SQL Server sprawl —1 5 individual databases with separate schemas —c reated silos that blocked cross-client insights and slowed AI innovation in an industry where providers operate on 1% margins.

 

This session shows how Ensemble consolidated onto Databricks Lakebase as their AI-ready transactional layer, eliminating brittle pipelines and enabling self-service pods to materialize views directly from harmonized Delta tables. The results: 3–5% net revenue yield improvement ($30M+ per $1B health system), 20% organizational efficiency gain, and 10x reduction in failure rates — while powering agentic AI workflows for denial prevention, AR follow-up, and payer-behavior prediction at scale.

speakers.name: Surya Sai Turaga
speakers.bio: My name is Surya! In the past I have played the role of a Field Engineering Leader and evangelist in the Advanced Analytics Space, I come with strong conceptual hands-on experience in Agentic AI, Cloud (AWS+Azure+GCP), Big Data and Data Warehousing environments. I worked as a developer and implemented FSLDMs on Teradata. I am passionate about turning ideas as Agentic AI automation systems. I enjoy developing high-performance teams, mentoring data enthusiasts and working in cross-functional environments.

sessions.title: A Unified Approach to Data Exfiltration Protection and Egress Monitoring to Build Secure Agents
sessions.body:
Data exfiltration is one of the most serious security risks organizations face. It can expose sensitive information, leading to reputational damage and regulatory penalties. The challenge is that exfiltration can happen in many ways, including external attackers, poorly configured AI agents, insider mistakes, or malicious insiders, and is often hard to detect until the damage is done.

 

In this lightning talk, we'll break down where exfiltration risks come from and what they may look like in Databricks (spoiler: it's not always a malicious actor!). We'll then introduce a framework for categorizing protection controls across three levels: data platform, compute, and storage. Using this framework, we'll discuss what risks to address today, tomorrow, and in the future with readily available controls at each level. 

 

As we wrap-up our session, we'll give you a glimpse into implementing comprehensive egress monitoring: what's here now and what's coming.

 

Walk away with a fresh perspective on data exfiltration risks and actions you can take today to secure and monitor your most sensitive workloads!

speakers.name: JD Braun
speakers.bio: JD is a Staff Security Field Engineer at Databricks. As part of the Databricks security organization, JD helps data teams solve the world's toughest problems by empowering customers to understand the security of the Databricks platform and by helping account teams address questions that come up during security reviews.

speakers.name: Robert Zhang
speakers.bio:
Robert Zhang is a product leader for networking and data security at Databricks. He is passionate about diagnosing challenging systems-level issues and translating them into scalable, user-centric products that drive real impact.

Robert studied at UPenn's Wharton Business School and Jerome Fisher M&T Program, blending engineering and business to develop a strong foundation in both technical depth and strategic thinking.

Beyond his work in technology, Robert is also known for his creativity and problem-solving outside of work—most notably as a winner of LEGO Masters Season 4, where he demonstrated teamwork, design thinking, and execution under pressure.

sessions.title: A Unified Future for Delta and Apache Iceberg™
sessions.body:
Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg™ have converged on similar ideas: columnar metadata for efficient pruning, manifest trees for scalability, and deletion vectors for fast updates. Yet today, we maintain two separate metadata structures, duplicating work and diverging in capabilities.

 

The next major evolution of Delta Lake reimagines metadata from the ground up. This talk introduces a unified metadata architecture where Delta Lake commits store content metadata directly in Iceberg v4's adaptive metadata tree. Delta Lake gains efficient tree-structured manifests and Iceberg interoperability while preserving the transactional guarantees that Delta users depend on.

 

Join us to see the future of lakehouse metadata.

speakers.name: Anoop Johnson
speakers.bio: I work on data lake infrastructure at Databricks, focusing on Delta Lake and Iceberg.

sessions.title: A–Z of Unity Catalog Business Semantics: Open and Unified Semantics for Agents, Apps and BI
sessions.body: Business semantics is the missing bridge between raw data and real understanding for humans and AI alike. In this comprehensive session, the product team behind Unity Catalog’s business semantics takes you from A to Z: what business semantics is, why it matters and how an open and unified semantic layer transforms the way agents, apps and BI tools consume your data. We’ll start with the foundations, defining and governing business glossaries, tags, and semantic metadata within Unity Catalog. Then we’ll show what’s new: the latest capabilities that make semantics flow seamlessly across AI agents, applications and BI tools from a single governed source. See live demos of how unified semantics improve agent reasoning, enrich app experiences and build dashboard trust. Whether you’re just starting or scaling enterprise-wide, walk away with everything you need to make your data universally understood.

sessions.title: Accelerating AI From Model to Impact at Workday With Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
Workday needed to put trusted ML insights directly in the hands of sales, customer success and finance—fast. Before, delivering a single internal app required a bespoke full‑stack build and repeated reviews, stretching timelines to nearly a year. By shifting to Databricks Apps and building where the data already lives, Workday compressed delivery to weeks, launched three production AI applications in a single year, and scaled its flagship Sales Companion to 4,500+ active users.

 

This session details the architecture and adoption playbook: Databricks Apps as the UI/middleware, MLflow‑powered components, retrieval‑augmented workflows for unstructured content, governed access with Unity Catalog and fast analytics via SQL Serverless—enabling conversational experiences that let business users self‑serve sentiment analysis, forecasting and KPI insights without waiting on the data science team or adding headcount.

speakers.name: Taylor Sewitt
speakers.bio: Taylor Sewitt is shaping the future of enterprise AI. As Director of GCO Technology & Architecture at Workday, Taylor leads one of the most ambitious AI transformations in enterprise software—architecting the systems, data, and agentic AI strategy behind Workday's multi-billion-dollar commercial organization. A trusted advisor to executives, a strategic partner to the world's leading technology vendors, and a builder at heart, Taylor sits where vision meets execution. His work is defining how Workmates will sell, serve, and operate in the age of AI.

sessions.title: Accelerating Corteva’s Data Source Onboarding With Lakeflow
sessions.body:
Onboarding a new data source at Corteva used to take 30–45 days. Now it’s 4–7 days, about 85% faster. The Lakeflow-first strategy and Unity Catalog helped standardize the ingestion‑to‑consumption pathway across 6 domains. Lakeflow Connect, Spark Declarative Pipelines and Jobs make pipeline runs repeatable and config‑driven. A lightweight metadata layer centralizes data cleansing, and an incremental DDL tool pushes schema changes safely through each environment.

 

This pattern now underpins Corteva’s operational analytics. It accelerates root‑cause analysis linking field variability to dryer‑bin stabilization, improves throughput across 35 seed sites, and strengthens seed quality. Today, the setup covers 5,000+ tables from 15+ sources, shortening time‑to‑insight and speeding partner onboarding. Attendees will leave with a reusable Lakeflow‑first ingestion pattern, a metadata‑driven data quality blueprint and a safe schema‑evolution workflow across environments.

speakers.name: Harshit Rai
speakers.bio: Harshit Rai is a Resident Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he partners with organizations to design and operationalize modern data and AI platforms on the Databricks. He holds an MS in Data Science from the University of Washington and brings 8+ years of hands-on experience across data engineering, data science, MLOps, and entrepreneurship. Combining deep technical expertise with a strategic, business-first mindset, Harshit helps teams turn analytics and AI initiatives into scalable platforms and measurable business impact.

speakers.name: Mehul Bhuva
speakers.bio: Mehul Bhuva is a Data & AI Platform Engineer with 22+ years of experience on Databricks and Azure. At Corteva Agriscience, he builds data engineering pipelines, Databricks Apps, Genie Spaces, AgentBricks apps, and enterprise-scale deployment frameworks. He is the developer of the Sprout-AI Framework (Seed Ops Savant) — a production RAG and Agentic AI solution built on Azure AI Foundry. A recurring guest on Microsoft Dev Radio, active speaker at Microsoft User Groups, regular author at SQL Server Central, and author of SharePointFix.com, Mehul is passionate about taking enterprise AI from prototype to production.

sessions.title: Accelerating ITSM Modernization with Lakeflow Connect: Nationwide’s Platform Upgrade
sessions.body: This presentation shows how Nationwide modernized its ServiceNow platform, transforming it from a highly customized, rigid system into a modern, scalable ITSM and data platform by leveraging Lakeflow Connect’s native capabilities to efficiently ingest, store, and curate data for current and future analytics needs. Previously, legacy data was extracted via APIs into Oracle and scattered across siloed stores, creating governance gaps, slow refresh cycles, and poor data quality. By adopting a Lakehouse foundation with incremental and CDC pipelines, Nationwide now benefits from unified governance, clear data lineage, simplified security, and faster time to value. The reimplementation also simplifies integrations, accelerates reporting, and reduces technical debt, all while preserving historical insight.

speakers.name: Ramki Lakshminarayan
speakers.bio: Data-focused product architect specializing in data engineering, governance, and enterprise platform integration at Nationwide. Experienced in designing and implementing scalable data platforms and enterprise integration patterns across tools and Databricks. Passionate about metadata strategy, data fabric, and AI/ML enablement, with a focus on making data more discoverable, trusted, and actionable for business outcomes.

sessions.title: Accelerating Rivian's Autonomy Flywheel: Geospatial Intelligence at Scale
sessions.body: Our team started on Geospatial journey with Databricks DBR 16.X, from legacy project migration and continued to expand by ingesting and processing three different geospatial datasets (HD USHR maps, public OSM and curated OSM (Overture)). We applied different optimization techniques to make spatial joins more performant and worked closely with Databricks Geospatial team in testing out incremental improvements in DBR, culminating in large scale performance increase on DBR 17.X bringing support to geospatial data types (GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY) as dedicated data types that could be stored in delta table. A significant optimization was observed in spatial joins, which could eliminate previously used optimization techniques, making data pipelines maintenance easier. All of these improvements enabled us to enrich internal datasets based on various road attributes from these datasets and use them in analytics, training and potential reinforcement learning applications where needed.

speakers.name: Filip Ilic
speakers.bio: Filip Ilic is a Senior Data Engineer working on large scale Geospatial analytics within the Autonomy group of Rivian.

speakers.name: Kent Marten
speakers.bio: Kent has been a speaker at Data +AI summit on 4 previous occasions; as the PM for the SQL Surface area and Geospatial at Databricks.

sessions.title: Accelerating the Monthly Financial Closing With Genie
sessions.body:
Closing the books every month is still slow and manual for many finance teams. In this session, we will walk through a monthly financial closing for a mid‑size retailer and show how we tackle two of the most painful steps with Databricks One: reconciling gaps between CRM invoices and accounting numbers and running variance analysis to explain differences between actual results and budget.

 

We will follow a finance controller using an AI/BI dashboard to spot issues, Genie in natural language to investigate root causes and draft variance commentary and a Databricks app to apply the corrections safely, update the numbers and generate the final reporting deck.Attendees will see how business users can make financial closing faster, simplify investigations and produce more reliable reports with less manual effort — all from a single, unified workspace.

speakers.name: Christophe Chieu
speakers.bio:
Christophe Chieu is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, with over 10 years of experience in data, strategy, and analytics. He works with customers across Central Europe, focusing on startups and digital native businesses, and supporting them in adopting modern data and AI platforms.

In his role, he helps teams move from ideas to production-ready systems, focusing on practical, scalable architectures. With a hands-on background in analytics, and machine learning, he works closely with both technical and business stakeholders to turn complex challenges into clear, actionable plans.

speakers.name: Silviu Tofan
speakers.bio: Part of a specialised team within the Databricks EMEA Field Engineering organisation, looking after our Serverless Compute Platform and Data Warehousing product. Working closely with large enterprises looking to onboard their end-to-end analytics capabilities safely and securely onto the Databricks platform for leveraging SQL at scale.

sessions.title: Accelerating the Speed to Value of Analytics with Databricks AI/BI & Agents
sessions.body: After migrating from Snowflake, Addepar ventured deep into Databricks' native AI/BI suite. This talk shares our practitioner's roadmap for accelerating "speed to value" by building analytics directly where data lives. We explore why we chose AI/BI over external tools and how we serve as early adopters pushing the platform's limits.Key takeaways:- The AI-Assisted Analyst: Leveraging Databricks Assistant to chat through notebook discovery, bypass syntax struggles, and cure "analyst's block" with AI-suggested Dashboard visuals.- Metadata as Code: Why rich Unity Catalog metadata is the critical UI for accurate GenAI.- Metric Views > Tables: Defining semantics once for both Dashboards and Genie to ensure consistent answers, rather than relying on static tables or views.- Genie & Agents: Tips for "teaching" Genie spaces and early experiments using Agent Bricks to orchestrate structured analytics alongside unstructured knowledge agents.

speakers.name: Chris Krysinski
speakers.bio: Chris Krysinski is Manager of Data Analytics at Addepar, where he leads a global team of analysts and partners with analytics engineers to deliver data infrastructure, semantic modeling, and AI-powered analytics across 10+ business domains. With 15+ years in financial services data roles — from portfolio reconciliation, valuation, and performance measurement to data management and analytics leadership — Chris brings a practitioner's empathy for stakeholders into every solution he builds. His team is building Addepar's BI platform on Databricks AI/BI and pioneering Genie Spaces as a modern form of self-serve analytics. Chris is passionate about treating metadata as the UI for GenAI and building analytics directly where data lives.

sessions.title: Activating AI With Lakeflow and Agent Bricks
sessions.body:
Enterprise knowledge is trapped in PDFs, images, and office docs—far from the reach of AI. This session demonstrates how to unleash that data by ingesting it with Lakeflow Connect and scaling it with Agent Bricks and Lakeflow Jobs.

 

We’ll cover:

  • Accessing with Lakeflow Connect: How to efficiently ingest from common AI sources, including email, cloud storage, and popular applications—as well as how to preserve the file permissions, metadata, and lineage that’s critical for secure AI.
  • Scaling with Agent Bricks and Lakeflow Jobs: How to turn AI models into production-grade ETL automation using AI functions and Databricks’ built-in orchestrator, with end-to-end patterns for search, data transformation, summarization, fuzzy matching and more.
  • Built-in governance: How to ensure these workflows are production-ready, with robust governance, observability, data quality, pipeline management, and more.

 

Stop letting your most valuable data sit idle. Join us to transform fragmented documents into a governed foundation for data intelligence.

speakers.name: Archika Dogra
speakers.bio: Archika is a Product Manager on the Mosaic AI Platform, focusing on AI governance, observability, and domain-specialized agents.

speakers.name: Jason Ping
speakers.bio: Jason is a Product Manager on Lakeflow Connect, focusing on unstructured data ingestion.

sessions.title: ADBC and the Future of Universal Data Connectivity for Agentic Systems
sessions.body:
Agents are becoming first-class users of the data stack, but they inherit 1990s-era connectivity: slow row-oriented APIs, heavy SDKs, and brittle system-specific connectors. For AI-driven workflows making fast tool calls across systems, this isn’t just slow—it’s terrible agent ergonomics, leading to failures, retries, and need for human intervention.

 

This talk explains why ADBC (Arrow Database Connectivity) is emerging as the universal connector for agentic data workflows: a vendor-neutral API and driver standard that ships Arrow columnar results, enabling fast data access across languages and engines. We’ll show why this matters for agents: frequent queries, tight latency/cost budgets, and the need for safe, reliable access to the tabular truth.

 

You’ll leave with a clear model for where ADBC fits in lakehouse architectures, why it aligns with Databricks and open standards, and a how to move from framework-heavy integrations to lean, CLI-first building blocks guided by agent skills.

speakers.name: Ian Cook
speakers.bio: Ian Cook is an Apache Arrow PMC member and co-founder and CEO of Columnar, a data infrastructure company enabling radically faster, simpler, and more secure database access for humans and agents.

sessions.title: Advanced SQL Patterns for Production Analytics
sessions.body: Modern analytics teams rely on SQL for far more than simple queries—but many advanced patterns remain underused or poorly operationalized. In this session, we’ll walk through proven SQL techniques including temporary tables, stored procedures, and multi-statement transactions, and show how to apply them safely in production. We will demonstrate how to build an efficient document extraction pipeline, and how to streamline sales funnel analysis with MATCH_RECOGNIZE. You’ll learn how to turn complex logic into reusable, governed assets using Unity Catalog, enabling faster iteration without sacrificing reliability or control. Expect practical examples you can apply immediately to real-world analytics and data engineering workflows.

speakers.name: Fabien Contaminard
speakers.bio: TBD

speakers.name: Serge Rielau
speakers.bio: Serge got into software as a teenager when one still memorized hex-arithmetic. He studied at TU Kaiserslautern, Germany and got into databases at IBM in 1996. After some 15 years as SQL architect and a detour through OpenPages he did a 5 year stint at Salesforce working on a PostgreSQL fork. Since 6 years Serge holds down a job as SQL Tsar, hobby doc writer, and error message wrangler at Databricks.

sessions.title: Agent as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation for the Agentic Era
sessions.body: Agents have arrived. Evaluation workflows need to catch up.The bottleneck is knowing what to evaluate. You can’t catch failures you don’t know exist, and in production agents, they’re subtle: unclear tool definitions, bloated context, brittle handoffs, and inefficiencies that compound across long sessions. Manual trace review is the only way to discover them, but it doesn’t scale. Blind spots accumulate.Agent as a Judge closes this gap. Where LLM-as-a-judge scores predefined criteria, evaluation agents do open-ended discovery. They work directly on raw traces, surface recurring failure modes, and turn those findings into targeted, high-signal evaluators — a step toward agents that improve agents.We’ll show how this works in Phoenix’s open-source evaluation agent, running on Phoenix’s own production traces. You’ll see what it surfaced, how it compares to human reviewers, and what it takes to trust agents with the work of evaluating agents.

speakers.name: Elizabeth Hutton
speakers.bio: Elizabeth is an AI Engineer. She is an interdisciplinary problem-solver, mathematical thinker, published author of scientific research, and experienced enterprise machine learning engineer. Language has been her core focus- first, as a researcher modeling how we learn it, and now, as an engineer building AI systems that can understand and reproduce it. Elizabeth has a background in computational math, cognitive science and NLP. Prior to Arize she was responsible for ML experimentation, model development, evaluation, and serving at Cisco, as the lead MLE on the Webex Contact Center AI Team creating the first in-house AI solutions from R&D to production.

sessions.title: Agent Evaluations
sessions.body:
This hands-on course introduces learners to evaluating, governing, and securing agentic AI systems on Databricks. You'll begin by exploring the motivation for evaluation and governance frameworks and how they connect to the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. Next, you'll learn how to apply MLflow evaluation metrics and a variety of evaluation techniques, including online evaluation, synthetic evaluation, and building evaluation datasets from MLflow traces. The course then examines how Unity Catalog governance extends to agents' functions, models, and tools, ensuring proper access control, auditability, and compliance. Finally, you'll learn Databricks AI Security Framework (DASF) and how to secure agents with Mosaic AI Gateway, applying guardrails, rate limits, and policy filters to enforce safe and reliable usage.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog for governance and model management
  • Intermediate Python programming experience
  • Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including RAG architectures and their components (chunking, embeddings, vector stores)
  • Basic knowledge of MLflow for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management
  • General awareness of data governance principles, including access control, data lineage, and data privacy

sessions.title: Agent Ready Data Governance: Databricks on Databricks
sessions.body: When your data consumers shift from 10,000 humans to 100,000 high-speed agents, “governance” can no longer mean a wiki page or a PDF policy document. Agents don’t read wikis; they need semantic, machine-readable guardrails. In this talk, the Data Platform team discusses our pivot to “agent-ready governance.” We are moving beyond simple access control lists (ACLs) to a model where Unity Catalog provides deep semantic context, usage constraints and “rules of the road” that our 100,000 agents can natively understand. Join us to see how we ensure that our digital workforce operates safely, preventing the chaos of 100,000 bots making bad decisions at machine speed.

speakers.name: Amit Pahwa
speakers.bio: Amit is a technical lead for the internal Data Platform function at Databricks. Amit has over a decade of experience working on Data Platforms of varying size, complexity, and industries. As the creator of Minerva at Airbnb, Amit paved the path for centralized metrics providing a consistent view for business analytics, experimentation, forecasting, and model training. At Databricks, Amit now helps shape how Databricks is used at Databricks with focuses on developer productivity, metric centralization, and data governance.

speakers.name: Prashant Gupta
speakers.bio: Prashant Gupta is a seasoned engineer with a track record of building high-scale systems across leading tech companies. He currently serves as a Senior Software Engineer at Databricks, where he leads third-party data ingestion within the Data Platform, focusing on scalable no-code SaaS integration with a strong emphasis on security and compliance. Previously at Google, Prashant led data platform in Google Cloud aimed at unifying data sources and enabling petabyte-scale, AI-driven insights. Prashant is passionate about creating resilient systems, streamlining developer experiences, and driving product innovation through data and infrastructure.

sessions.title: Agentic Admins: Managing Databricks @ Databricks
sessions.body: If we are building a future with 100,000 agents accessing our platform, relying on human administrators to click buttons and approve tickets is a non-starter. The math simply doesn’t work; human admin teams cannot scale linearly with an exponential agent workforce. This session explores how the Data Platform team is solving this by building “agentic admins” — autonomous systems capable of managing the platform for us. We will discuss the shift from manual provisioning to agent-led resource management, permissions granting and configuration tuning. Learn how we are architecting the control plane that allows a small team of humans to govern an army of 100,000 digital users without burning out.

speakers.name: James Burns
speakers.bio: James has spent more than two decades working at every layer of technology from ASICs to large scale distributed systems. Recently at Twilio, StitchFix, LightStep, and Snowflake, James has worked on secure and scalable observability and data handling. At Databricks, James leads initiatives related to security, privacy, and operational excellence within the Data Platform team handling petabytes of data daily across the globe.

sessions.title: Agentic Analytics on Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: Agents promise to scale instant access to data insights across organizations. However, most data warehouses were built for humans reading dashboards. Agents expose every assumption that breaks. Flawed semantics lead to hallucination, fragmented governance exposes improper data access, and cost/performance issues explode when one analyst becomes a thousand agents. In this session we'll walk through what agentic analytics looks like in practice on Databricks Lakehouse, demoing the patterns customers are running in production today. Following these patterns, you can dramatically increase your data team's impact across your organization while reducing time-to-insight. You'll leave with a clear model of approaches to agentic analytics at scale, and see why Databricks Lakehouse is built for it.

speakers.name: Ben Tripp
speakers.bio: [Placeholder]

sessions.title: Agentic Data Engineering with Lakeflow, Genie Code, and IDEs
sessions.body:
AI agents are changing how data engineering gets done. They can reduce manual work across the lifecycle of building and operating production pipelines, including authoring jobs and pipelines, testing changes, troubleshooting failures, and resolving incidents.

 

In this session, we show how Genie Code can be used with Lakeflow for data engineering. We demonstrate how builders can iterate on Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) and Jobs with Genie Code, accelerate authoring, and use agents to investigate failures by tracing logs, dependencies, and candidate fixes.

 

We also cover how local development tools can be used with Lakeflow, including IDEs and tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex. This lets teams use the tools they already have for Lakeflow development and troubleshooting.

 

Finally, we show how to safely adopt agents in real environments through sandboxing and guardrails to protect production data, as well as standard engineering practices such as source control, code review, testing, and CI/CD.

speakers.name: Gal Oshri
speakers.bio: Gal has been building AI products for the past decade. At Databricks, he works on the Databricks Assistant, helping make it a useful tool for all users across the platform. Previously, he worked on machine learning products at AWS (SageMaker Training), Google (TensorFlow), and Microsoft (ML.NET), contributing to tools used by developers and data scientists around the world.

speakers.name: Lennart Kats
speakers.bio: Lennart Kats is a Principal Engineer at Databricks, responsible for the development experience of Lakeflow. Lennart and team created Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs), the Lakeflow IDE, and Genie Code For Data Engineers. Lennart holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science.

sessions.title: Agentic Feature Engineering: How McAfee Drives Personalization With Agent Bricks
sessions.body:
McAfee protects millions of users through products like Scam Detector and Social Privacy Manager. Iteration on adaptive pricing models was bottlenecked by slow, manual feature engineering. To unlock value from massive user signals, we needed to move from ideation to production fast. In this talk, we show how we built an autonomous feature engineering agent on Agent Bricks that cut cycles by 60% and drove $54M+ in revenue—replacing manual SQL with an agent that reasons, iterates and converges.

 

Attendees will see a live blueprint of our agentic pipeline:

  • Analyze & ideate: Agent loads domain context and playbook from Unity Catalog, analyzes baseline and proposes features via LLM reasoning
  • Generate & evaluate: Agent writes code, executes in sandbox, evaluates against baseline and logs every iteration to MLflow.
  • Converge & deploy: Best features publish directly to Unity Catalog feature store.

 

Walk away with a reproducible blueprint for agentic feature engineering on Databricks.

speakers.name: Arul Bharathi
speakers.bio: Arul Bharathi is a Senior  Applied Science Manager at McAfee, leading distributed teams of Applied AI Scientists and ML engineers across Canada, the United States, and India. With 13+ years of experience shipping production ML systems, he has built and scaled models across fraud detection, dynamic pricing, personalization, and churn prediction — driving over $100M in incremental revenue across fintech, digital real estate, and cybersecurity. A strong advocate for humanizing AI through governance, fairness, and safety, Arul holds a  Master's in Computing Science from Simon Fraser University.

sessions.title: Agentic PHI De-Identification Across Multimodal Healthcare Data on Databricks
sessions.body: De-identifying clinical data is essential for research and secondary use, yet current approaches are costly and require constant manual tuning as data distributions change. This session introduces an agentic approach to automating privacy-preserving pipelines on the Databricks Lakehouse.We present an Agentic De-Identification Framework that treats the pipeline itself as an autonomous agent, minimizing human effort while maximizing security and compliance.Attendees will learn how to use Agent Bricks to fit de-identification models and entity resolution logic to customer data; apply agentic de-identification across structured data, clinical notes, and imaging metadata using Mosaic AI Agent framework; and register core de-identification logic as governed Unity Catalog Functions.We conclude by showing how AgentOps is operationalized with MLflow tracing, Unity Catalog governance, and Mosaic AI Gateway Guardrails to deliver auditable, secure PHI protection at scale.

speakers.name: David Talbey
speakers.bio: David Talby is the Chief Technology Officer at John Snow Labs, helping companies apply artificial intelligence to solve real-world problems in healthcare and life science. He has extensive experience building and running web-scale software platforms and teams – in startups, for Microsoft’s Bing in the US and Europe, and to scale Amazon’s financial systems in Seattle and the UK. David holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Master’s degrees in both Computer Science and Business Administration. He was named USA CTO of the Year by the Global 100 Awards in 2022 and Game Changers Awards in 2023.

speakers.name: Veysel Kocaman
speakers.bio: Veysel is a Healthcare AI leader and researcher specializing in clinical NLP, Generative AI, LLMs, and large-scale healthcare AI platforms. Veysel is the CTO & Head of Data Science at John Snow Labs, leading a 50+ person engineering and science organization delivering production-grade AI systems for healthcare and life sciences worldwide. PhD in Computer Science  focusing on self-supervised learning and robustness. Author of 40+ publications in applied AI, inventor on 2 U.S. patents, keynote speaker, and contributor to widely used healthcare AI ecosystems including Spark NLP, with expertise spanning multimodal AI, RAG, de-identification, and enterprise-scale healthcare deployments.

sessions.title: Agentic workflows: Transforming, structuring, enriching data at scale with AI
sessions.body: Every enterprise unfathomable volumes of unstructured data — documents, emails, transcripts, contracts, support tickets, web content — growing faster than anyone can use it. Agentic workflows promise to turn this data into insights and automations, but they're only as good as the data feeding them.AI Functions bridge that gap at scale: research-backed, composable building blocks optimized for batch processing millions of records. From SQL, they parse documents, classify text, extract structured insights, and resolve unstructured data into clean, governed inputs — one pipeline that feeds every downstream consumer. This session shows how to optimize running agents on your data at scale. We'll walk through how to compose AI Functions into end-to-end agentic workflows, and reveal new AI Functions that push batch enrichment and retrieval further than ever before.

speakers.name: Archika Dogra
speakers.bio: Archika is a Product Manager on the Mosaic AI Platform, focusing on AI governance, observability, and domain-specialized agents.

sessions.title: AI Agents for the Frontline: 7-Eleven’s GenAI Maintenance Assistant
sessions.body: Maintenance technicians at 7-Eleven rely on preventive maintenance, catalogue and parts documents for equipment like HVACs and ovens — often using only their phones. These documents span thousands of files in formats like PDFs and spreadsheets stored in shared drives, making it hard to find the right information quickly. High attrition and missed training sessions compounds knowledge gaps. To address this, 7-Eleven developed a GenAI agentic system using Mosaic AI, Agent Bricks and Databricks Hybrid Search that enables technicians to 1) Retrieve relevant maintenance documents with concise answers 2) Capture equipment images and receive troubleshooting solutions 3) Access parts information by equipment brand 4) Get solutions from the internet. This chatbot bridges knowledge gaps with instant access to institutional knowledge. We will walk through how we built this system, our evaluation methodologies and the three-step prompt framework including guardrails for safe internet searches.

sessions.title: AI Can’t Wait: How to Overcome GPU Scarcity and Keep Workloads Running
sessions.body: GPU scarcity, cloud capacity constraints, and regional outages are challenges enterprises simply cannot afford: they block model training and serving, and leave mission-critical workloads queuing or failing with no good recourse.  By intelligently routing workloads to the optimal compute while preserving each customer's data residency, security controls, and compliance boundary, Databricks is solving both problems transparently. In this talk, we'll show how we're delivering GPU access to customers who are capacity-constrained in their home region, and offering enterprise-grade availability guarantees for serverless workloads without requiring customers to manage multi-cloud infrastructure themselves.

speakers.name: Sheng Lu
speakers.bio: I'm a platform engineering manager, leading networking for Databricks. If a connection goes into or comes out of Databricks, I care about making it secure, performant, and easy to manage.

sessions.title: AI Mesh – The Age of the AI Products
sessions.body: This session explores the evolution from Data Products to AI Products, introducing "Agents" as scalable, composable building blocks for the enterprise. We will discuss how to apply product thinking to AI—ensuring agents are discoverable, connectable, and trusted within the Unity Catalog. The talk details the "Agents Maturity Model," guiding you from L0 (Observe) to L3 (Act) automation, and outlines a robust architecture where agents serve as domain experts. Finally, we will demonstrate a real-world energy use case, showing how to build and orchestrate reusable agents to analyze wind park data using Databricks Genie, significantly accelerating time-to-market.

speakers.name: Pascal Homberg
speakers.bio: Pascal Homburg is Team Lead at RWE Renewables, where he works on enterprise Data & AI platforms, Data Products, and agentic AI for renewable energy operations. With a background spanning software development, Data & AI strategy, DevOps, and organizational transformation, he focuses on turning trusted data into scalable AI products and autonomous agents that accelerate business processes. At Data + AI Summit, Pascal will share practical lessons from building governed agents with Databricks to analyze wind park data and support operational decision-making.

sessions.title: AI Will Go Wrong and the Blueprint to Get It Right
sessions.body: Most AI failures aren't technology problems — they're people, process, and architecture problems. In this hands-on session, you'll witness a live AI trainwreck: an agent operating without guardrails, governance, or the right organizational design. Then, in a real-time post-mortem, we will collectively dissect what broke and why. You'll map the missing middle layer: the intersection of roles, accountability structures, and platform architecture. And you'll work alongside peers to design practical fixes. The session closes with an exercise where attendees act as domain experts to train an AI Judge capable of scaling oversight across enterprise deployments. Expect minimal slides, maximum doing, and a concrete blueprint you can apply within 30 days. This session is built for executives who are tired of theoretical AI frameworks and want proven patterns that make AI projects safer, faster, and genuinely business-ready.

speakers.name: Lexy Kassan
speakers.bio: Lexy Kassan is a Lead Data and AI Strategist at Databricks, overseeing and guiding customer organizations through holistic transformation programmes built on industry trends and best practices. As an Ethicist, Lexy coaches companies on implementing responsible AI and works with public affairs to shape Databricks’ messaging to regulators and lobbyists. Outside of work, Lexy mentors for multiple initiatives supporting underrepresented groups in STEM.

speakers.name: Maria Zervou
speakers.bio:
Maria Zervou is a Greek-expat experiencing the London life… and weather! With a Data Science degree and a lot of curiosity about how coding and data can unlock new ways of solving problems, her journey to the data world started. Maria has worked as a Data Scientist and an ML engineer for the past 7 years, where she experienced how data actually challenges and transforms the way we think and operate. Today, Maria is working as a Senior Specialist Solution Architect @Databricks where she helps businesses leverage data and AI to solve their business challenges at scale. Her enthusiasm for emerging technologies aligns her trajectory with the LLM and GenAI wave, exploring how to harness these technologies for tangible, meaningful impact.

Fun Fact:
Fitness geek, I workout more than I actually work! and as Juvenal once said: ‘Mens sana in corpore sano’ or in Mark Wahlberg’s words “No pain no gain” !

sessions.title: AI_DIAGNOSE: Automating Spark Job Debugging With LLM Agents
sessions.body:
Debugging distributed Spark jobs is notoriously difficult, often requiring hours of sifting through massive logs to find root causes. We introduce AI_DIAGNOSE, a new Spark SQL procedure in Databricks Runtime that automates this process using large language models (LLMs).

 

This session explores the architecture of AI_DIAGNOSE, detailing how we implemented a ReAct-style agent within the Spark engine. We will demonstrate how the agent autonomously gathers context, retrieves distributed logs, and analyzes job failures. We'll cover technical challenges like managing LLM context windows with large logs, ensuring structured actionable outputs, and leveraging Databricks Model Serving for secure inference. Join us to learn how AI_DIAGNOSE works under the hood to drastically reduce Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) for data pipelines.

speakers.name: Allison Wang
speakers.bio: Allison is a software engineer at Databricks, working on Spark SQL and PySpark. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon University.

sessions.title: AI-Driven Unity Catalog Implementation at Navy Federal Credit Union
sessions.body:
We will summarize our successful integration of Unity Catalog (UC) at Navy Federal Credit Union (NFCU), resulting in $10M savings. Our initiative established UC as the central access point for data assets within the Enterprise Data Lake (EDL) and redesigned the enterprise ETL framework.

 

Key outcomes include:

  • Accelerated development cycles: Reduced pipeline build and deployment time by 40%, enabling faster time-to-market for data products.
  • Performance optimization: Achieved a 50% reduction in overall runtime and a 40% decrease in operational costs through efficient resource utilization and optimized job configurations.

 

We will explore the architecture and strategic use of access control in UC, providing actionable insights and best practices for improving data management efficiency. 

EY will present alongside Krishnakumar Subramanian, Cloud Data Modernization and Analytics Leader at Navy Federal.

speakers.name: Ansu Boby
speakers.bio: Ansu is a Data engineering leader with strengths across technology, delivery execution, communication, and people leadership. She focuses focus on continuous improvement using clear stakeholder alignment, and disciplined execution. Known as a trusted subject matter expert, she bridges legacy platforms and modern cloud technologies with a focus Databricks and Azure. She thrives in high‑impact leadership roles and brings strong technical acumen, sound decision‑making, and collaborative communication to deliver sustained organizational value.

sessions.title: AiChemy: How MCP-Powered Agents Cut Drug Discovery Research from Weeks to Minutes
sessions.body: Drug discovery demands sifting through millions of compounds, thousands of papers, and dozens of databases—a process that costs the industry an average of $2.6B and over 10 years per approved drug. Researchers spend days cross-referencing OpenTargets for genetic evidence, PubChem for chemical properties, and PubMed for supporting literature. What if agents could do it in minutes?Meet AiChemy, a multi-agent assistant that combines external MCP servers like OpenTargets, PubChem, and PubMed with your own chemical libraries on Databricks. Add Agent Skills to find druggable targets, drug candidates and their chemical properties and safety profiles, complete with supporting evidence.You can build your own multi-agent assistant in just 5 minutes using our no-code Agent Bricks. Plus, Databricks assets like Genie, Vector Search, and Functions are automatically turned into MCP servers for seamless integration. Stop scrolling through endless articles and databases—let your agents do it for you!

speakers.name: Yen Low
speakers.bio:
Yen Low brings 20 years of Health AI experience translating cutting-edge science into practical real-world products across Pharma (GSK), Payers (Optum, Aetna), Providers (Stanford), Regulators (WHO), and startups (Atropos Health). She received her PhD in Biomedical Informatics and has built teams and AI products from the ground up, spanning drug discovery, RWE, and clinical foundation models. Yen specializes in helping healthcare and life sciences organizations identify AI opportunities and designing systems to capture it.

Her latest creation, AiChemy, is a scientific AI agent built to accelerate drug discovery and real-world evidence by connecting custom chemical libraries and knowledge bases via MCP on Databricks.

sessions.title: Alinta Energy’s Data Platform: From Platform Migration to Enterprise Ready AI-Driven Energy Ops
sessions.body:
Alinta Energy has modernized its enterprise data estate by standardizing on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. Unifying over 90 systems and 2.4K objects, ADH now supports 36,000+ daily queries via an automated, reliable release pattern. This governed, cost-efficient foundation powers analytics and AI across generation, trading and retail.

 

Key session insights:

  • Business leaders: Learn how a single platform and operating model reduce risk and cost while accelerating time-to-insight through enterprise-scale adoption and repeatable savings.
  • Tech teams: Explore “Pilot for Teams” for scalable production, the ingestion of OT/generation telemetry for near-real-time ML and standardized patterns for lineage and auditability.
  • AI innovators: See how ML forecasts energy demand and how the Databricks agent framework enables agentic workflows for pricing and finance with responsible enterprise controls.
  • Walk away with a pragmatic roadmap to land governed, AI-ready capabilities in energy.

sessions.title: An Intro to Building and Scaling Agentic Apps
sessions.body: Agents have promised a lot lately, but most people just have a job they want done and don't want to spend time on endless science experiments. Teams stall on integration, struggle with scale, and wrestle with how to deliver agents to users safely and reliably inside a real application. This intro session shows how to build and scale agentic apps end-to-end on Databricks. You'll see how Agent Bricks lets you create managed, production-ready agents; how Databricks Apps delivers them to users with governance and observability built in; and how Lakebase powers the transactional backend so your app can act — not just answer. You'll walk away with a clear blueprint for turning your first agent into a production app your whole company can use, and the confidence to move from prototype to scaled deployment without rebuilding your stack.

sessions.title: Anthropic + Adidas + Databricks: Unlocking 400 Hours of Productivity Weekly with Conversational AI
sessions.body:
LLMs are transforming how enterprises explore data and make decisions. But how do you integrate conversational AI with existing analytics and data ecosystems?

 

In this joint session, we'll explore the common use cases and design patterns that leading enterprises are adopting. Anthropic will share insights from across their customer use cases on model selection, serving infrastructure, governance and cost optimization, and integration with downstream BI & applications.

 

Then, Adidas will walk through their production implementation: how they deployed Claude via a multi-agent orchestrator to enable 200+ marketing and CRM users to explore data conversationally, compress insight-to-action cycles, and unlock productivity gains. Adidas unlocked up to 400 hours of productivity weekly and accelerated insight-to-action cycles from weeks to days

 

Learn how Claude, Agent Bricks, AI Gateway and Databricks Genie come together to transform analytics from a bottleneck into a competitive advantage.

sessions.title: Apache Iceberg™ Interoperability: First-Class Open Support in Databricks Delta Sharing
sessions.body:
Open data sharing across platform boundaries is now a reality. As organizations move toward multi-engine environments, collaborating across different catalogs and ecosystems is a strategic necessity. With the launch of first-class Iceberg support in Databricks Delta Sharing, you can maintain a single governance layer while supporting a diverse, multi-platform data estate.

 

Key Highlights:

  • First-Class Iceberg Support: Share Delta tables as native Iceberg tables via the Iceberg REST Catalog API for zero-copy sharing to Snowflake, Trino, and Spark.
  • Bi-Directional Interoperability: Bring ""foreign"" Iceberg tables from AWS Glue or Snowflake into Unity Catalog and share them to any recipient.
  • Unified Governance: Share fine-grained Views via secretless authentication, even to non-Databricks platforms.
  • Open Standards, No Lock-In: Shift from closed sharing models to a transparent protocol that supports multiple clouds, formats, and platforms simultaneously.

speakers.name: Balaji Swamynathan
speakers.bio: Balaji Swamynathan is a leader at Foot Locker, where he leads enterprise data and analytics initiatives focused on modernizing retail data platforms. With deep expertise in Databricks, cloud data architectures, and large‑scale analytics, Balaji partners closely with engineering and business teams to deliver scalable, high‑impact solutions across customer, merchandising, and operations domains. He is passionate about leveraging the lakehouse architecture, AI‑driven analytics, and real‑time insights to enable faster decision‑making and measurable business outcomes in retail.

sessions.title: Apache Spark™ Connect: The Path to Modern, AI-Ready Spark
sessions.body: Spark Connect is more than a new client interface for Apache Spark™ — it is the foundation for a modern, AI-ready, and production-friendly Spark experience. As AI assistants generate more Spark code, the defaults they learn will shape how the next generation of data applications is built — that makes Spark Connect a strategic shift, not just a technical one. In this session, we will share our vision for making Spark Connect the default way developers build with Spark. We will discuss how DataFrame-first guidance, better AI-generated code compatibility, and machine-readable API discovery can make Connect the easiest path for developers. We will also cover the work needed to build production trust, including closing migration gaps, improving observability, and increasing ecosystem compatibility. Attendees will leave with a clear view of why Spark Connect matters now and what it will take to make it the standard interface for modern Spark applications.

speakers.name: Justin Breese
speakers.bio:
Justin is a Staff Product Manager at Databricks. He primarily focuses on their serverless products - versionless runtime, dependency management (environments), and containers.

When not thinking about execution engines, you can find him staying busy with soccer, hiking, brewing beer, roasting coffee, and older cars.

Justin lives in Topanga, CA with his wife, son, and daughter.

sessions.title: Applying Software Development Principles to a Data-Driven World: Automating SDP from Dev to Prod
sessions.body: Are you a data architect struggling to bring rigor and best practices to your data operations? This session highlights how the Intermountain Health Data Teams transformed their data platform by overcoming cultural resistance and technical gaps to fully automate production-grade data pipeline deployments. By combining Databricks Asset Bundles, GitHub Actions, and Spark Declarative Pipelines, they built a reliable CI/CD workflow supporting nearly all workloads. Parameterized deployments manage dev and prod seamlessly, while a trunk based Git strategy avoids the complexity of multi branch models. The impact: over 90% improvement in deployment reliability, fewer hotfixes, and 20% faster processing. And because transformation depends on people, we’ll share how Intermountain guided teams away from GUI only ETL habits, building trust, clarity, and excitement for this modern, maintainable approach.

speakers.name: Benjamin Swatling
speakers.bio: Ben Swatling is a Senior Analytics Engineer at Intermountain Health, focused on helping teams build data flows that don’t break in production. He designs scalable data patterns and development workflows, while enabling others to build reliable data pipelines using Databricks. Ben emphasizes strong CI/CD practices to make data work safer, more repeatable, and easier to sustain over time. His work helps analytics teams move faster without sacrificing quality or trust.

sessions.title: Apps Factory on Databricks​: Provision, Standardize, Observe and Govern 100+ Apps​
sessions.body: Databricks Apps makes it easy to publish the first app. We address the compounding challenges organizations face when scaling to 10, 50, or 100+ Databricks Apps: inconsistent architecture, unclear access control, missing standards, ungoverned AI components and runaway costs. We will walk through a comprehensive methodology, including solutions and principles to provision, govern and observe dozens of applications at enterprise scale. The session includes reference architecture, frameworks, templates, a production readiness checklist, CI/CD setup, security & access control, unified logging and cost tracking. Attendees receive a comprehensive technical governance and adaptation playbook to effectively manage and scale app ecosystems.

speakers.name: Domonkos Pal
speakers.bio: Domonkos Pal is Head of Digital Products at Hiflylabs, where he helps enterprises design and build data and AI applications on Databricks for clients across Europe and the US. His work centers on Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Genie, agents and the broader app ecosystem — particularly how to make AI applications scalable, secure, and maintainable in production, with a strong focus on DevEx and agentic  engineering workflows. As the world's first Databricks Apps MVP (2025–2026), Domonkos returns to the Data + AI Summit stage in 2026.

sessions.title: Architecting Agentic Security: Scaling Threat Detection with LLM and Lake house Architecture
sessions.body: When new threat intelligence lands, attackers are already moving. Adobe’s security team needed more than automation, so we built an agentic security platform that ingests data, orchestrates hunts, and surfaces detections with minimal human intervention. Using reasoning, agents analyze threats, validate attack paths, and execute fleet sweeps, reducing threat detection timelines from days to minutes.   In this talk, we’ll walk through how we built this system on a lakehouse architecture. Databricks Workflows orchestrate parallel hunt campaigns across various security logs, autonomously triggering jobs and aggregating results. You’ll learn how we designed for agentic behavior, including multi-source ingestion into a single pipeline, workflow orchestration logic that decides when and what to hunt, and production patterns that keep the system reliable at scale. We’ll share architecture and code so you can adapt these agentic security patterns in your own environment.

speakers.name: Sai Kiran Uppu
speakers.bio: Sai Kiran Uppu is a Senior Security Researcher on Adobe's Cyber Threat Research and Intelligence team, where he architects Adobe's agentic AI threat intelligence and fleet sweep platform protecting over a billion users. He is the 2026 Gold winner for AI Security Innovator of the Year at the Cybersecurity Excellence Awards and a Recorded Future RSA CTF champion. Kiran has delivered the keynote at ToroHack 10.0, served as an invited panelist at Johns Hopkins' Security Metamorphosis 2026, and spoken at IEEE SVCC, The Diana Initiative, BSides SLC, Penn State, and the UMBC Cyber Defense Lab. He judges Atlantic Council's Cyber 9/12 Strategy Challenge and student hackathons, and is CISSP, GCTI, and AWS Security - Specialty certified.

sessions.title: Architecting Data Warehouses for Large-Scale Deployments
sessions.body:
This advanced, half-day course covers how to architect Databricks SQL environments for enterprise scale — supporting hundreds or thousands of users across multiple business units. Participants will learn about designing scalable data ingestion pipelines with Lakeflow, planning multi-workspace and Unity Catalog strategies, implementing fine-grained security using row filters, column masks, and ABAC policies, and deploy solutions using Declarative Automation Bundles and GitOps. The course includes hands-on labs and demos.

Prerequisites

  • Working knowledge of Databricks SQL (SQL Editor, warehouses, dashboards, query profiles)
  • Unity Catalog fundamentals (three-level namespace, privileges, managed vs. external tables)
  • Delta Lake essentials (ACID, time travel, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM)
  • Cloud infrastructure concepts: Cloud storage, Networking, IAM, and Infrastructure-as-Code basics
  • Data warehousing concepts (medallion architecture, ETL/ELT, star schemas, multi-environment strategies)
  • Databricks workspace administration experience (users, groups, service principals, SSO)

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Architecting Data Warehouses for Large-Scale Deployments
sessions.body: This advanced, half-day course covers how to architect Databricks SQL environments for enterprise scale — supporting hundreds or thousands of users across multiple business units. Participants will learn about designing scalable data ingestion pipelines with Lakeflow, planning multi-workspace and Unity Catalog strategies, implementing fine-grained security using row filters, column masks, and ABAC policies, and deploy solutions using Declarative Automation Bundles and GitOps. The course includes hands-on labs and demos.PrerequisitesWorking knowledge of Databricks SQL (SQL Editor, warehouses, dashboards, query profiles)Unity Catalog fundamentals (three-level namespace, privileges, managed vs. external tables)Delta Lake essentials (ACID, time travel, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM)Cloud infrastructure concepts: Cloud storage, Networking, IAM, and Infrastructure-as-Code basicsData warehousing concepts (medallion architecture, ETL/ELT, star schemas, multi-environment strategies)Databricks workspace administration experience (users, groups, service principals, SSO)Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: AskPorto — a Unified Agentic AI Solution for Data Analytics and Discovery
sessions.body: The Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), Singapore’s social security agency, manages complex data across multiple business lines with unique analytical requirements despite centralising on Databricks Lakehouse. Users struggled with traditional querying methods and fragmented governance documentation across multiple sources, creating analytical silos. Employees needed intelligent systems capable of querying multiple sources without technical expertise, requiring contextualised responses understanding domain-specific terminology and automatic validation. Solution: unified conversational interface with multi-agent orchestration built on Databricks architecture. Orchestrating AI routes queries to specialised agents — Databricks Genie for contextualised data answers, Purview for metadata discovery, RAG-powered agents for governance knowledge — whilst maintaining audit trails and compliance. Stakeholders access comprehensive insights via conversational queries with automated accuracy checks.

sessions.title: AstraZeneca's Multi-Agent System: Lessons Scaling Agents by 10x With Agent Bricks
sessions.body:
AstraZeneca built a multi-agent system using Agent Bricks to transform how commercial teams access pharmaceutical data. The Brand Assistant uses a supervisor agent coordinating specialized sub-agents across therapeutic areas, combining structured data via Genie Spaces with unstructured documents via Knowledge Assistant.

 

Unity Catalog integration with Entra ID enforces strict permission boundaries. MCP unlocks third-party tool integration.The architecture scaled from 5-agent POC to 20+ agents in production, designed for 50+.

 

Key components:

  • Multi-Agent Supervisor for orchestration
  • Genie Spaces for NL-to-SQL
  • Knowledge Assistant for documents
  • Unity Catalog for row/column-level security
  • MLflow for tracing.

 

This session covers:

  • Multi-agent architecture patterns
  • Permission-preserving design
  • When to split supervisors vs. add agents
  • Human-in-the-loop testing
  • Why bad data breaks agents regardless of tech
  • Organizational challenges of agent ownership
  • Lessons from scaling

speakers.name: Brian Burke
speakers.bio: Brian Burke is a Senior Director of Platform Engineering for Data, Analytics & AI at AstraZeneca. Brian drives platforms and advanced analytics capabilities to deliver business value across commercial functions.

speakers.name: Homayoon Moradi
speakers.bio: Homayoon Moradi is a Staff AI Engineer on the AI FDE team at Databricks, leading EMEA customer engagements and specializing in production-grade agentic AI solutions.

sessions.title: Atlassian's Journey of Using AI/BI Genie From Pilot to Production and What's Next?
sessions.body:
This session is not a generic “AI is the future” talk. It is a practical, experience‑based guide to taking Databricks AI/BI Genie from a promising pilot to a trusted, production‑grade capability. Dashboards answer “what,” but not “why” or “what if.” Here is where Genie comes in.

 

We’ll walk through our journey at Atlassian from pilot to production—designing Genie spaces on curated tables and metrics, building an evaluation framework for accuracy and coverage, and integrating Genie into our everyday tools and Rovo AI agent. We will touch upon how Databricks and Atlassian partnered to bring the power of Genie to our Rovo Marketplace and built the ability to route a user question to the right Genie space.

 

In the end attendees will have a concrete “0‑to‑95*” playbook for unleashing their data with Genie to reach a point where roughly 95% of everyday questions can be answered accurately, safely, and self‑service freeing data teams to focus on higher‑value work and empowering faster decisions.

speakers.name: Manav Trivedi
speakers.bio: Manav is a distinguished Senior Product Manager with Atlassian's Rovo Chat. Manav spearheaded the Atlassian Databricks collaboration building the Rovo Databricks Genie connector product vision and enabling internal Atlassian teams to harness the power of Genie.

speakers.name: preddy preddy
speakers.bio: Prakash is a Data Engineering & Analytics Leader whose career spans 16+ years working with companies such as Linkedin and Atlassian where he has led modernization and transformations using his expertise in the intersection of Data and AI.

sessions.title: Automate Deployment with Databricks Asset Bundles
sessions.body:
This hands-on course covers DevOps principles, including CI/CD and testing, applied to Databricks data engineering pipelines. It focuses on continuous deployment using the Databricks REST API, SDK, and CLI, specifically incorporating Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) for streamlined deployment across environments. You will learn to modify, validate, deploy, and execute DABs for multiple configurations using the Databricks CLI. The course also introduces using Visual Studio Code as an IDE for local development and concludes with automating deployment using GitHub Actions and DABs. By the end, you'll be able to automate Databricks project deployments with DABs, improving efficiency through DevOps practices.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Strong familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform
  • Intermediate Python programming experience, including designing and implementing functions and classes
  • Intermediate SQL experience for data analysis and transformation
  • Experience with data ingestion and transformation using PySpark
  • Familiarity with DevOps practices and basic Git version control

sessions.title: Automating Document Work with Long-Horizon AI Agents
sessions.body: ~90% of enterprise data is unstructured, and a lot of that lives in the form of documents - PDFs, pptx, docx, etc. - powering a majority of enterprise knowledge work.AI agents have the potential to simultaneously better make sense of docs and also automate human workflows over them. Existing document AI use cases have either been long-running but constrained (e.g. a batch invoice processing through RPA), or non-deterministic but short-horizon (e.g. ChatGPT deep research over a collection of existing files). Going forward there's a huge opportunity to build long-running agents that can understand, reason over, and edit documents at scale.In this session, we'll walk through core advances in document OCR and agent orchestration that have given rise to initial use cases around doc extraction workflows and general-purpose chatbots (and share real-world customer use cases). We will then articulate some of the remaining gaps needed to achieve "long-running" document work automation.

speakers.name: Jerry Liu
speakers.bio: Jerry is the co-founder/CEO of LlamaIndex, the most accurate and secure platform to automate document workflows with AI agents. Before this, he led ML monitoring at Robust Intelligence, did self-driving AI research at Uber ATG, and worked on recommendation systems at Quora.

sessions.title: Automating KPI Reasoning and Narrative Generation With Agent Bricks and Databricks Apps
sessions.body: Monthly performance reporting previously required approximately 7 person-days each month, as analysts manually wrote queries, reviewed distributed datasets, interpreted metric relationships and produced presentation-ready reports. This repetitive process tied up analytical resources and slowed decision-making. To address this, I built an app-based automation pipeline using multi-supervised agents with Agent Bricks and Databricks Apps. The agent operates as an analyst, systematically analyzing relevant data sources through a structured, table-driven representation to identify key drivers, evaluate metric relationships, and generate narrative insights without manual querying. Outputs are delivered through Databricks Apps as a self-serve analytics platform with automatically refreshed metrics and visualizations, eliminating repetitive reporting work, reducing monthly effort by approximately 7 person-days, and enabling agent-authored reporting for both analytics and non-analytics stakeholders.

speakers.name: Seong Kyung Kim
speakers.bio: I am a Data Scientist focused on applying AI and machine learning to automate workflows, improve analytical systems, and support better operational decision-making. My work spans user behavior analytics, applied machine learning, and agentic AI, with an emphasis on transforming complex, fragmented processes into scalable and practical solutions. I am particularly interested in building analytical systems that make AI and data more actionable, measurable, and impactful in real-world environments.

sessions.title: Automating Phishing Triage With Agentic AI and Knowledge Graph Memory on Databricks
sessions.body: Phishing attacks remain a persistent threat, exploiting human trust through sophisticated impersonation. In this session, we present a Databricks-based compound agentic system using knowledge graphs, multiple agents, and MLflow to automate triage of reported phishing emails at scale, reducing analyst workload and accelerating threat response. We walk through scalable pipelines built on Spark Structured Streaming and Delta Lake, then describe how our knowledge graph provides long-term memory, storing historical emails to enable reasoning across campaigns. We demonstrate agentic orchestration with LangGraph where specialized agents use tools to analyze headers, sender reputation, body content, URLs, and behaviors before producing triage decisions with reasoning traces. We cover evaluations, observability, including hallucination detection, metrics, and tracking with MLflow. Join us to learn practical patterns that combine multi-agent reasoning with production workflows on Databricks.

speakers.name: Virender Dhiman
speakers.bio: Looking forward to speak about my work and networking with people at Data+AI summit.

speakers.name: Andrew Hinton
speakers.bio: Andrew Hinton is a Distinguished Engineer and AI Systems Architect shaping the next generation of cyberdefense with agentic AI. He leads the design of event-driven autonomous systems that help security teams detect, investigate, and respond to threats across large-scale enterprise environments. His architectures combine governed autonomy, durable memory, deterministic orchestration, and continuous evaluation to keep decisions fast, reliable, and auditable. Andrew’s work is helping redefine how defenders operate against increasingly automated adversaries.

sessions.title: BASF Coatings: Scaling Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems with Federated Governance on Databricks
sessions.body: As enterprises evolve from isolated AI assistants to domain-specific multi-agent systems, scaling innovation without overloading central teams becomes critical. BASF Coatings addresses this with MAUI (Multi-Agent Universal Interface), a Databricks-native platform that enables business to build, operate, and scale multi-agent solutions within a unified enterprise framework.MAUI expands the success of the MarketMind project across supply chain, marketing and sales. By separating responsibilities among domain experts, data stewards, and users, it accelerates deployment while maintaining security and governance. Technically, MAUI runs as Databricks Apps, using Lakebase for context store and UC for secure data access. Deployed across three units with 1000+ users, MAUI achieves 95% accuracy in cross-domain data retrieval, reducing query times by 50–80%. Its federated governance allows stewards to improve intelligence and expand usecases, with full enterprise rollout planned.

speakers.name: Bernhard Bartmann
speakers.bio: Bernhard is Product Owner AI Solutions at BASF Coatings in Münster, Germany. He turns high-impact AI use cases into scaled value, aligning AI strategy closely with business goals across the Coatings portfolio. Building on an academic foundation in Digital Business & Innovation Management and hands-on experience in Data & AI, he translates real organizational needs into robust, reusable platforms and architectures that accelerate time-to-value and enable scalable, compliant innovation.

speakers.name: Lars Schrameyer
