speakers.bio: Lars is Head of the Data & AI Office at BASF Coatings GmbH in Münster, Germany. In this role, Lars leads the strategic implementation of the company’s AI and data initiatives, driving innovation and operational excellence across business units. With a strong background in digital transformation and enterprise data platforms, Lars is passionate about building robust data ecosystems and fostering a culture of advanced analytics. Lars’s leadership ensures that AI strategy is aligned with business goals, enabling BASF Coatings to harness the full potential of data-driven decision-making.

sessions.title: Behind the Curtain: How We Do Eval in Genie
sessions.body: Evaluating AI systems is notoriously challenging—especially when correctness isn’t binary. In this talk, we’ll walk through how the Genie engineering team approaches evaluation at scale, from defining what “good” looks like to building reliable, automated eval pipelines. We’ll cover our mix of offline benchmarks, human-in-the-loop validation, and production feedback loops, along with the tradeoffs we’ve encountered. The goal is to share practical patterns and lessons learned that can help teams move faster while maintaining trust in their models.

sessions.title: Behind the curtain: Key learnings from building Genie
sessions.body: As organizations scale, the real challenge isn't just single talk AI — but designing a system like Genie that can coordinate multiple agents, domains, MCP connections, structured data, unstructured data, etc. while keeping the user experience effortless.We've introduces a unified, multi-agent interface that allows anyone to ask complex questions across their entire data and agent estate and get answers without needing to understand how the system works underneath.In this session, we’ll pull back the curtain on how Genie was designed and share the best practices we developed to make multi-agent analytics usable, reliable, and scalable.In this session, we’ll cover:- How to design a unified experience across multiple agents and data domains- How to route, orchestrate, and combine results from different agents- How to balance flexibility with simplicity for business users- Key lessons learned building and deploying multi-agent systems in production

speakers.name: Yi Liu
speakers.bio: Yi is a Sr. Staff Software Engineer at Databricks.

sessions.title: Benchmarks Don't Lie: Inside Lakebase Performance Engineering
sessions.body:
Get an inside look at how the Lakebase engineering team designs benchmarks that reflect real-world workload patterns rather than synthetic best-case scenarios, and how we isolate variables across the storage, compute, and network layers to understand where time is actually spent. From there, we'll walk through results from our latest engineering work, covering throughput under concurrent load, latency across workload types, and the optimizations that moved the needle most.

 

This is not a marketing benchmarks talk. It's an engineering post-mortem on what we tested, what surprised us, and what the numbers mean for how you architect and tune your own Lakebase workloads.

speakers.name: David Wein
speakers.bio: David Wein is a Principal Software Engineer on Databricks Lakebase, focused on performance and scalability for cloud-native transactional workloads. With nearly three decades of experience building enterprise OLTP databases at Sybase, SAP, AWS Aurora PostgreSQL, and now Databricks, he has designed core kernels, logging, and durability systems, holds multiple patents in database internals, and is a frequent speaker on running mission-critical applications in the cloud.

sessions.title: Best Practices for Disaster Recovery and Resilience on Databricks
sessions.body:
When a region goes down, every minute counts. But building disaster recovery for a lakehouse is often complex, requiring coordination across data, metadata, and workspace assets.

 

In this session, we’ll share best practices for designing resilient data and AI platforms on Databricks. Learn how to think about recovery objectives, including RPO and RTO, and how to architect for cross-region availability across your data, governance layer, and production workloads.

 

We’ll walk through common patterns for replication, failover, and recovery, along with tradeoffs between cost, complexity, and performance. You’ll also see how to reduce operational overhead, avoid brittle DIY approaches, and ensure applications can recover quickly when disruptions occur.

 

Whether you’re supporting mission-critical analytics or production AI systems, walk away with practical guidance to design, test, and operate disaster recovery with confidence.

speakers.name: Bart Samwel
speakers.bio: Bart is a Principal Software Engineer at Databricks. He works on disaster recovery and Delta Lake.

speakers.name: Sirui Sun
speakers.bio: Sirui is a Sr. Staff Product Manager at Databricks, working on making Delta simpler and more performant. Prior to Databricks, he's spent time working on Google Cloud and at Microsoft. At the Data + AI Summit, he'd love to talk to you about your data goals and challenges!

sessions.title: Best Practices for Lakebase
sessions.body: This deep-dive session covers architectural and operational best practices for building production-grade applications on Lakebase. You'll learn how to design schemas and connection patterns for performance, how to leverage autoscaling and branching for cost-efficient development workflows, and how to apply governance controls at scale using Unity Catalog. Whether you're migrating an existing PostgreSQL workload or building something new, you'll leave with actionable guidance for running Lakebase reliably in production.

speakers.name: Som Natarajan
speakers.bio: Som Natarajan is an SA working in the digital natives space helping them scale their data and AI initiatives across EMEA. Som has worked with global organisations for over 20 years focusing on enterprise AI, data governance and hybrid cloud technologies.

sessions.title: Best Practices for Running dbt on Databricks: From SQL Models to Production Pipelines
sessions.body: Many teams use dbt to standardize transformations, but still struggle with brittle orchestration and inconsistent governance. This session shows how to run dbt on Databricks as part of a unified analytics engineering workflow, from SQL models through production pipelines. We’ll cover proven patterns for building a medallion-style architecture, orchestrating dbt jobs directly in Databricks, and applying governance and observability using Unity Catalog for a faster, more reliable delivery of analytics-ready data at scale.

speakers.name: Ramiz Bozai
speakers.bio: [Placeholder]

speakers.name: Srilekha Dornadula
speakers.bio: [Placeholder]

sessions.title: Beyond Batch: Engineering Self-Evolving Ingestion with Databricks Auto Loader
sessions.body:
Is your data engineering team trapped in brittle schema fixes and rising costs? As data sources multiply, traditional ingestion stalls enterprise insights. At Capital One Software, we’ve moved beyond static ETL to a “self-evolving” framework that treats data as a dynamic stream. This session reveals our modular architecture using Databricks Auto Loader to bridge multi-platform data into S3 with zero manual overhead. We’ll dive into how Schema Evolution and Rescue Columns handle upstream drift automatically, keeping pipelines live when source systems change.

 

Key takeaways:

  • Modular design: Decouple ingestion from transformation for reusable, enterprise-scale patterns
  • Dynamic schema management: Strategies to detect and adapt to drift without breaking dependencies
  • Cost optimization: Real-world tactics for balancing trigger intervals and compute for peak efficiency.
  • Transition from reactive maintenance to automated data empowerment

sessions.title: Beyond Dashboards: How Grupo Bimbo Delivers Insights with Databricks AgentBricks
sessions.body:
Commercial operations at Grupo Bimbo generate thousands of transactions every day across sales routes. While dashboards highlight valued insights, commercial team are constantly on the move and don’t have time to explore BI tools.

 

Grupo Bimbo rethought insight delivery using Databricks Agent Bricks — moving from “look at dashboards” to “ask and receive answers.” For supervisors, we implemented AI/BI Genie as a conversational AI layer over sales data, enabling natural-language questions like “Which clients were missed this week?”— no dashboards required.

 

For executives, we built an AI query agent powered by Claude that automatically reads multiple KPIs and summarizes insights, generating reports delivered directly by email.

 

All agents run on Databricks with Unity Catalog ensuring secure data access.

 

We’ll share the real architecture, prompt design choices and lessons learned and how this approach accelerated decisions, expanded insight adoption and improved sales process efficiency.

speakers.name: Esteban Ramirez
speakers.bio: Data scientist with a mathematical background and over 7 years of experience in applied analytics, primarily in retail and research environments. Currently, I lead a team at Grupo Bimbo, where I develop data-driven solutions to improve key business processes.

speakers.name: Mauricio Imenez
speakers.bio: Global Internal Audit & Data Analytics Leader (CIA) with 20+ years of experience building and scaling data-driven assurance functions for multinational organizations. Proven track record implementing continuous auditing programs, leading global analytics teams, and delivering risk reduction, cost savings, artificial intelligence projects and process automation. Big Four background with deep expertise in Data Analytics, Internal Controls (COSO/SOX), Fraud Detection, and Continuous Assurance.

sessions.title: Beyond Medallion: Architecting Disney’s DATOS for Complex, Real-Time Data Streams With Databricks
sessions.body: Disney’s Medallion architecture laid a strong foundation for enterprise data governance, but emerging needs—ranging from personalized user experiences to real-time financial insights—required a richer, near real-time view across domains such as subscriptions, billing and payments. DATOS addresses this by serving as a contextual aggregation and abstraction layer built on the Databricks Lakehouse Platform. Using Structured Streaming and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, DATOS ingests diverse sources like Kafka, Kinesis, and data lakes while absorbing upstream schema and delivery variability to provide stable, reusable data products. Liquid Clustering enhances performance on high‑volume tables, and Unity Catalog ensures unified governance and security. This session explores how DATOS reduces operational overhead, decouples producers and consumers, accelerates onboarding, and delivers a context-aware source of truth that powers real-time analytics, Unity Dashboards, and advanced AI/ML workloads.

sessions.title: Beyond Monitoring: Lakeflow Observability for Operational Health
sessions.body:
It is 3 AM. A dashboard is stale, an SLA slipped, and everyone is guessing which job, pipeline, or dependency broke first. That is when surface-level monitoring stops being useful. You need observability that shows the health of your workflows and helps you find the cause fast.

 

In this session, we will show how Lakeflow Observability helps data engineering teams move from reactive monitoring to real operational health. You will see how to monitor runs, tasks, dependencies, alerts, and health metrics across jobs and pipelines, and how Databricks system tables provide the historical depth needed for root-cause analysis, performance analysis, cost tracking, and reliability reporting at scale.

 

We will also cover practical patterns for tracking streaming backlog, freshness, SLA risk, and failure trends, and show how Genie Code can help teams troubleshoot faster using natural language. Your 3 AM self will thank you.

speakers.name: Theresa Hammer
speakers.bio: Theresa is a product manager working on Lakeflow observability. Previously, she was a team lead and enterprise account manager at Oracle, focusing on the core tech business for the German market. Theresa has also worked in analytics and sales for electronic trading solutions at Bloomberg. She holds a master’s degree in the field of computer science from the University of Pennsylvania.

sessions.title: Beyond One-Shot AI: How to Design Context-Aware Agents
sessions.body: Most AI agents today are one-shot: they answer a question and forget. But the agents delivering real enterprise value run for minutes, hours, or days — completing multi-step tasks across tools and systems. That introduces challenges most teams aren't prepared for: state management, fault tolerance, and orchestration across long-running workflows.This session explores the design patterns required to build reliable context-aware agents. You'll learn how to persist state across steps, recover from failures gracefully, coordinate workflows across multiple tools, and monitor execution so agents can complete complex tasks over extended periods — without losing context or starting over when something breaks.You'll walk away with a practical blueprint for designing agents that move beyond one-shot answers — and deliver the kind of sustained, context-aware work that drives real business outcomes.

speakers.name: Aravind Segu
speakers.bio: Software Engineer at Databricks working on AI Agents

speakers.name: Elise Gonzales
speakers.bio: Elise is a Product Manager on the Agent Bricks team at Databricks focused on building agents. Before Databricks, she ran the product team at Amperity, a Customer Data Platform, as well as working on HoloLens at Microsoft and Alexa at Amazon. She got her undergraduate degree in Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon.

sessions.title: Beyond Simple Q&A: Building an Agent Orchestrator for Enterprise Analytics
sessions.body: What does it take to go from multiple separate Genie spaces to a single agent that can coordinate across them all? How do you ensure they reference context from your unstructured data, pull up relevant BI reports, and loop in downstream reporting agents? In this breakout session, we’ll share how the World Bank built a multi-agent system that coordinates Genie spaces, document retrieval, and downstream reporting behind a single interface.What we'll cover:Orchestrator architecture: Designing a LangGraph-based orchestrator that routes natural-language questions to the right domain Genie, decomposes multi-step queries, and synthesizes unified answers.Consistency through the metrics layer: Introducing metrics-grounded Genie spaces to reduce answer variability.Bridging structured and unstructured data: Combining Genie's structured query capabilities with a RAG-powered agent for document retrieval and an auto-visualization agent that can show users plots and surface relevant BI reports.

speakers.name: Max Marcussen
speakers.bio:
Max Marcussen is an AI Engineer on Databricks’s AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team. This team delivers professional services engagements to help our customers build and productionize first-of-its-kind AI applications. The team also works cross-functionally with engineering and research to shape product direction.

Max has worked with customers in manufacturing, life sciences, CPG, and financial services on production-grade GenAI projects, including multi-agent systems, intelligent document processing use cases, RAG, and text-to-SQL solutions. His work frequently involves designing evaluation frameworks with LLM judges and using prompt optimization techniques like GEPA to systematically improve agent quality.

speakers.name: Suresh Kaudi
speakers.bio: Suresh Kaudi is a seasoned data professional with over two decades of experience in data analytics, engineering, governance, and platform development. His expertise spans the design and execution of robust data architectures, advanced analytics solutions, and governance frameworks that ensure data integrity and compliance. Suresh has a proven track record of leading high-impact initiatives, notably spearheading the development and successful implementation of a comprehensive data strategy for MDB. His ability to align technical solutions with business objectives has consistently delivered transformative outcomes in complex, data-driven environments.

sessions.title: Beyond the Dashboard: Designing Premium, AI-Powered Operations Apps on Databricks
sessions.body: Connected systems generate massive operational telemetry, yet most teams still consume it through generic dashboards that can bury insight behind filters and grids. Turning raw signal into decisive action across hundreds of assets is as much a product and design challenge as a data one.This session shows how to deliver branded, business-facing operations experiences on Databricks using Apps, Lakebase, Model Serving, and Genie as a single substrate for data, AI, and product.We follow an operations lead through a custom app built around an aircraft fleet: a top-level overview, deeper insight views with recommended actions, and an AI chat that answers natural-language questions on the same governed tables.The talk focuses on patterns you can reuse: shaping noisy telemetry into decision-ready gold tables, designing apps that feel like products rather than dashboards and orchestrating multiple AI agents.

sessions.title: Beyond the Sandbox: Scaling Autonomous AI Agents with Anthropic and Edmunds
sessions.body: As enterprises move from AI prototypes to production-grade agents, one challenge dominates: deploying systems that reason deeply over proprietary data, securely and at scale. This session shows how Anthropic Claude's frontier reasoning, natively integrated into the Databricks Platform with Unity AI Gateway for governance and Databricks Apps as the deployment runtime, provides the full-stack foundation for domain-specific agents enterprises can trust.We will hear from Edmunds on how they built a multi-agent digital workforce powered by Claude on Databricks. We'll deep-dive into how a "hunting party" of specialized agents autonomously writes code, opens merge requests, and audited 101 legacy schemas in one afternoon (vs. two weeks manually). Attendees will learn how 40+ composable skills yield exponential capability, how a self-improving flywheel slashed prototype-to-production lead times by 50% and how tasks that once cost $640 in human effort now run for $25 in agentic compute.

sessions.title: Beyond the Trace: adidas’ Agent Digital Twin for Governance, Cost and ROI
sessions.body:
Your agent answered but can you prove why, what it cost, and what breaks when a tool or prompt changes? AI spend is forecast near $1.5T in 2025 and GenAI at $644B, yet Gartner predicts >40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end-2027 as costs rise and controls lag. At adidas (200+ serving endpoints, 300+ data and AI products, 6k+ registered models, 600k+ pipeline runs), we go beyond per-run traces to an agent digital twin: A lakehouse control plane mapping agent → tool → prompt → retrieval → model call → post-processing, then rolling up risk, quality and unit economics across a fleet. You’ll see a Databricks pattern with MLflow Tracing, Unity Catalog + system tables for audit evidence and DBU/cost signals, plus eval/optimization loops with governance guardrails.

 

Key highlights:

  • Digital-twin control plane for fleets
  • Per-hop unit economics + cost leak forensics
  • Continuous audit evidence by design
  • ROI attribution by agent behavior

speakers.name: Mahavir Teraiya
speakers.bio: Mahavir Teraiya is a Senior Resident Solutions Architect at Databricks with 15+ years of experience in Data, ML, and large-scale AI platform design. Formerly with AWS and Zalando, he now focuses on helping enterprise customers scale GenAI through agentic workflows. At DAIS, Mahavir will present the groundbreaking GenAI platform built with Adidas the first of its kind in EMEA driving 20% productivity gains and up to 91% cost savings. He is currently pursuing a PhD in Federated Learning and an MBA in IT. A passionate technologist and frequent speaker at AWS events and GopherCon, Mahavir thrives at the intersection of cutting-edge tech and business value.

speakers.name: Pandey, Rahul
speakers.bio: Rahul is a Senior Solution Architect at Adidas, where he focuses on constructing ML architecture designs that are both cost-effective and efficient. Currently, he is taking responsibility as a Machine Learning Journey Owner in the Lakehouse platform, taking charge of advancing the field of machine learning. One of his primary motivations is to promote awareness of sustainability in AI among Data Science teams

sessions.title: Bionic Supply Chain: Architecting a Unified Agentic Framework for Risk & Cost Recovery
sessions.body:
The modern supply chain is fractured, stuck in a “visibility vacuum” of cost asymmetry and a “triage trap” where material and production planners miss critical risks and purchasing managers miss cost targets due to cognitive overload. To bridge this gap, we present a unified vision for the AI-enabled supply chain ecosystem, moving beyond disparate tools to a cohesive intelligent platform.

 

We introduce an agentic architecture built entirely on the lakehouse, utilizing Databricks Apps and Unity Catalog to serve distinct personas. For purchasing managers, we deploy NOVAA, an engine using MLflow to benchmark “should-costs” and Mosaic AI to arrest margin leakage and generate negotiation playbooks. Simultaneously, SONAR, our supply planners’ control tower, empowers them by aggregating SAP/TMS data into a unified truth. Here, a hierarchical agentic workflow, powered by Agent Bricks, bridges classical ML with GenAI to predict disruptions and orchestrate sub-agents for autonomous resolution.

speakers.name: Collin Brosko
speakers.bio: Collin Brosko is an experienced data and analytics leader currently serving as the Manager of Data & Analytics at Rivian Automotive LLC. He specializes in building scalable data architectures, driving AI and machine learning implementations, and leading engineering teams to deliver end-to-end solutions that optimize complex operations. Prior to his current role, Collin held key data science and architecture positions at industry-leading organizations, including IBM and ZF Group. Throughout his career, he has focused on modernizing data platforms, deploying advanced analytics, and transforming raw data into strategic, actionable business value. Collin holds a Master of Applied Data Science from the University of Michigan

speakers.name: Nikhil Pande
speakers.bio: Nikhil Pande is a distinguished data leader and Staff Data Architect at Rivian, specializing in the design of scalable data ecosystems and the orchestration of agentic AI. Having played an instrumental role in migrating Rivian’s data landscape to Databricks, he holds registered intellectual property for his innovations in real-time PLM ingestion pipelines. Currently, Nikhil champions AI adoption by architecting agentic frameworks; he recently pioneered a Procurement Negotiations App utilizing a master-agent architecture and human-in-the-loop feedback. With over a decade of expertise and a Master’s in Data Science from the University of Illinois, Nikhil balances technical rigor with a lifelong passion for scuba diving and hiking.

sessions.title: Blue Origin — Using Data to Build a Road to Space
sessions.body:
At Blue Origin, Databricks is the central data lakehouse for design, manufacturing, and launch operations. Scaling to thousands of pipelines without scaling headcount required rethinking how we manage data in the first place. We will share how we use AI and automation to build pipelines and tables with no human intervention required and how we automated data quality and metadata management to make our data AI ready. This enables federated data teams across the company to use trustworthy data and AI to build a road to space!

 

We will walk through a multi-agent system built on this foundation to manage satellite telemetry. An orchestrator queries a knowledge graph of prior episodes and a vector store of resolution procedures, then routes tasks to specialist agents for anomaly classification, forecasting, resolution, and command safety validation. Each execution is captured, clustered, and distilled back into procedural memory, so the system improves from its own operational history.

speakers.name: Clark Stevens
speakers.bio: Clark Stevens is the Director of Enterprise Data Management & AI at Blue Origin, where he leads the data and AI capabilities that connect data across the design, build and operate lifecycle of space systems. His teams focus on making Blue Origin’s data available, trustworthy, annotated and searchable by both humans and AI agents so decisions are grounded in real operational context. Previously, Clark led development of large-scale cloud data platforms and analytics products at Amazon, advised enterprises as a consultant on modernizing their data and BI stacks, and helped early-stage startups build their first data and ML capabilities—experience that gives him a blend of deep technical judgment, product sensibility, and pragmatic execution.

speakers.name: Theodor Talvac
speakers.bio: Theo Talvac is a Senior Manager of Ground Software at Blue Origin, where he leads an engineering team building the satellite ground system for the Blue Ring program. He serves as single-threaded leader for a multi-agent AI platform for autonomous satellite operations and is architecting Blue Ring's Mission Planning System to support the platform's various missions across the commercial, civil, and government space. . Previously, Theo held principal engineering and product management roles at York Space Systems, AST SpaceMobile, and Kratos, spanning Command & Control, Flight Dynamics, and Mission Planning across various programs in GEO and LEO orbit regimes. He holds a B.S. & M.S. in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Maryland.

sessions.title: Blueprint to Breakthrough: Activating Banking Analytics, AI, and Agentic Use Cases
sessions.body:
This session continues the story of how a Regional Bank is modernizing its AI and analytics journey, evolving from building the foundation to activating value through measurable business outcomes. Powered by Databricks and Deloitte’s industry experience, the Enterprise Data and Analytics Hub is a one-stop shop for line-of-business and enterprise consumption, anchored by a governed Data Marketplace that simplifies discovery and reuse of trusted data products. As part of this evolution, Databricks serves as the knowledge base for enterprise agentic and AI capabilities, and Databricks Genie is being leveraged to accelerate development and delivery of business-ready solutions through conversational and developer-enabled experiences.

 

The session will highlight how the bank is operationalizing these capabilities through a prioritized pipeline of high-impact use cases by accelerating speed to insight, improving consistency across reporting and analytics, and realizing value at scale. Discover how the bank is embedding advanced analytics and AI, including agentic and multi-agent systems, into decisioning and workflows with strong governance, security, and controls.

speakers.name: Mohan Sankararaman
speakers.bio: Mohan Sankararaman is executive vice president and chief information officer for First Horizon Corporation. Sankararaman joined the company in 2009 and has served in his current role since 2020. Prior to this role, he was director of strategic initiatives, leading efforts with a focus on executional excellence and managing the day-to-day activities for several mergers and acquisitions to ensure a smooth integration, conversion, and transition for the bank’s clients and associates.

speakers.name: Shailender Sidhu
speakers.bio: Shailender is a leader in Deloitte Consulting's Financial Services Industry AI & Engineering practice. He works with US and Global financial services institutions to deliver and advise on large scale enterprise AI & Data driven transformations and change agenda. He supports line of business leaders across the financial services industry segments to drive growth, regulatory, compliance and efficiency agenda.

sessions.title: BP Accelerates Maintenance Decisions With Conversational Analytics With Genie
sessions.body: BP, a global energy company, operates complex, asset-intensive environments where maintenance, reliability, safety and logistics decisions must be made quickly and with confidence. Across refineries and sites, teams rely on data from dozens of systems, including SAP and multiple operational tools, to plan maintenance work, manage materials and ensure equipment safety. Before Databricks AI/BI Genie, accessing this information required deep system knowledge, manual coordination across teams, long request queues and weeks of engineering effort to produce custom reports. With Genie, BP introduced a simple, natural language interface to its maintenance data, giving a large number of business users an intuitive way to access insights without bottlenecking on a small number of colleagues with deep technical expertise.

speakers.name: Julie Nguyen
speakers.bio:
- Finalist for Data Leader of the year 2021, Women in IT Award
-Working at bp for 21 years and have spent most of her career in Trading and Shipping. Started in Digital before working in risk management for bp Trading and then moving back to Digital! During these 21 years, the one discipline that has remained at the heart of her work is data
- Oversee a team of more than 200 data engineers and over 100 projects across the organization.

sessions.title: BP Cut Cloud Spend by 43% and Speed Critical Jobs From Days to ~8 Hours With Databricks SQL
sessions.body: BP is a 117-year-old global energy company spanning upstream exploration and production, refining, trading, retail, and growing low-carbon businesses. Its data estate evolved across classic enterprise warehouse patterns and cloud stacks split by business unit—upstream on Azure and retail on AWS. Hadoop-era systems became too slow at scale, and Redshift-based serving was costly and hard to right-size. BP standardized on Databricks SQL as its warehouse and BI serving layer across clouds, using Unity Catalog and Delta Sharing to reuse governed data without copying it. The team reduced cloud cost 43% and accelerated key processing from days to ~8 hours, while powering Power BI and other tools through Databricks SQL Serverless warehouses.

speakers.name: Julie Nguyen
speakers.bio:
- Finalist for Data Leader of the year 2021, Women in IT Award
-Working at bp for 21 years and have spent most of her career in Trading and Shipping. Started in Digital before working in risk management for bp Trading and then moving back to Digital! During these 21 years, the one discipline that has remained at the heart of her work is data
- Oversee a team of more than 200 data engineers and over 100 projects across the organization.

sessions.title: Branching the Database: What Engineering Teams Can Finally Do When the Database Forks in One Second
sessions.body: AI is moving from models to autonomous agents and governance must evolve with it. Traditional approaches break down when agents dynamically access data, tools, and APIs across systems.In this session, Databricks and Thoughtworks introduce a new approach to AI governance built on a single, data-centric foundation. Learn how to extend governance from data to models, agents and tools using Unity Catalog, consistent permissions and end-to-end observability.We’ll double click on the Databricks AI Governance roadmap, covering identity-aware access, open and interoperable controls across frameworks, and intelligent monitoring to detect risk in real time. Thoughtworks will share architectural principles for building governed agentic systems at scale.Walk away with practical guidance to move fast with AI without losing control.

speakers.name: Cameron Casher
speakers.bio: Cam Casher is a Senior Data Engineer at Thoughtworks focused on digital transformation, cloud infrastructure, and modern developer platforms. He specializes in designing robust data architectures and Agentic AI solutions, recently partnering with Databricks to co-author the technical series on automating database branching with Backstage and Lakebase. A passionate advocate for Responsible Tech, Cam combines his data platform expertise with deep experience in open-source sustainability, GreenOps, and FinOps best practices to build cost- and carbon-optimized technical ecosystems.

sessions.title: Breaking Down Data Silos: Mastercard’s Path to Comprehensive, Privacy‑Safe Marketing Intelligence
sessions.body: In today’s rapidly evolving marketing landscape, global and multi market teams in companies like Mastercard face unprecedented complexity - fragmented Martech tools, siloed data, proliferating channels, and stricter privacy regulations. The results are shallow insights, weaker personalization, and difficulty measuring ROI across channels. A unified data platform built on a governed, scalable data lake addresses these challenges by integrating global data into a single source of truth, enabling identity resolution, advanced segmentation, real time activation, and consistent full funnel insights. We will explore how Mastercard is building a CDP in Databricks with marketing data sources powered by Unity Catalog. Using Data Vault modeling within the CDP allows data to be onboarded easily and enables teams to ingest data quickly. Finally, we will cover how Unity Catalog enables governance, ensuring each team has access to only the data they need, while sensitive attributes remain protected.

speakers.name: Aaron Beyer
speakers.bio: Aaron Beyer is a Senior Data Engineer at Rearc with more than eight years of experience designing, building, and optimizing modern data platforms. He specializes in architecting and maintaining scalable data pipelines and services in Databricks, and he holds the Databricks Solution Architect Champion certification.

speakers.name: Aarti Bhasin
speakers.bio:
Aarti Bhasin is Vice President of Software Engineering at Mastercard and a technology leader in Marketing Technology Solutions (MarTS). With 19+ years of experience, she specializes in building cloud‑native platforms and driving large‑scale marketing technology transformations.
At Mastercard, Aarti leads marketing technology platforms including Marketing Data Platform, focused on unifying fragmented data into a scalable, governed foundation for full‑funnel marketing. Her work enables marketers to understand audiences, evaluate campaign effectiveness, and optimize funnel performance.
Prior to Mastercard, she led MarTech transformations at Prudential, delivering omni‑channel, hyper‑personalized solutions to improve engagement and acquisition.

sessions.title: Breaking the Bottleneck: Automating the Journey from Power BI to UC Metrics
sessions.body: As the agent builder Kasal evolves, we are transitioning MetricsJet/Converter from an award-winning innovation into a first-class backend capability. Originally developed by David Schwarzenbacher and Kyle Hale, MetricsJet solves a critical blocker for Unity Catalog (UC) adoption: the automated translation of complex reporting logic (e.g., Power BI measures) into governed, reusable UC Metrics. By embedding this capability directly into Kasal, we eliminate fragmentation and provide a seamless migration path for downstream analytics. This strategic alignment follows a milestone-heavy quarter, including winning the FE Product Innovation Award and receiving strong validation from the UC Metrics Product team. With proven demand from global enterprises like Coca-Cola HBC, we are now finalizing the code integration to combine MetricsJet with Kasal's core architecture. This session explores how this unified approach accelerates governance and simplifies the Lakehouse journey.

speakers.name: David Schwarzenbacher
speakers.bio:
David Schwarzenbacher is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks in Zurich, where he architects data and AI platforms for Fortune 500 enterprises. He is the co-creator of Kasal, an agentic AI platform on the Databricks Marketplace, and MetricsJet, an award-winning BI semantic layer translator - winner of the FE Product Innovation Award.
Prior to Databricks, David led an 8-person engineering team at Coca-Cola HBC managing a 450TB data platform, and conducted neural network research at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and Disney Research Zurich. He holds a BSc & MSc in Health Data Science from Heidelberg University (A+), an engineering degree in environmental technology and an MBA in Business Management.

speakers.name: Maximilian Kohnen
speakers.bio: Maximilian is a Senior Data Quality Scientist at Coca-Cola HBC in Zurich, where he works within the Data Insights & AI team of Coca-Cola HBC. He drives the development of agentic AI solutions using Databricks technology like Kasal with Databricks Apps. His work on LLM-powered data enrichment using Perplexity, Gemini, and OpenAI has cut manual labor by over 50% and enabled new business cases across multiple domains. Previously, Max developed a conditional latent diffusion model for medical CT synthesis and conducted computer vision research at EPFL in Lausanne (Switzerland) and bioinformatics research at NUS Singapore. He holds an MSc in Bioinformatics from Heidelberg University and co-authored various papers.

sessions.title: Bridging Transactional Speed and Analytical Depth with AI/BI, Genies Lakebase & Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
Discover how Databricks transformed a basic Gradio app into GTM Hub 2.0, an enterprise-grade platform serving 10,000+ global users (Sales, Marketing, XDR) with personalized insights.

 

Core Architecture & Achievements:

  • Databricks Apps (Enterprise Scale): Built a React/FastAPI application serving 10k+ concurrent users with <3s load times. Features include RBAC, multi-persona views, and seamless cross-origin embedding.
  • AI/BI Dashboards: Embedded dynamic dashboards with global filters, bookmarkable states, and usage tracking for optimized analytics.
  • Genie (Conversational AI): Integrated multi-agent support. A supervisor agent (via MLFlow) routes natural language queries across specialized spaces, eliminating the need for SQL.
  • Lakebase (State Management): Leveraged PostgreSQL on Databricks to handle user preferences, session history, and caching for real-time personalization.

 

The Result: A unified, modular analytics experience with robust telemetry and a future-proof architecture.

speakers.name: Abhinav Bhatnagar
speakers.bio: I am a technical leader specializing in building data science and AI capabilities that drive business value. At Databricks, I lead teams to deliver scalable, enterprise-grade Data & AI solutions, fostering innovation, mentorship, and inclusivity.  I excel at aligning technical vision with business goals to deliver impactful results.

speakers.name: Wenwen Xie
speakers.bio:
Wenwen Xie is an experienced Machine Learning and Generative AI Solutions Architect at Databricks, based in Jersey City, New Jersey. At Databricks, Wenwen specializes in the design and deployment of advanced ML systems, focusing heavily on model evaluation and validation frameworks. She is particularly passionate about Evaluation-Driven Development, advocating strongly for integrating robust model evaluation as a foundational practice in ML system design.
Prior to joining Databricks, Wenwen served briefly as a Data Scientist Lead Vice President at J.P. Morgan. Her earlier role as Senior Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer at LexisNexis significantly shaped her expertise in generative AI and natural language processing (NLP).

sessions.title: Bringing Agents to Data: How Workday Architects Governed Agentic AI with Iceberg and Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
Traditional “data-to-compute” models create latency and fragmented governance that hinder Agentic AI. To solve this, Workday and Databricks advocate “bringing agents to data” via the Databricks Lakehouse. By operating on data in situ, autonomous agents maintain real-time consistency without the risks of replication. This architecture enables reliable multi-agent coordination at scale while ensuring unified data integrity and reduced operational costs across the enterprise.

 

The technical core uses Apache Iceberg for ACID transactions and snapshot isolation, providing a stable foundation for agent reasoning. Databricks Unity Catalog adds a unified governance layer, enforcing fine-grained security, lineage, and auditability. This production-grade approach significantly cuts query latency and storage expenses, allowing organizations to scale from single-agent pilots to hundreds of coordinated agents across multiple departments like Customer Experience, RevOps and Analytics.

speakers.name: Jason Reid
speakers.bio: Jason Reid is a Director of Product Management at Databricks and co-founder of Tabular. He's currently working on enhancing data compatibility and interoperability between lakehouse formats.

sessions.title: Build and Deploy Databricks Projects Using Automation Bundles and Agents
sessions.body:
Modern data engineering teams struggle with environment drift, manual deployment errors, and fragmented assets that make it difficult to reliably scale, govern, and productionize complex data and ML workflows.

 

With Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs), engineers can easily build, deploy, and operate data and AI projects on Databricks. By defining your entire project as a declarative bundle of assets, DABs help you apply proven software engineering practices like source control, testing, and CI/CD consistently and at scale.

 

In this session, you’ll walk through structuring real DABs projects, handling dev vs. prod differences, integrating with GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps, and using new workspace authoring and debugging capabilities to keep deployments safe and repeatable.

 

We’ll close with a first look at BrickOps, Databricks’ new operating model for data engineering in the age of AI, showing how DABs‑powered blueprints, governed deployments, monitoring, and agents work together to reduce toil, detect and troubleshoot pipeline and job issues, and give teams an auditable, AI‑ready foundation for production data products.

speakers.name: Kristóf Molnár
speakers.bio: Kristof leads Databricks's Developer Ecosystem PM team, including Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs). An expert in AI-driven engineering productivity, he previously served as a Group PM at Google, where he spearheaded the AI transformation of internal developer tools, resulting in over 50% of new code being AI-written as of late 2025.

speakers.name: Lennart Kats
speakers.bio: Lennart Kats is a Principal Engineer at Databricks, responsible for the development experience of Lakeflow. Lennart and team created Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs), the Lakeflow IDE, and Genie Code For Data Engineers. Lennart holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science.

sessions.title: Build Better & Faster on Databricks with the AI Dev Kit
sessions.body: AI-assisted development tools have transformed how software is built, yet lack native integration with enterprise data platforms. The AI Dev Kit is an open-source framework enabling AI code-generation services—Claude, Cursor, Gemini, and others—to build and deploy production workloads directly on Databricks. It provides platform-aware tooling allowing AI assistants to generate Databricks-native code adhering to best practices across pipelines, jobs, and Unity Catalog. Critically, it enables non-technical analysts to build robust Databricks workflows through natural language, dramatically lowering the barrier to entry. Since launch in January 2025, the project surpassed 100 GitHub stars in one week with accelerating organic adoption. This session covers architecture, real-world use cases, and implications of AI-assisted development for the Databricks ecosystem.

sessions.title: Building “Vehicle 360” at Daimler Truck & Bus — How We Find Needles in a 30,000 Parameter Haystack
sessions.body:
Daimler Truck & Bus built “Vehicle 360” to break down organizational silos on a global scale and create one trusted, up‑to‑date view of each vehicle. We combine configuration and production records, sales and aftersales processes, over‑the‑air updates and more than 300 GB of daily vehicle log files to maintain this view across more than 1,000,000 vehicles — each with 30,000+ parameters. On an open lakehouse architecture, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines keep data fresh and organized, while Unity Catalog provides unified governance and easy sharing.

 

It gives teams one place to see a vehicle’s current state, drill into recent parameter changes, find vehicles with specific characteristics, orchestrate dynamic over‑the‑air updates, and diagnose issues faster. Beyond day‑one wins, this foundation also enables proactive anomaly detection, AI‑driven support and our journey to a software‑defined vehicle.

speakers.name: Marco Sturm
speakers.bio: Marco Sturm has spent the last 7.5 years at Daimler Truck and currently works as a Data & AI Consultant. After supporting engineering teams in bringing data to every engineer’s desk, he moved to the Intelligent Vehicle Cloud Platform, where he drives the data and AI strategy. With experience across data science, analytics, and engineering, he focuses on building a reliable data platform and trustworthy data products that enable data-driven decisions—and on using AI to make insights accessible to everyone.

sessions.title: Building a Data Marketplace for Investment Teams Using Agent-powered Conversational Analytics
sessions.body:
Ares set out to modernize how data moves across the firm to a unified, governed data marketplace that could serve investment professionals, operations and finance. We’ll walk through Ares’ journey building a consolidated data delivery platform and how we extended it with a conversational user interface for data discovery and data intelligence.

We’ll cover the architectural choices that enabled our different investment strategies to share common data products without sacrificing autonomy or security. You’ll learn how Ares used Unity Catalog to implement a scalable governance model, by standardizing data ownership, access controls, and lineage.

Finally, we’ll show how we used agents to deliver insight and analytics to end users and highlight best practices that helped the assistant better understand user intent and respond in a way that fits different audiences. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for operationalizing governance, data quality, and AI-assisted self-service.

sessions.title: Building a Data Telescope to Study the Vast Expanse of Social Media
sessions.body:
Researchers studying extremism and misinformation need massive social media datasets but face infrastructure and budget constraints. Traditional solutions offer dashboard access to pre-aggregated data, limiting flexibility. Princeton’s Accelerator gives researchers direct Databricks workspace access with pre-built Typical Activity Datasets, enabling custom queries and analysis. We built a multi-tenant data and AI-powered platform serving R1 institutions.

 

Our medallion architecture ingests data via Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines: Bronze captures raw data, Silver applies filtering/text enrichments, and researchers can query via semantic search powered by MLOps. Leveraging Databricks Asset Bundles, REST APIs, and Unity Catalog, we built solutions for cross-workspace monitoring. Users who spent months building scrapers start work in days, querying 100+ languages and discovering content patterns while learning valuable skills. This talk shares our architecture for democratizing data infrastructure with engineering rigor.

speakers.name: Kai Pak
speakers.bio: Kai Pak is Director of Engineering at the Accelerator, an international research consortium housed at Princeton University's School of Public and International Affairs. The Accelerator builds shared tools to improve the speed and quality of research on the information environment. Kai leads the platform's technical development, spanning data infrastructure, applied ML, and large-scale pipeline engineering. Prior to Princeton, he spent several years at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory working on machine learning and remote sensing applications. He holds master's degrees in Applied Physics from Columbia University and Computer Science from UIUC.

speakers.name: Lilly Amirjavadi
speakers.bio:
Data scientist with a background in computational social science and a focus on applied machine learning, scalable data pipelines, and actionable insights. I design and deploy end-to-end workflows that support everything from exploratory analysis to production-grade modeling, with experience across industries including research, media, and public sector data.

At Princeton’s Research Accelerator, I develop systems that process and analyze large volumes of real-world data, supporting research into digital ecosystems and key performance indicators. My work emphasizes clarity, reproducibility, and measurable impact.

sessions.title: Building a Foundation Model for Energy on Databricks with Applied Computing
sessions.body: Energy is arguably the most critical industry on earth, and yet the complexity of the processes and the implications of getting it wrong have been barriers to AI adoption, until now. This session will give context to the current challenges faced by the energy sector and explain how Orbital, the foundation model for energy developed by Applied Computing, can address those challenges by providing an AI model that is both physics-informed and domain specific. The session will also unpack how Databricks provides the enterprise-ready backbone for Orbital, supporting rapid data ingestion, creation, indexing, model training and more

sessions.title: Building a Lakehouse Data Strategy for Healthcare
sessions.body: Michael Uohara—CDAO at HSS has gone all in with Databricks taking HSS's 30 data sources and ingesting them into Databricks. He and his team are under a 18-month transformation effort to modernize their data architecture, focusing on finance, clinical data, operations and HR while creating a foundation where HSS can start to build applications like patient scheduling, surgical parts inventory and MD360—all built on Databricks. Michael is a previous surgeon and now leading the data strategy for the number one orthopedic hospital in the world. He is a visionary in the space and an incredible leader. Besides being an incredible champion and massive Databricks advocate, he approaches his Databricks implementation with calmness, tactical outcomes and has built an incredible culture at HSS. He will discuss his vision to implement a lakehouse architecture at the Hospital for Special Surgery while building a team and culture that can thrive with Databricks' platform.

sessions.title: Building a Production: Scale Dimensional Data Mart With Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and AUTO CDC
sessions.body:
At 84.51˚, we replaced legacy ETL processing in our retail sales data mart with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines to simplify development while improving reliability at scale. In this session, we’ll walk through how a low-code, declarative approach enables dimensional modeling for both slowly changing dimensions and high-volume fact data.

 

You’ll see how to use AUTO CDC to handle data updates across batch and streaming pipelines, supporting continuously arriving sales transactions alongside rapidly changing product, store and customer attributes. Our ETL crunches approximately 8 million sales transactions and over 80 million purchased items per day in support of our 84.51˚ Stratum platform.

 

Attendees will leave with practical guidance for designing and operating dimensional data marts using Spark Declarative Pipelines, including patterns for CDC, schema evolution, and hybrid batch/streaming workloads that can be applied immediately in production environments.

speakers.name: Scott Gordon
speakers.bio: Scott is a lead data engineer at 84.51˚. He has worked in Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence for several decades. Scott has achieved Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional as well as previous certifications from TDWI, Oracle, Microsoft and IBM.

speakers.name: Shu Li
speakers.bio: Senior Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks

sessions.title: Building a Scalable Customer Data Foundation with Identity Resolution
sessions.body: Identity resolution is foundational to effective customer360, AI, analytics, activation, and measurement. However, frequently shifting privacy requirements and fragmented data make it harder than ever. In this session, learn how organizations are using LiveRamp Embedded Identity within Databricks to resolve and unify customer touchpoints without moving or exposing data. We’ll demonstrate how to extend this solution to enable secure data collaboration, improve match rates across partners and channels, and create a data foundation for AI-powered marketing— grounded in trust. Join us to see how top brands are modernizing their workflows to turn fragmented data into exceptional customer experiences.

sessions.title: Building Agentic Applications on Databricks
sessions.body:
This hands-on course introduces how to build single-agent, multi-agent, and multi-model systems on Agent Bricks, including key components, architectures, and use cases. You'll learn how to create agent tools using Unity Catalog functions to extend agent capabilities. You'll begin by using Genie to build agents that can interact with structured data, before extending these concepts to create a second agent designed for working with unstructured data and external resources. Finally, you'll explore how Agent Bricks provides a declarative approach to building multi-agent applications, offering a streamlined alternative to manual development.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces and notebooks
  • Intermediate Python and SQL proficiency
  • Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including LLMs and prompting strategies
  • Familiarity with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture
  • Familiarity with API usage and function calling for LLM interactions with external tools and services

sessions.title: Building Agentic Apps on the Databricks Platform: Architecture, Considerations, and Key Patterns
sessions.body:
Agentic applications are fundamentally different from traditional software: they don't just retrieve data, they reason over it, take actions, and update state in response to the world around them. That makes the database layer a critical design decision, not an afterthought. When agents need to read fresh operational data, write back results, and coordinate across concurrent tasks, the infrastructure underneath determines what's actually possible.

 

This session covers what makes agentic apps so powerful, what can go wrong without the right foundation, and how the Databricks Platform addresses the core requirements. You'll learn how Lakebase provides the low-latency, transactionally consistent operational store that agents need to act on live data, how Unity Catalog enforces governance across agent actions and the data they touch, and how Databricks Apps simplifies deployment and scaling. We'll also walk through a reference architecture that shows how these pieces fit together, from agent orchestration and tool use to state management, observability, and safe rollback using database branching.

speakers.name: Yassine Essawabi
speakers.bio: Yassine is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he helps customers to be successful in designing, building and deploying their Data and AI use cases in production at scale for on-premise and cloud deployments using different technologies. His engagements with customers covers various domains including Machine learning, Automation, Data engineering and Architecture review. He is a certified Solutions Architect on Azure and AWS.

sessions.title: Building Agentic Business Applications on Databricks with Lakebase, MCP and Marvis AI
sessions.body:
Many organizations use Databricks for analytics and AI, but still build business applications on separate stacks, disconnected from the lakehouse.

 

We share how we use Databricks as a full application platform, combining analytics, operational data and AI into production-grade systems.

 

We will show how we built DNA Port and Marvis AI using Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Lakeflow Sync Tables and MLflow for governed model lifecycle management. We will also demonstrate how MCP securely exposes trusted lakehouse data to AI copilots. Through real-world demos, we show how user actions write to Lakebase, trigger AI workflows and surface insights in real time.

 

Today, this platform supports 200+ vessels and 300+ on-shore employees, reducing manual reporting by 40% and improving application time to market by 50%.

 

Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, governance with Unity Catalog, and lessons learned in building scalable, AI-powered enterprise applications on Databricks.

speakers.name: Simon Fassot
speakers.bio: Leading the Software, Data Analytics and AI team at Hafnia

sessions.title: Building AI That Matters: Powering Global Healthcare at The Virtue Foundation
sessions.body:
Ever wonder how The Virtue Foundation connects medical resources with underserved regions? As the first collaboration under Databricks for Good, the foundation partnered with us to build an AI-powered platform improving medical outcomes across 73 countries. This talk breaks down the production Lakehouse architecture behind the system that continuously curates healthcare data to match volunteers with communities in need.

 

What we’ll cover:

  • LLM extraction at scale: Processing 5M+ web pages with OpenAI models via bespoke multimodal pipelines running natively on Spark, reducing cost while improving precision.
  • Data engineering on Spark: Running skewed, multi-terabyte workloads using Spark for parallelism, Photon for performance at scale, and production-grade orchestration.
  • Making data trustworthy: Unifying millions of healthcare facilities through entity resolution.

 

A candid, systems-level look at what it takes to move LLM-powered data extraction from proof of concept to global impact.

speakers.name: Michael Berk
speakers.bio: Michael Berk has a background in data science with skills of inferential statistics, time series forecasting, and generative AI. Since joining Databricks, he has specialized in the retail vertical, where he has implemented a range of data engineering, platform, and machine learning solutions. Beyond his professional work, Michael is committed to ocean conservation and education activism, serving as a project lead on the Databricks for Good team.

speakers.name: Nicolas Douard
speakers.bio: Nicolas Douard uses AI and geospatial data to solve real-world problems in global health. As Tech Lead at Virtue Foundation, he builds solutions to identify medical deserts and match underserved communities with healthcare resources. He is also a researcher affiliated with the University of Strasbourg, publishing on large-scale NLP and cross-disciplinary innovation linking engineering and biology.

speakers.name: Priyanka Mehta
speakers.bio: Priyanka Mehta is an AI engineer passionate about building intelligent systems that create real-world impact. At Databricks, she works as an AI FDE at the intersection of AI, machine learning, and data engineering, helping organizations deploy scalable, production-ready AI solutions.

sessions.title: Building an AI Database for Agentic GTM Operations
sessions.body:
Rippling leverages Databricks to power agentic GTM operations across RevOps, PLG, marketing, sales and account management. Built on Apache Iceberg™-compatible tables and Lakeflow, we ingest and unify large-scale market intelligence data, perform ML-based entity resolution across heterogeneous sources, and apply LLM-driven summarization and classification to generate structured outputs.

 

These enriched profiles power a 360° GTM portal that enables personalized outreach and engagement at scale. Using Databricks AI/BI, we conduct deep performance analysis across campaigns, segments, messaging, and personalization dimensions—closing the loop between intelligence generation and revenue outcomes.

 

We'll dive deep into how Rippling combines scalable data pipelines, interoperable Iceberg storage, AI/BI analytics, evaluation frameworks and generative AI on Databricks to move from fragmented GTM workflows to measurable, agentic operations that drive revenue impact.

sessions.title: Building an AI-ready Customer 360 on Databricks
sessions.body: Learn how data and business teams can turn raw customer data into trusted, business-ready Customer 360 profiles on Databricks. This session will explore best practices for building golden customer records, resolving customer identities, enriching profiles with third-party data, and continuously improving data quality, all while maintaining the security and governance your enterprise depends on with Unity Catalog.In this session, you’ll learn:- How to transform raw data into golden Customer 360 records ready for business and marketing use- How to resolve customer identities and enrich customer profiles with third-party data- How to use marketplace data to improve activation-ready intelligence

speakers.name: Patrick Yang
speakers.bio: Computer Whisperer at Databricks

sessions.title: Building an Explainable AI Research Agent With Databricks Genie
sessions.body: Forecasting sales at more than 7,000 retail stores generates frequent inquiries into forecast drivers, and traditional methods like driver dashboards or SHAP fail to give field leaders clear narratives. Data scientists were spending days writing ad‑hoc SQL to answer basic “why” questions. In partnership with Databricks, we built an AI/BI Genie-powered Research Agent that delivers fast, plain‑language forecast explanations using governed data. The agent joins core datasets, computes variances and accuracy metrics, correlates key drivers and links every answer to underlying SQL, cutting analysis time from days to minutes and revealing model biases. This session covers how we used Unity Catalog as the semantic backbone and encoded business rules in the Genie Knowledge Store so the agent reasons like a retail analyst. We’ll demo the agent with Deep Research and share key lessons and a repeatable blueprint for operationalizing Genie.

speakers.name: ChaD Novek
speakers.bio: Chad Novek is a Director of Data Science at CVS Health, leading labor forecasting and staffing analytics for retail and pharmacy operations. He oversees the development and monitoring of large‑scale demand models for store labor drivers and owns multiple decision support and optimization products, including a composite staffing risk metric and a requisition optimization engine for pharmacists and technicians. His teams focus on bringing forecasting, optimization, and applied ML into production to power workforce decisions.

speakers.name: Rohan Parikh
speakers.bio: Rohan Parikh is a Solutions Architect at Databricks specializing in Data & AI for healthcare and life sciences (HLS). With 10+ years of experience, he helps HLS organizations harness data & AI to improve patient outcomes, drive interoperability, support value-based care, and more.

speakers.name: Ruo-Ting Sun
speakers.bio: Ruo‑Ting (Adrienne) Sun, PhD is a Senior Data Scientist at CVS Health, where Adrienne builds large‑scale forecasting and decision systems on distributed data platforms and develops GenAI solutions, including Genie, to enable faster insights generation. Adrienne’s work has driven over $35M in cost savings through PySpark‑based automation of planning and scheduling. Previously, Adrienne was an Applied Machine Learning Scientist at Teladoc Health, developing ML‑driven risk stratification and intervention policies that improved diabetes outcomes. Adrienne holds a PhD from the University of Illinois at Urbana‑Champaign and is based in Chicago.

sessions.title: Building Autonomous, Always-On Agentic Systems on Databricks
sessions.body: Agentic commerce could drive up to $1T in retail revenue by 2030, but the real opportunity spans every industry. Most agentic systems today are still reactive, relying on chat prompts. True transformation requires always-on, long-running agents that monitor data, reason through exceptions, and act autonomously.In this session, we’ll walk through how to build asynchronous, event-driven agentic systems on Databricks using a supply chain example. Learn how to move beyond chatbots to resilient, system-to-system workflows by orchestrating Structured Streaming, Model Serving, Lakebase, and Agent Bricks.Key takeaways:• A scalable design pattern for long-running, event-driven agents• Always-on anomaly detection with streaming + ML• Stateful task queuing and high-concurrency routing with Lakebase• Multi-step agent reasoning with tools and safe execution• Evaluation and human-in-the-loop escalation for edge cases

speakers.name: Sathish Gangichetty
speakers.bio: Sathish Gangichetty, a Lead Solutions Architect at Databricks, is a distinguished expert in artificial intelligence and machine learning with over 15 years of industry experience. Prior to his time at Databricks, he worked in the AI/ML practice at various companies like Snowflake, SAS, Activision and Zappos where he honed his skills in leveraging cutting-edge data platforms building and architecting for AI and ML applications. Sathish's expertise is backed by numerous certifications from industry leaders such as Microsoft, Google, AWS, and Databricks. As a thought leader in the field, he regularly shares his knowledge through his blog on Medium, where he explores advanced topics in ML and AI.

sessions.title: Building Better Apps: Architecture Best Practices and Common Patterns on Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
Building a data-driven application is easy; building one that is secure, performant, and scalable is where most teams struggle. This session provides a definitive field guide to the architectural patterns used by the most successful builders on the Databricks App platform. We will break down the ""how-to"" for the most in-demand app categories: Internal Tools, AI Copilots, Agentic Workflows, and Customer-Facing Products.

 

For each pattern, we will dive into the technical specifics that matter most:

  • Connectivity & State: Best practices for integrating with Databricks SQL and Lakebase.
  • Identity & Auth: Implementing On-Behalf-Of (OBO) tokens and service principal delegation to ensure data privacy.
  • Agentic Design: Orchestrating LLMs and tool-calling within a full-stack environment.
  • Performance: Strategies for caching and low-latency UI responses.

 

Join us to learn how to avoid common pitfalls and leverage standardized blueprints to ship better apps.

speakers.name: Anant Pingle
speakers.bio: Anant is a Sr. Specialist Solutions Engineer at Databricks, where he focuses on data engineering and warehousing. With a passion for streaming data, he helps organizations build robust, real-time data architectures. Before joining Databricks, he worked as a data engineer in the retail and insurance industries.

sessions.title: Building Custom Models That Know Your Enterprise Knowledge with Reinforcement Learning
sessions.body: In this session, we will discuss how Databricks is using reinforcement learning to customize open source models to power our internal agents at a fraction of the cost and much higher speed. We will also discuss how our customers are using the same tools on Databricks AI Runtime (AIR) to do the same thing for their enterprise agents. We will go over the ingredients needed to successfully perform custom RL, the process of developing custom models using RL, and the novel tools and RL methods we have developed at Databricks to make this powerful technology available for enterprises.

speakers.name: Jonathan Frankle
speakers.bio: Jonathan Frankle is Chief Scientist (Neural Networks) at Databricks, where he leads the research team to efficiently train neural networks. He arrived via Databricks’ $1.3B acquisition of MosaicML, where he was on the founding team. He completed his PhD at MIT, where he empirically studied how neural networks learn (his "Lottery Ticket Hypothesis" - ICLR Best Paper).

sessions.title: Building Data Pipelines with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
This hands-on course introduces users to the essential concepts and skills needed to build data pipelines using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) in Databricks for incremental batch or streaming ingestion and processing through multiple streaming tables and materialized views. Designed for data engineers new to Spark Declarative Pipelines, the course provides a comprehensive overview of core components such as incremental data processing, streaming tables, materialized views, and temporary views, highlighting their specific purposes and differences.

 

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Medallion Architecture, Lakeflow Jobs, and Unity Catalog
  • Experience ingesting raw data into Delta tables using the read_files SQL function (CSV, JSON, TXT, Parquet)
  • Intermediate SQL proficiency, including intermediate-level queries and joins
  • Understanding of ETL concepts and batch/streaming workflows

sessions.title: Building Enterprise Applications with Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
This hands-on course introduces Databricks Apps, a new feature that empowers developers to build and deploy secure data and AI applications directly on the Databricks platform. It is primarily designed for data scientists, data engineers, and developers who need to create custom applications that make data insights accessible to non-technical users within their organizations.

 

The course begins with an overview of the main components of Databricks Apps, followed by the deployment of a simple app using available templates. Next, you will learn how to build and deploy a data-driven application that integrates with other platform features. The course then covers how to set up an IDE for Databricks Apps, and how to edit and deploy an app using an IDE. It concludes with how to implement security and best practices for an enterprise app.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with core Databricks components, including workspaces, clusters, SQL warehouses, Unity Catalog, Jobs, and Model Serving

sessions.title: Building Enterprise-Scale Agentic Claims Automation and AI Observability With Databricks
sessions.body:
As enterprises move from GenAI experimentation to production, the hardest problems are no longer models or agent frameworks—they are enterprise‑scale orchestration and observability.

 

At Suncorp, we have deployed 16 production‑grade agentic AI solutions that are now converging into an enterprise claims automation capability. This session shares the reference architectures and engineering patterns behind this journey, focusing on two pillars: agentic orchestration, where Databricks supports low‑latency, governed workflows and shared agent memory using Delta Lake, Vector Search, Agent Bricks, and Lakebase, and AI observability at scale, where we use MLflow evaluation, OpenTelemetry, Databricks Apps, and AI/BI Dashboards to trace agent behaviour, decisions, quality and risk.

 

Attendees will leave with practical patterns for building orchestrated, observable agentic AI in a regulated enterprise.

speakers.name: Kranthi Nekkalapu
speakers.bio: As an AI practice executive and GenAI subject matter expert, Kranthi brings deep experience in the global financial services and insurance sectors. His background includes leading Suncorp's ML Engineering and research unit within the COE, where he established a strong record of successfully deploying large-scale AI solutions into production. Kranthi is passionate about bridging the gap between innovative AI capabilities and tangible business outcomes, consistently driving data-driven strategies that deliver measurable results.

speakers.name: Shivam Panicker
speakers.bio:
Shivam Panicker is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, specializing in designing and delivering data and AI-driven solutions for enterprise customers, particularly within the financial services sector. With deep expertise in modern data platforms, Shivam works closely with organizations to unlock value from data through advanced analytics, machine learning, and real-time decisioning systems.

With a strong focus on emerging AI capabilities, including agent-based systems, Shivam is passionate about how enterprises can operationalise AI at scale to drive efficiency, customer experience, and innovation.

sessions.title: Building higher quality Genie Spaces: How to ensure accuracy and trust
sessions.body: High-quality Genie spaces are built on a foundation of clear metadata, curated semantics, and continuous iteration. New capabilities make it faster than ever to bootstrap and develop Genie spaces.In this session, we'll show how to design, refine, and scale Genie spaces that consistently deliver accurate, trusted results. Topics include:- Using Unity Catalog Business Semantics (Metric Views) improve accuracy and consistency from the start- Leveraging Genie Code and knowledge mining to automate space setup- How to define metadata and context in the Genie knowledge store- How to use evaluation and Benchmarks to measure accuracy and guide improvements- Best practices for monitoring and optimizing Genie spaces at scale

speakers.name: Shah Amini
speakers.bio:
As an Engineering Leader at Databricks since 2021, Shah has driven innovation across some of the company’s most strategic product areas. Currently leading engineering for Genie Spaces, a flagship AI-powered product that enables users to "talk to their data," Shah is at the forefront of integrating LLMs into enterprise workflows to unlock intuitive and powerful analytics experiences.

Before Databricks, Shah held impactful engineering roles at Meta and Google, contributing to massive-scale consumer products and platform security. His work has consistently blended user experience, system reliability, and strategic foresight to drive customer and business value.

sessions.title: Building Intelligent Data Discovery with Unity Catalog: Domains and Discover
sessions.body: As data estates scale across teams and workspaces, governance and discovery must operate at the account level, not just within individual projects. In this session, we’ll explore how Discover Page, Domains, and recommendations in Unity Catalog work together to scale data governance and discovery across the enterprise. You’ll learn how Domains provide a business-aligned governance layer, how Discover Page curates trusted data and insights across the account, and how recommendations leverage metadata, lineage, and usage signals to surface the right data at the right time. We’ll share real customer patterns and practical guidance for building a governed, intelligent discovery experience that grows with your organization.

sessions.title: Building Permission-Aware AI for Enterprise Content with LakeFlow Connect
sessions.body:
In this session, we’ll explore how to build scalable, permission-aware AI applications by ingesting files and metadata from Google Drive and SharePoint into Databricks.We’ll examine how LakeFlow Connect ingests structured files (Excel, JSON), semi-structured data, and unstructured documents (PDF, DOCX, and more) from enterprise content systems, while capturing rich metadata and preserving file-level permissions for secure downstream use. You’ll learn how to process change feeds, handle deletes, manage schema evolution, and synchronize access controls, ensuring that AI systems respect enterprise security boundaries without sacrificing performance or scalability.

 

We’ll then showcase how this ingestion foundation powers high-impact GenAI applications, including knowledge assistants and enterprise search with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), transforming distributed enterprise content into governed, AI-ready intelligence that delivers trusted answers and actionable insights.

speakers.name: Sandip Agarwala
speakers.bio: Sandip is a Staff Software Engineer at Databricks, where he specializes in designing and building scalable, efficient data ingestion technologies. Prior to joining Databricks, he was the founding engineer and technical lead at Springpath—a scale-out storage startup acquired by Cisco—where he architected and developed a petabyte-scale distributed file system from the ground up for private cloud environments.

sessions.title: Building Production Data Products: HDC Journey from Asset Bundle Automation to Genie Orchestration
sessions.body: Programmatic advertising teams drown in data signals yet struggle to synthesize coherent media strategies. This session reveals how MiQ engineered a production-grade AI agent using Databricks Unity Catalog, Genie workspaces, and MCP integration to transform fragmented intelligence into prescriptive media plans. We'll demonstrate our ReAct-pattern agent that autonomously orchestrates queries solving the "Inference Gap" between data retrieval and strategic action. Key technical deep-dives include: (1) Building reproducible yet adaptive LLM workflows in LangGraph with Databricks SDK,  (2) Context persistence optimization  (3) Multi-layered evaluationAttendees will learn battle-tested patterns for orchestrating Databricks workspaces as agent tools and reasoning engine, achieving enterprise-grade reliability from non-deterministic LLMs, and reducing media planning cycles from days to minutes while standardizing expertise across teams.

speakers.name: Abhishek Pandey
speakers.bio:
With a decade of experience at the intersection of marketing technology and machine learning, Abhishek Pandey serves as the Global Product Lead for Intelligence at MiQ, specializing in architecting enterprise-grade adtech data products and pioneering agentic solutions that redefine how brands navigate the digital landscape.

Armed with a Masters in Data Science, Abhishek has a proven track record of translating complex technical frameworks into high-impact business tools. Their work has resulted in award-winning, industry-leading global planning capabilities that empower major brands and agencies to achieve precision at scale. A dedicated innovator, they are focused on the next frontier of autonomous AI in advertising.

sessions.title: Building Production-Grade SQL ETL on the Lakehouse
sessions.body: ETL pipelines are often the most brittle part of the analytics stack — spread across tools, written in multiple languages, and hard to operate at scale.
