This session shows how teams build production-grade SQL ETL on Databricks Lakehouse using a unified, SQL-first approach. We’ll cover how to ingest, transform, and manage data using declarative pipelines, apply governance and quality controls consistently, author and optimize with AI, and deliver reliable datasets directly to analytics and downstream workloads. The focus is on simplifying architecture, reducing operational overhead, and enabling faster iteration without sacrificing correctness or scale.

sessions.title: Building Query Expert MCP: Using RAG to Build an Analytics Agent That Goes Beyond Text-to-SQL
sessions.body:
LLMs are fast and confident SQL writers that can unlock self-serve analytics across your business. But actionable insights require more than SQL syntax—they demand business context, domain expertise and nuances that live outside your schema docs.

 

In this talk, we'll deep-dive into how Block built Query Expert MCP, a scalable AI agent that captures and distributes institutional data knowledge using Databricks. You'll learn how we:

  • Automated documentation at scale—using query_ai sub-agents to generate standardized table documentation across 11,000+ tables
  • Captured SQL nuances—Databricks sub-agents categorize and label domain-specific query patterns across 1M sample queries
  • Human in the loop—Databricks Apps allow users to directly edit, remove or upload context to the agent’s memory
  • Enabled intelligent retrieval—Databricks Vector Search indexes for RAG-powered query generation that scales to a 12,000 person org, while supporting domain-specific scoping for teams' use cases

speakers.name: Alyssa Ransbury
speakers.bio: Alyssa is a tech lead at Block

speakers.name: Philip Azar
speakers.bio: Phil is a data scientist and machine learning engineer on the Applied AI team at Block.

sessions.title: Building RAG Agents with Agent Bricks
sessions.body:
This hands-on course teaches you how to build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agents on Databricks using Agent Bricks’ tooling—including Vector Search, AI Playground, and the Foundation Model APIs. First, you'll begin with prompt engineering and the fundamentals of retrieval and augmented generation. Next, you'll learn how to ingest, process, and prepare documents for use in a retrieval pipeline. Then you'll explore embedding vectors, vector database design, and how to use Vector Search in a Databricks environment. Finally, you will build a retrieval agent end-to-end and trace its behavior using MLflow Tracing for observability and debugging.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog
  • Intermediate Python programming experience
  • Basic SQL proficiency for querying and creating functions
  • Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including large language models (LLMs) and prompt engineering
  • Basic knowledge of MLflow

sessions.title: Building Reliable Conversational Agents with Genie
sessions.body:
This course teaches you how to design, build, and maintain a Databricks Genie Space, a natural language interface that enables business users to ask questions about governed data and receive SQL-backed answers without writing code.

You will learn how Genie fits into the Databricks AI/BI product family and how it translates natural language into reliable SQL queries. The course focuses on what it takes to create a Genie Space that delivers accurate, consistent, and trustworthy results.

You will follow a complete end-to-end workflow, from understanding source data and defining benchmarks to configuring and refining a Genie Space using the full set of Knowledge Store curation tools. These include metadata, synonyms, prompt matching, SQL logic, example queries, and text instructions.

You will also learn how to share Genie Spaces through Databricks One, understand how Unity Catalog governance is automatically enforced, and use monitoring and user feedback to continuously improve quality over time.

By the end of the course, you will be able to create and manage a production-ready Genie Space that delivers governed, self-service conversational analytics at scale.

Prerequisites

General familiarity with the Databricks workspace - You can navigate the workspace UI, attach compute resources, and run notebooks.

Familiarity with Unity Catalog concepts - You understand catalogs, schemas, and tables in Unity Catalog. Prior experience with permissions, tags, or column masks is helpful but not required.

Intermediate SQL proficiency - You can read and write SQL queries including SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions.

Access to a Databricks workspace with the Databricks SQL entitlement and CAN USE permission on a serverless SQL warehouse.Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Building Secure AI-Powered Analytics Experiences Across Organizational Boundaries
sessions.body: Data sharing between organizations has come a long way — but the next wave is about much more than moving files or granting table access. It's about delivering rich, intelligent experiences to partners, customers, and collaborators while keeping sensitive information protected on both sides. In this talk, we explore how the collaboration landscape is evolving: smarter defaults, stronger privacy guarantees, and AI-powered capabilities that make shared data more useful without increasing risk. You'll hear about the engineering principles behind building privacy-safe collaboration features at scale — balancing openness with control, and convenience with governance. Whether you work with external partners, internal business units, or cross-industry data networks, this session offers a look at where modern data collaboration is headed. Plus, see an early look at what's coming in a live demonstration.

speakers.name: DJ Sharkey
speakers.bio: I'm the Tech Lead for Databricks Clean Rooms and was previously Head of Engineering for AWS Clean Rooms.

sessions.title: Building Secure Retail Data Sharing at Walmart With Databricks Delta Sharing
sessions.body: Secure retail data sharing is becoming a foundation for collaboration between retailers, brands, and partners. In this session we will present how Databricks Delta Sharing and clean rooms can be used to build governed, privacy-aware data-sharing solutions that unlock transaction, customer, inventory, and performance insights for external stakeholders. Attendees will learn practical implementation patterns, clean room design principles, governance best practices, and strategies for delivering secure data products that are accessible to technical and non-technical business users. We’ll also present a Walmart Scintilla Cloud Feeds use case built on Delta Sharing, demonstrating how Walmart built their direct cloud-to-cloud sharing can simplify partner access to first-party retail data, reduce operational complexity, and support faster access to insights.

speakers.name: Harish Rajagopalan
speakers.bio: Harish Rajagopalan is an accomplished Solutions Architect with over 17 years of experience in cloud computing, analytics, and AI/ML. Currently at Databricks, he specializes in designing transformative solutions for retail strategic accounts, leveraging the Lakehouse architecture to unify data engineering, machine learning, and analytics workflows. Previously, Harish played a pivotal role at AWS in guiding enterprises through large-scale cloud migrations and architecting resilient solutions.

speakers.name: Karan Sinha
speakers.bio: Karan is a seasoned product leader with stints at Walmart and Sabre

sessions.title: Building Semantic Models with UC Metric views
sessions.body:
In this hands-on course, you’ll learn how to empower your data consumers to get validated business insights with less burden on you and the rest of your enterprise's data and AI team. Through building a semantic layer on top of your gold layer, you'll offer decision makers and business analysts the opportunity to explore key business performance indicators in novel ways, while still maintaining efficient data operations and enterprise-vetted metrics. 

Prerequisites

  • Proficiency in Databricks SQL
  • Understanding of Databricks data modeling concepts 

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Building the Commercial Lakehouse: AI-Driven, Open and Interoperable
sessions.body:
AstraZeneca modernized its Commercial data estate, transitioning from legacy EMR to a high-performance global commercial lakehouse. At the core lies Unity Catalog (UC), established as the unified governance layer. We demonstrate how UC enables a true open architecture, orchestrating seamless federation for legacy Glue workloads and utilizing Iceberg REST integration to provide zero-copy access for iceberg clients e.g., Snowflake.

 

The transformation was powered by a multi-agent AI migration system, utilizing LLMs and testing agents to automate the conversion of 250+ pipelines into a rigorous Medallion architecture. Key components include Databricks Asset Bundles for versioned CI/CD, Liquid Clustering for storage optimization.

 

Processing complex external data sources (Claims, CRM, Digital), this platform delivered 50% cost savings. This session covers the multi-agent migration architecture, UC-centric interoperability design patterns and lessons from modernizing commercial data at scale.

speakers.name: Alessandro Moro
speakers.bio: Alessandro Moro is a Delivery Solutions Architect at Databricks with nearly a decade of experience in Data and AI across highly regulated industries, including Banking and Pharma. Since joining Databricks in 2022, he has helped several enterprises deliver strategic AI use cases and deploy open, interoperable Lakehouse architectures at scale.

speakers.name: Paul Kuntz
speakers.bio:
I am a Capability Lead, with 12+ years in banking and 14+ years in the Pharmaceuticals Industry. Currently, I am the Capability Lead for the Commercial Data Lake at AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals. I have worked in a broad range of IT capacities, from business analyst, database developer, to data warehouse design and information architect, providing a wide range of technical skills: from cloud services, to database platforms, to modern technology like Databricks.
During my time at AstraZeneca, I was instrumental in the implementation of our data lake capabilities. Recently I spear-headed the journey to migrate to Databricks Lakehouse capabilities, leveraging the full compliment of Databricks technologies to evolve our Commercial capabilities.

sessions.title: Building the Foundation for AI: McKinsey’s Transformation from Legacy to Lakehouse
sessions.body: As enterprises race to operationalize AI at scale, legacy data warehouses have become a critical bottleneck. In this session, Databricks and McKinsey share proven, real-world best practices for modernizing data platforms to unlock analytics, GenAI and agentic workloads with speed, governance and cost efficiency. Drawing from large scale transformations including McKinsey’s Nebula platform, we outline a pragmatic modernization blueprint that balances risk, payback period and business impact. Attendees will learn how to migrate from brittle legacy architectures to an open lakehouse and federated data mesh, reduce total cost of ownership by up to 40%, accelerate time to insight and enable secure self-service analytics and AI across the enterprise. This talk delivers concrete lessons for executives and practitioners navigating modernization in the AI era.

sessions.title: Building With Community Connectors: Custom Data Sources, Managed Reliability
sessions.body:
Are you tired of building fragile, costly API scripts for niche data sources that lack enterprise-grade features like lineage, retries and unified governance?

 

Community Connectors are built on the foundational power of Lakeflow Connect and bridge the gap between "DIY" and “fully managed." These new AI-powered, open-source templates help you build, manage and host your own ingestion paths while inheriting many of the robust, built-in features of the Databricks Platform.

 

In this lightning talk, we’ll explore:

  • Built-in tooling: Use out-of-the-box observability, SCD Type 2 handling, automatic retries and more
  • Flexible customization: Use open-source templates to meet requirements that go beyond standard managed connectors
  • Unified governance: Centrally manage credentials, pipelines, data and lineage via Unity Catalog

 

Join us to get started and learn how they offer the flexibility of a DIY approach with the scale and reliability of a managed Databricks service.

speakers.name: Peter Pogorski
speakers.bio: Peter is a Staff Product Manager, focused on data ingestion.

sessions.title: Building Workforce Intelligence With Unity Catalog and Databricks Genie
sessions.body:
Mars Inc., with more than 140,000 associates across its confectionery, pet care, and food businesses, set out to reimagine how workforce decisions are made. Leaders needed a single, trusted view of the associate journey to move beyond fragmented dashboards and enable faster and fairer decisions.

 

Partnering with Tiger Analytics, Mars established Associate 360, a unified workforce intelligence platform. A common data model brings together hire-to-retire data across segments, standardizes definitions, and ensures trust through Unity Catalog. Natural language querying enabled through Databricks Genie lets business users get insights and visualizations instantly.

 

Impact delivered:

  • One connected view of the end-to-end associate lifecycle
  • Consistent, trusted metrics across businesses
  • Time-based insights for better workforce planning
  • Faster onboarding of acquisitions without compromising data quality
  • A shift from static reports to decision-ready workforce intelligence

speakers.name: Rachel Belino
speakers.bio: Thriving at the intersection of data and technology, Rachel’s current role as HR Data Officer allows her to continue working on Mars’ digital transformation by creating the data foundations needed to enable People and Enterprise Analytics.

speakers.name: Vishal Puri
speakers.bio:
Vishal is an innovator and technology leader with over 20 years of experience and a proven track record helping large enterprises innovate by providing architecture, solution and delivery leadership in transforming to next generation digital architectures. He has been recently involved in creating and leading high performance teams in delivering complex transformations involving big data, advanced analytics, blockchain and IOT using cloud native, microservices, real time and distributed architectures with agile & devops

Vishal is interested in challenging leadership roles where he can bring to bear his deep digital process, technology and architecture expertise, combined with experience leading high performance innovation teams in delivering digital transformations.

sessions.title: Building Your Open Security Lakehouse: Ingest, Normalize, and Model Security Data at Scale
sessions.body: Many organizations are experimenting with “security data lakes,” but struggle to move from DIY projects to an operational architecture the SOC can live in every day. This session walks through Lakewatch’s reference architecture for an open security lakehouse — how to onboard and unify diverse security, IT, and business telemetry on open storage, normalize it to OCSF, and organize it into bronze, silver, and gold tables optimized for SecOps. We’ll cover ingestion patterns for common data sources, Medallion modeling for security analytics, governance with Unity Catalog, index and search strategies, and how to safely bring in multimodal data like emails and documents. You’ll leave with an opinionated architecture to evaluate or design your own security lakehouse, plus guidance on when to augment versus replace existing SIEM tooling.

speakers.name: Kristin Dahl
speakers.bio: Kristin Dahl is a cybersecurity trailblazer with over 15 years of experience in security research and threat intelligence. As a Specialist Architect at Databricks, she empowers organizations to harness the full potential of data and ML in their cybersecurity efforts. Her mission: to revolutionize the field through data-driven insights and foster a safer digital world. With a background spanning air traffic systems, critical infrastructure, and threat analysis, Kristin brings a unique perspective to solving complex challenges. Her expertise in formal methods, threat modeling, and distributed systems allows her to build solutions that push the boundaries of what's possible. A passionate advocate for innovation, Kristin has contributed to cutting-edge research like DARPA's High Assurance Cyber Military Systems. She holds a patent in memory protection that was a recipient of the 2020 Stratus Award for Cloud Computing. She is dedicated to advancing the field through education and outreach.

sessions.title: Built on Databricks: How CMSPI Scaled Payments Routing and Optimization Using Lakebase and DBSQL
sessions.body:
CMSPI built a Databricks-native analytics app that automates payments optimization at enterprise scale — replacing spreadsheets with a governed platform that processes billions of transactions and delivers measurable time and cost savings for global merchants.

 

Lakebase powers real-time scenario configuration, while Delta tables and SQL warehouses enable interactive analytics. Databricks Workflows orchestrate a mathematical solver (PROM) that evaluates billions of routing combinations and returns results in 30–40 minutes — eliminating 30+ hours of manual work per initial analysis and uncovering ~10% incremental savings opportunities.

 

This session shares CMSPI’s path to productization: access control with Entra ID groups, MLOps for approval-rate prediction models and external monetization via Delta Sharing to non-Databricks consumers. The architecture demonstrates the “built on Databricks” pattern for secure, governed apps — with plans to expand collaboration using Databricks Clean Rooms.

speakers.name: Jordan Pierce
speakers.bio:
Jordan Pierce is VP of Data at CMSPI, where he leads the development of the company’s modern data, analytics, and AI platform. His work focuses on using Databricks, Azure, machine learning, and advanced optimization to help global merchants improve payments performance, reduce costs, and make better strategic decisions.

He has led CMSPI’s transition to a scalable lakehouse architecture, supporting growth to billions of transactions processed each week. Today, Jordan leads CMSPI’s use of Databricks across MLOps, AI-powered analytics, and payments routing optimization, while driving the next phase of innovation through natural-language insight generation and emerging agentic workflows.

speakers.name: Sanjay Ashok
speakers.bio: Sanjay Ashok is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, acting as a technical advisor to digital-native and emerging enterprises across EMEA. He assists customers in evaluating, adopting, and scaling the Lakehouse platform for production AI and analytics workloads. With over 10 years’ experience in AI/ML, big data, and cloud architecture, he has worked across the US, India, and the UK, including at AWS, developing cloud-native data and ML solutions. At Databricks, he guides organisations from technical strategy to data-driven business transformation in gaming and fintech. His work covers GenAI applications, ML pipelines, real-time analytics, and self-serve BI dashboards. He holds an MS from the University at Buffalo.

sessions.title: Buliding ETL Pipelines with SQL
sessions.body:
This hands-on course teaches you how to build production-ready ETL pipelines using pure SQL on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You'll learn the declarative building blocks — Streaming Tables, Materialized Views, and AUTO CDC — that replace complex procedural ingestion and transformation logic with concise, incremental, and fully managed pipeline definitions. Following a realistic retail dataset through the medallion architecture, you'll incrementally ingest files with Auto Loader, build pre-computed Silver-to-Gold transformations with incremental refresh, manage SCD Type 1 and Type 2 dimensions with AUTO CDC, and orchestrate the full pipeline using Lakeflow Jobs with SQL File tasks and DAG-based workflows.

Prerequisites

  • Navigating the Databricks workspace — sidebar, Catalog Explorer, and SQL Editor
  • Unity Catalog basics — catalogs, schemas, tables, and volumes
  • Intermediate SQL — SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, CAST, COALESCE, CREATE TABLE, and INSERT
  • Data warehousing concepts — fact tables, dimension tables, star schemas, and the medallion architecture
  • Basic understanding of ETL — Extract, Transform, Load workflows and why incremental processing matters  

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Bulk Metadata Generation To Bring Genie to Life
sessions.body: Genie benefits significantly from the presence of column metadata. In this talk we will describe the various components that feed into a high-quality Genie space and review some code you can use to populate the base Unity Catalog column metadata in bulk. The code makes use of customizable prompts and optional data sampling to produce high-quality metadata across entire schemas or even catalogs.

speakers.name: Scott Eade
speakers.bio: Scott Eade is a Lead Solutions Architect at Databricks, partnering with enterprise customers across Australia (and beyond) to design and deliver data and AI platforms at scale. He works closely with customer data teams and is passionate about helping them generate valuable insights from their data using Genie and the wider Databricks platform.

sessions.title: Cache Smarter, Not Harder: Building a Semantic Cache Gateway with Lakebase and MLflow
sessions.body: As LLM applications move into production, redundant calls quietly drive up latency, cost, and complexity. Traditional caching falls short — exact string matches miss the majority of real-world queries where users ask the same question in different ways.In this session, we introduce semantic caching: a smarter approach that retrieves responses based on intent, not syntax. You'll learn how to build a production-ready semantic cache gateway using Lakebase and MLflow to capture paraphrased and context-aware queries. We'll walk through why exact-match caching breaks down at scale, how to design a low-latency caching layer with a FastAPI gateway on Databricks Apps, and how to incorporate conversational context for multi-turn accuracy — plus the observability and governance patterns that make it production-safe.Walk away with a deployable architecture and proven patterns to cut LLM costs by up to 80% while improving response speed and reliability.

speakers.name: Ananya Roy
speakers.bio: Ananya Roy is a  Specialist Solution Architect focusing in GenAI/Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence. She has extensive experience in helping people on thinking the right way while building enterprise scale AI applications. Before Databricks , she was working as a ML Specialist at AWS where she has worked across globe helping industries implement large scale ML/AI use cases in their organisations.

speakers.name: Brian Law
speakers.bio: Brian Law is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks with a specific focus on Machine Learning and Advanced Analytics. Previously, he was a Solutions Engineer at Cloudera and worked in industry as a Data Scientist on various use cases from Timeseries Forecasting through to NLP and Computer Vision

sessions.title: Cascading Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
sessions.body: Evaluating multi-agent systems requires a fundamental shift in perspective: we are no longer just testing model outputs, but the integrity of the coordination layer. Instead of just getting one bad response, we get a complex palette of hidden—and not-so-hidden—issues like poisoned shared memory, sub-optimal decision patterns, and distributed hallucinations.In this session, we’ll cover how to identify these glitches with MLflow observability, how to move from passive monitoring to active intervention, and which Databricks components can actually prevent the chaos from happening in the first place. The goal of this talk isn't to give you a recipe for every possible disaster, but to broaden your thinking in a world where agents are becoming more autonomous—and significantly more creative with their mistakes.

speakers.name: Oleksandra Bovkun
speakers.bio: Oleksandra is a Developer Advocate at Databricks. She enjoys sharing her knowledge, experience, and insights about AI systems, AI governance, and Databricks. Throughout her career as a Data Engineer, AI Engineer, and Databricks Solutions Architect, she’s experienced firsthand how challenging it can be to embark on a Data and AI journey. Based on her extensive experience with building real-world AI solutions, architecting and implementing data platforms, and running large-scale performance optimization projects with commercial and open source technologies, she is passionate about breaking complex topics and helping the community democratize data and AI for their projects.

sessions.title: Česká Spořitelna: Unifying Oracle, Cloudera and Snowflake Workloads to a Single Platform
sessions.body:
Česká Spořitelna recently selected Databricks as their unified cloud data platform. After long-running PoCs and the evaluation of some of Databricks latest features—SQL functions, multi-statement transactions, exclusive groups, and others—Česká decided to pivot from Snowflake to Databricks, unifying their existing platforms and aligning with the strategy of the Erste Group. This includes the migration of an Oracle DWH, Cloudera and existing Snowflake environments to a unified data platform for all their AI, ML & data science, DWH, and data engineering use cases, cutting massive integration costs necessary to integrate all the legacy platforms.

 

The Ceska’s Head of Data Platforms Engineering, together with the Databricks Lead Specialist Solutions Architect who supported the evaluation, will present the customer journey and why this decision is strategic and aligned with their broader enterprise data strategy.

speakers.name: Diego Fanesi
speakers.bio: After a career as a software developer and in the big data space, Diego has been working with data lakes and data warehouses for more than 10 years, across 2 continents and over 3 countries. Today, Diego is a Lead Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, located in Switzerland and he is a specialist in Data Warehousing, Data Engineering and AWS cloud platform.

speakers.name: Karol Zemko
speakers.bio:
Karol Zemko is the current Head of Data Platforms Engineering in Česká spořitelna responsible for platform design, adoption of new features and roadmap planning for the complete data platform stack (Databricks, Snowflake, Cloudera, Oracle)
His previous experience as Lead Architect in several projects for international clients gave him the opportunity to build specialized scalable platforms but targeted for a specific use-case. Model training & MLOPS, Warehousing/Reporting, building AI systems and so on.
Now he uses this experience to realize Česká spořitelna‘s and by extension, Erste‘s Group vision, of a unified Databricks platform.

sessions.title: Cielo modernized its data platform and migrated 6,000+ pipelines from EMR to Databricks.
sessions.body: Cielo, a leading LATAM payment processor, operated a fragmented analytics landscape across AWS EMR, Oracle Exadata/DW, and decentralized governance. This architecture increased operational overhead, limited lineage and observability, and constrained AI adoption.In this session, we present how Cielo migrated multiple enterprise-grade platforms to a unified Databricks Lakehouse. Over 6,500 pipelines were assessed and over 3,000 legacy jobs eliminated. The migration leveraged Delta Lake, serverless compute, standardized engineering patterns, and Unity Catalog–ready governance.Key takeaways include a ~40% cost reduction in ingestion pipelines, improved reliability and reprocessing, and more than 1,000 users enabled through self-service analytics. We also share practical migration patterns from AWS EMR and Oracle Exadata/DW to Databricks, governance-by-design lessons, and how AI-assisted refactoring accelerated modernization while improving developer productivity.

speakers.name: Gabriel Mochnacs de Arruda
speakers.bio:
Gabriel Mochnacs de Arruda is the Executive Superintendent of Data & AI at Cielo, leading enterprise-scale initiatives in Data, Artificial Intelligence, and Generative AI for one of Latin America’s largest financial technology companies.

Recognized for driving large-scale AI transformation, Gabriel leads the strategy behind intelligent platforms, AI governance, advanced analytics, and agentic AI ecosystems that are reshaping customer experience, operational efficiency, and business growth at scale.

sessions.title: Clean, Correct Change Data Capture with Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
Learn how to construct clean, correct, cost-conscious CDC pipelines that conquer chaotic change, column creep and complicated SCD calculations. Today, implementing CDC typically means writing complex, expensive merge logic. Handling straightforward cases is manageable — but complexity escalates quickly when you introduce out-of-order data, duplicates, schema evolution and slowly changing dimensions. What works in development often breaks under real production conditions.

 

Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) addresses this with Auto CDC, a declarative API that abstracts away merge orchestration and correctness guarantees. Instead of implementing imperative patterns, you declare intent — such as applying SCD Type 2 — and SDP executes it with built-in consistency, incremental processing and resilience.

 

In this session, we’ll walk through the Auto CDC API, examine how it automates complex merge operations and show how declarative CDC improves reliability across batch and streaming workloads.

speakers.name: Andreas Neumann
speakers.bio: With a career defined by "massive scale," Andreas Neumann currently serves as the Technical Lead for Declarative Pipelines at Databricks. From his early work at Yahoo! and IBM to his time at Google and his journey as the founder of Cask Data, Andreas has spent decades solving the data industry's toughest architectural puzzles. Beyond his corporate leadership, he is a dedicated advocate for open-source software, having mentored several Apache projects from incubation to maturity. Andreas holds a PhD in Computer Science for his pioneering research in document querying.

sessions.title: Cleared for Takeoff: Modern Air Operations Intelligence on Databricks
sessions.body:
Amadeus Airline & Airport Operations (AOP) is accelerating its industry-leading platform by migrating from Synapse to Databricks to unlock advanced data, AI and automation capabilities. Serving 135+ airlines and 200+ airports, AOP now gains a unified Delta Lake foundation, shared metadata catalog, secure data sharing and automated workflows. This migration enables faster engineering, real-time analytics, ML-driven disruption management and emerging agentic and MCP-enabled workflows forming the AI backbone for seamless passenger experiences, optimized airport operations and automated decisioning across the global AOP ecosystem.

 

You’ll learn how Amadeus’ aviation expertise and Databricks technology together built the backbone for predictive, real-time aviation operations.

speakers.name: Abhishek Krishna
speakers.job_title: Head of Data, AI & Platform, Product
speakers.bio: Abhishek Krishna heads Amadeus’ AirOps Data, AI, and Platform product team, where he works to modernize how airlines and airports operate. With over a decade in aviation, Abhishek is passionate about using data and AI to make air travel more efficient, resilient, and traveler-focused. He champions better data collaboration and robust data foundations, believing these are key to unlocking the next wave of AI-driven improvements in operational efficiency and traveller experience. Abhishek remains dedicated to upholding data integrity, security, and compliance, ensuring that innovation is pursued with both boldness and responsibility.

speakers.name: Gurpreet Arora
speakers.bio:
As Director of Data & AI for Travel & Hospitality, Gurpreet works with airlines, hotel groups, cruise lines and travel tech companies across pillars like revenue management, loyalty, dynamic pricing, and airline operations translating complex AI capabilities into outcomes that actually move the needle.
With over a decade in the industry and hands-on experience across Fortune 100 travel organizations, he has been part of teams delivering over a billion dollars business impact through modern data platforms, ML ops & agentic AI systems.
A frequent thought leader on AI adoption in travel, Gurpreet brings a practitioner's perspective on what works, what doesn't, and what's worth betting on next

sessions.title: Closing the Feedback Loop: Self-Evolving Agent Test Harness with MLflow
sessions.body: "Most teams iterate on agent quality through vibe-checking: try a question, read the answer, fix what looks wrong, repeat. It works initially, but breaks down as the project grows. Each fix can revive an old bug or introduce a new class of issue. Coding agents add to the strain. They rewrite the agent in seconds while verification still happens by hand.Offline evaluation is one answer, but it is hard. Traditional eval requires setting up golden datasets, metrics, and judges b efore it pays off, and many teams don't get past the setup cost.This session introduces a new approach in MLflow: a self-evolving test harness for agent quality that builds itself from inside the vibe-checking loop. Each piece of feedback on a bad answer becomes an automated test, and every coding-agent fix runs against the accumulated suite.We'll walk through a live demo and share what we've learned."

speakers.name: Yuki Watanabe
speakers.bio: A software engineer at Databricks and a full-time core maintainer of MLflow based in Japan. Leveraging applied machine learning background in several domains to shape tools that makes ML development flow more efficient and reliable.

speakers.name: Adam Gurary
speakers.bio: Adam Gurary is a Product Manager at Databricks working on Vector Search and Document Parsing. Before joining Databricks, Adam was a Product Manager at C3 AI working on inference for LLMs and embedding models.

sessions.title: Closing the Insight-To-Action Gap With Databricks AI/BI Genie, Apps and Databricks One
sessions.body: Finance teams often identify insights but lack streamlined ways to operationalize them. In this demo-driven session, KPMG demonstrates how Engagement Management Coordinators (EMCs) within the Finance organization close the insight-to-action gap using Databricks AI/BI Genie, Databricks Apps and Databricks One. EMCs use conversational analytics to evaluate engagement performance and financial risk across scenarios, while Databricks Apps embed those insights directly into workflows such as forecasting revisions and exception handling. Databricks One provides a consistent business-facing entry point supported by Unity Catalog governance. The session shares adoption strategies, governance considerations, and lessons learned from enabling finance teams to move from analysis to action through guided demonstrations.

speakers.name: Gidget Santos
speakers.bio: Gidget Santos is a Senior Director in KPMG's Finance and Accounting organization, where she is instrumental in driving financial excellence across the firm’s Audit, Tax, and Advisory portfolios. She leads a high-performing global team who is responsible for the comprehensive financial and administrative lifecycle of client engagements.

speakers.name: Mohana Gudepu
speakers.bio:
Mohana Vamshi Gudepu is part of the Data Strategy and Enablement team within the Digital Nexus organization at KPMG, where he focuses on driving data and AI-led innovation. He specializes in designing and delivering modern data platforms on Databricks, enabling governed analytics, AI/BI solutions, and data applications that empower business users.

With experience leading large-scale implementations, he works at the intersection of data, AI, and enterprise decision-making, helping organizations move from insights to action through scalable, user-centric solutions. At Databricks Summit, he shares practical approaches for operationalizing AI/BI and governance to enable real-world decision-making at scale.

sessions.title: Comprehensive Data Warehouse Migrations With Lakebridge
sessions.body:
Lakebridge is Databricks' free, AI-powered solution for migrating legacy data warehouses to the Lakehouse. Migrating from a legacy warehouse means confronting decades-old code, converting proprietary dialects, and reconciling bespoke differences between source and target systems. With Lakebridge, AI agents handle that automatically. We'll show how Lakebridge uses Genie Code to accelerate the migration lifecycle:

  • Assessment: analyze legacy code automatically to surface complexity, dependencies, and risk before work begins
  • Conversion: Use agents to convert proprietary dialects into open ANSI SQL, automatically validating syntax and semantic intent
  • Data Migration: Use LakeFlow Connect to replicate data from a wide range of sources, either as a one-time snapshot or incremental change capture
  • Reconciliation: easily identify discrepancies between source and target systems
  • With Lakebridge, migrations are faster to scope, easier to deliver, and no longer dependent on expensive manual workflows.

speakers.name: Jonathan Brito
speakers.bio: Jonathan Brito is a Staff Product Manager at Databricks, where he currently works on Databricks SQL and Lakebridge. Prior to his current role, he launched Databricks' suite of Apache Iceberg products as part of the Lakehouse Storage team.

sessions.title: Connecting BI and Partner Tools to Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: Did you know you can connect your favorite BI tools directly to Databricks Lakehouse — without spinning up an extra data warehouse? In this session, we’ll explore how Databricks integrates seamlessly with tools like Excel, Google Sheets, Copilot Studio, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and more. You’ll see how these integrations empower your business users to tap into the full power of the Databricks Platform right inside the applications they already use every day.

speakers.name: Matt Holzapfel
speakers.bio: Matt Holzapfel is a Product Adoption leader at Databricks where he helps customers adopt emerging product capabilities. Prior to Databricks, he was the Chief Product Officer at Tamr. Matt earned an MBA from Harvard Business School and a bachelor's degree in engineering from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

speakers.name: Toussaint Webb
speakers.bio: Toussaint Webb is a Product Manager at Databricks, where he leads efforts to improve connectivity and user experience with ISV technology partners. Previously, he was a Product Manager at LinkedIn, where he built advertiser safety tools and content understanding and personalization systems for the LinkedIn Feed. Toussaint holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Princeton University.

sessions.title: Consumer Industries Forum | Sponsored by: Deloitte
sessions.body: Join retail, consumer goods, and travel & hospitality leaders for a deep dive into how Databricks’ open, agnostic platform is powering the next era of intelligent commerce single foundation built on a single intelligent platform with elusive enterprise knowledge. From real-time personalization to collaborative supply chains connecting retailers and suppliers, discover how the industry’s most ambitious companies are bringing together structured and unstructured governed data to deploy AI that actually understands their business. This forum explores the imperatives reshaping the industry: demand intelligence, dynamic pricing, retail media monetization and AI-powered employee productivity. Through candid conversations and real-world results, hear directly from leaders already delivering measurable outcomes and leave with a practical playbook for scaling AI across the organization.

speakers.name: Karthik Iyer
speakers.bio: Karthik Iyer is Group Vice President of Intelligent Merchandising at Albertsons, with 25+ years of experience driving global transformation across retail and banking. He leads enterprise pricing and promotion intelligence, bringing together model-ready data, Explainable AI, statistical machine learning, deep learning, and agentic AI into a unified decisioning system. His work focuses on orchestrating the full AI lifecycle-from data to prediction to reasoning to action-enabling real-time decisions at scale. Previously, he pioneered CNN-based digital onboarding at NAB, widely covered in Australian media. He is pursuing doctoral research in AI focused on world models, latent representation learning, and explainability using JEPA.

speakers.name: Rob Saker
speakers.bio: Rob Saker is the Global Industry Leader for Consumer Industries at Databricks, leveraging extensive experience in data and analytics from roles at MillerCoors, ConAgra, Crossmark, and NCR. He actively contributes to the industry through speaking engagements and advising AI startups, demonstrating a passion for innovation and collaborative culture. In his current position, Rob oversees strategies, partnerships, and solutions, guiding industry executives to harness data and AI for business impact

sessions.title: Consumer Industries: The Last Mile of Intelligence— Building Apps That Actually Reach the Frontline
sessions.body:
Building an app has never been easier. Deploying an enterprise app— governed, scalable, connected to real-time data— has never been harder. Store associates, restaurant managers, and operations teams make thousands of decisions a day— but the apps they rely on are slow to build, disconnected from analytics, and starved of real-time context. The reason? A wall between analytical and operational systems that forces teams to maintain fragile ETL pipelines, over-provision databases, and wait months for production-ready tools.

 

Lakebase tears that wall down. Databricks' serverless Postgres eliminates the infrastructure overhead, the ETL pipelines, and the DBA bottleneck that have kept intelligent apps out of frontline hands. In this session, we'll show what it means to build AI-first applications for consumer industries, walking through the end-to-end process: from use case design to live deployment, including a live app build on stage. Hear from brands already shipping Lakebase-powered apps, and leave with a repeatable framework for turning lakehouse intelligence into the tools your frontline teams actually use.

speakers.name: Rob Saker
speakers.bio: Rob Saker is the Global Industry Leader for Consumer Industries at Databricks, leveraging extensive experience in data and analytics from roles at MillerCoors, ConAgra, Crossmark, and NCR. He actively contributes to the industry through speaking engagements and advising AI startups, demonstrating a passion for innovation and collaborative culture. In his current position, Rob oversees strategies, partnerships, and solutions, guiding industry executives to harness data and AI for business impact

speakers.name: Sathish Gangichetty
speakers.bio: Sathish Gangichetty, a Lead Solutions Architect at Databricks, is a distinguished expert in artificial intelligence and machine learning with over 15 years of industry experience. Prior to his time at Databricks, he worked in the AI/ML practice at various companies like Snowflake, SAS, Activision and Zappos where he honed his skills in leveraging cutting-edge data platforms building and architecting for AI and ML applications. Sathish's expertise is backed by numerous certifications from industry leaders such as Microsoft, Google, AWS, and Databricks. As a thought leader in the field, he regularly shares his knowledge through his blog on Medium, where he explores advanced topics in ML and AI.

sessions.title: Context Is Everything: Lakebase Agent Memory
sessions.body: This hands-on lab covers building and deploying a stateful AI assistant with both short-term and long-term memory using an agent framework, Lakebase, and Databricks Apps. Attendees create Unity Catalog function tools, give the agent the ability to remember conversations and recall user preferences across sessions, and deploy it as a chat application. By the end, attendees will understand how both memory systems work together and have a deployed stateful agent.

sessions.title: Control and Governing Your Coding Agents with LLMOps
sessions.body: Coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI are transforming how software gets built, but without observability they remain a black box. This talk shows how to take control of your coding agents using MLflow. We cover tracing agent sessions to understand token usage and tool calls, evaluating output quality with LLM judges and custom scorers, routing LLM traffic through AI Gateway for cost control, and automating workflows with MCP and skills. Walk away with practical techniques to monitor, measure, and maximize your coding agent investment.

sessions.title: Cost Governance at Scale @ Databricks
sessions.body: “With great compute power comes great financial responsibility.” As the internal Data Platform team, we manage one of the largest Databricks environments in the world, which means we also manage one of the largest cloud bills. This session unveils our internal FinOps practices. We will demonstrate how we use System Tables, budgets and tagging policies to attribute costs to hundreds of internal teams, identify waste and enforce accountability. Learn how to implement the same governance controls that we use to keep our finance team happy while empowering 10,000+ employees to innovate.

speakers.name: Arpan Ghosh
speakers.bio: Arpan leads Data Platform teams at Databricks, which build and scale the data-driven systems behind some of the company’s most critical business solutions. Previously, he led Data & AI initiatives at multiple startups — taking products from the first line of code to real-world impact. He was Databricks’ very first paying customer back in 2015, as a one-man data platform team at a high-growth startup, long before lakehouses were cool.

speakers.name: Bogdan Kyryliuk
speakers.bio: Staff Software Engineer @ Data Platform

sessions.title: Cost Management for Serverless Compute: Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines
sessions.body: Serverless compute removes infrastructure overhead, but platform teams still need to govern who can use it and how much each workload can spend. This session covers the cost-control model now for serverless Notebooks, Jobs, and Lakeflow Pipelines, current features, recent developments, and the roadmap ahead.We walk through the new primitives: entitlements that grant or revoke serverless access per user, group, or service principal, and per-workload rate limits that cap the spend rate of an individual Job or Pipeline. Attendees leave with a concrete migration path from cluster policies to serverless cost controls.

sessions.title: Creating Better Travel Experiences for All — Confronting Airline Pricing Pressures From Legacy Tools
sessions.body: easyJet carried nearly 90 million passengers last year, flying more than 1,200 routes, with a fleet of 300+ planes. Even as one of Europe’s leading low-cost airlines, the company faced mounting pressure to modernize, as traveler expectations necessitate seamless booking, flexible changes and personalized offers. Across Europe, high costs, thin margins and digital-first competitors only raised the stakes for all airlines. With core systems still tied to a decade-old desktop app and one of the region’s largest SQL Server databases, easyJet struggled with frequent engineering bottlenecks, fragmented workflows and more. Moving to the Databricks Platform helped the airline consolidate their commercial tools into a single hub and cut deployment timelines from up to nine months to three — a pace shift that put innovation back on track for easyJet.

sessions.title: Cross-Cloud Delta Sharing: Eliminate Egress cost with Delta Sharing Global Distribution
sessions.body: Cross-cloud and cross-region data sharing introduces egress costs that grow with recipient query volume, creating a scaling challenge for large-scale data providers. This session covers best practices for architecting cost-efficient Delta Sharing deployments across clouds and regions, and introduces a new Databricks capability designed to change how providers manage cross-cloud/region delivery at scale.

sessions.title: Customer Zero: How Retool Scaled 1 Million Databases on Databricks Lakebase
sessions.body:
Learn how Retool, an enterprise AppGen platform for building intelligent applications and agents, became an early adopter of Databricks Lakebase, creating over 1 million serverless Postgres databases to power its operational foundation. We’ll share the architecture, governance, and lessons learned as Retool scaled its own platform to support production-ready apps and agents that turn governed business data into action.

 

You’ll see how Retool’s Lakebase-powered operational layer now gives Databricks customers a proven path to run more workloads and remove data silos, whether they use Retool’s layer or connect directly to their own databases. The session includes a live demo to help you move from prototype to production with unified governance, automation, and lower operating costs through autoscaling.

speakers.name: Abhishek Gupta
speakers.bio: Abhishek Gupta leads Product at Retool, the leading enterprise AppGen platform trusted by over 10,000 companies including Amazon, LVMH, Colgate-Palmolive, and Stripe. He recently spearheaded the launch of the world's first Enterprise AI AppGen platform, enabling anyone to build production-ready internal software using natural language. Prior to Retool, Abhishek served as SVP of Product at Motive, where he led a 70+ person team automating the physical economy for 120,000+ customers, and held product roles at Uber and Box. Abhishek holds a B.A. in Computer Science from the University of California, Berkeley and resides in San Francisco.

sessions.title: Cybersecurity Forum | Sponsored by: Deloitte
sessions.body:
In the AI era, security is fundamentally a data problem. As cyberattacks shift from human-operated to machine-scale autonomous agents, traditional security architectures have hit a breaking point, forced into a "fidelity trade-off" between spiraling costs and dangerous visibility gaps.

 

Join us for the Cybersecurity Industry Forum to discover how Databricks is disrupting the legacy SIEM market with Lakewatch, the industry’s first open, agentic SIEM built on the security lakehouse. This 90-minute session explores how to “fight fire with fire” by deploying swarms of defensive AI agents to meet machine-speed attackers. We will dive into the architectural shift required to unify security, IT, and business data into a single, governed environment, eliminating the “ingestion tax” and enabling petabyte-scale detection and response at a fraction of the cost of legacy providers.

 

Hear from security innovators and Lakewatch design partners who are moving beyond experimental AI to operationalize agentic security at scale. Learn how to leverage open formats (OCSF) and “Detection-as-Code” to build a proactive, high-velocity SOC that identifies threats in minutes, not days.

sessions.title: DABs: Do Like a Pro—All the Best Tips and Tricks
sessions.body: This session is a live, practical deep dive into Databricks Asset Bundles (DABS) — focused on how to use them like a pro in real projects, not just in docs.Instead of theory, I’ll run a live demo showing the most valuable patterns, shortcuts, and real-world tricks that dramatically improve how you build, deploy, and manage Databricks workflows.The session combines: proven techniques from my articles on Databrickster (Medium) battle-tested practices from real projects hidden features and non-obvious behaviors you won’t find in basic tutorials

speakers.name: Hubert Dudek
speakers.bio:
Hubert Dudek is a Databricks MVP and data engineer who enjoys solving messy data problems and making things actually work in production. He builds scalable data platforms using tools like Unity Catalog and Delta Lake.

His biggest passions are FinOps—finding smart ways to save money—and CI/CD, making sure data solutions get to production smoothly and reliably. He’s also active in the community as a blogger, YouTuber, and frequent social media contributor, sharing practical tips and real-world insights.

sessions.title: Data + AI for Good: How Nonprofits Are Transforming Mission Impact with Databricks
sessions.body: Nonprofits are tackling some of society’s most urgent challenges, but many are constrained by limited budgets, fragmented data, and limited technical capacity. In this session, we will share how Databricks for Good helps mission-driven organizations overcome these barriers through nonprofit pricing, technical enablement, and hands-on support from Databricks experts.Attendees will learn how nonprofits can use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to unify data, strengthen analytics foundations, explore responsible AI, and turn information into insights that support better decisions and greater mission impact.The session will feature stories from Crisis Text Line and GO Project, highlighting their missions, data journeys, implementation lessons, and the opportunities they see to use data and AI more effectively. Attendees will leave with a practical playbook for how nonprofits can get started with Databricks and accelerate meaningful, measurable social impact.

speakers.name: Joydeep Kamdar
speakers.bio: oydeep Kamdar is Head of Delivery Solutions Architects for Digital Natives Business at Databricks, where he leads a team helping some of the world’s most innovative companies accelerate their path to production with data and AI. sessions.title: Data Analytics with Multi-Modal Data
sessions.body: AI is becoming a very powerful commodity tool to turn unstructured data into structured data. This has greatly improved the importance of unstructured data and is posing new challenges in the world of data analytics: how to govern the data, how to store the data, how to access the data efficiently, and how to make the data available to ML models. In this talk, we will discuss how we're approaching these problems given the state of the world with open table formats such as Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, as well as new file formats such as LanceDB.

sessions.title: Data Governance at Scale
sessions.body:
This hands-on course equips learners with hands-on expertise to implement robust, enterprise-scale data governance in Databricks using Unity Catalog. Implement access control at scale with ABAC, enable comprehensive observability and auditing, monitor and assure data quality, visualize and manage complete data and model lineage, and effectively track usage, costs, and data quality across your platform.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces, notebooks, and basic cloud concepts
  • Intermediate SQL experience, including creating and managing tables, views, and functions, and granting/revoking privileges
  • Working knowledge of data governance concepts, including access control, security policies, and fine-grained techniques such as row-level filters and column masking
  • Understanding of Unity Catalog's object model (metastore, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, functions, models) and basic data lineage principles
  • Basic awareness of metadata management and data discovery practices

sessions.title: Data Governance at Scale with ABAC at Atlassian
sessions.body: Atlassian’s internal data platform is the backbone for analytics, product insights and business decisions across the company. Managing data access policies at this scale is complex. In this talk, we’ll share how Atlassian embeds robust data governance policies, balancing agility with compliance, and innovation with security. Learn how we handle access management, data classification, and policy enforcement across diverse teams and tools. A key part of our approach is leveraging Databricks Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) to manage and abstract complex business policies. ABAC enables us to flexibly enforce fine-grained access controls (FGAC) using data tagging along with tag-driven policies, adapting quickly to changing requirements while keeping implementation logic abstracted from users. Join us for insights into the challenges, lessons learned, and solutions that keep our data platform secure and well-governed.

speakers.name: Erik IJzermans
speakers.bio: Erik is a product manager on the Unity Catalog team at Databricks, focused on fine-grained access controls for tables and volumes. He helps customers scale their data platforms while staying firmly in control of access and governance.

sessions.title: Data Intelligence for SaaS Threat Hunting: How Obsidian uses Databricks at scale
sessions.body: Security teams are overwhelmed by fragmented SaaS logs, identity signals, and investigation workflows spread across tools. Obsidian Security unifies SaaS security telemetry across cloud apps and identity providers to detect real-world threats like account takeover, suspicious OAuth activity, and insider risk.In this session, Damien Miller-McAndrews (Threat Researcher, Obsidian Security) shares how Obsidian leverages the Databricks Lakehouse to accelerate threat investigations using anonymized, high-volume security telemetry stored in a unified Databricks data lake. See how Databricks enables fast, repeatable investigations by combining scalable query performance, structured and semi-structured data processing, and governance-friendly workflows.Attendees will learn practical patterns for building modern cybersecurity investigation pipelines on Databricks—turning security data into 'investigation ready' intelligence and enabling faster detection, triage, and response.

speakers.name: Damien Miller-McAndrews
speakers.bio:
Damien Miller-McAndrews is a Threat Researcher at Obsidian Security, focused on real-world attacks against SaaS applications and cloud identity systems. He investigates how attackers combine SaaS abuse, identity compromise, and social engineering into fast-moving breaches, and develops detection strategies to help teams respond faster to account takeovers, OAuth abuse, and anomalous access across enterprise SaaS environments.

At Obsidian, Damien uses the Databricks Lakehouse to run high-scale investigations across anonymized security telemetry—accelerating triage, enriching threat hypotheses, and turning raw activity signals into investigation-ready intelligence. He brings a practitioner’s perspective to threat hunting and regularly shares research and practical insights to help security and IT teams better protect their organizations.

sessions.body:

Participants will learn to implement, manage and optimize a data environment where tables can be accessed by both Delta and Iceberg clients, enabling cross platform analytics and eliminating data silos.Prerequisites

We will show how we use Unity Catalog’s fine-grained access controls, dynamic masking and attribute-based access control (ABAC) to enforce GDPR and CCPA compliance internally. See how we ensure data utility for our engineers without ever compromising on privacy.

sessions.title: Data You Can Trust: Agentic Data Quality Monitoring from Lakeflow Jobs to Genie
sessions.body:
Organizations have more data than ever — but less confidence to use it. Traditional quality checks rely on manual rules applied to a handful of tables, leaving blind spots across the data estate.

 

In this session, we’ll show how Databricks reimagines data quality with an agentic AI approach. Instead of writing rules, AI agents learn your data’s normal behavior and seasonlity. Data quality anomalies are detected automatically and scale with your data.

 

Detection is only the first step. We’ll cover how quality signals integrate directly into Lakeflow Autopilot for automated root cause analysis, tracing anomalies upstream to the responsible job so engineers fix the right thing fast. And to prevent the business from using unreliable datasets, we’ll show you how health is surfaced in Genie, warning business users in real time when data behind their answer may be stale, before a critical decision is made on bad numbers.

speakers.name: Jacqueline Li
speakers.bio: Jacqueline is a product manager on the Data Quality Monitoring team at Databricks. At the Data + AI Summit, she'd love to talk with you about data quality, model monitoring, and PII detection!

sessions.title: Databricks Apps for Everyone: Build Custom Apps Without Writing a Line of Code
sessions.body: You shouldn't need to be a software engineer or experienced data practitioner to turn your data and AI into something your team can actually use. This session previews a new native AI-powered development experience on Databricks - one where anyone can go from idea to working application through a simple, conversational workflow. We'll show how a purpose-built agent, deeply integrated with the Databricks platform, makes building apps faster and more accessible than anything a general-purpose tool can offer. Whether you're a data analyst, a business user, or a developer who just wants to move faster — the future of app building on the Lakehouse is for you.

sessions.title: Databricks Apps: A Magic Wand for Driving Data Quality Adoption and Observability
sessions.body:
Most data quality tools don’t fail because the checks are wrong. They fail because users don’t understand how to use them.In this talk, we’ll share how we rebuilt our internal data quality platform using Databricks Apps and Databricks Workflows table triggers to prioritize usability and holistic visibility. We moved away from a config-file-driven model owned by a small group of platform engineers toward a user-centric approach that empowers teams to create, test and manage their own data quality rules.

 

With a Databricks App as the central interface, users can define and test rules, inspect production run history, and track data quality trends across the tables and teams they own. Combined with table-triggered workflows, checks run automatically as data changes without added operational complexity.This session covers our architecture, key design decisions, and lessons learned, and shows how Databricks Apps can turn data infrastructure into a user-friendly platform.

He writes and speaks on policy-as-code, medallion architecture, and the operational side of running a modern data platform at scale.

sessions.title: Databricks FinOps Genie — Cost Observability Meets Optimization Insights
sessions.body: We will showcase Databricks FinOps Genie, a cost observability and optimization capability that combines a Databricks‑native FinOps dashboard, Genie space and FinOps agent, proven at scale across 1,000+ workspaces in a large bank. Learn how to turn Databricks usage and billing data into a lightweight, reusable cost intelligence layer that surfaces key drivers of spend, anomalies and optimization opportunities through a single dashboard. See how a Genie space lets users “talk” to their FinOps data in natural language and receive detailed explanations and recommendations. Take home patterns for using a FinOps agent and recommendation model to right‑size clusters, address anomalous workloads and enable teams on Databricks FinOps best practices, so you can apply the same approach in your own estate.

sessions.title: Databricks on Databricks Marketing: How our Marketing Team runs Campaigns on Databricks
sessions.body: You’ll get a front row seat to see how Databricks Marketing Technology and Engineering teams work together to bring industry-leading marketing campaigns to life, using the Databricks platform as a centerpiece to a broader MarTech stack. Using a combination of existing tech and new capabilities, the session will be a deep-dive with concrete implementation details on running Marketing on Databricks.

sessions.title: Databricks on Databricks: Automating Service Reliability at Scale
sessions.body: Rapid product delivery makes service reliability a core engineering challenge. This talk shows how we use Databricks on Databricks to build production systems that automate reliability detection and investigation for user-facing services.I’ll cover 2 systems. KPI Miss Auto-Investigator automates KPI regression analysis by detecting dips, ranking error contributors, computing customer blast radius, and syncing annotations across team and global dashboards. Built with Databricks Jobs and ETL pipelines with inter-job dependencies, it cuts on-call investigation time by 67%.User Error Anomaly Detection is a Databricks-based system for logging, detection, and monitoring. User error logs are ingested via Zerobus into Delta tables, analyzed by Jobs using Asset Bundles, and monitored through SQL Alerts and AI/BI dashboards. The system detects incidents up to 3 hours before customer reports, reducing discovery time by 95% and customer impact by 90%, with 95% recall and 98% precision.

sessions.title: Databricks on Databricks: Build Your Own Experimentation Platform
sessions.body:
Commercial experimentation platforms promise everything – feature flags, metrics, and analysis, but often limit flexibility when you want to go beyond the basics.

 

At Databricks, we took a different approach: we built our own full-stack experimentation platform entirely on our internal Databricks and used it to power hundreds of product releases every month.

 

In this talk, we’ll show how you can do the same.

 

You’ll learn how we:

  • Use Unity Catalog to centralize and govern feature enablement data
  • Define reusable, trustworthy metrics with our internal Metrics Platform
  • Run scalable experiment analyses with Lakeflow Serverless Jobs
  • Deliver fast, intuitive user experiences with Lakehouse Apps

 

Beyond the platform itself, we’ll share how we extend it with advanced methodologies that go far beyond what commercial tools support.

 

Whether you’re a data scientist or platform engineer, you’ll walk away with a blueprint for building a reliable, extensible, and fully owned experimentation platform on Databricks.

sessions.title: Decathlon’s Race to Unified Governance: Securing Interoperability at Scale
sessions.body:
Decathlon, operating in 70+ countries, aims to make wellbeing accessible through sport. Scaling to thousands of tables strained our legacy metadata management (AWS Glue). Moving to Unity Catalog (UC) unified governance for 2,000+ users but created a key challenge: How to centralize governance within the Databricks Lakehouse while maintaining interoperability with external engines?

 

This session details Decathlon’s migration from AWS Glue to Unity Catalog, focusing on how we ensured "openness" so that external engines—EMR, Athena, Polars, DuckDB—remain compatible and performant under UC. We will share the framework used to automate the transition of thousands of tables and present metrics on improved metadata rendering speeds and streamlined platform administration.

sessions.title: Deep Dive Into Streaming and Batch ETLs With Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body: Let's deep dive into the new declarative ETL pipeline framework in Apache Spark™, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP). Let's peel it off to learn how SDP's high-level Python and SQL abstractions translate into lower-level Spark SQL and Spark Structured Streaming queries. During the talk, you will learn how SDP automatically resolves complex dependencies and builds optimized Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) for both batch and streaming workloads. We will walk through the internal state management and orchestration logic that allows SDP to handle retries and incremental processing out of the box, replacing thousands of lines of imperative "glue code." You will leave with a clear mental model of the engine's architecture, the pros and cons of SDP, and be ready to debug and optimize your pipelines. You'll understand where and how to use it (alongside your existing ETL pipelines).

sessions.title: Deep Dive Into Streaming on Databricks
sessions.body:
A factory detects an equipment anomaly and needs the alert in seconds. A financial platform needs to process a transaction, enrich it with account history, and flag it for fraud—all before the customer closes the app. These workloads both involve streaming data, but they have very different requirements under the hood.

 

This session introduces the two core streaming capabilities on Databricks, Real-Time Mode and Zerobus Ingest, and how to match them to your workload.

 

Real-Time Mode on Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming is for when data needs to be acted upon, not just stored. With sub-second, event-driven computation and expressive stateful processing via TransformWithState, it's the right choice for operational workloads where latency directly affects business outcomes: live betting platforms, ad attribution pipelines, fraud detection, and real-time personalization.

 

Zerobus Ingest is a Kafka-free ingestion capability that lets applications and devices write event data directly into Delta Lake, no message broker, no compute overhead, governed delivery out of the box. It's designed to move data fast and at scale. It does not process or transform data in flight, and for ingestion-heavy workloads, that's exactly the right tradeoff.

 

We'll contrast both tools, walk through a workload decision framework, and show you when to use each, and how to chain them together for end-to-end real-time data flow on Databricks.

sessions.title: Deep Dive: Why the Best Data Warehouse Is a Lakehouse
sessions.body: As organizations accelerate AI adoption, the need for a unified platform that delivers trusted, high-quality data across the business has become critical.Join this 90-minute deep dive to learn why leading organizations are standardizing on the lakehouse architecture for data warehousing, analytics, and AI. You’ll see how modern lakehouses unify teams around a single source of truth, reduce costly data movement, simplify governance, and provide analysts, engineers, and AI practitioners with access to fresher, more complete data.We’ll explore how a lakehouse supports both BI and AI workloads on one open platform while integrating with tools like Fivetran, dbt, Tableau, and Power BI. You’ll also learn how to lower costs with serverless SQL compute, improve trust with automated lineage, eliminate silos, and modernize legacy warehouse-centric architectures with a scalable, governed foundation for analytics and AI.

The most successful PS firms of this decade will be the ones that leverage AI to enable their clients to deliver on their AI bets. sessions.title: Delta Kernel <> Catalog-Managed Tables
sessions.body: With the introduction of Catalog-Managed Tables, Delta Lake has unlocked unified governance, enforceable constraints, and a path towards multi-table updates.As a result, Delta connectors must adapt to properly load, read, and write Delta Tables, as the Catalog is now the authoritative broker of commits, not the filesystem.In this talk, learn how we designed Catalog Managed Tables support in Delta Kernel—the one right Delta abstraction to rule them all. We’ve built a unified catalog-agnostic API against which connectors can develop, enabled deep and powerful engine integrations for DuckDB, Delta-Spark, and Delta-Flink, all while keeping the complexity of catalog support out of Kernel.

speakers.name: Scott Sandre
speakers.bio: Scott Sandre is a Sr Software Engineer at Databricks on the Delta Ecosystem team, where he leads the design of catalog-managed Delta tables and drives the catalog integration support in Delta Kernel.  Based in San Francisco, Scott is passionate about open-source technologies and building performance-intensive systems.

sessions.title: Delta Sharing SecureConnect: Simplify Network Configuration for External Data Collaboration
sessions.body: As Delta Sharing deployments scale to more recipients, managing per-recipient IP allowlists and allowing direct storage access becomes a significant operational burden. It can also be a blocker for data providers that want to keep their storage hidden behind firewalls. This session covers how Delta Sharing SecureConnect addresses this problem by introducing a Databricks-managed network intermediary that proxies storage access on behalf of recipients. Providers perform a one-time network configuration regardless of the number of recipients. SecureConnect then handles routing across AWS, Azure, and GCP without requiring storage to be exposed to the public internet. We'll cover the architecture, cloud-specific configuration patterns, and how SecureConnect offers private and simple data sharing at scale.

sessions.title: Delta Sharing: The Most Widely Adopted Open Protocol for Data and AI Sharing
sessions.body:
AI is only as good as the data that fuels it. To build and scale models, organizations need a way to move past fragmented data silos and complex ETL. Delta Sharing provides the industry’s most widely adopted open protocol for the secure, real-time exchange of the datasets and AI assets required for modern innovation.

 

We’ll dive deep into:

  • Fueling AI With Openness: How to share live data, volumes and AI models with any recipient—regardless of their platform—to accelerate model training and deployment.
  • Latest Innovations: A first look at enhanced governance, automated provider workflows and expanded support for complex assets like AI functions and unstructured data.
  • Real-World Scale: Real-world use cases showing how organizations use the protocol to unify their data ecosystems and manage AI assets at scale.

 

From live demos to architectural best practices, you’ll walk away with a roadmap to unify your data ecosystem and lead the next wave of open collaboration.

sessions.title: Democratizing Data and AI at Freshworks With Governed Lakehouse and Freddy AI
sessions.body: Freshworks has standardized its data and AI strategy on a Databricks‑powered lakehouse called Baikal, built to serve 70,000+ customers and 1,500 internal users across 14 business functions. Databricks ingests data from dozens of operational and third‑party sources into Delta Lake bronze, silver, and gold layers governed by Unity Catalog, enabling high‑quality, discoverable datasets and fine‑grained access control with full auditability. Dedicated BI, AIML, product and functional workspaces run on governed & segregated compute with centralized monitoring, improving reliability, observability and cost attribution. On this foundation, Freshworks trains and operates Freddy AI agents, copilots and insights using Databricks ML, MLflow and an open AI ecosystem to move seamlessly from experimentation to production. This architecture modernizes legacy Hadoop systems, delivers 2–5x faster processing and democratizes AI across the company.
