sessions.title: Deploying and Monitoring Agents on Databricks
sessions.body:
This hands-on course guides you through deploying and monitoring agentic AI systems in the Databricks environment. You will start by learning how to deploy agents in batch mode using AI Functions and integrate them into data pipelines. Next, you'll explore real-time deployment using Model Serving, including deploying agents as REST endpoints and managing autoscaling, versioning, and governance via Mosaic AI Model Serving. You'll then turn to observability and monitoring, using MLflow tracing and scoring functions to capture metrics, analyze requests and responses, and detect anomalies in production. Finally, you'll learn best practices for deploying agents with built-in trace collection, inference logging, and feedback loops to support ongoing evaluation and robustness.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including Unity Catalog and Delta Lake
  • Intermediate Python programming experience
  • Familiarity with Generative AI fundamentals, including LLMs, RAG architectures, and prompt engineering
  • Familiarity with Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) 
  • Basic SQL proficiency, including use of functions like ai_query
  • Basic understanding of MLOps/LLMOps principles and software deployment concepts, including CI/CD pipelines, REST APIs, and YAML configuration

sessions.title: Designing beautiful, effective dashboards: Best practices for visual story telling in AI/BI
sessions.body: A great dashboard isn’t just fast and accurate. It’s intuitive, engaging, and easy to act on. Yet many fall short, cluttered with too many visuals, unclear layouts, and designs that don’t translate across devices.AI/BI Dashboards make it easier to build polished, interactive experiences, but strong design still depends on thoughtful choices around layout, hierarchy, and usability. With rising expectations for mobile access, dashboards need to deliver the same clarity whether viewed on a large screen or in the palm of your hand.We’ll cover practical design best practices to help you create dashboards that don’t just display information, but make it easy to understand and act on.- Design dashboards with clear visual hierarchy and focus- Choose the right charts and layouts to communicate insights effectively- Design responsive dashboards that work seamlessly across desktop and mobile- Avoid common design mistakes that cause clutter, confusion, and misinterpretation

speakers.name: Eason Gao
speakers.bio: Eason is a Product Manager at Databricks who loves turning complex data into easy-to-understand and interactive dashboard. He's passionate about making data make sense for everyone. When he's not at work, you can find him up early watching Formula 1 races or standing in line at the best ramen shop in town.

speakers.name: Mohit Hingorani
speakers.bio: Mohit Hingorani is a Product Designer at Databricks, specializing in data visualization. At Databricks, Mohit is responsible for AI/BI dashboards and mobile app, Genie.

sessions.title: Designing Data Models and Architectures
sessions.body:
This practitioner-focused course is a deep dive into designing data models within the Databricks Lakehouse.

The course explores three leading data warehousing approaches — Inmon's Corporate Information Factory, Kimball's dimensional modeling, and Data Vault 2.0 — and shows how each maps to the medallion architecture. Participants will also learn how to extend these foundations to modern use cases such as data products for scalable, governed data sharing across domains.

Prerequisites

  • Working knowledge of SQL
  • Conceptual understanding of relational databases
  • Completion of an introductory Databricks or Lakehouse Fundamentals course
  • Optional: prior exposure to Python and PySpark

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Destination Databricks: Hertz’s Data Platform Modernization Journey
sessions.body:
Hertz is executing a multi-phase transformation to decommission its 15-year-old Teradata/Informatica/Cognos ecosystem and establish a modern data platform that powers BI and analytics across global reservations, rentals, billing, fleet management and enterprise operations.

 

Hertz’s Databricks-powered data platform enables real-time analytics and enterprise-scale AI while improving data governance and significantly lowering operational expenses.

 

In this talk, we walk through Hertz’s data landscape and our approach migrating from legacy systems.

sessions.title: Detecting and Reducing Manipulative AI Outputs With Interpretable Governance Signals
sessions.body:
Large language models are increasingly embedded in data platforms and decision workflows, yet they can generate manipulative and propagandistic content at scale, often without obvious policy violations. In this talk, I present a production-oriented approach to detecting and mitigating manipulation in generative AI systems using interpretable, data-driven signals.

 

Drawing on real-world pipelines I’ve built, I show how manipulative techniques can be operationalized as measurable indicators within AI evaluation workflows. I demonstrate how these signals can be used to monitor model behavior, compare outputs across model versions, and guide alignment strategies that significantly reduce harmful generation while preserving utility.

 

This session focuses on how to integrate responsible AI checks into data pipelines, how to reason about governance beyond binary safety flags, and how interpretable metrics enable more trustworthy AI systems at scale.

speakers.name: Julia Jose
speakers.bio:
Julia Jose is a Computer Science Ph.D. candidate at New York University, advised by Rachel Greenstadt, focusing on responsible and trustworthy AI. She is also an Applied AI Engineer at King Street, where she builds and deploys large language model–driven systems in production. Her work uses natural language processing and deep learning to study misinformation, propaganda, and manipulative behavior in LLMs, with an emphasis on detection and mitigation at scale.

Previously, Julia worked as a Data Scientist at Atos building production ML systems, and as a Venture Capital and Machine Learning Fellow at Atento Capital. She has also conducted R&D in multilingual NLP and social computing at the Qatar Computing Research Institute.

sessions.title: DevConnect Meetup
sessions.body:
The DevConnect Meetup is a multi-track event dedicated to exploring the latest innovations shaping the future of data, AI, and agentic systems. This technical meetup series offers distinct data engineering,  applied AI, and AI research tracks that bring together developers, researchers, and innovators across the ecosystem.

This event will dive deep into GenAI and agentic applications, highlighting how intelligent systems can reason, plan, and act autonomously across real-world data workflows.   Sessions connect practitioners from academia, startups, and industry to share insights, tackle implementation challenges, and showcase the next generation of data-to-AI architectures.

Attendees will gain firsthand perspectives from engineers and researchers driving progress in agentic AI, from dynamic orchestration of data pipelines to the deployment of self-directed, real-world AI agents.

To view the schedule for the day, please head to bit.ly/devconnect-dais-26.

sessions.title: Developing BI Dashboards with AI/BI
sessions.body:
In this hands-on course, you’ll learn how to use the features Databricks provides for business intelligence needs: AI/BI Dashboards and AI/BI Genie. As a Databricks Data Analyst, you will be tasked with creating AI/BI Dashboards and AI/BI Genie Spaces within the platform, managing the access to these assets by stakeholders and necessary parties, and maintaining these assets as they are edited, refreshed, or decommissioned over the course of their lifespan. This course intends to instruct participants on how to design dashboards for business insights, share those with collaborators and stakeholders, and maintain those assets within the platform. Participants will also learn how to utilize AI/BI Genie Spaces to support self-service analytics through the creation and maintenance of these environments powered by the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. 

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Basic SQL proficiency for querying data in Databricks
  • Basic familiarity with the Databricks Workspace UI
  • Basic understanding of statistical analysis and data interpretation
  • Familiarity with dashboards and business intelligence concepts

sessions.title: Developing BI Dashboards with AI/BI
sessions.body:
In this hands-on course, you’ll learn how to use the features Databricks provides for business intelligence needs: AI/BI Dashboards and AI/BI Genie. As a Databricks Data Analyst, you will be tasked with creating AI/BI Dashboards and AI/BI Genie Spaces within the platform, managing the access to these assets by stakeholders and necessary parties, and maintaining these assets as they are edited, refreshed, or decommissioned over the course of their lifespan. This course intends to instruct participants on how to design dashboards for business insights, share those with collaborators and stakeholders, and maintain those assets within the platform. Participants will also learn how to utilize AI/BI Genie Spaces to support self-service analytics through the creation and maintenance of these environments powered by the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. 

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Basic SQL proficiency for querying data in Databricks
  • Basic familiarity with the Databricks Workspace UI
  • Basic understanding of statistical analysis and data interpretation
  • Familiarity with dashboards and business intelligence concepts

sessions.title: Diagnosing Performance Bottlenecks in Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: In complex analytics environments, performance issues are rarely isolated — and surface-level tuning often misses the real bottleneck. This deep dive session presents an advanced framework for diagnosing performance problems in Databricks Lakehouse, grounded in how the engine executes queries at scale. We’ll walk through how to distinguish query-level inefficiencies from data layout issues, concurrency pressure, and system-level constraints, and how to interpret execution plans and runtime signals to identify the true root cause. Attendees will leave with a repeatable diagnostic approach they can apply to large, multi-tenant production workloads and examples of using AI to assist in finding and resolving your performance bottlenecks.

speakers.name: Shannon Barrow
speakers.bio: Shannon has spent the last 7 years at Databricks helping enterprise customers modernize their analytics platforms to maximize value from their data and drive down the total cost of ownership.  Specializing in performance for data engineering and SQL consumption, he is a leading SME in benchmarking and POC efforts across Enterprise North America.  Before joining Databricks in 2019, he was a Principal in Accenture's Innovation and Thought Leadership team.  Shannon has a Masters in Computer Science from Georgia Tech and 2 Bachelor Degrees from Florida State University.

sessions.title: Dialing Up with Genie: How Telecom Providers are Winning with Natural Language AI/BI
sessions.body:
In an industry where network reliability and customer experience are sacred, telecommunications leaders need accurate, real-time insights fast. Yet business and data teams have long existed in silos, keeping these crucial insights out of reach for those who need it in-the-moment the most. But now, operators are able to break down these silos with AI-powered conversational business intelligence, made possible by solutions like AI/BI Genie.

 

In this session, discover how Genie is empowering business users across telecommunications to get the answers and insights they need from their data in natural language, allowing them to ask complex questions and receive instant, governed insights. Learn how experts at leading operators including Frontier, GCI, and DIRECTV conversational intelligence are using Genie to eliminate traditional data bottlenecks and identify new strategies to move their business forward. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint for scaling AI-driven conversational BI and get a firsthand look at how Genie is enabling real telecom organizations to do more with their data.

sessions.title: Dialogues with Data: Accelerating Pre-Sales Discovery through Agentic AI
sessions.body: Pre-sales Solution Architects (SAs) lose momentum navigating enterprise information silos. At Databricks, hyper-growth GTM and a fast-changing product stack amplify the problem. We built an Agentic Research Assistant that turns internal GTM knowledge into a conversational solution-design engine aligned to real pre-sales workflows.This session is a technical deep dive into the pipeline: a streaming event-driven architecture integrated with Databricks Model Serving, MLflow, and Lakehouse-native state management for real-time adaptability and observability.Highlights Workflow-to-tool modeling for field-aligned agent actions Lakehouse state store for conversation memory + tool-call trajectories Intent-aware retrieval with Instructed Retrievers Conversational reasoning using a DSPy ReAct extension Continuous optimization with DSPy + GEPA from historical trajectoriesA blueprint to move beyond basic RAG to self-improving agents that accelerate technical discovery and solutioning.

speakers.name: Colton Peltier
speakers.bio: I am a Staff Data Scientist at Databricks in Professional Services helping customers develop and deploy cutting-edge ML solutions.

speakers.name: Luis Moros
speakers.bio: Luis Moros is a Staff Machine Learning Engineer consultant at the ML Practice of Databricks. He has been working in software engineering for more than 20 years, focusing in GenAI, Data Science and Big Data in the last 8. Prior to Databricks, Luis has applied Machine Learning and Data Science in different industries including: Financial Services, BioTech, Entertainment, and Augmented Reality.

sessions.title: Ditch the Message Bus with Zerobus Ingest
sessions.body:
Streaming is evolving—quickly. Modern architectures are eliminating infrastructure sprawl in favor of a direct-to-lakehouse model, eliminating the need for intermediate message buses and the expense of maintaining them. Zerobus Ingest allows you to push data directly to the lakehouse with near real-time writes, high throughput, and support for thousands of concurrent clients.

 

In this demo-packed session, we’ll cover:

  • How Zerobus works and how to build production-ready pipelines—without the heavy ownership costs of DIY infrastructure.
  • The latest supported interfaces (e.g., REST, OTel, and Kafka-compatible APIs), as well as new features designed for massive scale (e.g., liquid clustering, JSON variant type support, etc.).
  • See how global innovators like Joby Aviation and Toyota Motor Corporation have embraced this shift to streamline their real-time architectures.

 

Join us and discover a direct ingestion framework to simplify your stack and accelerate your impact.

speakers.name: Victoria Bukta
speakers.bio: Victoria is a product manager at Databricks on the LakeFlow team. She previously was a PM at Tabular, and an engineering manager at Shopify where she led teams working on large-scale, low-latency ingestion and pioneered lakehouse adoption. She is based out of Toronto and sails in her spare time.

sessions.title: Doubling Medical Safety: Fine-Tuning Open LLMs for Women's Health Without Human Labels
sessions.body:
Enterprises building LLM features in healthcare hit the same wall: satisfying dozens of safety rules simultaneously—crisis escalation, treatment boundaries, referral language—while real user data is off-limits and expert labeling is prohibitively expensive.

 

We'll show how Flo Health broke through using RFT-inspired synthetic fine-tuning, transforming Llama 3.3 70B into a healthcare-compliant assistant for women's health that doubled safety compliance versus our previous iteration. The key insight: instead of investing expert time in labeling, we redirected it into designing LLM judges that scale.

 

Our system uses 60 LLM judges—52 for medical safety, 8 for usefulness—with priority-weighted reward aggregation where P1 safety rules dominate over P2 quality rules. You'll learn patterns for multi-judge evaluation systems, reward aggregation strategies for binary constraints, and why simpler approaches beat complex alternatives. For anyone building AI where "mostly safe" isn't good enough.

speakers.name: Andras Meczner
speakers.bio: András Meczner is a Director of Medical Accuracy and Safety at Flo Health. His team at Flo Health ensures that the features, including the AI initiatives, are medically accurate and safe in the Flo App. He is also a practicing pediatrician at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust and has years of experience building a symptom checker.

speakers.name: Michael Shtelma
speakers.bio: Michael Shtelma is a Lead Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks. Michael focuses on developing and operationalizing large-scale Machine Learning use cases on the Databricks platform. Before Databricks, Michael worked for Teradata, helping Teradata customers build data and machine learning solutions.

speakers.name: Vladislav Nedosekin
speakers.bio: Vladislav Nedosekin is Director of Engineering AI Platform at Flo Health. He leads the AI platform behind Flo Health, focussing on modernising data architectures, accelerating product delivery with AI, and enabling engineering teams to ship faster without compromising medical safety. Before Flo Health, he spent years at AWS helping high-growth companies design cloud platforms built for scale, reliability, and radical cost efficiency.

sessions.title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. H-AI-de: Using MLflow and AI Judges to measure model alignment and safety
sessions.body: Emergent misalignment sent shockwaves through the AI community in 2025. We discovered that a model fine-tuned on narrow tasks could suddenly pivot from a "helpful tool" into a "rogue actor." In early 2026, Nature warned that mistrained models "quickly go off the rails," making AI safety a non-negotiable for enterprise innovation. To build with confidence, we must move beyond blind trust toward empirical control.In this 20-minute lightning talk, we will demystify the process of assessing model integrity. We'll walk through the practical steps to:- Build custom judges designed to detect latent misalignment and goal-drift.- Deploy judges in MLflow to automate the evaluation of frontier open-source models.- Benchmark against emerging standards like HarmBench to quantify operational risk.Learn how to stay in control and inherently understand the internal "compass" of your models. The last thing your enterprise needs is an assistant that turns into a monster the moment you look away.

sessions.title: Driving Enterprise Transformation With an AI‑Enabled Field Assistant
sessions.body: Lilly’s presentation will highlight how a dual business and technology strategy is guiding the rollout of an AI field assistant and enabling scalable governance and organizational change management across diverse groups of field users. We will highlight why we chose the platform and how the Databricks ecosystem is accelerating innovation by unifying data, analytics and AI capabilities to support smarter, faster decision making. We expect to share expanded updates on emerging features such as Genie, which will ease prompt constraints and support more abstract, data aware questions, along with new agentic actions that streamline workflows and broaden what users can accomplish through natural language interaction. Throughout the presentation we will share lessons learned from deploying the platform at scale. Together, these advancements illustrate how coordinated business and technical innovation are shaping more adaptive, AI enabled solutions.

speakers.name: thomas raborn
speakers.job_title: Exec Director, Lilly US Field Operations
speakers.bio: Thomas Raborn is a seasoned commercial operations leader with more than 23 years of experience driving commercial strategy and field effectiveness across the pharmaceutical industry. Currently serving as Exec Director within a Global Operations organization, he leads a high-performing team focused on commercial strategy, field effectiveness, and the integration of data and AI into sales operations.

sessions.title: Duct Tape to Databricks: 3 Years of Brickbot at Data & AI Summit
sessions.body: Brickbot started as a simple chatbot hacked together for DAIS 2024. DuckDB in memory, parquet files in git and a prayer that Heroku wouldn't go down. At DAIS 2025 we improved it with tool calling and direct integration with RainFocus, but it was still mostly cobbled together. Now, for DAIS 2026, we've rebuilt it entirely on Databricks with no custom infrastructure, using Agent Bricks, Vector Search, Databricks Apps, Lakebase, UC Functions as MCP tools and Lakeflow. This talk traces that journey, the lessons learned shipping an AI app to 30,000 conference attendees, and how the Databricks' platform evolved alongside it.

sessions.title: Effective document management and retrieval for generative AI
sessions.body: Building production RAG systems requires far more than embedding documents. This 90-minute deep dive covers the complete technical pipeline: document structuring principles, semantic vs. fixed-size chunking tradeoffs, contextual and multi-modal embeddings, and advanced retrieval optimization, accompanied by practical implementation on Databricks. We'll demonstrate a real-world Databricks RAG pipeline covering pre-processing at scale, embedding optimization and advanced retrieval techniques—including re-ranking, contextual filtering and real-time quality evaluation. Beyond retrieval, we showcase how Agent Bricks transforms RAG systems into autonomous, agentic applications capable of multi-step reasoning and complex tasks. The session also explores emerging trends—vision-space retrieval, contextual clustering and real-time quality assurance—critical for production systems where accuracy directly impacts outcomes.

speakers.name: Xintia Gyenge
speakers.bio: Xintia Gyenge is a Solution Architect at Databricks, where she helps organizations across Europe design and scale modern data and AI platforms. She works closely with customers on data modernization initiatives spanning cloud architecture, data governance, analytics, and AI adoption - helping teams turn complex technical challenges into scalable solutions.

speakers.name: Yevgeniy Ilyin
speakers.bio: Yevgeniy Ilyin, CFA, is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks based in Zurich, helping customers across Central and Eastern Europe develop real-world, innovative data and AI solutions on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. He brings 25+ years of experience in software architecture and technical leadership across financial services and enterprise technology, with a focus on data platform architecture, MLOps, governance, and agentic AI. Yevgeniy regularly speaks at industry data and AI conferences and develops and delivers hands-on workshops for practitioners. He holds a CFA charter, a Certified IT Specialist credential from ETH Zurich, and an MSc in Physics and Computer Science.

sessions.title: Eliminate the Engineering Bottleneck: The Next Generation of Feature Authoring
sessions.body: Taking a feature from idea to production is a gauntlet. A data scientist prototypes in a notebook on historic data; an ML engineer rebuilds it in production; someone backfills historic data for online serving. Weeks disappear — and subtle bugs slip in between the trained model and production.What if one feature definition drove the whole process? That's the premise behind Declarative Feature Engineering, the next-generation feature authoring experience on Databricks. You'll see how data scientists go from hypothesis to production-serving feature without filing a ticket or switching tools. One declaration captures source, entity, aggregation, and time semantics — and the platform turns it into managed pipelines, automatic backfills, and low-latency online serving, no reimplementation required.Whether you're blocked on engineering cycles or tired of maintaining hand-rolled pipelines, you'll leave with the patterns to ship features and models at the speed of experimentation.

sessions.title: Embedded Analytics with Databricks AI/BI
sessions.body: We often focus on using Databricks AI/BI to power internal business intelligence, but what about delivering those same insights directly to your customers?In this hands-on session, you’ll learn how to embed Databricks AI/BI Dashboards and Genie into external, customer-facing applications. Discover how to seamlessly integrate analytics and conversational AI to turn your apps into data-driven experiences that empower users to make informed decisions right within their workflow.Workshop topics:-Overview of Embedded Analytics with Databricks AI/BI-Embedding Dashboards with iframe-based and token-based methods-Integrating AI/BI Genie using Conversational APIs

speakers.name: Doyoung Jung
speakers.bio: Doyoung Jung is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he partners with VC-backed startups to design scalable data systems. With a strong interest in the convergence of AI, BI, and customer-facing applications, Doyoung helps emerging businesses build smarter data products.

sessions.title: Embracing Serverless SQL at Riot Games
sessions.body:
At Riot Games, we found that embracing serverless compute—rather than limiting it—allowed us to scale more effectively while improving performance, governance and user experience.

 

In this session, we’ll share Riot’s shift from a cost-first mindset to an enablement-driven approach using Databricks SQL Serverless, with Unity Catalog as a key enabler. Consistent governance, lineage and usage visibility gave us the confidence to adopt serverless while maintaining transparency and accountability.

 

We’ll explore how serverless SQL warehouses support diverse analytics and reporting needs through strong performance, simplified user experiences and elastic, on-demand cost efficiency. We’ll also discuss how serverless compute streamlined the data engineering lifecycle by reducing infrastructure management.

 

Finally, we’ll cover Riot’s broader adoption of serverless for jobs and general workloads, the resulting operational and cost benefits, and how we manage costs in a serverless-first model.

sessions.title: Emotional Congruence at Scale: Using Databricks AI to Align Ads and Content
sessions.body:
TV advertisers know context matters, but most contextual signals stop at coarse attributes like genre or keywords. What about emotion? What we watch shapes how we feel—and how we feel influences how we engage with brands.

 

At NBCUniversal, we built an Emotional Congruence engine to quantify whether alignment between these emotional signals drives intent and conversion—and how to scale it using Databricks.

 

Using foundation models served on Databricks, we extract and summarize unstructured signals from content and ads, tagging each with a standardized emotional taxonomy across themes, tones and personal values. Governed end-to-end with MLflow 3.0, the system is orchestrated for rigorous testing and deployment.

 

Testing shows emotional alignment drives measurable lift—often in the double digits. As a result, it is now embedded within NBCUniversal’s broader contextual advertising offering.

sessions.title: Empowering Non-Technical Users in Pharma With Dashboards and Chatbots Working Together in Databricks
sessions.body: The presentation shows how Databricks enables non‑technical users in pharma to gain scientific insights by uniting dashboards, chatbots, documents and data. The foundation is data and documents from source systems organized in Unity Catalog and a semantic layer of schemas, tables with definitions, metrics views with business logics, keys linking datasets, SQL functions, Genie and Agent Bricks. Clinical study data is complex, with interpretation depending on context often described in documents. We use a dashboard for context, with visuals and filters conveying the overarching story, while Genie and Agent Bricks offer insights via natural-language questions. Traditional dashboards excel at data storytelling but lack flexibility and tends to grow into overwhelming complexity, by adding context-aware chatbots we address these challenges. Insights can also be embedded into platforms like Teams and SharePoint, ensuring easy access, while having data and calculations centrally governed.

speakers.name: Half Scheidl
speakers.bio: Half Scheidl is a Senior Delivery Solutions Architect at Databricks with 15+ years of experience spanning cloud architecture, data platforms, analytics, and AI. He focuses on turning ambitious ideas into production-ready solutions, helping customers move from first concept to real-world impact. Known for bridging business goals and technical detail, he translates advanced capabilities into practical, high-leverage outcomes. Half holds a BSc in Computer Engineering and an MSc in IT Management. Before Databricks, he led AI, analytics, and data platform initiatives at H&M. At DAIS, he will focus on how dashboards, semantic layers, and natural-language interfaces can make data exploration more intuitive, reliable, and impactful.

speakers.name: Sinna Lisa Vange
speakers.bio: Principal information & data architect in the pharmaceutical industry with 30 years' experience, mainly in clinical development but also research, pre-clinical, and medical affairs. Core skills include scientific communication, data visualisation, information and data architecture, IT systems design, and leadership. I have in different roles been involved in numerous clinical projects across multiple therapy areas, as well in IT projects spanning resource planning, document management, data standardisation and visualisation, study design, and product master data. I enjoy combining detail with overview, complexity with simplicity, and synthesize it all into meaning that can help others obtain new insights.

sessions.title: Enabling a Low-Latency Data Mesh at Warner Music Group Using Lakebase, Iceberg and Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
Today’s enterprises face daunting challenges when creating impact with data, from fundamental trust issues to dynamically evolving AI use cases. Legacy systems with technical debt impede business value even as users expect trustworthy, low-latency insights for both natural language queries and classic insights. Furthermore, pipelines are often distributed across different engines. This environment demands a flexible approach to drive impact that brings cohesion to an often-messy data environment.

 

This session describes how WMG Tech leveraged Databricks to develop a declarative data platform that realizes a compositional data mesh designed to tackle this challenge. This architecture includes:

  • Iceberg as an engine agnostic data layer for access to diverse sources
  • Unity Catalog for compositional access to data products
  • Lakebase for native low latency analytical APIs

 

Together, this platform enables an array of data products that serve AI queries and WMG's applications.

speakers.name: Michael Jones
speakers.bio: Michael Jones is a Senior Director of Software Engineering at Warner Music Group leading the Data and Insights organization responsible for ML/AI, data engineering and infrastructure, and data serving. He has a background in software engineering and has extensive experience leading engineering teams across a variety of domains including digital ads, cloud, and unmanned systems.

sessions.title: Enabling Evolutionary Database Development with Database Branching
sessions.body: This talk builds on the foundations of Evolutionary Database Design, applying the framework of Values, Principles, Methods, Practices, and Tools to a revolutionary capability: database branching.In 1999, Thoughtworks pioneered evolutionary design out of necessity, leading to modern standards like migrations and tools such as Flyway and Liquibase. However, despite improvements in testing and automation, teams still lacked the ability to branch databases as easily as code.Lakebase changes this. Its copy-on-write technology creates a full-fidelity, governance-aware production clone in roughly one second, regardless of size, with zero initial storage.Kevin and Pramod will demonstrate how database branching transforms workflows:* Self-Sufficiency: Enabling teams to be more productive and autonomous.* Collaboration: Shifting the DBA from a "gatekeeper" to a design contributor.* Innovation: Empowering teams to run unlimited experiments to find optimal solutions.

speakers.name: Kevin Hartman
speakers.bio:
Kevin Hartman leads the Partner Solutions Architects team at Databricks, who help consulting partners build Data and AI solutions on the Databricks platform.

Kevin has spent a career solving complex problems using technology and data. His specialty is formulating high-impact solutions that leverage technology innovation. He has inspired, influenced, and led the creation of hundreds of digital products — working from both inside and alongside teams of researchers, scientists, designers, engineers, and enthusiasts. He has a masters degree in Information and Data Science from UC Berkeley and later became a faculty member to the program. He is based in Chicago.

speakers.name: Pramod Sadalage
speakers.bio:
Pramod Sadalage is Director at ThoughtWorks leading the Modern Data Architecture service for North America, he enjoys the rare role of bridging the divide between database professionals and application developers. He is usually sent in to clients with particularly challenging data needs, which require new technologies and techniques. In the early 00’s he developed techniques to allow relational databases to be designed in an evolutionary manner based on version-controlled schema migrations.

He is co-author Refactoring Databases: Evolutionary Database Design, co-author of NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence and continues to speak and write about the insights he and his clients learn.

sessions.title: Energy & Utilities Industry Forum | Sponsored by: Infosys
sessions.body:
The energy transition is the defining industrial challenge of our time and data is its most critical infrastructure. Join energy and utilities leaders for an essential forum on how Databricks’ Data Intelligence Platform is enabling companies to navigate decarbonization, grid modernization and the rise of distributed energy resources with confidence and speed.

 

Whether you're optimizing upstream exploration, managing a complex grid at scale or building the analytics backbone for a net-zero commitment, Databricks provides the unified, open platform that turns petabytes of operational data into real-time intelligence. This forum explores the imperatives shaping the sector: predictive asset management, emissions monitoring and reporting, energy trading and risk analytics, renewable integration, and AI-powered demand forecasting. Learn how leading energy companies are eliminating data fragmentation and accelerating decision-making from wellhead to wall socket.

 

Gain insights from peers who are already harnessing the power of data to drive the energy transition forward and build lasting competitive advantage. Features leaders from Chevron, Shell, Constellation and Alinta Energy.

speakers.name: Anne Marie Hensley
speakers.bio:
Anne Marie Hensley is Chevron’s General Manager of Manufacturing Ops Digital Engineering.  She is an enthusiastic and proven IT leader with over 20 years of experience delivering transformational change using technology as a catalyst.  One of Anne Marie’s key strengths is her natural ability to take complex ideas and challenges and break them down into manageable and actionable solutions.  This, along with her no-nonsense communication style and her contagious optimism, make her an extremely effective leader.
 
Anne Marie earned her bachelor’s degree in civil engineering and a master’s degree in environmental engineering from Manhattan College.  She lives in The Woodlands, TX with her husband Chad and two teenagers, Taggart and Mary-Cate.

speakers.name: Doug Way
speakers.job_title: GM West Gas and Power Trading
speakers.bio:
Doug Way brings over two decades of experience to his role as General Manager Trading at Shell Energy North America. Based in San Diego, CA, Doug oversees trading desks in Canada and the United States, focusing on natural gas and power trading, including energy, capacity, and environmental attribute products.

Doug's journey with Shell began in 2002 in Calgary, Canada, where he worked on various trade desks primarily focused on natural gas trading. In 2021, he relocated to the San Diego office, taking on responsibility for the gas and power trading desks. His role expanded in 2023 to include managing the North American real-time power trading team. Throughout his career, Doug has prioritized exposure management of various products to meet Shell's customer needs and has been dedicated to developing innovative solutions to help customers achieve their renewable energy goals.

speakers.name: Jay Cavalcanto
speakers.bio: Jay Cavalcanto is the SVP and CIO at Constellation, where he sets the strategic direction for technology, operations, cybersecurity, and the ongoing growth of the company’s digital platforms. In addition to leading the major initiative to separate Constellation from Exelon, a complex project involving the seamless migration of thousands of users and applications to a secure, modern environment with no technical debt, Jay has played a key role in overseeing multiple large-scale mergers and integrations. His leadership has been instrumental in guiding multi-year transformation projects, managing enterprise-wide technology upgrades, and orchestrating successful implementations of new platforms to support business growth.

speakers.name: John OBrien
speakers.bio: John is the Portfolio Manager for Data, Analytics, and AI at Shell Energy Americas. With 25+ years of experience, he specializes in transforming innovative data solutions into production realities. In 2022, he implemented the first Lakehouse at Shell Energy Trading, now ingesting 2500+ datasets from 60+ sources using both structured streaming and batch techniques. Business users create data products managed directly in Unity Catalog. John leverages Databricks and AI techniques to revolutionize data governance in production. He’s a passionate speaker, sharing his experiences and tips with the community.

speakers.name: Julien Debard

speakers.name: Shiv Trisal
speakers.bio: Shiv is responsible for worldwide adoption of Databricks in the manufacturing, transportation & energy sectors through new solutions, partnerships >TM programs that bring differentiated value to CxO priorities. Shiv has a proven track record of leading diverse teams and delivering game-changing data & AI-led innovation across Manufacturing and Transportation and Logistics industries, with roles at EY, Strategy& and Raytheon. He regularly connects with senior executives to unfold data & AI strategies and unlock competitive advantage in their businesses. Shiv majored in Electronics Engineering from the Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology in Punjab, India and holds a MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania.

sessions.title: Engineering the AI-Powered Practice: Scaling Vertical AI on a Foundation of Three Trillion Data Points
sessions.body:
The promise of digitization in healthcare has long been overshadowed by administrative toil, a landscape of "clicks and fragmentation" where 73% of physician office hours are spent away from patients. To address this, ModMed is building the "AI-Powered Practice," fueled by a clinical engine processing 3PB of data monthly, including three trillion data points. The AI-Powered Practice will bring powerful AI assistants to automate the entire medical practice including clinical, billing, front-office & patient engagement.

 

Learn how the Databricks Platform is supporting this end-to-end AI solution at massive scale: proprietary model training across 750M+ patient encounters and 2B+ diagnoses, plus low-latency production inference via Model Serving. Discover how ModMed, through purposeful collaboration with Databricks, is leading the charge in vertical AI in transforming healthcare operations, reducing provider burnout and elevating the human connection in medicine with visionary, cutting-edge AI.

speakers.name: Venkatesh Jayaraman
speakers.bio: Venk Jayaraman (VJ) serves as chief technology officer at ModMed, where he is responsible for providing strategic direction and technical leadership for the product engineering organization. VJ is a seasoned technology architect with over 30 years of experience driving high-stakes innovation. Today, he leads the charge in AI-powered transformation, moving beyond traditional software architecture to build intelligent, self-evolving systems. A pioneer in operationalizing Lean Agile practices at scale, VJ specializes in blending human ingenuity with machine intelligence to unlock business agility and growth. VJ holds a certificate from the Wharton Chief Technology Officer Program, a master’s degree in engineering management from the University of Florida, and a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from India’s National Institute of Technology.

sessions.title: Engineering Velocity Under Constraints: How Lakebase Database Branching Helped Us Deliver Faster in a Regulated Industry
sessions.body: In this session, HTEC shares how Lakebase Database Branching accelerated delivery of G2 Nimbus, a multi-year cloud transformation under strict PCI DSS constraints with parallel client migrations. We'll show how the database shifted from bottleneck to first-class SDLC citizen, enabling branch-per-feature work, safe schema evolution, and faster hotfixes without compromising compliance. You'll leave with concrete best practices and how to bring the same productivity gains to your own regulated, high-complexity programs.

sessions.title: Enterprise AI at Scale: Serving Google Gemini on Databricks for Production Workloads
sessions.body:
Foundation models are moving beyond chatbots and copilots into the core of enterprise data pipelines — enriching records, classifying documents, resolving entities, and powering agentic workflows at massive scale. This session shows how Google Gemini and Databricks are partnering to make this real for production enterprises today.

 

Google Cloud shows how Gemini is available as a first-party model on Databricks, served natively via ai_query() and Model Serving — with built-in governance via AI Gateway, including cost controls, rate limits, usage tracking, and Unity Catalog logging.

 

HG Insights then brings this to life with a production use case: a multi-stage AI pipeline processing 7 billion records where rules and custom BERT models handle the predictable cases, and Gemini acts as an agentic enrichment layer — autonomously reasoning over incomplete company profiles and resolving missing attributes across hundreds of millions of inference calls. Orchestrated by Lakeflow and monitored via AI/BI dashboards, this pipeline directly generates the revenue-critical datasets HG Insights delivers to Fortune 500 customers.

 

Whether you're enriching CRM data, building document classification pipelines, or deploying agentic data quality workflows, this session gives you the architecture patterns and lessons learned to run Gemini on Databricks at enterprise scale.

sessions.title: Enterprise Cost Management for Data Warehousing with Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: This session shows you how to gain visibility into your Databricks Lakehouse spend and ensure cost efficiency. Learn about the latest features for AI-driven insights into Lakehouse expenses so you can easily monitor and control your costs. Find out how to enable cost attribution to internal projects, improve performance and cost with agentic workload optimizations, and take advantage of intelligent compute and storage capabilities that do the tuning for you.

speakers.name: Jiabin Hu
speakers.bio: Tech-lead on DBSQL Warehouse Management

speakers.name: Joo Ho Yeo
speakers.bio: JooHo is a Product Manager on the Databricks SQL team, where he leads efforts to enhance warehouse management and monitoring for data platform admins. Prior to Databricks, he was a software engineer at Meta, building safe and scalable products. JooHo holds an MBA from Stanford and a B.S. in Computer Science from Cornell.

sessions.title: Enterprise Observability with ZeroBus and OTEL at Scale with Databricks
sessions.body:
OpenTelemetry has become the industry standard for collecting traces, metrics, and logs from modern distributed systems. However, operating observability platforms at enterprise scale often requires proprietary tools and fragmented data pipelines.

 

In this session, we present an end-to-end architecture for enterprise observability using OpenTelemetry and ZeroBus with Databricks as the analytics and visualization backbone. We will show how OpenTelemetry telemetry streams can be ingested through ZeroBus and stored in Delta Lake, enabling scalable processing and long-term retention of traces, metrics, and logs.

 

We will demonstrate how to build a custom Databricks App to visualize flame graphs, explore distributed traces, and correlate metrics and logs in a unified interface - delivering capabilities similar to proprietary platforms but powered by the Lakehouse.

speakers.name: Aleksandar Dragojevic
speakers.bio: Aleksandar is a Staff FDE at Databricks with more than a decade of software-engineering and technical-leadership experience. They specialize in architecting and delivering high-performance, scalable systems that remain elegant and easy to reason about. At Databricks, Aleksandar partners with enterprise customers worldwide to design, deploy, and operate cloud-native data platforms at massive scale, helping organizations unlock actionable insights and accelerate innovation.

sessions.title: Enterprise Reporting and Embedded Analytics with AI/BI Dashboards
sessions.body: Modern BI isn't just about ad hoc exploration—it's about delivering trusted data to internal teams and external users, wherever they work. Yet many organizations still rely on fragmented tools, leading to inconsistent metrics, duplicated data, and added cost.AI/BI Dashboards bring enterprise reporting and embedded analytics directly into the Databricks Platform—with no separate BI infrastructure and no licenses. From scheduled delivery to Slack and Teams to embedded dashboards and Genie experiences, teams can deliver governed insights at scale.We'll dive into how to design, deploy, and scale reporting and embedded analytics using AI/BI Dashboards and Genie. Topics include:- Production-ready reports with scheduling, parameterization, and consistent metrics- Embedding dashboards and Genie into internal tools and customer-facing apps- Governance, security, and performance at scale- Architectural patterns to scale reporting and embedding without duplicating data, logic, or cost

speakers.name: Maggie Li
speakers.bio: Maggie is an Associate Product Manager at Databricks.

sessions.title: Essential Ingredients to Successful Digital Data Transformation Program
sessions.body: GM Financial led a multi‑year data and AI transformation on Databricks, moving from traditional reporting to a modern analytics and GenAI‑enabled ecosystem guided by a clear enterprise vision. This session shares the people and process “recipe” behind that change: formal data governance and operating bodies, a data strategy board, stewardship practices, and communities of practice that increased literacy, trust, and SOX‑ready data. We will highlight the Databricks Center of Excellence—onboarding, study groups, certifications, office hours and best‑practice sharing—that accelerated adoption and improved CSAT/NPS. The talk also introduces AI/BI Genie—a Databricks chatbot that turns natural language into SQL over curated documentation, enabling governed self‑service analytics. Finally, we show how a Databricks‑centric FinOps framework gives pipeline‑to‑query cost visibility, enables show‑back of spend and drives continuous cost optimization without sacrificing agility.

speakers.name: Latha Subramanian
speakers.bio: Latha Subramanian is an experienced Leader specialized with 28+ years of specialization in AI/ML, Data, Analytics and Reporting domains in several industry verticals ranging from Healthcare, P&C and specialty Insurance, Financial Services, banking, multi-media publishing, technology, high tech industry, auto financing. Latha has led and successfully executed several multi-million-dollar data programs and is viewed as a trusted CXO advisor. She is a distinguished speaker at various CDO/CDAO summits. Latha is an Executive Board member of CDO Magazine. In her spare time, Latha loves traveling the world and spending time with her family.

sessions.title: Evolution of the Databricks Commercial Motion: Building Scalable Intelligence on Databricks
sessions.body: A truly "data-driven" enterprise requires close collaboration between Business and Data Science. In this session, we share our journey using Databricks to bridge the gap between technical complexity and operational reality.We detail our journey: We start by centralizing fragmented sources via Unity Catalog, surfacing descriptive trends via AiBi dashboards. We then move from descriptive to prescriptive insights, using Lakeflow orchestration to automate generation and understand causal effects. Then, we evolve from static insights to dynamic optimization, exemplified by a contract scoring system that helps sellers structure deals, built on MLflow and integrated with Salesforce. Finally, we explores how Databricks' AI products amplify the values of the previous stages.Attendees will learn to unify Databricks’ core capabilities, transitioning from high-level vision to a functional reality where AI and human strategy are woven together.

speakers.name: Jason Huang
speakers.bio:
Jason Huang is a Staff Data Scientist at Databricks. His recent work spans statistical methods and packages to quantify the impact of go-to-market motions, deal
scoring models guiding strategic deal-making, and pricing-model simulations for serverless and AI products. He partners closely with commercialization,
engineering, and product leadership to turn data into strategic decisions. Prior to Databricks, Jason worked on incentive design, pricing, and experimentation
at Uber and Robinhood after completing his Econ PhD.

speakers.name: Stephen Moss
speakers.bio:
Stephen Moss is Vice President of Business Incubation and Commercialization at Databricks. He leads the team responsible for bringing new products and capabilities to market and contributes to the company's broader product strategy. Stephen works closely with leaders across the company on the launch and growth of major new product lines and initiatives spanning data, analytics, AI, and apps.

Before Databricks, Stephen was a Partner at McKinsey & Company, where he advised technology companies on commercialization and go-to-market strategy. Earlier in his career, he held a senior commercial leadership role at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. He has a PhD in atomic physics from MIT.

sessions.title: Evolving Apache Spark Structured Streaming in Open Source: A Year in Review and the Road Ahead!
sessions.body: Apache Spark Structured Streaming has quickly become the foundational open-source technology for powering mission-critical streaming ingestion and ETL pipelines worldwide. The Spark 4.1 release introduces powerful updates, most notably a new Real-Time Mode that enables operational pipelines to process data with latencies in milliseconds, all within the Spark ecosystem. Stateful transformations have been significantly bolstered through TransformWithState and stream-stream join enhancements, offering broader coverage and higher performance. Furthermore, robust improvements—such as revamped locking and integrity verification—provide improved stability for stateful queries. Looking ahead to Spark 4.2, the roadmap includes state repartitioning, query evolution, hybrid sources, and other enhancements, further establishing Spark as the gold standard for all streaming workloads. Join us to explore these recent advancements and the exciting future of open-source Structured Streaming!

speakers.name: Anish Shrigondekar
speakers.bio: Anish is a Software Engineer at Databricks working on the core streaming team. Prior to joining Databricks, Anish has worked in other systems groups at Splunk Inc, and VMware, Inc. His areas of interest include operating systems, databases, storage, filesystems etc.

speakers.name: Jerry Peng
speakers.bio: Jerry Peng is currently an Staff Software Engineer at Databricks extensively working Apache Spark Structured Streaming. Before joining Databricks, he was a Principal Software Engineer at Splunk working on streaming and messaging projects especially with Apache Pulsar and Apache Flink. Jerry is a committer and PMC member of Apache Pulsar, Apache Storm, and Apache Heron projects. Before Splunk, he worked at Streamlio (acquired by Splunk), Citadel, and Yahoo on distributed systems and stream processing. Jerry has been working in the area of distributed systems and stream processing since his days in grad school at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.

sessions.title: Faster Queries in Local Laptop Mode for Apache Spark™
sessions.body: Apache Spark™ is optimized for distributed large-scale processing, but this architecture introduces significant overhead for small, local datasets — often making sub-100 MB queries take several seconds. In this talk, we present a suite of optimizations that dramatically improve Spark’s local-mode performance across three fronts: smarter query compilation and task scheduling that eliminates unnecessary shuffles, an Arrow-based df.cache implementation that cuts cache load and query times in half and a novel shuffle-free execution mode using Java virtual threads for lightweight in-process data transfer. We will walk through the design, benchmarks and engineering trade-offs of each approach, and show how together they position Apache Spark as a practical gateway engine from laptop-scale exploration to petabyte-scale production.

speakers.name: Daniel Tenedorio
speakers.bio: Daniel Tenedorio is a senior staff software engineer at Databricks, working on Spark Core and Spark SQL. He interacts with the Apache Spark™ open-source community to develop and review query processing features. Daniel has a breadth of experience in database systems development from building and launching features underpinning multiple major production services over time.

sessions.title: Faster, Leaner, and Easier to Debug: PySpark UDFs in 2026
sessions.body: PySpark has long provided one of the most powerful and flexible ways to bring Python logic to large-scale distributed data processing. In this talk, we focus on two major advances in the PySpark UDF ecosystem: performance optimizations and improved debuggability. First, we introduce Arrow-based execution for Python, including Native Arrow UDFs and Arrow UDTFs, which operate directly on columnar Arrow data without Pandas conversion overhead. This design reduces memory usage, improves support for complex types, and delivers faster execution compared to earlier Python UDF approaches. Second, we present new debuggability enhancements for Python running inside Spark tasks, including built-in faulthandler integration for clearer crash diagnostics and improved profiling support to better understand CPU and memory behavior of UDFs. Together, these improvements make PySpark UDFs not only faster and more scalable, but also significantly easier to diagnose and optimize in production environments.

sessions.title: Feature and ML Platform Powered by Databricks
sessions.body:
This presentation offers a comprehensive exploration of the Feature & Machine Learning Platform, focusing on its architectural design, essential components and seamless integration with Databricks. The platform harnesses Databricks for advanced feature engineering, structured streaming, declarative pipeline orchestration and end-to-end model training and serving, supporting both scheduled and event-driven workflows for maximum flexibility.

 

Key technologies highlighted include the DBX Feature Engineering SDK, Apache Spark Structured Streaming and Databricks Lakeflow jobs, all of which contribute to scalable, efficient data processing. Online feature computation is facilitated through the DBX Unity Catalog with Python UDFs, while Databricks Online Feature Stores powered by Lakebase enable real-time use cases. For batch feature consumption outside Databricks, managed Delta UniForm and Iceberg read-only feature tables provide robust solutions.

sessions.title: Financial Services Industry Forum
sessions.body:
Financial intelligence beats general intelligence. Trading books reprice in milliseconds, fraud patterns shift with every payment rail, and supervisors in your backyard are already asking how your models work, not if you use them. Generic AI can summarize the noise; it cannot safely move capital or satisfy regulators. Financial intelligence — built on unified, governed, and secure data — can.

 

At the Financial Services Forum, leaders from retail and community banks, asset managers, insurers and advisory firms will share how they are unifying data, deploying domain‑trained models and running agentic AI with firm governance controls. The result: AI decisions that are fast, explainable, audit‑ready and built on the unified intelligence only your data can provide.

speakers.name: Bobby Grubert
speakers.bio: Bobby Grubert is Head of AI and Digital Innovation at RBC Capital Markets, leading the firm’s development of the end-to-end AI and digital innovation strategy driving client value, revenue growth, & competitive advantage. He oversees the Centre of Expertise for Digital & AI Innovation, partnering across RBC to deliver measurable outcomes. Bobby is accountable for embedding AI-driven innovation across business lines to help RBC compete in a digital world. Previously, Bobby advanced the electronification of RBC’s Global Equities Markets and helped implement award-winning algorithmic trading platforms Thor & Aiden with RBC Borealis AI. Bobby is on the RBC CM Operating Committee, lectures at MIT Sloan, and serves as Chairman Emeritus of RMH-NY.

speakers.name: Michael Tran
speakers.job_title: Managing Director, Head of AI Product

sessions.title: Fireside Chat: A Candid Conversation on AI, Data Stacks and What Matters for the Next 24 Months
sessions.body:
Join us for a candid fireside chat with David Meyer, SVP of Product at Databricks and Josue Bogran, VP of Data + AI at zeb.co and Databricks MVP as we cut through the noise around AI, data stacks and enterprise transformation.

 

We’ll unpack what actually matters over the next 24 months: from real-world adoption trends to widespread misconceptions about Databricks and the modern data stack. No slides and no hype, just an honest, interview-style conversation shaped by community questions, grounded in what leading teams are doing today as well as insights from Databricks’ roadmap.

speakers.name: Josue Bogran
speakers.bio:
Josue Bogran is a Databricks MVP, product advisor, and VP of Data + AI Architecture at zeb.co, a Databricks and AWS partner with 1,500+ team members.

He’s had the privilege of learning from and interviewing Databricks leaders including Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, and Reynold Xin, and has helped shape several Databricks products behind the scenes.

Josue also advises product companies such as EnrollHere.com, a fully integrated platform for carriers and agencies.

He lives in North Carolina with his wife and five children, soon to be six. When not working on data and AI, you’ll find him on a pickleball court.

To check out my videos interviews and product demos with Databricks leaders:

sessions.title: Fireside Chat: No Hype, No Slides: The 24-Month Data and AI Decisions That Actually Matter
sessions.body: There is no shortage of AI predictions. There is a critical shortage of honest conversations about what enterprise leaders should actually do next. In this no-slides, no-hype fireside chat, Databricks SVP of Product David Meyer and zeb.co VP of Data + AI Architecture Josue Bogran — one of the most followed voices in the Databricks community — dissect what is genuinely changing in data stacks and enterprise AI adoption over the next 24 months. They'll surface the most persistent misconceptions leaders have about the modern data stack, reveal what separates organizations generating real returns from those still in experimentation mode, and share candid insight from Databricks' product roadmap. Questions are shaped by the community in advance. This is the session for leaders who want an unfiltered signal, not vendor positioning.

speakers.name: Dmitry Luchnik
speakers.bio:
I am a passionate Data & Analytics architect with extensive hands‑on experience of building and scaling enterprise data platforms. I have led the design and evolution of multiple analytics platforms, including serving as lead architect for a Lakehouse platform that enabled scalable, self‑service Data&AI applications. My work has been focused on making data work for everyone by removing bottlenecks and enabling analysts, data scientists, and engineers to focus on insights.

Today, as Director of Enterprise Architecture for Data & AI at adidas, I drive enterprise‑wide data and AI governance and the evolution of the technology landscape to ensure data becomes a true competitive advantage in a fast‑moving global company.

speakers.name: Niclas Schlautkoetter
speakers.bio:
With over 20 Years with SAP, Niclas Schlautkötter is an experienced business technology professional, specializing in hybrid data, analytics and AI architectures in large enterprises. In his long term consulting career he advised global SAP customers on their data strategy, designing complex, end-to-end IT system landscapes integrating SAP and non-sap technology and leading multi-year SAP implementation projects.

Now, Niclas serves as Global Head of Strategic Architecture Advisory for SAP Business Data Cloud leading a global team of Blackbelt IT architects. His team accelerates cloud transformation for SAP’s most strategic customers, helping them maximize the value of their data estates leveraging Business AI and acting as a critical bridge between SAP field organizations and product engineering, ensuring customer centricity remains at the core of SAP’s product development efforts.

sessions.title: First‑Class Containers Across Databricks: A Unified, Portable Dependency Management Strategy
sessions.body:
Databricks is bringing first‑class Docker support everywhere. This session shows how we’re making containers a core part of the Databricks developer experience, delivering faster startup, tighter governance, and clearer observability.

 

We’ll walk through the product architecture, the UX investments that reduce time‑to‑first‑result, and how we approach compatibility and safe rollout for critical workloads at scale.

speakers.name: Justin Breese
speakers.bio:
Justin is a Staff Product Manager at Databricks. He primarily focuses on their serverless products - versionless runtime, dependency management (environments), and containers.

When not thinking about execution engines, you can find him staying busy with soccer, hiking, brewing beer, roasting coffee, and older cars.

Justin lives in Topanga, CA with his wife, son, and daughter.

sessions.title: Flipping the Switch to Serverless: How McAfee Modernized Its Infrastructure and Halved Compute Costs
sessions.body:
At McAfee, we empowered 1,000+ end users and transformed our data platform — migrating over a third of production workloads to Databricks Serverless and unifying governance with Unity Catalog. Serverless compute put self-service analytics directly in users' hands, driving a 34% jump in monthly active users, a 30%+ lift in job efficiency, and $400K+ in projected annual savings — all delivered by a lean platform team. Our phased, data-driven migration playbook made adoption safe and reversible, using decision dashboards and clear revert-to-classic paths. To date, we've hit 65% infrastructure modernization — 90% of warehouses and 40% of jobs on Serverless.

In this session, we'll share how we governed workloads with Unity Catalog, selected high-impact migration candidates, overcame serverless limitations, and built the dashboards and tagging strategies that earned executive confidence. Attendees will leave with a proven blueprint to scale serverless adoption and unlock real value — increased velocity and reduced costs.

speakers.name: Amisha Singh
speakers.bio: Amisha Singh is a Delivery Solutions Architect at Databricks, where she works closely with High-Tech and Manufacturing enterprise customers to help drive technical success and turn big data ambitions into reality with the Lakehouse platform. Over the past three years, Amisha has helped customers design and scale solutions on Databricks, guiding them from onboarding to production success. She leverages her cloud architecture background and Databricks platform experience to empower customers on their data and AI journeys, focusing on delivering meaningful business outcomes through collaboration, trust, and shared success.

speakers.name: Mandar Pargunde
speakers.bio: Mandar is Director of Data Engineering at McAfee and he leads teams that power McAfee's cloud-native data platform on Databricks and AWS. His career path from cybersecurity operations to data engineering leadership gives him a rare lens on building platforms that are both performant and secure.

sessions.title: Forecasting at Databricks: One Framework Behind Consumption and Infra Cost
sessions.body: Consumption forecasting and infrastructure cost forecasting at Databricks share three challenges: trust and stakeholder adoption, model accuracy under hierarchy and outliers, and data signal quality. We addressed them on a unified Databricks-native stack. For trust and adoption: a self-serve human-in-the-loop Databricks App lets infra cost owners review recommended forecasts and inject inorganic shifts the model won’t see, while  AI/BI dashboards and Genie Spaces let users self-serve insights, and decomposition keeps consumption forecasts explainable. For model accuracy: Unified Forecasting Framework, the backend behind AI_Forecast() function scheduled on Lakeflow Jobs validates model selection across the hierarchies. For data and signal quality: Unity Catalog, Metric Views, and Lakeflow form the governed data backbone for cost forecasting and the feature-selection substrate for consumption. Attendees leave with Databricks-native patterns for forecasts domain owners self-serve and leadership defends.

speakers.name: Alex Wang
speakers.bio:
Alex Wang is a Sr. Data Scientist on the Infrastructure Data Science team at Databricks. He leads the development of scalable solutions for infra cost efficiency, with focus on planning and forecasting of cloud usages, unit price, and automated cost overage diagnostics.

Prior to Databricks, Alex was a Sr. Applied Scientist at Amazon, where he led internal cloud capacity planning that drove data center expansion decisions. He also worked as a Sr. Data Scientist at Lululemon, developing forecasting system that directed global shipment to retail stores.

Alex is passionate about building AI-native, human-in-the-loop solutions that bridge the gap between science and business to tackle real-world capacity planning and forecasting challenges.

sessions.title: Format Co-Evolution: How Iceberg v4 and Delta 5.0 Share a Unified Metadata
sessions.body:
For years, Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg co-evolved as parallel standards. That era is ending. This session goes deep on the technical “how” of this convergence. We first walk through Apache Iceberg v4’s adaptive metadata tree: what is changing in the redesign and how the new structure enables single-file commits to significantly accelerate performance.

 

We then cover how Delta Lake 5.0 adopts the Iceberg v4 metadata tree as its native content metadata. This produces a single on-disk structure that both Delta and Iceberg clients read and write directly. No translation layers, no conversion overhead. Just one format.

speakers.name: Anoop Johnson
speakers.bio: I work on data lake infrastructure at Databricks, focusing on Delta Lake and Iceberg.

speakers.name: Ryan Blue
speakers.bio: Ryan is the original co-creator of Apache Iceberg and spent the last decade working on big data infrastructure at Tabular, Netflix, Cloudera, and now Databricks. He is an ASF member and a committer in the Apache Parquet, Avro, Polaris, and Spark communities.

sessions.title: Fox One: Video Content Personalization Powered by GenAI
sessions.body:
*Copresenting with Fox.

 

When Fox introduced Fox One, its short-form video platform, we needed to deliver engaging recommendations at launch despite sparse, noisy engagement signals. Rather than waiting months for reliable data, we used GenAI to bootstrap personalization and guide early decision making under real-world constraints.

 

In this talk, we describe how we designed a modular, production-ready personalization system on Databricks that blends GenAI with classical machine learning and evolves as data matures. We will cover how we used Gemini to extract structure from video content, leveraged Databricks Functions to infer early preference signals, built millisecond-level video retrieval on Databricks Lakebase, and developed offline evaluation using GenAI to provide directional insight when traditional A/B testing was unreliable. Attendees will learn how we weaved GenAI into classical recommendation systems on the Databricks lakehouse to ship personalization under data constraints.

speakers.name: Nicole Catalino
speakers.bio: Nicole Catalino is a Staff Product Manager on the Emerging Technology team at FOX, leading AI- and data-driven products across news, sports, and entertainment. She builds multimodal platforms that transform video and text into intelligent, searchable systems powering both newsroom operations and consumer experiences. Her recent work includes launching FOX One's "Shorts," an autonomous pipeline that uses AI to detect topics, clip video, and deliver personalized short-form content in real time.

speakers.name: Rini Gupta
speakers.bio:
Rini Gupta is an AI Forward Deployed Engineer at Databricks, where she builds and deploys production-grade AI systems across a range of domains. Her work focuses on generative AI, and she specializes in integrating large language models with traditional machine learning and optimization techniques to solve complex, real-world problems.

Previously, she worked as a data scientist at C3.ai and Appian. She holds a master’s degree from UC Berkeley.

sessions.title: From "Hidden Costs" to "High Efficiency": Scaling DV's Lakehouse Observability
sessions.body:
A practical guide to the internal monitoring tools we built on Databricks System Tables to make our data platform more efficient and performant. Hear directly from our Data Platform Engineering team about what worked for us and what we learned along the way

 

We’ll dive into the backend strategies that transformed our platform, including:

  • Dashboards We Actually Look At: Tracking real costs and table/column sizes.
  • Practical Alerts for Real Problems: Identifying costly unused tables, tables with missing or excessive retention policies, long-running queries, and constantly failing jobs.
  • The "Orphan" Hunt: Programmatically identifying unreferenced files and un-vacuumed data by auditing Delta logs against cloud storage.
  • The Cost/Read Metric: Using recursive lineage queries to expose expensive, high-maintenance tables with little or no downstream value.
  • Footer Analysis: Scanning Parquet footers at scale to isolate metadata bloat from actual data —even in complex nested types.

speakers.name: Saul Tawil
speakers.bio:
30+ Years in the data management space

Spark Developer since its early introduction.

sessions.title: From 0 to 100: How One NASCAR Team Is Moving up the Grid With Databricks and Zerobus Ingest
sessions.body:
Trackhouse Racing set out to close a narrow competitive gap with a small team of 5 developers. In ~12 months, they went from no platform to a race-ready data and AI stack on Databricks — turning video, telemetry and race reports into decisions teams can act on in hours, not weeks.

 

In this session, Trackhouse will share the playbook and architecture behind three high-impact deliverables:

  • Pit crew performance: Dashboards paired with stop video to quantify where milliseconds are won/lost.
  • Unified race data foundation: Bringing in 25+ bespoke racing systems (timing/scoring, setup sheets, ECU logs, sim outputs — and “weird” sources) with repeatable patterns.
  • Race report intelligence: Enabling engineers and non-technical leaders to retrieve answers instantly.

 

Attendees will leave with a concrete “small team, fast wins” blueprint: how to prioritize the first data products, design reliable ingestion for messy sources and ship analytics and GenAI experiences that actually get used.

speakers.name: Chris Abele
speakers.bio: With over 15 years in the aerospace, automotive and motorsports industries, Chris brings wide ranging data analysis, applied mathematics, and software engineering experience to solve data driven problems at scale.

speakers.name: Nick Ragonese
speakers.bio: With over a decade of experience in data, Nick Ragonese has specialized in driving AI innovation for sports leagues and teams since joining Databricks in 2021.

sessions.title: From Agentic SIEM to Digital Twin: Lakehouse-Native Cybersecurity Red-Team Simulation
sessions.body: Modern security platforms collect massive telemetry but remain reactive. We present a Lakehouse-native cybersecurity Digital Twin architecture powered by an Agentic SIEM that transforms raw logs into simulation-ready intelligence.An AI-driven SIEM parses and normalizes heterogeneous security data into a governed Lakehouse schema. This structured foundation enables construction of a Digital Twin that models enterprise assets, identities, privileges, and network relationships directly from telemetry.AI agents then simulate realistic attack chains—privilege escalation, lateral movement, and credential harvesting—validating each step against Lakehouse-derived state. Instead of estimating risk from alerts, the system verifies exploitability with confidence scoring based on data coverage and fidelity.We demonstrate how the Lakehouse becomes an active simulation engine for measurable cyber risk validation, not just a passive data store.

speakers.name: Dennis Wen
speakers.bio: 20 year+ experience in Software and Cybersecurity industry, from service operations to DevOps and developer, and now product management—illustrates a relentless drive to bridge technical expertise with customer-centric innovation. With a proven track record of building products that solve pressing security challenges, Dennis continues to evolve, ensuring that every solution he deliver meets the demands of an ever-changing landscape.

speakers.name: Spark Tsao
speakers.bio: Spark is a highly experienced data scientist and storyteller at Trend Micro. Prior to joining Trend Micro, he worked with companies such as Intel and Sony Online Entertainment. Now he lead Trend Micro AILAB to find opportunities to make the world safer.

sessions.title: From App to App Ecosystem: An Operating Model for Thousands of Enterprise-Scale Databricks Apps
sessions.body: When you go from one AI app to a hundred, the bottleneck isn't building — it's governing. Who owns each app? Who manages costs, permissions, and networking? What breaks when a team goes rogue? This session lays out a practical operating model for enterprise-scale app deployment on Databricks: how to divide platform and team responsibilities, how to enforce governance without creating a bureaucratic chokepoint, and how to build an "app factory" foundation where identity, resources, and networking are standardized from day one. Whether you're managing five apps or five hundred, you'll leave with a clear framework for scaling without losing control.

sessions.title: From Bottlenecks to Breakthroughs: Empowering Comcast SLT with Self-Service Analytics
sessions.body: This initiative enables self-service analytics for Comcast’s Senior Leadership Team (SLT) by reducing IT dependency and establishing trusted “golden” KPIs. Using Databricks tools — AI/BI Dashboards, AgentBricks, Genie, and Apps — it provides intuitive interfaces for SLT users to explore data, generate insights, and build reports independently. The platform consolidates BI tools into a unified experience, accelerating insight generation and decision-making. Turnaround times improve from two weeks to about three days, delivering significant cost savings. Standardized KPIs reduce reliance on inconsistent ad hoc reporting, ensuring decisions are based on accurate, trusted data while improving efficiency and agility.

sessions.title: From Bowls to Bots: CAVA's Ask Astro Multi-Agent Supervisor on Databricks
sessions.body:
At CAVA, we serve Mediterranean bowls to millions of guests—and data insights to hundreds of employees. But getting those insights used to take hours of analyst time and SQL knowledge. Not anymore.

 

Meet Ask Astro: CAVA's production multi-agent supervisor that lets anyone ask any data question in plain English and get accurate answers in seconds. "What was our top-performing restaurant yesterday?" "Show me loyalty redemption rates by region." Ask Astro routes each question to the right specialized agent—finance, operations, customer analytics, HR, Jira, or the web—then synthesizes a unified answer.

 

In this session, you'll see how we built it:

  • Multi-agent orchestration: Why a supervisor pattern beats a single monolithic agent, and how we route questions across four Databricks Genie spaces, Atlassian APIs, and web search
  • Production guardrails: How we prevent hallucinations, block sensitive queries (compensation, PII), enforce content safety, and handle edge cases at scale
  • From prototype to production: The hard lessons from deploying in Databricks Apps and Slack—what broke, what we rebuilt, and how we earned trust with real users
  • Measuring success: Adoption metrics, time savings, and ROI beyond the demo
