  • Live demo: Watch Ask Astro answer real CAVA business questions in real-time, routing across multiple agents and data sources

 

You'll leave with:

  • A blueprint for building your own multi-agent supervisor
  • Prompt engineering and routing strategies that work in production
  • Guardrails and safety patterns for enterprise AI
  • A roadmap from "cool prototype" to "thousands of daily users"

 

Whether you're building your first agent or scaling your tenth, this session will show you how to turn bowls of data into bots that actually ship. And yes, the bot will be there to explain itself.

speakers.name: Matt McDonald
speakers.bio: Have worked for over a decade in the data space in various industries supporting data modernization at large scale.  Databricks user since 2018

speakers.name: Sudhakar Selvarajan
speakers.bio:
Sudhakar Selvarajan is a Senior Manager of Data & AI at CAVA, leading initiatives focused on modern data platforms, advanced analytics, and AI-driven innovation. With extensive experience in enterprise data architecture, Databricks, cloud technologies, and scalable analytics solutions, he helps organizations transform complex data ecosystems into strategic business assets.

He specializes in building high-performing data and AI teams, driving data modernization efforts, and enabling intelligent decision-making through scalable platforms and machine learning solutions.

sessions.title: From Classic ML to Agentic Predictions
sessions.body: How DealSumm evolved from one-shot model outputs to an orchestrated system that retrieves evidence, reasons with structure, and verifies every claim — without burning compute. If you have ever built ML for contract analytics, you know the pattern: you ship a model that looks great on a benchmark, then reality shows up — one client has a different template, another uses a jurisdiction-specific term, and a third buries the key clause in an amendment scanned in 2008. At DealSumm, our goal is not just prediction — it is turning messy commercial lease documents into trustworthy, referenced data that teams can review, analyze, and act on inside a single AI-ready platform. The problem is that lease abstraction is not a single prediction problem — it is a chain of dependent mini-decisions: find the right clause, interpret it in context, map it into a client schema, and then prove you did not hallucinate.

speakers.name: Jonathan Bauman
speakers.bio: Jonathan Bauman is the CTO of DealSumm, where he leads technology strategy, R&D, and AI-driven product innovation for enterprise lease abstraction and document intelligence. He builds scalable systems that transform complex commercial real estate documents into trusted, actionable data for global organizations. With leadership experience across proptech, fintech, and digital insurance, Jonathan has managed teams across R&D, product, IT, DevOps, architecture, and automation. He has led digitization initiatives, SaaS platforms, APIs, microservices, and data-driven systems that improved efficiency, performance, and business outcomes. His work combines AI, legal data, real estate operations, and enterprise execution.

sessions.title: From Cost Mystery to Cost Mastery COPA Airlines Journey to Lakehouse Efficiency
sessions.body:
In an industry where profit margins are razor-thin and operational variables are global, COPA Airlines has emerged as a "shining star" of financial prosperity. By maintaining the world’s third strongest operating margin and leading the industry in on-time performance, COPA faced a high-stakes challenge: How do you scale world-class operations without exponential data costs?

 

This presentation reveals the "Global Masterclass" in transitioning from legacy data silos to high-velocity lakehouse architecture.

speakers.name: David Garcia
speakers.bio: David Garcia is a versatile leader with over 20 years of experience, currently serving as the Director of Software and Data Engineering at Copa Airlines. He has deep expertise in modernizing data platforms and working with public cloud providers like Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Databricks. David has led and mentored teams of 60+ members across multiple countries, driving large-scale cloud migration, implementing DevOps CI/CD practices, and transforming legacy applications into microservices-based architectures. His achievements include creating a mobile center of competence, deploying omnichannel service layers, and modernizing big data architectures for real-time analytics.

sessions.title: From Dashboards to Data Products: MBC Shahid's App-Driven Revolution
sessions.body:
MBC Shahid, the world’s leading Arabic streaming service serving tens of millions of users, has evolved beyond static dashboards to a curated Data Product culture. In this session, discover how we leveraged Databricks Apps, Model Serving and Unity Catalog to operationalize AI for non-technical teams.

 

We will showcase two game-changing internal apps: “Enigma,” which empowers media buyers and leadership teams with predictive show performance, an actionable, interactive real-time voice of the customer and sentiment analysis experience, and a GenAI social media tool that automates viral reel creation by identifying high-impact frames and flagging sensitive content. Join us to learn how adopting a serverless, app-driven architecture is saving thousands of hours, merging the worlds of traditional tabular data, clickstream events, qualitative customer feedback and video data, all on Databricks Lakehouse, while ensuring governance, and delivering massive business value in record time.

speakers.name: Phillip Badenhorst
speakers.job_title: Director of Data, AI and Strategy
speakers.bio:
Accomplished data and AI leader with expertise in AI product development, data platforms, software engineering, governance, and business strategy. Proven track record building high-performing teams and scalable AI/data platforms leveraging data from consumer applications serving 30M+ MAUs.

Experienced delivering AI-driven products, intelligent data applications, and large-scale data ecosystems that enhance consumer experiences, operational efficiency, and business growth. Passionate about nurturing talent, fostering innovation, and aligning AI and data strategies with measurable business outcomes through practical deployment of AI at scale.

sessions.title: From Dashboards to Decisioning: How We Rebuilt Marketing
sessions.body:
Every enterprise marketing organization is trying to escape the same trap: fragmented data, backward-looking reporting, and AI pilots that never make it into daily operations. At Databricks, we decided not to layer AI on top of a broken foundation — we rebuilt the foundation first.

 

In this session, we’ll walk through our end-to-end transformation from descriptive analytics to AI-driven insight and activation, powered entirely by the Lakehouse. We’ll show how consolidating marketing signals into a governed, scalable data architecture unlocked a new operating model: real-time intelligence accessible to non-technical marketers, AI-assisted decisioning embedded in workflows, and closed-loop activation across our CDP.

 

We'll talk about the vision, what worked, what broke, and what changed in how marketing teams plan, execute, and measure impact.

sessions.title: From Data Platform to App Platform: Building Production Apps on Lakebase
sessions.body: Your Lakehouse handles analytics beautifully. But the moment someone needs low-latency reads, transactional writes, or an app serving layer, you're stitching together external databases and sync pipelines. Lakebase offers a different path — this session shows you how to build on it.A Databricks MVP will walk through practical patterns for building production apps where Lakebase serves as the operational layer, fully integrated with Unity Catalog governance and Lakehouse analytics. We'll cover architecture patterns, the interplay between Lakebase and Databricks Apps, latency and scaling considerations, and the honest gaps practitioners need to plan around.You'll leave with architecture patterns, design decisions, and a realistic assessment of production readiness.

speakers.name: Doug MacWilliams
speakers.bio:
Doug MacWilliams is a director in the Data Engineering and Analytics practice at West Monroe, a management technology consulting company. Doug has a passion for designing and building data solutions at the intersection of business and technology. He architects solutions that unlock data and deliver the needed insights in a pragmatic approach, optimized for long term maintenance and client skill sets. With his business background he understands what insights business leaders want and how to model data to represent the business process. Doug has a proven track record delivering many successful projects and leads teams focused on enterprise data strategies, building data platforms and analytics. He is a thought leader in data fabric methodology.
Doug received his undergrad at University of Colorado in Business Operations and started his career in custom manufacturing and furniture making. He pivoted and moved into technology and data with a master’s in computer science focused on Computer Vision from DePaul University 15 years ago. He then worked in telecom and boutique BI consulting company before joining West Monroe 8+ years ago.
Doug has had the opportunity to travel extensively around the world, especially during his Semester at Sea in college, and lived abroad after college. He now resides with his family in the Chicago Suburbs. He is a mentor through his alumni program and volunteers in his local community.

https://www.westmonroe.com/our-team/doug-macwilliams

sessions.title: From Data Silos to Patient 360: Building Real-Time Cohort Analytics With Zero-ETL Graph Technology
sessions.body:
Healthcare organizations generate 50+ petabytes annually, yet 80% remains siloed. This session demonstrates how PuppyGraph's zero-ETL graph layer transforms fragmented Databricks lakehouse data into unified patient 360 views without moving a single byte.

 

The challenge: Identifying high-risk patients requires complex 50+ line SQL queries—slow and inaccessible.

 

The solution: Graph technology excels at entity resolution. By linking attributes (addresses, providers) into networks, it matches records like "John A. Smith" and "J. Smith" through relationship patterns. We’ll compare traditional SQL joins against five-line graph traversals following the patient journey: Patient → Condition → Visit → Prescription.

 

Graph queries mirror clinical thinking—connected journeys, not isolated tables.

 

Key takeaways:

  • Zero-ETL graph analytics on lakehouse data
  • Integrating AI agent-ready graph infrastructure
  • Unified governance through Unity Catalog

sessions.title: From Data to AI: Securing the Modern Attack Surface
sessions.body:
GenAI is reshaping the attack surface — from cloud infrastructure to a layered ecosystem of data, models and applications. As organizations build on platforms like Databricks, data becomes both the foundation of AI innovation and the primary source of risk.

 

This session explores how to secure AI applications end-to-end across infrastructure, data, models, guardrails and runtime. Attendees will gain a clear framework for understanding AI risk across the full lifecycle and see how visibility into systems like Unity Catalog help teams understand data exposure, model usage and emerging risks across the AI lifecycle.

 

Finally, we’ll show how Wiz integrates with Databricks to bridge security and data teams — surfacing insights, identifying risks and enabling a unified approach to securing AI from code to runtime. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to reduce AI risk without slowing down development.

speakers.name: Jiong Liu
speakers.bio: Jiong Liu leads the product marketing team for Wiz and is responsible for product GTM strategy and cross-functional execution. She loves working closely with customers to securely accelerate their cloud and AI journeys. Before that, Jiong led the GTM strategy and product marketing team for Okta's customer identity products and Business Value practice. Jiong holds bachelor’s degrees in Economics and Interdisciplinary Studies from the University of California, Berkeley, and an MBA from the University of Pennsylvania, Wharton School.

sessions.title: From Data to Decisions: how Quest's Automated Data Product Factory Accelerates Value on Databricks
sessions.body: Every data leader is being asked some variant of the same question: Where's the value? Databricks gives organizations a powerful foundation, but the gap between raw data and trusted, decision-ready data products can be where time, cost and credibility are lost. In this session, Quest Software will showcase that Automated Data Product Factory, purpose-built to help Databricks customers close that gap. We'll show how organizations are compressing data product delivery from months to days, reducing manual effort and putting governed, trustworthy data into the hands of the business faster than ever. Attendees will see how the Factory accelerates time-to-insight, lowers the cost of scaling data product delivery and builds the trust that drives adoption (all while extending the value of extending Databricks and Unity Catalog investments). You will leave with a clear view of how an automated, outcome-focused approach turns your Databricks investment into a faster engine for business results.

sessions.title: From Day-Old Data to Real-Time Retail: Modernizing CDC With Spark Declarative Pipelines and Lakeflow
sessions.body:
Retail operations depend on accurate, timely data, but many organizations still rely on legacy change data capture approaches that behave like batch pipelines, creating delays, data inconsistencies, and operational risk.

 

In this session, we share our real-world journey modernizing ingestion from a retail depot management platform.

 

We will discuss the successes and pitfalls, and how we crafted and curated our new solution iteratively, with the use of new Databricks functionality such as AutoCDC and Lakeflow Connect. Transforming our complicated, cumbersome legacy solution into a streamlined and scalable workflow.

speakers.name: Marius-Cristian Panga
speakers.bio: Solutions Architect at Databricks with considerable experience in business intelligence, data warehousing, and data engineering. Deeply committed to exploring the potential of data and technology to tackle real-world issues.

speakers.name: cassidy louch
speakers.bio:
Since starting data engineering in 2020, my passion for engineering multiplied over time!
Specialising in the retail sector, I have worked at 2 of the UK's top food and life services providers.

sessions.title: From Eight Hours to Eight Minutes: Automating A/B Test Analysis on Databricks
sessions.body: Mobile game studios run multiple experiments simultaneously, but daily insights are often delayed by manual data preparation, inconsistent methods and ad hoc notebooks. This presentation shows how SEGA HARDlight migrated from Tableau to Databricks and built an automated framework for experiment analysis. It ingests definitions and telemetry, applies uniform statistical models and publishes a daily dashboard with an LLM-generated summary and KPI diagnostics. Unity Catalog manages assets and lineage, while Lakeflow streamlines pipelines. MLflow ensures consistent experiment tracking, and AI/BI dashboards with Genie enable natural language exploration. The dashboard locks in results and decisions, creating an auditable record of truth. Early estimates show over eight hours saved weekly for the data team and roughly half a day saved per new query through automation, aiming to double testing capacity — while also boosting trust and consistency across experiments.

speakers.name: Joel Dias
speakers.bio:
Joel Dias is a Senior Data Scientist at SEGA HARDlight, where he builds scalable analytics systems for live mobile games. He specialises in automating complex data workflows, combining statistical methods with modern AI to accelerate decision-making across product, live operations, monetization and user acquisition functions.

Joel has led the development of Databricks-based analytics and experimentation frameworks that reduce analysis time from hours to minutes, alongside LLM-powered insights and self-service tools that make data accessible beyond technical teams.

At Data + AI Summit 2026, he shares how automation and AI can transform A/B testing into a fast, reliable, and scalable decision engine.

speakers.name: Sanjay Ashok
speakers.bio: Sanjay Ashok is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, acting as a technical advisor to digital-native and emerging enterprises across EMEA. He assists customers in evaluating, adopting, and scaling the Lakehouse platform for production AI and analytics workloads. With over 10 years’ experience in AI/ML, big data, and cloud architecture, he has worked across the US, India, and the UK, including at AWS, developing cloud-native data and ML solutions. At Databricks, he guides organisations from technical strategy to data-driven business transformation in gaming and fintech. His work covers GenAI applications, ML pipelines, real-time analytics, and self-serve BI dashboards. He holds an MS from the University at Buffalo.

sessions.title: From Factory Floor to AI-Ready: Building Industrial Data Pipelines for Databricks
sessions.body: Industrial data is unlike other data. Industrial companies across manufacturing, energy, lifesciences, and logistics run on PLCs, SCADA, historians, MES, inspection systems, AGVs, and more.This data is more raw and harder to work with than IT data. Standard ELT pipelines move thisproblem downstream rather than solving it. As industrial companies race to adopt AI, thisproblem is amplified further.Industrial DataOps addresses this by contextualizing and modeling data at the source, producingAI-ready data products that arrive at Bronze ready to progress through the medallionarchitecture.Gousto, a UK meal-kit manufacturer, put this into practice with HighByte, AWS, and Databricks.Their Unified Namespace and Lakehouse became the foundation for automated fault detection,ML-driven predictive maintenance, and digital twins, driving 98% equipment availability, a 10%throughput gain, and 5x more recipes.Learn how to unlock the value of your industrial data with Databricks.

speakers.name: Jeffrey Schroeder
speakers.bio: Jeffrey Schroeder is Director of Product Management at HighByte, focused on guiding the company’s product strategy. His areas of responsibility include market research, product positioning, product roadmap, and ecosystem integration strategy. Jeffrey is an experienced technologist who brings more than a decade in technology leadership roles in the automotive and discrete manufacturing industries to his role at HighByte, offering deep domain expertise and perspectives on information technology, operations, and management for industrial organizations.

sessions.title: From Fragmented Data To AI-Driven Portfolio Impact With Digital Operations
sessions.body: Years of inorganic growth left TK Elevator (TKE) with data silos, inconsistent KPIs and limited ability to steer its services. By consolidating IoT, operational and financial data on a governed Azure Databricks Intelligence Platform — aligning enterprise semantics through the CDP Nexus program — TKE created a single, trusted data foundation from board to field ops. Medallion architecture ensures reliability and reuse, while Unity Catalog provides governance. On this foundation, TKE extended the same semantics and controls to unstructured data such as contracts and service logs, using LLMs to extract risks, obligations and renewal signals. Intelligent agents combine contract insights with operational performance data to support portfolio decisions with human‑in‑the‑loop validation. This session shows how Digital Ops, standardized KPIs and AI‑ready data products leveraging Genie enabled productivity gains and faster, more consistent decisions, setting context for the Session B deep dive.

speakers.name: Matthias Gohl
speakers.bio:
09/2023- today: CDO TK Elevator
2017-2022: Global Head of ZEISS Digital Innovation Partners
2014-2016: Global Head of Strategy and M+A ZEISS Group
2007-2014: McKinsey & Company
2005-2007: German Ministry for the Environment (BMU)

sessions.title: From Fresh Data to Big Impact: Afresh and Lakebase Fuel Retail Innovation
sessions.body:
In grocery retail, every hour on the shelf raises spoilage and margin risk. Afresh combats this with data-driven inventory insights delivered directly to fresh department order writers. But running these workloads on standard PostgreSQL caused contention, table locks, ETL failures and heavy maintenance, limiting innovation.

 

This session details how Afresh migrated its mission-critical Postgres instance to Databricks Lakebase—a fully managed, serverless PostgreSQL engine natively integrated with the Databricks Lakehouse. Using Lakebase’s separation of storage and compute, Afresh eliminated locking and scaling bottlenecks. By orchestrating DBSQL http_request pipelines in dbt, Afresh replaced custom sync frameworks with automated, bidirectional data flows, cutting overhead and boosting reliability.

 

Attendees will learn:

  • How to migrate from self‑managed OLTP to serverless Lakebase
  • Performance and reliability strategies
  • Ways streamlined architecture drives efficiency and innovation

speakers.name: Erin Leonhard Zhang
speakers.bio: Erin Leonhard Zhang leads data foundations engineering at Afresh, where ML-driven demand forecasting helps grocery retailers cut food waste at scale. She architected and drove Afresh's migration from Azure Postgres to Databricks Lakebase, running the technical evaluation, facilitating the go/no-go decision with 20+ engineering stakeholders, and executing a production rollout that eliminated custom sync code and unlocked self-service data access across the org. A full-stack engineer who gravitates toward data architecture and platform problems, Erin has spent 4+ years as Afresh's primary technical authority on data sync patterns and pipeline design, including leading the company's reverse ETL cutover from Snowflake to Databricks.

sessions.title: From Governed Data to Operational Decisions: A Customer Playbook for Databricks and Palantir
sessions.body: In this session, Rich Products shares how we use Databricks and Palantir together to move from governed enterprise data to operational business outcomes. We will walk through the architecture playbook our platform team uses to decide where data lives, where logic runs, and when validated outputs should be written back for broader downstream consumption.As a real example, we will show how we replaced a legacy cost allocation process tied to SAP ECC with a new production workflow that uses Databricks as the governed data foundation, Foundry for allocation logic and operational review, and Databricks again as the publication layer for downstream finance processes. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for balancing speed, scale, and safety across joint-platform solutions without overspecializing to a single use case.

speakers.name: Brandon Lyles
speakers.bio:
Brandon Lyles leads Data & AI Platforms on the Enterprise Data and Analytics Team at Rich Products, a Global Family Owned Food Company in Buffalo, NY. With over 6 years at Rich’s, Brandon is helping shape the company’s enterprise AI strategy - focusing on scalable data and AI platforms, and practical innovation that delivers business impact.

Brandon is passionate about turning complex challenges into solutions that drive value creation, drawing from a background that blends technology, creativity and strategic thinking. Outside of work, he enjoys spending time with his two children, playing guitar & piano and cheering on his hometown team as a die-hard Buffalo Bills fan.

sessions.title: From Job Clusters to DBSQL Serverless: How GetYourGuide Improved DBT Pipelines
sessions.body:
At GetYourGuide, we used to run ETL transformations with an internal tool called Rivulus on top of Databricks job clusters. When we standardized on dbt-databricks, we migrated these workloads to DBSQL Serverless and had to rethink how we design and operate our pipelines. We'll walk you through what changed and what we wished to know before we started.

 

What changed for us:

  • Pipelines run ~60% faster and costs dropped ~20%
  • Time to production for new models went from days to minutes, backfills from weeks to hours
  • ~4 months of annual overhead from DBR version upgrades disappeared
  • 100% of our core models are now automatically documented with AI
  • Finance and marketplace teams now rely on fresher data with less friction

 

Attendees will leave with:

  • A clear view of how the migration to DBSQL Serverless was performed
  • How we turned curve balls into wins along the way
  • Concrete steps to apply similar ideas in their own dbt-databricks setups, including using ai_query for automated model documentation

speakers.name: Giovanni Corsetti Silva
speakers.bio:
Giovanni Corsetti is a Data Engineer at GetYourGuide, where he focuses on building and evolving large-scale data platform foundations, with a strong emphasis on reliability, scalability, and data governance, including GDPR-related challenges in Europe. As a GetYourGuide user himself, he has explored dozens of countries, giving him a personal connection to the product he helps build.
He is also an active contributor to open-source projects, with a strong interest in building and sharing practical, scalable data tooling with the broader engineering community.

sessions.title: From Lakehouse to Production App: Building Governed AI Apps with Replit + Databricks
sessions.body: Enterprise teams are sitting on years of valuable lakehouse data, but building apps to act on that data has always required scarce engineering resources and weeks of lead time. Replit and Databricks have changed that. With Replit's AI-powered development environment and Databricks AppKit, any team can go from a plain-language prompt to a production-ready app running natively on Databricks Apps, inheriting Unity Catalog governance, enterprise authentication, and observability out of the box. In this session, we'll share how enterprise teams are using this integration to put their Databricks data to work: building revenue scenario tools for sales teams, real-time ops dashboards, and AI-powered internal companions, without waiting on engineering. You'll leave with a clear view of the Replit + Databricks Apps architecture, a live demo of the full build-and-deploy flow, and concrete patterns for rolling this out in your organization.

speakers.name: Axel Torbenson
speakers.bio: Axel is a Field Engineer at Replit, where he helps enterprise customers build production-ready apps on top of their data infrastructure. Axel has been at the forefront of Replit's integration with Databricks since its launch in February 2026, helping enterprises go from idea to governed, production-ready data apps without requiring a traditional development team. He works with customers across financial services, consulting, logistics, and technology to roll out the Replit + Databricks Apps workflow. Prior to Replit, Axel was a data science and AI engineering consultant, where he helped enterprises operationalize ML and AI on modern data platforms. He is based in Foster City, California.

sessions.title: From Legacy Bottlenecks to High-Performance Platforms—Databricks Makes It Possible
sessions.body: Do you want to modernize your data processes by moving from on‑prem to Cloud Databricks? At 84.51°, we leveraged Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines to build dimension and fact tables, used Delta Lake and Unity Catalog for data reliability, and applied Databricks Asset Bundles and workflows to create a cost‑efficient, scalable end‑to‑end system.This migration enables teams to work with health data to support our mission to improve patient outcomes through same‑day, personalized engagement with at‑risk or high‑value patients. The solution processes ~40 tables and millions of daily rows, supporting append logic, SCD Type 2 handling, and identity columns.Join us to learn how 84.51° applied SDPs, DABs, Delta Lake, and Unity Catalog to successfully migrate from legacy systems.84.51° is a retail insights, media, and marketing company using first‑party data from 60M households to drive Kroger’s customer‑centric journey.

speakers.name: Alex Yan
speakers.bio: Data Engineer at 84.51º for almost a year and a half! Graduated from Purdue prior.

speakers.name: Piu Mallick
speakers.bio: Senior Data Engineer @ 84.51

sessions.title: From Molecule to Market: How Life Sciences Companies are Compressing the Data-to-Decision Curve with Databricks
sessions.body: The life sciences industry sits at an extraordinary inflection point. The same AI capabilities that are reshaping drug discovery are now being applied to clinical trial design, real-world evidence generation, digital twin simulation and commercial launch strategy — and the organizations moving fastest are those who've unified these workloads on a single data intelligence platform. In this session, we take a sweeping look at how Databricks is powering the full life sciences value chain: accelerating target identification and molecular screening in R&D, enabling adaptive trial designs with richer patient data, building synthetic cohorts and digital twins that reduce time and cost, and equipping commercial teams with the AI-driven insights needed to reach the right patients faster. We'll explore the common thread running through each of these use cases — a governed, interoperable data foundation — and make the case that the most durable competitive advantage in life sciences today is not any single model or dataset, but the platform on which all of them live.

speakers.name: Raman Singh
speakers.job_title: Head of Enterprise Data Platforms & Srvs

sessions.title: From Oracle Cloud to a Governed Lakehouse: Real-Time Streaming With Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
Flutter SEA invested heavily in OCI, but platform limits—high costs, low observability and operational complexity—became blockers for real‑time engagement, event processing and fast delivery. The previous Spark Structured Streaming architecture used custom code with minimal monitoring, no standardized data quality and limited governance, causing slow iteration and high maintenance.

 

This session shares the migration to a governed, observable Databricks Lakehouse using Spark Declarative Pipelines and Delta Lake, built by a “triforce” team: Flutter SEA, Databricks PS and Reply. We’ll cover architectural choices like single‑plex vs. multi‑plex pipelines and their impact on scalability, cost and simplicity, plus data quality, end‑to‑end monitoring, KPIs - 40% savings and 96% bronze-to-silver performance improvements, lessons learned and best practices for modernizing streaming systems to reduce cost, improve governance and enable AI‑driven real‑time engagement.

speakers.name: Andrea Santurbano
speakers.bio:
I’m a Resident Solution Architect at Databricks with expertise in designing large-scale, enterprise-grade data systems and software development.
Previously, I developed the national e-prescription system for the veterinary domain for the Italian Ministry of Health with the goal of fighting antibiotic resistance.
Additional interests:
- Passionate about CrossFit.
- I enjoy making pizza from scratch.
- I love making Japanese cuisine, especially ramen!

speakers.name: Francesco Milone
speakers.bio: Francesco Milone is a data and technology leader with over a decade of experience in driving complex data transformation programmes in fast-paced, regulated environments. He is currently the Data Lakehouse & Transformation Senior Manager at Flutter Southern Europe & Africa and has a proven track record in designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, covering everything from architecture to governance, data quality, cataloguing, lineage and privacy compliance.

sessions.title: From Petabytes to Proactive Defense: Powering an AI Swarm With Databricks
sessions.body:
As AI accelerates cyber offense in a post-Mythos world, the constraint in security operations is no longer data — it’s the speed of the OODA loop. At Arctic Wolf, we process trillions of events daily across 10,000+ organizations, where delayed access to data means delayed defence.

 

We re-architected our platform on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform — combining Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Liquid Clustering, and AI/Genie — to enable real-time, agentic security operations at petabyte scale. Liquid Clustering and Predictive Optimization eliminated data skew and costly acceleration layers, reducing file counts by 50%, improving freshness from hours to minutes, and accelerating 90-day queries by up to 8× (51 seconds to 6.6 seconds).

 

Architecture: Multi-PB Delta Lake → Liquid Clustering + Predictive Optimization → GOLD telemetry → Genie-orchestrated Swarm of Experts.Outcomes: Sub-second to seconds-level queries, 10–100x alert reduction, >70% precision gains, and earlier detection of cross-tenant attack campaigns.

 

Attendees will learn how to unify data and AI to compress the OODA loop, power agentic workflows and transform petabyte-scale telemetry into proactive defence.

speakers.name: Justin Lai
speakers.bio: Justin Lai is a Data Architect at Arctic Wolf, where he designs scalable data and AI platforms to support cybersecurity operations and analytics. He works with engineering, product, and data teams to build systems that power the Arctic Wolf Data Lake, enabling efficient access for both analytics and AI use cases. With a background in cloud infrastructure and deep expertise in Databricks, Justin focuses on building production-grade solutions that support real-time processing, machine learning workflows, and AI model deployment. He has spent the past five years helping teams implement end-to-end data and AI architectures with an emphasis on scalability, performance, and reliability.

speakers.name: Rajneesh Arora
speakers.bio: Rajneesh Arora is a Senior Delivery Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he works with customers across industries to accelerate their data and AI transformation journeys and unlock successful paths to production on the Databricks platform. He holds an M.Tech degree in Information Technology from the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee, India.

sessions.title: From Power BI DAX to Metric View KPIs: How Mercedes-Benz Korea Built “Talk to Your Data” at Scale
sessions.body: Mercedes‑Benz Korea runs its business on a rich set of sales and steering KPIs maintained in Power BI semantic models and a central Master KPI catalog. Over time, this BI‑centric implementation made it hard to reuse KPI logic for new AI experiences and across platforms. To enable “Talk to Your Data” on top of governed KPIs, Mercedes‑Benz Korea partnered with Databricks to move KPI logic into the Databricks Lakehouse and Unity Catalog. In this session, we show how we developed an automated DAX‑to‑SQL transpiler that converts existing DAX measures into Unity Catalog Metric Views, while preserving semantic parity with legacy reports. We’ll walk through the architecture, how we use the Master KPI List as the semantic contract, and how we tuned Databricks Genie with KPI‑aware metadata and instructions. Finally, we’ll share lessons from making AI agents production‑ready—from handling complex DAX patterns to rolling out self‑service “talk to your KPIs” capabilities across markets.

speakers.name: Fares Kamal
speakers.job_title: Chief Data & AI Officer, MB Korea
speakers.bio: Fares Kamal is the Chief Information Officer at Mercedes-Benz Korea and Mercedes-Benz Group Services Philippines, beginning in November 2020, where the focus is on transforming legacy IT into agile, product-oriented teams to enhance business value. Prior to this role, Fares Kamal held various leadership positions at Mercedes-Benz AG from April 2014 to October 2020, including team lead for IT in retail, where significant contributions included standardizing global IT governance and introducing monetization strategies. Previous experience includes managing major transformation programs in the Russian market, overseeing the international rollout of wholesale systems in Europe, and driving strategic IT projects in Eastern Europe, demonstrating a strong commitment to innovation and operational excellence throughout a career with Mercedes-Benz that began in 2003.

speakers.name: Sai Yang
speakers.bio: Sai Yang is a Solutions Architect for the Automotive Manufacturing sector at Databricks. With 6 years of experience in the data & AI domain, Sai has strong expertise in Data Science, Machine Learning, AI, and Data Governance. At Databricks, he has led multiple large-scale platform migration projects and AI use cases for global leading automotive companies. These initiatives enabled the organizations to build and implement scalable analytics and AI solutions with unified governance on Databricks, helping them become the industry leaders in data and AI. Before joining Databricks, Sai worked in technology consulting, where he designed, developed, and deployed reliable machine learning systems in production for Fortune Global 500 companies.

sessions.title: From Prompt to Production: Vibe Coding an App with Genie Code
sessions.body: This course explores how AI-assisted development can accelerate the journey from concept to functional application. In this hands-on lab, participants will use Databricks Genie Code to transform plain-language ideas into a working Databricks App, then iteratively refine that app by identifying issues, improving prompts, and applying production-oriented best practices. Along the way, attendees will examine common pitfalls in AI-generated code, understand how prompt quality impacts outcomes, and develop practical strategies for creating more accurate, reliable, and enterprise-ready applications. Ideal for developers, architects, and technical professionals looking to harness generative AI as a meaningful part of the modern software development lifecycle.

sessions.title: From Raw Signals to Real-Time Insights: Building an End-to-End IoT Pipeline With Zerobus
sessions.body: In the world of IoT, every additional hop in your data pipeline is a tax on speed, a risk to governance and a driver of unnecessary cost. To solve this problem, we developed DataLink, an internal use wireless data collection platform that streams high fidelity data directly into Unity Catalog at near real-time speeds. With Zerobus, we built an IoT ingestion pipeline that delivers fast access and robust governance at a fraction of the traditional cost and complexity. This architecture transforms raw lab data from across the globe into structured insights in near real time. In this presentation, we will take a deep dive into our architectural strategy for connecting IoT devices to Zerobus endpoints and setting up ingestion. We will also discuss how we leveraged alerts, dashboards, and automated failure analysis to streamline workflows for engineering teams. Finally, we will walk through a live demo showcasing the end-to-end pipeline from data generation to consumption.

speakers.name: Kirat Mokha
speakers.bio: Kirat Mokha is a Machine Learning Engineer on Milwaukee Tool’s Analytics, Algorithms, and AI Applications (AAA) team. He earned his bachelor’s in Electrical Engineering and master’s in Machine Learning from Milwaukee School of Engineering in Wisconsin. Kirat began his career at Milwaukee Tool as an Electrical Engineering intern, where he helped build standardized datalogging platforms for new product development. That early exposure sparked a lasting interest in data and algorithms, eventually leading him into ML engineering. Today, his work spans MLOps, data pipelines, Databricks, and IoT systems that bring real-time engineering data into analytics and ML workflows.

speakers.name: Maxwell Merget
speakers.bio: Max is a Sr. Manager of Machine Learning Engineering at Milwaukee Tool, where he leads a cross-functional team spanning firmware, electronics, data engineering, and applied AI. His work focuses on transforming data into user-focused solutions through scalable systems that connect product development, testing, and manufacturing on modern platforms like Databricks. His team has delivered customer-facing innovations such as AUTOSTOP and TORQUE-SENSE, along with internal solutions that enhance how Milwaukee Tool designs and manufactures industry-leading products.

sessions.title: From Reactive to Proactive Mobility Insights: Caltrans’ Agentic Solution on a Unified Lakehouse
sessions.body: Caltrans is transforming Traffic Mobility Insights (TMI) into an agent-forward transportation AI platform built on the Databricks lakehouse and lakebase. At its core is an agentic architecture that unifies structured telemetry, geospatial data, and unstructured documents within a governed Delta foundation—eliminating fragmented pipelines and legacy database silos. Lakebase enables high-performance operational lookups and spatial workloads, while the lakehouse provides scalable analytics, model training, and data sharing. A centralized AI switchboard—powered by Databricks Model Serving and MLOps—routes intent across domain agents, enforces policy guardrails, orchestrates tools, and manages state and evidence. This is decision intelligence, not a chatbot. The future state evolves to a federated, Agent-as-a-Product model, where interoperable agents collaborate under a centralized AI control plane—delivering secure, explainable, and proactive transportation management at statewide scale.

speakers.name: Ajali Sen
speakers.bio:
Ajali is a Managing Director at Accenture and leads Public Sector Data and GenAI Solutions for the West US Region. She has 20 years of experience in complex data and analytics transformation coupled with business process change for large clients within state, private sector. She is passionate about using technology to make government services more efficient, accessible, and equitable. Her work focuses on leveraging AI and analytics to enhance public health, education, and social programs. Through strategic insight and human-centered design, she helps states unlock the full potential of their data to serve communities better and create lasting impact.
Ajali also leads the Accenture data quality and analytics implementation team for CDPH.

speakers.name: Duper Tong
speakers.bio:
Duper Tong has over 30 years of experience in transportation planning, design, traffic safety, electrical systems, and traffic operations across the public and private sectors, including 26 years with Caltrans. He currently serves as Chief of the Division of Traffic Operations, leading statewide initiatives in Generative AI applications for Traffic Mobility and Road Safety Insights, the Middle Mile Broadband Network, the Managed Lanes Program, and Intelligent Transportation Systems.

Previously, he was District 10 Deputy District Director of Traffic Operations, overseeing multidisciplinary teams and safety and mobility programs. He began his Caltrans career in the Traffic Investigation and TASAS branches and later served as District 10 Traffic Safety Branch Chief, HQ Office Chief in Traffic Operations, and in the Division of Design.

Duper is active with TRB and AASHTO committees. He is a licensed PE (Civil, Traffic Engineering) and holds BS and MS degrees from CSU Sacramento.

sessions.title: From Repetition to Reuse: The Evolution of Apache Spark™ Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
Learn how to build batch and streaming pipelines faster while improving correctness and reducing operational complexity with Apache Spark™ Declarative Pipelines.

 

Production Spark pipelines often require extensive orchestration code for dependency management, checkpointing, retries, and execution ordering—surrounding a relatively small amount of transformation logic. As pipelines scale, this scaffolding becomes increasingly difficult to maintain and evolve.

 

Introduced in Spark 4.1, Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) shifts this model by allowing developers to declare datasets and transformations while Spark constructs and manages the execution plan. By separating what a pipeline does from how it runs, SDP reduces boilerplate and accelerates time to production.

 

We’ll examine the architectural foundations of declarative development in Spark and how SDP handles dependency resolution, parallelization, checkpoint coordination, and failure recovery. We’ll also cover incremental processing and emerging testing patterns for declarative pipelines.

speakers.name: Andreas Neumann
speakers.bio: With a career defined by "massive scale," Andreas Neumann currently serves as the Technical Lead for Declarative Pipelines at Databricks. From his early work at Yahoo! and IBM to his time at Google and his journey as the founder of Cask Data, Andreas has spent decades solving the data industry's toughest architectural puzzles. Beyond his corporate leadership, he is a dedicated advocate for open-source software, having mentored several Apache projects from incubation to maturity. Andreas holds a PhD in Computer Science for his pioneering research in document querying.

sessions.title: From Search to SQL: How Glean Agents Tap Databricks Genie for Everyday Analytics
sessions.body:
Modern enterprises need both the “what” from governed metrics and the “why” from surrounding context. We’ll show how customers use Glean Agents with Databricks AI/BI Genie and SQL actions to turn natural‑language questions into live warehouse queries that any employee can run. A single agent can route a prompt to Genie, execute the generated SQL on Databricks, then combine resulting tables with unstructured context from email, docs, tickets, and Wikis in one answer, all while respecting app‑level permissions. Attendees will leave with concrete architecture and prompt patterns they can use to scale self‑serve analytics without adding more load on data teams.

 

Audience takeaways:

  • Pattern for building Databricks-powered agents that run live, governed queries without extra indexing
  • Examples of combining Databricks results with unstructured work knowledge to deliver a complete story
  • Practical guidance on permissions, debugging Genie output, and tuning Genie spaces for enterprise copilots

speakers.name: Joel McKelvey
speakers.bio: Joel McKelvey is VP of Product and Solutions Marketing at Glean, where he helps organizations turn AI initiatives into practical, metrics-driven business transformation. He brings more than 30 years of experience across engineering, marketing, and strategy, with deep expertise in AI, machine learning, analytics, and data architectures. His work focuses on how enterprises move from experimentation to execution using AI agents, enterprise search, and trusted data foundations to improve productivity, decision-making, and customer and employee experiences.

sessions.title: From SIEM to Data Platform: Scaling Threat Detection with Lakewatch, Unity Catalog, and AI at Adobe
sessions.body:
Traditional security detection workflows, often confined to proprietary SIEM platforms, struggle to scale, evolve, and integrate with modern data ecosystems. At Adobe, security operations are being reimagined by extending detection capabilities into Databricks using Lakewatch, Unity Catalog, and AI-powered investigation. This approach complements existing SIEM workflows while unlocking new levels of scalability, automation, and data-driven insight.

 

In this session, we present how detection rules are migrated into version-controlled YAML with automated testing and backtesting gates, enabling repeatable and auditable development. By leveraging Lakewatch’s ingestion and normalization of cybersecurity telemetry into OCSF-formatted Delta tables, detections are enriched with both real-time and historical data from Unity Catalog. Detection logic is expressed in SQL and PySpark, with reusable components implemented as SQL UDFs, replacing traditional macro-based approaches.

 

Additionally, we showcase how AI-powered agents transform raw Lakewatch alerts into structured investigation summaries with actionable analyst recommendations, streamlining triage and response. Adobe is modernizing its detection workflows, accelerating development, improving detection fidelity, and establishing a unified, scalable security analytics platform within its broader data ecosystem.

speakers.name: Bharat Gamini
speakers.bio:
Bharat Gamini is a Lead Security Data Engineer at Adobe. Over the past few years at Adobe, he has focused on designing and building advanced analytical data lake solutions with a cybersecurity focus.

Prior to Adobe, Bharat was with AWS, where he managed complex enterprise data lake migration projects and architected solutions for hyperscale data environments. His expertise spans large-scale distributed systems, enterprise data lake architecture, ETL pipeline development, and analytical infrastructure design. He has successfully implemented high-performance data processing frameworks while optimizing petabyte-scale workloads through innovative engineering solutions.

sessions.title: From SIEM to Lakehouse: A Practical Path to SOC Modernization on Databricks
sessions.body:
Security teams are hitting the limits of traditional SIEM architecture. Rising ingestion costs, fragmented telemetry and brittle detections force tradeoffs between visibility and budget.

 

This session outlines a practical, phased path from SIEM-centric operations to lakehouse-driven security analytics. We will explain how SOC teams have cut costs and boosted performance by offloading telemetry from legacy SIEMs to Databricks, without breaking detections. We’ll also show how security teams run and correlate detections natively across their data sources, and use AI agents to automate detection engineering, tuning, and triage while reducing noise and vendor lock-in.

 

Attendees will leave with a clear roadmap to building a modern, AI-driven SOC on Databricks, and how they can unlock broader detection coverage, lower costs at scale, improved triage efficiency and a realistic path to full SIEM replacement.

speakers.name: Alan Mazankiewicz
speakers.bio: Alan is Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks in Germany. At Databricks he works with various cybersecurity customers and partners. He regularly speaks publicly about the intersection of cybersecurity, data and AI.

sessions.title: From Silos to Signal: How BeOne Built an Enterprise Data Mesh for Scalable Enterprise Analytics
sessions.body: Across industry, data is growing exponentially—yet decisions are still slow, manual, and fragmented. Teams spend more time reconciling numbers than acting on them, and many AI initiatives stall because the data foundation isn’t ready.In Pharma R&D, this challenge is amplified. Our data spans internal systems, CROs, investigator sites and partners—within a highly regulated, time-sensitive environment where delayed insight can mean delayed medicines for patients.In this session, we’ll share how we reframed data strategy as decision strategy. Within a year, we built a trusted, scalable foundation powering R&D, Finance, and TechOps—enabling faster portfolio prioritization, improved clinical visibility, smarter resource allocation, and AI readiness by design.Through real R&D use cases, we’ll show how reusable data products, embedded governance, and a modern Databricks architecture turned fragmented data into decision-ready intelligence.

speakers.name: Chirayu Desai
speakers.bio: Chirayu leads enterprise data strategy and AI enablement across R&D and corporate functions. Focused on building governed, scalable foundations that turn data into a strategic decision asset in regulated pharma environments.

speakers.name: SUBHRANSU PANI
speakers.bio: Subhransu leads enterprise information architecture and lakehouse strategy. Designs scalable data foundations that power governed AI and measurable business outcomes across R&D.

sessions.title: From Space to Scale: What to Do (and not do) for Secure, Fast, Production AI/BI
sessions.body: Learn the essential, Databricks AI FDE -tested playbook for deploying production Genie. Start by scoping topic-focused Spaces that leverage Unity Catalog and knowledge-store metadata along with parameterized example SQL rather than free-text queries. This approach drives both clarity and speed. Before scaling out, establish pragmatic, business-centric benchmarks using trusted assets and value dictionaries to measure what truly matters. Integrate Genie into multi-agent workflows through the Conversation API, Teams, and the integration into Databricks’ Agent Framework. Operationalize at scale with pre-joined and trimmed tables, audit-driven monitoring, and a lightweight review cadence.We'll share proven do's and don'ts, common pitfalls to avoid, and a reusable checklist to accelerate your time-to-value, all grounded in Unity Catalog metadata and real-world enterprise deployments.

speakers.name: Yinxi Zhang
speakers.bio: Yinxi Zhang is a Staff Data Scientist at Databricks, where she works with customers to build GenAI applications at scale. Prior to joining Databricks, Yinxi worked as an ML specialist in the energy industry for 7 years, optimizing production for conventional and renewable assets. She holds a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Houston. Yinxi is a former marathon runner, and is now a happy yogi.

sessions.title: From Training to Production: MLOps for Deep Learning on Databricks
sessions.body: Deep learning breaks most MLOps playbooks. Multi-gigabyte weights, GPU-heavy training, distributed checkpoints, and fine-tuning loops don't fit the lifecycle patterns built for classical ML. Teams end up stitching together fragile pipelines to move models from notebook to production — and paying for it in downtime, drift, and missed retraining cycles.This session shows how to run deep learning MLOps end-to-end on Databricks: distributed training with MLflow tracking, model registry workflows for large models, GPU-aware serving with traffic splitting and autoscaling, and automated monitoring that catches regressions before users do.You'll leave with a reference architecture for deep learning MLOps on Databricks — and the patterns to ship models that stay reliable long after launch.

speakers.name: Michael Shtelma
speakers.bio: Michael Shtelma is a Lead Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks. Michael focuses on developing and operationalizing large-scale Machine Learning use cases on the Databricks platform. Before Databricks, Michael worked for Teradata, helping Teradata customers build data and machine learning solutions.

speakers.name: Puneet Jain
speakers.bio: Puneet is a Specialist Solution Architect at Databricks currently working from the London office. Puneet has over 10 years of experience bringing Data and ML solutions from whiteboard to production ranging from Recommendation Systems to Price optimization frameworks. He is passionate about everything Data and AI

sessions.title: From Transactions to Analytics: How Lakebase Works with Lakehouse
sessions.body: Applications generate valuable transactional data — but analyzing it often requires copying data into a separate analytics system. In this session, you’ll learn how Lakebase integrates with Lakehouse to simplify this workflow. We’ll cover the basics of Lakebase, how transactional data becomes immediately available for analytics, and the types of applications and teams that benefit most from this approach. Designed for beginners, this session focuses on understanding the architecture and knowing when — and why — to use it.

speakers.name: Gaurav Saraf
speakers.bio: Gaurav manages the Databricks SQL product space.

sessions.title: From Two Hours to Two Minutes: Panasonic’s Global Scale Engineering With the Data Intelligence Platform
sessions.body:
Panasonic’s global footprint—from EV batteries to smart mobility—demands real-time precision. To fulfill the vision of "making tomorrow better," Panasonic transformed its data backbone into a unified Lakehouse. This session explores the engineering feat of unlocking SAP, Salesforce and SharePoint data, slashing SAP data latency from two hours to just two minutes.

 

Learn how Panasonic is scaling from a single use case to an enterprise-wide strategy, deploying Lakeflow Connect to unify ingestion across multiple data sources and AI Query to structure unstructured data.

 

We’ll also review strategic deployment of Auto Loader and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines for high-scale CDC and Unity Catalog for cross-domain lineage and governance. And hear how automation and Lakeflow Jobs have eliminated overhead and empowered 10+ global teams.

 

Finally, we’ll preview our roadmap for AI Agents, showing how a robust engineering foundation enables the next generation of autonomous intelligence.

speakers.name: Brendan Byrne
speakers.bio: Brendan Byrne is a Data Engineer at Panasonic of North America, specializing in modern data architectures built on the Databricks Lakehouse platform. He played a key role in transforming legacy full‑load pipelines into efficient Change Data Capture solutions, reducing runtimes from hours to minutes while significantly improving stability and manageability. His work leverages Databricks Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Lakeflow orchestration, and Auto Loader to deliver scalable, reliable data solutions. He continues to focus on expanding Panasonic’s data catalog and platform capabilities to support enterprise‑scale analytics and innovation.

speakers.name: Priyanka Kasliwal
speakers.bio:
Priyanka is a Field Engineering professional at Databricks, specializing in architecting high-scale solutions within the Lakehouse ecosystem. With her system design and architecture background, she focuses on technical enablement—helping organizations move beyond infrastructure to build functional, intelligence-driven solutions. She is passionate about solving engineering hurdles in real-time ingestion and data lifecycle management.

With architectural expertise across Azure, AWS, and GCP, Priyanka excels at navigating the shift from legacy silos to unified platforms plus bridges the gap between complex engineering and business ROI, accelerating time-to-value for production-grade innovation.

sessions.title: From Unstructured Data to Structured Insights: How YipitData Scales Data Enrichment with AI Agents
sessions.body:
YipitData analyzes billions of unstructured data points at petabyte scale to deliver high fidelity insights to institutional investors and Fortune 500 companies. With 100s of heterogeneous data sources, regex, classic ML and NLP techniques never met our accuracy hurdle, limiting our product breadth for years.

 

In this session, we reframe entity resolution as an agentic problem and share our production-grade enrichment platform built on Apache Spark™, Agent Bricks, Vector Search and Lakebase. This AI-native architecture continuously discovers and tags data at 90%–95% accuracy, reliably covering 60,000+ companies—a 20x improvement.

 

Data/ML leaders, engineers and practitioners will learn:

  • Modular, pipeline design applicable to any classification scenario
  • Batch inference patterns in Spark that streamlines infrastructure
  • Techniques for continuous, low maintenance entity discovery

 

Join us and leave with a blueprint to turn enrichment bottlenecks into self-improving, AI pipelines.

speakers.name: Anup Segu
speakers.bio: Anup Segu is Chief Architect at YipitData, a leading alternative data provider to institutional investors and corporations. He has built and led YipitData's Data Engineering and Platform Engineering organizations, architected its petabyte-scale data and AI platform, and driven company-wide adoption of lakehouse and agentic AI. Earlier, Anup worked in investment banking at Citigroup and studied at Indiana University.

speakers.name: Edward Goo
speakers.bio: Edward Goo is the Head of Data Engineering at YipitData, a leader in the alternative data industry providing insights to investment firms and Fortune 500 companies. He leads the data engineering organization in building large-scale data pipelines that transform messy, unstructured datasets into high-fidelity insights. His team is focused on centralizing internal data and developing a company master dataset powering entity resolution at scale. Over his eight-year tenure, Edward has architected systems processing billions of data points at a petabyte scale. He holds a degree from Syracuse University and previously worked in investment funds.

sessions.title: From Vector Search to AI Search: Rebuilding Retrieval for the AI Era
sessions.body: Search bars, recommendations, entity resolution, real-time matching, agents — all run on retrieval, and all stand or fall on whether the right result arrives fast enough and ranked well enough. Teams now need hybrid keyword-plus-semantic search, reranking as a first-class step, domain-tuned models, retrieval quality evaluation without hand-labels, and feedback loops that turn traffic into better results.We've rebuilt Databricks Vector Search from the ground up — and today we're relaunching it as Databricks AI Search: an AI-native retrieval platform that unifies search, ranking, evaluation, and continuous learning on the Lakehouse. You'll see what's shipped — BM25 and full-text indexes, hybrid retrieval with a native reranker, domain-tunable rerankers, LLM-judged evaluation, high-QPS endpoints — and what's next: click logging, continuous quality monitoring, and learn-to-rank.Walk away with best practices for measuring retrieval quality and a production-ready stack for the AI era.

speakers.name: Ankit Vij
speakers.bio: Ankit is a Software Engineer at Databricks with a deep interest in information retrieval and machine learning. He is the founding engineer and TL for the vector search team and has been working in the search domain for over 10 years. Ankit holds a Master's degree in Computer Science from the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

sessions.title: From Web to Warehouse: Building a Real-Time Competitive Intelligence Agent on Databricks
sessions.body: Your competitor just dropped their price. How long until you know? In this session, see how we built an e-commerce agent natively on Databricks - combining LangGraph, LLMs, and live web data from Bright Data, all persisted in Unity Catalog for historical analysis. We'll walk through the architecture, deploy a working agent live, and show how retailers can turn the open web into a queryable table.

sessions.title: From Wellhead to Insight: Halliburton’s Real‑Time Data Sharing with Chevron
sessions.body: How can raw well data be made available more quickly and more consistently across organizations, without relying on manual data movement? In this joint session, Halliburton and Chevron showcase a breakthrough in energy data collaboration. Halliburton shares how they can publish curated well completion and treatment datasets directly into Chevron’s environment using Delta Sharing, enabling more timely visibility into well performance, deferment drivers and optimization opportunities. We’ll walk through the technical architecture that allows Halliburton and Chevron to collaborate securely across Azure and AWS clouds without the latency associated with traditional ETL. We will cover the practical lessons learned during implementation — including establishing robust data contracts and security considerations, and discuss the ROI of Delta Sharing. Attendees will leave with a practical, repeatable understanding on how to deliver trusted, live oilfield data to support more efficient analytics and production decisions, with zero‑copy data sharing.

speakers.name: Kshitij Dawar
speakers.bio: Kshitij Dawar is a Lead Data Architect and Engineer at Chevron, where he designs enterprise‑scale, AI‑ready data platforms across subsurface and wells domains. His work focuses on cloud‑native lakehouse architectures, real‑time data products, master data standardization, and applied Generative AI for extracting insights from structured and unstructured data. With a Ph.D. in Petroleum and Natural Gas Engineering and a strong foundation in machine learning, reinforcement learning, and large‑scale data engineering, Kshitij bridges advanced research with production‑grade AI systems. He is also Vice Chair of the SPE Gulf Coast Section Data Analytics Study Group and an active mentor and speaker on AI, data architecture, and analytics in energy.

speakers.name: Shahab Jamali
speakers.bio: As Chief Data Scientist at Halliburton, Shahab Jamali Ghare Tape bridges the gap between complex engineering data and executive-level insights. Leading a team at the intersection of ML, AI, and GenAI, he specializes in creating "decision-ready" data environments. At the 2026 Data + AI Summit, he is showcasing a breakthrough in energy industry collaboration, demonstrating how Halliburton and Chevron use Delta Sharing to eliminate ETL latency and share live well-performance data across cloud boundaries. When he isn't optimizing oilfield datasets, Shahab can be found on the soccer field or playing the Setar.

sessions.title: Game Day at Global Scale: How PepsiCo Foods Uses AI to Feed the World Cup
sessions.body:
FIFA World Cup comes to the Bay Area this June. 70,000+ fans at Levi’s Stadium will consume millions of servings of Frito-Lay products, and millions more will be watching across North America. PepsiCo Foods doesn’t get a second chance to stock the right SKUs, in the right quantities, at the right locations. Get it wrong and you have bare shelves.

 

This session shows how PepsiCo Foods runs 125 million demand forecast combinations weekly on Databricks, achieving 80%+ DSD accuracy while reducing compute cost 60% after migrating from on-prem solution. We’ll demo how supply planners model what-if scenarios in real time using Databricks Apps and Lakebase, query demand drivers through Genie, and how agentic AI is beginning to automate anomalous demand detection across Sales, Marketing, Finance and Supply Chain.

 

You’ll learn:

  • How PepsiCo runs driver-based forecasting at 125M combinations/week on Databricks
  • How Lakebase and Apps enable real-time what-if scenario planning

speakers.name: Michael Cleavinger
speakers.job_title: VP Global Data Science and Analytics
speakers.bio: Michael Cleavinger is Vice President of Data Science at PepsiCo, leading a global organization that builds AI, machine learning, and decision science capabilities across marketing, planning, supply chain, consumer, commercial, and finance. With experience across retail and CPG, he focuses on turning complex, high-volume data into scalable strategies that drive growth, improve efficiency, and enable better decisions. He has led enterprise forecasting and optimization platforms that reduce cost, increase reuse, and deliver business impact at global scale.

sessions.title: Genie at scale: Best practices for enterprise rollout
sessions.body: As organizations adopt agentic AI at scale, getting access, governance, and deployment right is more critical than ever. Rolling out Genie and AI/BI across thousands of users demands clear policies for user access, data governance, and content distribution to ensure secure, consistent, and scalable adoption—including on mobile devices under enterprise policies.We’ll walk through best practices for deploying Genie and AI/BI at scale, helping you move from isolated use cases to organization-wide impact.Topics include:- Onboarding and provisioning users efficiently across business teams- Managing data access and permissions to ensure secure, governed usage- Publishing dashboards and Genie experiences for maximum reach- Enabling secure mobile access aligned with enterprise device and security policies- Monitoring usage, manage sharing, and identify opportunities to drive adoption- Deployment patterns and best practices for scaling adoption across the enterprise

speakers.name: Austin Green
speakers.bio: Austin Green is a Staff Software Engineer at Databricks, focused on discovery and sharing surfaces.

speakers.name: Dillon Bostwick
speakers.bio: Dillon Bostwick is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he’s spent the last five years advising customers ranging from startups to Fortune 500 enterprises. He currently helps lead a team of field ambassadors for streaming products and is interested in improving industry awareness of effective streaming patterns for data integration and production machine learning. He previously worked as a product engineer in infrastructure automation.

sessions.title: Genie Code for data science: Work at the speed of your ideas
sessions.body: What if you could go from a raw dataset to a trained model in a single conversation?Data scientists spend a lot of time on the repetitive parts of the lifecycle: finding data, wrangling it, writing features, tuning hyperparameters, and not enough time on the creative work that actually moves the needle. Genie Code is an autonomous AI partner built into Databricks that changes the equation. Tell it what you want to explore, and it writes the code, runs the analysis, and iterates with you.In this session, we’ll walk through how to apply Genie Code across the data science lifecycle. We’ll cover:- How to use Genie Code for exploratory data analysis and feature discovery- How to build and iterate on machine learning models with less manual effort- When to steer and when to let Genie Code drive- Best practices for working effectively with Genie Code as a data science partner

speakers.name: Gal Oshri
speakers.bio: Gal has been building AI products for the past decade. At Databricks, he works on the Databricks Assistant, helping make it a useful tool for all users across the platform. Previously, he worked on machine learning products at AWS (SageMaker Training), Google (TensorFlow), and Microsoft (ML.NET), contributing to tools used by developers and data scientists around the world.

sessions.title: Genie is a Game Changer
sessions.body: We would like to share our vision, strategy and learnings with Databricks Genie. You want to know something, you ask, you get an answer. By enabling our users to interact with our data, AkzoNobel can anticipate developments in Supply Chain Management, Finance and Service Delivery more quickly driving impact. This requires a new form of cooperation between business and IT. The responsibilities will be shared and clearly defined as IT will be in control to safeguard standards and the business will provide semantics.  For the users there is also a change to be managed, most will think in reports when asking questions to Genie while DeepSearch allows much more.  Further innovation with Genie DeepSearch allows us to bring insights to our management in the form of podcasts or videos.  Genie is a gamechanger when done right. It allows for completely different ways of interacting with insights but also offers opportunities for IT to simplify the Analytics landscape.

speakers.name: Kristi Blaisdell
speakers.bio:
Kristi leads the Enterprise Reporting team at AkzoNobel, driving data innovation and empowering business insights at scale.
With a passion for analytics and storytelling through data, she transforms complexity into clarity. Kristi brings contagious energy to every challenge—because great data should inspire action.

speakers.name: Peter Jan Snoep
speakers.bio:
Peter Jan Snoep is Domain Architect Data & Analytics at AkzoNobel, driving the modernization of the Data & Analytics estate.
Throughout his career Peter Jan has held different positions in the domain of analytics, working both national and international. As Domain Architect Data & Analytics with AkzoNobel he oversees the modernization of the Analytics landscape by integrating Enterprise Reporting with Self Service Analytics and AI/ML in a cloud-based platform. What drives him is providing business value through technology and data with the motto; “data brings us all together”.

sessions.title: Genie, Who Broke My Cluster? Using AI Functions, APIs and Genie Code to understand your workload
sessions.body: Have you ever wondered what happened in your Databricks environment? Have you spent time looking through logs and audit tables? Join us for this live demo of using Genie code to gain insights into your system. If Genie is new to you, you'll learn how easy it is to get started. If you are already a Genie expert, you'll discover ways to improve and enhance your experience using APIs, joins, AI Functions, and more. Take the guesswork out of auditing by setting up your own Genie with the real-world, practical examples shown in this session.

sessions.title: Get Started Ingesting Data with Lakeflow Connect
sessions.body:
Thousands of organizations use Lakeflow Connect to turn raw data into actionable intelligence. In this session, we’ll show you how to streamline your ingestion strategy and accelerate your path to value.

 

We’ll cover:

  • Expanding the 80+ connector ecosystem: Explore what’s new across databases (e.g., Oracle, Postgres, SQL Server), applications (e.g., Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Google Analytics), file sources (e.g., SharePoint, Google Drive), and message buses (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ).
  • Introducing open-source tools: Learn how to build, scale, and even open source your own connectors using the same robust framework.
  • Optimizing cost and performance: Discover how to slash costs and complexity by eliminating architecture hops with Zerobus Ingest. Take advantage of new cost and performance levers. And learn what we’re building behind the scenes to help.

 

Join us and learn how to stop battling pipelines and start building value.

speakers.name: Elise Georis
speakers.bio: Elise Georis is on the product team at Databricks, focused on Genie: an enterprise AI that connects your people, data, and systems to help you get work done. Previously, she oversaw product for Lakeflow Connect.

speakers.name: Giselle Goicochea
speakers.bio: Giselle leads product marketing for Lakeflow Connect, including Zerobus Ingest, as well as Spark Structured Streaming and its Real-Time Mode capabilities.

sessions.title: Getting started with AI Governance on Databricks
sessions.body: As AI agents move from prototypes to production, a new architectural layer is emerging: the tool gateway. Models alone aren't enough — agents need secure, real-time access to data, APIs, and enterprise systems. Integrating these tools consistently and safely has become one of the biggest bottlenecks to adoption.In this session, we explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and tool gateways redefine how agents interact with the world. MCP standardizes how agents discover and use tools dynamically, while AI Gateway acts as the enterprise control plane to govern access, manage credentials, and monitor usage across every tool and model. Together, they replace fragmented APIs with a unified, governed interface — letting agents securely connect to managed, external, and custom MCP servers and select tools at runtime.Through real architectures, you'll see how to design agent systems that are flexible, interoperable, and production-ready across internal data and third-party systems.

speakers.name: Stefania Leone
speakers.bio: Stefania is a product manager at Databricks working on Unity Catalog and the Databricks Runtime. She holds a PhD in Computer Science from ETH Zurich.

sessions.title: Getting the Most out of AI in BI: From Dashboard Creation to Intelligent Insights
sessions.body: AI is rapidly reshaping business intelligence but for many teams, it’s still unclear how to move beyond isolated features to real, end-to-end impact.In Databricks, AI is embedded across the entire BI workflow. From using Genie Code to build and maintain dashboards, to applying AI-driven capabilities like forecasting and key driver analysis, to enabling conversational exploration directly within dashboards, AI becomes part of how analytics is created, delivered, and used.This shift allows teams to move faster, reduce manual work, and unlock deeper insights without adding complexity.In this session, we’ll walk through how to apply AI across the full BI lifecycle:- How to use Genie Code to accelerate dashboard creation and maintenance- How to leverage built-in AI features such as forecasting and intelligent insights- How to embed Genie directly into dashboards for conversational exploration- Best practices for combining AI and BI to drive adoption and real business impact

sessions.title: Getting the Most Out of Spark Declarative Pipelines: Deep Dive on What’s New and Best Practices
sessions.body:
Declarative pipelines are becoming the default way teams scale production data pipelines in Spark. Maximizing their value requires understanding the execution model, tradeoffs, and best practices.

 

In this 90-minute-deep dive, distinguished engineer Michael Armbrust explores how to get the most out of Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP), drawing on real-world usage and the latest platform advancements. You’ll learn how to:

  • Apply proven design patterns for building reliable, maintainable pipelines
  • Use SDP effectively across batch and streaming workloads
  • Avoid common pitfalls as pipeline complexity and scale increase

 

This session is the definitive technical deep dive for teams scaling through declarative frameworks in Spark.

sessions.title: Global Toymaker ZURU Fuels AI-Driven Innovation with Crisp Retail Data in Databricks
sessions.body: ZURU (Mini Brands, Snackles, Bunch-O-Balloons, and the latest plush trends) operates at the cutting edge of modern retail by investing in strong data infrastructure and enabling organization-wide intelligence. Teams leverage centralized AI-ready insights across major retailers, to inform fast daily decisions across inventory, marketing, product, and more. Retail-specific semantic modeling creates a trusted foundation for AI workflowsAt the core of ZURU’s retail strategy is Databricks. Clean, real-time data is delivered into Databricks daily via Crisp, and informs Agentic AI workflows across supply chain, sales, and marketing.AI-enabled retail intelligence has been the key for ZURU to scale their multi-category business globally.This session explores how pairing clean, AI-ready data from Crisp with Databricks enables responsive decision-making and supply chain excellence at retail scale.

sessions.title: Goldman Sach's Fully-Interoperable Lakehouse With Iceberg
sessions.body: Goldman Sach's Lakehouse platform with Iceberg, allows zero-copy data sharing and iceberg rest catalog integration across vendor engines, and seamlessly manages trust, entitlements and governance across these engines. This session will detail Goldman Sachs' journey in developing an "Iceberg-first" data platform, leveraging Lakehouse architecture and will cover the critical architectural and design choices that underpinned this initiative.

speakers.name: Abhishek Narang
speakers.bio: Abhishek leads Data Engineering and Data Modeling efforts across the firm, responsible for helping revenue divisions identify, prototype, and use data to meet their client and business objectives.
