He is also responsible for co-creating the firm's cloud data strategy, partnering with divisional Engineering teams and implementing solutions to migrate existing data to the cloud. Abhishek leads firmwide efforts to provide rapid access to cloud-based vendor data repositories. In addition, he manages the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Beacon team, which focuses on identifying and curating ESG data for multiple businesses across the firm. Previously, Abhishek led the SecDiv Data Services team in India, where he managed the SecDiv lake, founded the PURE team in India and optimized access to high quality data for the Securities Division. Prior to that, he was a founding member of the Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities Core team in India.

sessions.title: Governed Data Sharing & Collaboration at Scale: Deep Dive On Security Best Practices for Zero-Trust Architectures
sessions.body: Sharing data openly shouldn't mean sharing it insecurely. As enterprises scale Delta Sharing to hundreds of recipients across clouds and platforms, security and governance architectures quickly become the bottleneck. This session dives into how Databricks enables governed, zero‑copy collaboration using open Delta Sharing, Clean Rooms for multi‑party analytics without exposing raw data, and Private Exchanges in Databricks Marketplace for curated partner ecosystems. We'll tackle the three pillars of secure sharing at scale: OIDC token federation for secretless auth with external identity providers, attribute‑based access control (ABAC) for fine‑grained row/column policies, and the Storage Network Gateway for one‑time network setup that eliminates manual firewall/IP allowlisting. You'll see a live zero‑trust reference architecture, backed by Unity Catalog lineage and audit logging, powering cross‑cloud Databricks‑to‑Databricks and open recipients, plus monitoring. Expect code, configs, and field‑tested patterns, including a security checklist, ABAC policy templates, and an OIDC integration guide you can apply Monday morning to scale governed collaboration without replication.

speakers.name: Bhavin Kukadia

speakers.bio:
Work hard, have fun, make money.
Brickster since 2017, all things platform security

speakers.name: Krishan Kumar
speakers.bio: Krishan Kumar is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks specializing in governed data sharing, security architecture, and cross-platform data collaboration. He leads Databricks' internal Digital Natives Delta Sharing SME Group, a community of practice that develops best practices, reference architectures, and field enablement for Delta Sharing at scale. Krishan has served as the Solutions Architect for the largest Delta Sharing customer at Databricks globally — a customer whose Delta Sharing-powered data product generates millions in annual revenue. Prior to Databricks, he led MLOps at Gap Inc., where he built and operationalized ML infrastructure at enterprise scale. Krishan holds a B.S. in Computer Science from Stanford University.

speakers.name: Michael Saltzman
speakers.bio:
Michael Saltzman is a Senior Cloud Architect at Databricks
with deep expertise in cloud migrations, infrastructure architecture, and modern data platforms. Based in New York, he specializes in helping organizations design and scale secure, high-performance cloud environments across complex enterprise ecosystems. His background spans cloud networking, security, automation, and large-scale data infrastructure, with a strong focus on enabling organizations to modernize their analytics and AI foundations.

Michael brings a highly technical, hands-on perspective to cloud transformation initiatives, backed by advanced certifications including AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, AWS Advanced Networking Specialty, and AWS Security Specialty. He is passionate about open data architectures, platform interoperability, and helping customers operationalize modern data and AI workloads at scale.

sessions.title: Governed Data Sharing at Scale: UBS RiskLab + LSEG via Unity Catalog and Delta Sharing
sessions.body:
Databricks and LSEG will jointly present how Databricks Unity Catalog and its Delta Sharing capabilities enable LSEG to provide UBS RiskLab: the bank’s model development lab platform, with direct, compliant access to LSEG’s extensive financial data products. This gives UBS data scientists governed, auditable self-service access, accelerating raw data exploration, business intelligence, and rapid prototyping of Data and AI solutions under a robust control framework.

 

The session will demonstrate how analytics are accelerated by securely combining UBS internal data with LSEG Delta Share data through Unity Catalog, with policy-based entitlements, and centralized governance. This approach reduces the lengthy, siloed analysis typically associated with onboarding external data feeds. With the Unity Catalog AI Assistant and Genie, data scientists can quickly and confidently derive insights from a unified view of UBS internal and LSEG external data.

speakers.name: Krithika Kalaiarasan
speakers.bio: Krithi is a seasoned Solutions Architect at Databricks with 20 years of experience in Data and Analytics. With a robust background as a practitioner architect and a degree in machine learning, Krithi specializes in designing scalable solutions for petabytes of data, ensuring seamless integration and optimized performance. She has extensive experience in the financial services and insurance sectors, having worked on mission-critical applications and strategic architectures. Krithi is renowned for leading digital transformation journeys, guiding enterprises toward strategic cloud architectures that future-proof their operations. Her deep understanding of complex data ecosystems and her ability to translate technical concepts into actionable insights have been pivotal in solving customers' pain points and challenges.

sessions.title: Governing at Hyper-Growth: How HelloFresh Cut Data Access from Days to Minutes With Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
At HelloFresh, speed is our currency. But with 70,000+ tables generated across decentralized domains, our rapid growth threatened to outpace our ability to govern it. We reached a critical inflection point where the “data mesh” approach began to look like a “data mess” — fragmented across AWS Glue, obscured by complex IAM policies, and creating bottlenecks where data access took days to approve.

 

This session unpacks the strategic pivot from reactive catalog management to a unified, scalable governance model on Databricks Unity Catalog. We will move beyond the technical migration to discuss the architectural shifts required to balance autonomy with control. You will learn how we dismantled the trade-off between security and agility, replacing brittle object-based permissions with a streamlined privilege model that empowers data owners.

 

We will share our blueprint for a zero-downtime migration (using Hive Metastore Federation) and the cultural changes required to make governance stick.

speakers.name: Adam Komisarek
speakers.bio:
Adam studied computer science in Poland/Poznan, and started working there in small startup building computer assisted translation tools.

Over the years, Adam experienced all different assets of software delivery cycle - starting with frontend, and quickly jumped to the backend, ended up after years in Data. Now he works at HelloFresh, changing how people eat forever, and building great Data Platform for the internal users.

His current interests include data processing tools such as Spark and Flink, ensuring users can access data easily and securely from various sources.

sessions.title: Governing MCPs at scale with Unity AI Gateway
sessions.body: As AI agents move from prototypes to production you need a centralized governance layer for tool access and we uniquely have a way to solve this with Unity AI Gateway. Integrating tools, and MCP servers consistently and safely has become one of the biggest bottlenecks to adoption.In this session, we explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and tool gateways redefine how agents interact with the world. MCP standardizes how agents discover and use tools dynamically, while Unity AI Gateway acts as the enterprise control plane to govern access, manage credentials, and monitor usage across every tool and model. Together, they replace fragmented APIs with a unified, governed interface — letting agents securely connect to managed, external, and custom MCP servers and select tools at runtime.Through real architectures, you'll see how to design agent systems that are flexible, interoperable, and production-ready across internal data and third-party systems.

sessions.title: GPU-Accelerated Operations Research: Production-Grade Optimization with NVIDIA cuOpt on Databricks
sessions.body: Enterprises face a surge of optimization challenges—workforce scheduling, supply chain planning, resource allocation, etc. that are computationally explosive as scale and constraints grow. Learn to solve these problems with Databricks using NVIDIA cuOpt on serverless GPUs, with large-scale linear, mixed-integer, and routing models in minutes instead of hours. We will walk through end-to-end architectures on the Databricks Lakehouse—parameterizing and submitting optimization jobs to serverless GPU clusters, managing data with Unity Catalog and Delta tables, and orchestrating workloads alongside existing ML pipelines. Learn from real-world examples I.e. shift scheduling, production allocation, and route optimization with performance benchmarks and cost benefits compared to traditional CPU solvers. Leave with practical patterns for modeling constraints, validating feasibility, and knowing when GPU-accelerated optimization can drive measurable gains in efficiency and delivery performance.

speakers.name: James Maki
speakers.bio: James Maki is a senior solution architect on the NVIDIA Media & Entertainment SA team focused on the intersection of agentic and generative AI with video games. James has a master's degree in data analytics from Penn State.

speakers.name: Josh Melton
speakers.bio: I’m a Delivery Solutions Architect at Databricks, where I partner with manufacturing and logistics organizations to unlock the power of their data—helping them turn complex questions into actionable insights.

sessions.title: Grounding Legacy BI: Etihad Airways’ Transition to AI-Powered Self-Service with Genie
sessions.body:
Modern airlines need more than dashboards. They need intelligence at speed. Etihad Airways is transforming its analytics landscape by moving from traditional BI platforms to Databricks AI/BI, redefining how data is accessed, understood and acted upon across the enterprise.

 

This session tells the story behind that shift, beginning with a bold pilot in Catering that demonstrated the power of generative, natural-language insights and sparked immediate executive engagement from day one. We’ll explore Etihad’s journey from complex, siloed reporting to an AI-first, self-service experience powered by Databricks Genie, turning data into an always-on business co-pilot.

 

Attendees will learn how this transformation accelerated speed-to-insight, reduced technical debt, and scaled rapidly across diverse business units. We’ll conclude with a demo of our current Genie implementation and a forward look at Etihad’s evolving roadmap in the Databricks ecosystem, offering practical lessons for anyone.

speakers.name: Evan Digney
speakers.job_title: Head of Enterprise Data & AI Platforms
speakers.bio:
Evan Digney is the Head of Enterprise Data & AI Platforms at Etihad Airways, where he leads the transformation of the airline’s data and AI platform. He is responsible for defining and executing a modern, cloud-native data strategy that powers real-time operations, advanced analytics, and enterprise-wide decision-making.

Evan specializes in building scalable lakehouse architectures on Databricks.

At Etihad, he is driving a shift away from traditional data tooling toward unified, high-performance platforms—enabling faster innovation while reducing operational overhead. He brings a pragmatic, outcome-focused approach to data and AI, ensuring technology investments translate into measurable business impact.

speakers.name: Ketan Patel
speakers.bio:
Ketan built his career doing the hard part of data transformation, fixing what’s messy, making it work, and making sure it keeps working.

Across Lloyds Banking Group, TSB, Virgin Money, and now Etihad Airways, he has led large-scale transformations, turning fragmented legacy systems into modern, self-service platforms that deliver real business value.

He is currently building the Finance Analytics function at Etihad from scratch, focused on AI enabled decision making. Ketan is also cofounder of BreachAware®, operating in 140+ countries, and BITs Software LLC, building data-driven solutions that solve real world problems.

Ketan is known for cutting through noise, no buzzwords, no over engineering, just clear thinking + strong execution.

sessions.body: Don’t miss this year’s Healthcare and Life Sciences Industry Forum. Through candid conversations and real-world use cases, this forum will examine how the industry is streamlining healthcare operations, accelerating research and discovery and driving measurable improvements in patient outcomes.

speakers.name: Matt Meador

sessions.title: High-Throughput, Low-Latency: The Databricks Playbook for Production Model Serving
sessions.body: Modern AI applications don’t just need accurate models, they need to serve them at massive scale, with low latency and strict reliability guarantees. In this session, we’ll go under the hood of Databricks Model Serving to show how we support high QPS (300K+ QPS), production-grade workloads on a unified Lakehouse platform. We’ll walk through the serving architecture, autoscaling strategies, and optimizations across GPU/CPU utilization, request routing, and caching that enable sustained high throughput without sacrificing latency or cost. You’ll see real patterns from customer deployments, learn how to design your endpoints for bursty and always-on traffic, and leave with practical guidance for running mission-critical ML and LLM workloads on Databricks Model Serving.

sessions.title: How Circle K Powers Personalized Loyalty Programs with Customer Data at Scale
sessions.body: Circle K is activating customer data and loyalty insights via their CDP to deliver more relevant, personalized experiences across the customer journey. In this session, Jay Malepati, Global Director of Customer & Marketing Data Science at Circle K, will share how his team is building a stronger customer data foundation to better understand customer behavior, improve loyalty engagement, and automate personalization at scale. Attendees will learn how Circle K approaches customer intelligence, segmentation, and data-driven marketing in a complex, high-volume retail environment.

sessions.title: How Data Warehousing Changes in the World of Agents
sessions.body: The rise of agentic applications is reshaping what we demand from data warehouses. Agents don't operate on yesterday's batch — they require fresh, consistent data with sub-second latency to reason, decide, and act in real time. In this session, we examine why traditional data warehousing patterns, built around scheduled ETL and human-speed concurrency and latency, fall short when the consumer of your data is an army of agents making thousands of decisions per minute. We address the challenges this shift introduces: tighter freshness SLAs, evolving governance when agents —not people — query your data, and the complexity of always-on pipelines. We then explore how real-time lakehouse capabilities — streaming ingestion, incremental materialization, high concurrency and low-latency query serving, and unified governance — support agentic applications at scale. This session offers a framework to make your lakehouse real-time and agent-ready.

speakers.name: Ruwen Henning Hess
speakers.bio: Director, Product Management

sessions.title: How Databricks Apps Facilitated Model Retraining
sessions.body:
At Bridgestone, our mission is “serving society with superior quality.” As the world’s largest manufacturer of tire products, Bridgestone has a unique opportunity to leverage data and insights to improve manufacturing efficiency. Bridgestone’s Bandag Retread Solutions has over 65 years leading retread innovations.

 

In this talk, we will focus on how our data scientists used Databricks Apps to improve a computer vision model that facilitates decision-making during the tire retread process. We will show how in 3 weeks, a fully-fledged computer vision labeling application could be built using apps, saving our retread SMEs months of manual effort and thousands of dollars in a 3p software.

 

Our talk will also highlight the benefits of choosing Databricks apps to host our solution:

  • The ease of integration with existing Databricks resources
  • Out of box compliance with internal security standards
  • The speed in developing a front-end application, without the need of managing cloud infrastructure

speakers.name: Gregory Islas

speakers.name: Tim Hanchin

sessions.title: How Databricks Runs Databricks Across Clouds and Regions
sessions.body: Running a data platform on one cloud is standard — running it across AWS, Azure, and GCP simultaneously is advanced. But running it across 100+ distinct regions while maintaining a unified experience? That is the Databricks Data Platform team's daily reality. In this session, we reveal the architecture of our massive internal global mesh. We will dive into the challenges of data gravity, cross-region replication, and unified identity at a scale few companies face. Learn how we abstract away the chaos of 100+ regions to provide a seamless, singular "Databricks experience" to our internal developers — proving that you really can build a true multi-cloud lakehouse without getting locked in.

speakers.name: Clara MacAvoy
speakers.bio: Clara is a Sr. Software Engineer on Databricks' Data Platform, operating the largest Databricks workspaces in the world to power the company's Data + AI initiatives. She specializes in multi-cloud scalability and data governance, ensuring Databricks can reliably, safely, and efficiently process and store critical business data. Clara plays a pivotal role in building and managing multi-cloud workspaces to facilitate internal Data + AI consumption. Passionate about UX, Clara is committed to designing intuitive systems that empower users to make data-driven decisions seamlessly. Clara has a BS/MS from Stanford, where she won the Terman Engineering Award and was a 2023 Siebel Scholar.

speakers.name: Peng Chen
speakers.bio: Peng Chen is a Senior Engineering Manager on Databricks’ Data Platform team, building the multi-cloud platform for secure workload deployment and workspace provisioning that powers the company’s next generation of Data + AI workloads. Previously, he led large-scale data and ML infrastructure teams at Pinterest and Instagram/Meta, building ads ingestion, indexing, database, delivery, and reporting infrastructure at petabyte scale. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Indiana University Bloomington.

sessions.title: How Databricks Ships AI Safely: Inside the Team Enabling Secure Innovation
sessions.body:
The pace of AI development has reset what security teams need to deliver. At Databricks, we've built an AI Security team that operates at the frontier of the technology it defends. This session is an inside look at how.

 

We'll share the human-in-the-loop agents we built to assess security issues across our AI products and services, and why an early, disciplined bet on agent benchmarking got us to 95.8% accuracy on agent-generated findings, and how we use expert reviewers validating every result so nothing slips through.

 

Then we'll open the hood on how we secure the coding agents our own engineers use every day: managed client-side settings, agent sandboxes, an AI Gateway and MCP Gateway enforcing policy server-side where admin access can't reach, and continuous scanning of every Databricks App, plugin, and skill.Real architecture. Real numbers. Real failure modes. A practical look at what a modern AI security function looks like in production.

speakers.name: Alex Warnecke
speakers.bio: Alex is an AI Security Engineer at Databricks. Prior to that he obtained his PhD from Technical University of Berlin where his research was dealing with the intersection of machine learning and computer security.

speakers.name: Nishith Sinha
speakers.bio: Nishith leads the AI Security Team at Databricks. His team is responsible for securing Databricks AI Products (Genie Code, Model Serving, Databricks One) as well as the enterprise usage of AI within Databricks. Nishith is a subject matter expert in AI Security, specializing in agents identity and security. In the last year, he has filed 10 GenAI Security patents.

sessions.title: How Databricks Uses Databricks to Run Its Own Finance Organization — and Why That Changes Everything
sessions.body: The most credible proof of a platform's power is how the company that built it uses it to run its own business. Databricks' Office of the CFO has gone all-in on the Databricks platform to unify transactional data from ERP, CRM, HRIS, and planning systems into a single, governed source of financial truth,  eliminating the 'which number is right?' debate that costs enterprises countless hours in every close cycle. In this fast-paced, demo-forward lightning talk, you'll see how Genie and AI/BI enable natural language financial analytics and forecasting, how Unity Catalog ensures SOX compliance and audit readiness, and how RowZero enables seamless data ingestion from spreadsheets into governed pipelines without disrupting the workflows finance teams already use. If your CFO or finance team is still living in spreadsheets, this talk demonstrates what it looks like when finance becomes a first-class data organization. Expect less theory, more demo.

sessions.title: How Hilton Grand Vacations Optimizes Inventory with AI on Databricks
sessions.body: Timeshare and hospitality inventory decisions are complex, spanning multiple revenue streams and liabilities, constrained by thousands of contractual and operational rules. This talk explores how HGV’s Inventory AI transformed yield and revenue optimization into an AI-powered, simulation-driven workflow that enforces business guardrails, scores alternative moves, and surfaces real-time revenue impact. Powered by Databricks, the solution builds on our modernization program that migrated thousands of data elements and analytics workloads to Databricks, enabling scalable data engineering and ML operations. We’ll showcase how these components integrate into an AI-first decisioning platform - a conversational interface bridging business users and data science, and the evolution from decision support to semi-autonomous agentic AI for “What If...” simulations that streamline inventory processes. Finally, we’ll share organizational success predictors for enterprise AI adoption.

speakers.name: Evgeny Bob
speakers.bio: Engineering nomad with 20+ years of experience solving genuinely hard problems. Spanning a wide spectrum of tech stack from RF Layer1 FPGA levels towards 100K CPUs HPC clusters. Previously working in Telco, Public Safety and Security spaces. Currently solving for Artificial Travel Intelligence helping customers to get their best memories.

sessions.title: How HP is building an AI-Ready, B2B GTM Data Infrastructure for Global Marketing
sessions.body: As marketing teams look to deliver more tailored, measurable, and efficient customer experiences, a trusted Data Infrastructure is foundational to modern martech strategy. In this session, Luis Alonso, Head of Data Strategy & Engineering for Global Martech at HP, will share how HP is approaching customer data, identity, and analytics to support global marketing use cases across segmentation, activation, measurement, and AI. Attendees will learn what it takes to build a scalable customer data foundation that connects marketing ambition with governed, enterprise-ready data infrastructure.

sessions.title: How Mastercard Turns Transaction Data into Trusted Merchant Insights with AI
sessions.body:
We are the first team at Mastercard to build an AI-powered, API-based product on Databricks—GAIME. GAIME is a fuzzy-matching algorithm, which matches transaction/merchant descriptors with Mastercard's real-time merchant database. GAIME consists of entity recognition, candidates retrieval via embeddings + vector search and uses AI-as-a-judge to produce a final match decision.

 

The talk is organized around three foundational pillars of an AI-powered product: governance, responsible AI and quality control. We will discuss how these pillars become accelerators rather than constraints at the regulated financial sector. Finally, we will share the journey of moving GAIME from POC to production and demonstrate what role data science plays in scaling high-impact AI products within a regulated environment.

speakers.name: Tomáš Drietomský
speakers.bio: Tomáš is a Lead Data Scientist at Mastercard, overseeing a rapid prototyping team, where he architects end-to-end solutions from concept through production. He holds an MSc. in Data Science from the Technical University of Vienna and a BSc. in Computer Science from the Czech Technical University in Prague. In his free time, he enjoys snowboarding or hiking in the Alps.

sessions.title: How Musinsa Built a Self-Optimizing Semantic Layer on Databricks
sessions.body:
Musinsa, South Korea's #1 fashion platform ($3.4B GMV, 8,000+ brands, 10M+ users, 13 countries), faced an architecture trilemma where every pipeline forced trade-offs between productivity, latency and cost. The root cause was not technology but a mental model: "build a table before you analyze." This caused "Organizational Amnesia": marts preserved results but lost the logic. We built a TVF-based semantic layer on Databricks SQL, shifting from "which table to query" to "what logic to compose." Four time-standardized TVFs, demand-driven caching (CTVF) on Delta Lake, and three AI agents (AI/BI Genie, MCP) enable self-optimizing analytics managed via Unity Catalog.

 

Results: 75% fewer managed assets (1,000 to 250), 98% faster analysis (7 days to 2 hours), 3.6x self-service increase (15% to 55%).

 

Attendees leave with a trilemma framework and concrete TVF patterns. Includes a live SQL demo.

speakers.name: Junyoung Chang
speakers.bio:
Junyoung Chang is a Data Engineer at Musinsa, Korea's leading fashion platform, where he drives the architecture behind one of Asia's most complex e-commerce data ecosystems. Over the past years across quick-commerce, e-commerce, crypto platforms, EV mobility and fashion tech, he has built critical data infrastructure from zero, spanning real-time pipelines, lineage systems, schema management, and semantic layers, with a consistent focus on solving the productivity-latency-cost trilemma that most data teams quietly accept as inevitable.
His broader mission is empowering every colleague to access trusted data easily and accurately, turning data-driven decisions into an organizational default rather than a privilege.

sessions.title: How Nubank Migrated to Databricks SQL Reducing Costs by 40% and Doubling Queries
sessions.body:
At Nubank, we successfully migrated to Databricks SQL over 12 months, addressing the needs of our large-scale data environment with 17k users, 40MM monthly queries, and operations globally serving 100MM+ customers. Main goals: improve cost efficiency, enhance scalability, and maintain business continuity during explosive growth.

 

Key aspects:

  • Zero-downtime throughout the 12-month migration period
  • Successfully scaling platform to handle 100% query growth (20MM to 40MM monthly queries)
  • Comprehensive workload migration supporting 17k users globally
  • +40% annual cost savings 
  • Leverage of UC for centralized data governance in highly regulated FSI industry

 

This migration significantly improved our cost structure, enhanced our ability to support business growth and provided a scalable foundation for serving LATAM’s largest fintech, ultimately demonstrating that platform transformation and business velocity can succeed simultaneously in highly regulated environments.

speakers.name: Vinicius Pessoa Duarte
speakers.bio: Brazilian, graduated in Computer Science by the University of São Paulo, has been working for the last 6 years as a Machine Learning Engineer at Nubank, focusing in MLOps and Data Engineering.

sessions.title: How Open Lakehouse Architectures Drive Data and AI Platform Modernization
sessions.body:
At GEODIS, we have launched a complete data and AI cloud platform modernization with the three main objectives. First, reduce Platform engineer workload with a range of best of breed managed services—including Databricks. Second, keep all the development and investment done on our previous architecture "compatible" with the new one—no bing bang. And last and most importantly, keep the platform fully open, interroperable and modular.

 

In that context, we have been able to integrate with our legacy Cloudera technology in MS Azure new components—Astronomer, Privacera, Databricks and Starburst, relying on open standards and technologies—full Apache Iceberg™ data lake, catalog interroparability and Apache Spark™ data quality validation.

 

I propose to discuss the challenges we have faced like Iceberg interroperability—Iceberg v2 vs v3, multi-engine integration—Databricks, Starbrust/Trino and Cloudera, and migration strategy—performance and interroperability enforcement.

speakers.name: Delio Amato
speakers.bio: Delio began his career at GEODIS a little over 20 years ago. He started on the Infrastructure side, where he was responsible for leading the systems production and datacenter teams. Since 2019, he has held the position of Chief Architect Officer, overseeing Enterprise Architecture and Urbanization for the group. His first mission in this area was to build a common data stack for all the logistics company’s business lines. Since early 2024, the role of Chief Data Officer has been added to his responsibilities within the Architecture domain. His mission is now to bring the two areas together with a pragmatic and efficient approach to Data Management

speakers.name: Vitor Lundberg
speakers.bio: Data Transport Specialist

sessions.title: How Pfizer and REDCap Cloud Modernized Clinical Data Sharing
sessions.body:
Pfizer has transformed clinical trial data exchange by moving from manual, batch-oriented ingestion to a real-time, cross-organizational architecture. Previously, fragmented systems delayed data access and complicated collaboration with research partners. This session explains how Pfizer and RCC used Delta Sharing and UC to enable secure, live data access across different cloud providers and platforms.

 

What you will learn

  • Real-time architecture: move from 24-hr batch cycles to 5-min readiness
  • Cross-cloud sharing: share live data between Azure, AWS and external CDMS platforms without egress complexity
  • Simplified governance: managing strict Life Sciences compliance and data privacy at scale using Unity Catalog
  • Operational efficiency: reducing costs by consolidating legacy orchestration into serverless compute and unified workflows.
  • Interoperability: facilitated direct sharing between REDCap Cloud’s CDMS and Pfizer’s internal analytics environment for faster clinical decision-making

speakers.name: Jaya Prakash Rao
speakers.bio:
Software and services executive with 35 years of extensive general management and strategic IS background for Information Technology companies.

Specialties: Enterprise software, corporate strategy, mergers and acquisitions, business / alliances development, developing new market initiatives, new products, and services delivery.

speakers.name: Jennifer Rola
speakers.bio: A data and analytics leader focused on transforming complex, regulated data ecosystems into scalable platforms for AI-driven innovation. Specializes in building enterprise architectures that activate data—enabling real-time insights, advanced analytics, and machine learning at scale across global organizations. Working at the intersection of clinical data and cloud platforms, has led the transformation of fragmented data landscapes into interoperable, production-grade ecosystems. Challenges the tradeoff between governance and speed, demonstrating that innovation and compliance can be engineered together. Known for advancing data products, metadata-driven architectures, and secure access models that drive enterprise AI adoption.

sessions.title: How Photon Unlocks New Performance Gains for Streaming
sessions.body:
Databricks’ Photon engine has revolutionized Spark execution, delivering state-of-the-art query performance and cost efficiency. While many Structured Streaming workloads already benefit from this vectorized execution engine, a subset of streaming-specific operators has historically relied on the standard JVM execution model, leaving potential optimization on the table. Until now.

 

In this session, we reveal our recent engineering initiatives to expand Photon coverage to these critical streaming operators. We will dive into the technical journey of “Photonizing” these components, detailing the complex engineering challenges we overcame to bring vectorized execution to stateful and streaming-specific logic.

 

Attendees will see side-by-side performance benchmarks demonstrating how these enhancements translate into lower latency, higher throughput, and reduced Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for streaming pipelines

speakers.name: Siying Dong
speakers.bio: Siying Dong is a software engineer specializing in database engines and large-scale distributed systems. He is currently at Databricks, focusing on Spark Structured Streaming. Previously, during his tenure at Meta, Siying worked on Hive, HDFS, and ETL systems before leading the development of RocksDB, the widely adopted high-performance key-value storage engine.

speakers.name: Huanli Wang
speakers.bio: Huanli Wang is a Software Engineer at Databricks, where he is a core contributor to Spark Structured Streaming. His work focuses on advancing large-scale stream processing, data ingestion architectures, and optimizing complex data pipelines within the Apache Spark ecosystem. Prior to joining Databricks, Huanli gained extensive industry experience as a Software Engineer at both Google and Amazon. He holds a Master of Science in Computational Science and Engineering from the Georgia Institute of Technology and a Bachelor of Engineering from Zhejiang University.

sessions.title: How Samsara Built a Multi-Agent System to Drive a 36x Lift in Meeting Bookings on Databricks
sessions.body: Samsara faced a critical bottleneck: sales reps spent 60 minutes researching each prospect, yet meeting booking rates stagnated at 0.18%. To solve this, we built 'Smart Flows' on Databricks—a multi-agent system orchestrating Agent Bricks AI agents, AI/BI Genie and a custom MCP server for deep web research. This architecture moves beyond simple automation to agentic reasoning. A supervisor agent routes tasks: the MCP server gathers account intelligence, while Genie agents query CRM data to hyper-personalize outreach. The state is managed via Lakebase (Serverless Postgres) and reusable Unity Catalog functions. The results were transformative. Prospecting time dropped to under five minutes—12x productivity—and agentic personalization drove meeting booking rates to 6.49%—a massive 36x uplift. We will demonstrate this live, generating a fully researched outreach sequence in real-time to show how agents can drive hard revenue metrics.

speakers.name: Vipul Panwar
speakers.bio:
Senior AI Engineer with over seven years of experience building production-grade AI systems across enterprise environments. He holds a Masters in Geophysical Technology from IIT Roorkee, India and began his career at Schlumberger before moving into the AI space at Databricks, where he spent three years building multi-agent frameworks, LLM-powered platforms, and internal AI tooling adopted across 50+ engineering teams.
He currently works at Samsara, focused on building platforms for agentic AI systems, LLM evaluation frameworks, RAG pipelines, and enterprise integrations using LangGraph, MCP, and the AWS/Databricks stack. His work sits at the intersection of applied AI research and backend engineering.
Based in Bangalore, India.

sessions.title: How Supercell Uses Databricks to Serve Nearly 300M Monthly Players and Prevent Player Harm
sessions.body: Supercell, the creator of hits like Clash of Clans and Brawl Stars, aims to build games that are played for years and remembered forever. To achieve this, they need to blend the art of game design with the science of hard facts. Supercell uses Databricks to democratize data access, simplify data processing and enable everyone from game designers to product managers to make hypothesis-driven decisions that keep nearly 300 million monthly players engaged. In this presentation, Supercell will describe their journey with Databricks, highlighting data ingestion with Auto Loader, part of Lakeflow Connect, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Spark Structured Streaming, orchestration with Lakeflow Jobs, governance with Unity Catalog, and the experiences from going all-in on serverless compute, all at massive scale. Presentation culminates in discussing how Trust & Safety team detects and prevents player harm with advanced machine learning algorithms built on these same data foundations.

speakers.name: Ilari Vaha-Pietila
speakers.bio: Data Scientist at Supercell

sessions.title: How TBC Bank Uses AI and Lakebase to Stop Money Laundering
sessions.body:
Anti-money laundering (AML) teams are buried under fragmented tools, scattered data, and manual workflows. Adding more rules has not solved the problem. TBC Bank took a different path, consolidating intelligence on Databricks to create a unified, AI-powered investigation environment.

 

This session shows the production use cases in action: a counterparty AML search engine across sanctions, internal, and external watchlists; an AI engine comparing invoices, contracts, and customs documents; a transaction purpose scanner detecting dual-use and restricted goods; and Genie for natural-language analytics. All built on a shared Lakehouse and delivered through one investigative workspace using Databricks Apps and Lakebase.

 

The result is a fundamental shift in how AML works at TBC Bank: from reactive monitoring to contextual, AI-assisted investigation.

speakers.name: Istvan Viz
speakers.bio:
Istvan is helping companies in Eastern Europe to democratise data and AI for their business goals, working as Enterprise Account Executive at Databricks for more than 2 years.

Beforehand I worked at Salesforce and Mulesoft for altogether almost a decade.

When I’m not at Databricks, I’m a proud dad of two amazing girls, keeping them entertained with my DJ skills.

sessions.title: How the FDA Is Scaling Secure AI with Databricks for Government
sessions.body:
AI in the public sector has moved from pilot to mission critical, and the agencies leading the way are the ones that have mastered the path from experimentation to production in FedRAMP and IL5 environments.In this session, we will share the best practices customers should follow to get their AWS GovCloud environment ready for the most secure and mission-critical workloads — covering infrastructure-as-code security patterns, governed foundation model access, lineage and auditability, and the networking configurations needed to connect Unity Catalog to the right data sources.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

 

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will then showcase their experience getting their Databricks environment ready to support the most advanced workloads using Unity Catalog and the platform's GenAI capabilities. After migrating from legacy systems to Databricks on AWS GovCloud, FDA is now using serverless compute, model serving, Unity Catalog, and Genie to modernize over 1,000 legacy dashboards into interactive, AI-powered experiences — eliminating technical debt and accelerating mission impact.

speakers.name: Filippo Seracini
speakers.bio: Joined Databricks as Product Manager in 2021, I lead the company-wide program that ensures that our customers can process data regulated by compliance standards like HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP etc. During my tenure at Databricks, I launched the Enhanced Security & Compliance Add-on and more recently, the Databricks on AWS GovCloud offering.

sessions.title: How to agentify contact center at enterprise scale
sessions.body: At Europe’s largest gas distributor, the customer contact center handled approximately 120,000 calls per month using a traditional IVR system. This resulted in 22,000 calls dropped during navigation and 10,000 calls resolved through automation. Thus the IVR was replaced with a conversational AI agent built on Databricks. The AI Gateway provides the backbone for real-time agent serving, while MLFlow tracks performance. Data is securely accessed from Unity Catalog, while the tools are served via MCP through a Databricks app. The agent interacts with callers in natural language, gathers contextual information, and accurately routes users to the correct resolution path. The solution reduced call drops during navigation by 50% and increased automated resolution by 44%. This session shares how we designed and operationalized a production-grade conversational AI on Databricks, used Unity Catalog as a governed knowledge layer for GenAI, and defined measurable KPIs.

speakers.name: Delli, Serena
speakers.bio: Serena Delli is the Head of Data & AI Architect, Engineering & Innovation at Bludigit,  Italgas' tech hub. With a background in logic research, Serena applies analytical thinking to design effective data architectures. At Bludigit, she focuses on building scalable data platforms that integrate with AI systems, implementing governance frameworks, and supporting team autonomy across departments.

speakers.name: Nicola Giorcelli
speakers.bio: Nicola is a Lead Consultant at Cluster Reply, specialising in data and AI platform architectures. With deep expertise in technologies such as Databricks and Microsoft Azure, he guides customers through their digital transformation journeys, helping them unlock the full potential of their data assets. His work focuses on designing scalable, efficient, and future-proof solutions that leverage advanced features and innovative approaches, seamlessly combining data and AI capabilities to deliver intelligent, high-performing architectures that accelerate real business value.

sessions.title: How To Be an Agentic Analyst
sessions.body: AI is changing the data analyst role — staying competitive requires a shift from manual tasks to architecting intelligent systems. This session provides a roadmap for analysts to move beyond technical toil toward building governed AI intelligence layers. We'll explore new ways of working and delivering value throughout the analytics lifecycle, and how Databricks can help. We will cover the following typical analyst journeys: accelerating data discovery and wrangling with agent mode in Databricks Assistant; ensuring data consistency by defining business semantics in the Metric View UI; enabling stakeholder self-service through conversational AI analytics with Genie; democratizing data products by connecting them to popular tools like Excel and Slack; building custom, high-impact interfaces for advanced scenarios using Databricks Apps. This session offers a blueprint for becoming an augmented analyst, delivering scalable AI services that grow with your organization.

speakers.name: Kyle Hale
speakers.bio: Kyle Hale’s journey into data and analytics began at age 8 when he created his first database to analyze baseball statistics, and hasn’t stopped yet. He’s a 20 year veteran of the data warehousing and BI space, having worn every hat from report development, modeling, and performance tuning to architecture, strategy, and governance. Having been a trusted advisor to well over 1,000 organizations big and small: Kyle has seen things.His proudest moment is being recognized by his peers at Databricks as a Data and Analytics SME - game knows game.When he’s not secretly plotting like all good BI professionals to kill Excel once and for all, he enjoys crafting synth pop soundtracks to imaginary movies, solving chess puzzles, and roaming the countryside with his wife and 4 kids in search of cool museums and awesome fried chicken. He is also an avid collector of dad jokes.

sessions.title: How to Bridge the Gap Between No-Code and Pro-Code with Lakeflow Designer
sessions.body:
Data engineering has a bottleneck: there are too many pipelines to build, not enough engineers to build them. Lakeflow Designer changes the equation by giving SQL analysts and citizen developers a visual, no-code interface to create production-grade ETL pipelines, backed by the same engine that powers Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP).

 

This session explores the full Lakeflow spectrum. We'll start with Lakeflow Designer's drag-and-drop canvas and GenAI assistant, showing how a business analyst can build a medallion pipeline in minutes without writing code. Then we'll show how a data engineer extends that same pipeline with custom Python logic, data quality expectations stored in Unity Catalog, and Data Quality Monitoring with anomaly detection.

 

We'll demonstrate how Lakeflow Connect ingests from sources like Salesforce and PostgreSQL, how SDPs handle the transformation layer, and how Jobs orchestrate.

 

You'll see how visual and code-based interfaces coexist, enabling collaboration.

speakers.name: Germaine Ong
speakers.bio: Germaine Ong is a Senior Solutions Engineer at Databricks, working with Digital Native Business and Emerging Enterprise customers across ASEAN. Before Databricks, she spent 3.5 years at AWS helping startups and public sector enterprises in the region build and scale their cloud infrastructure. Her data journey started as a Process Engineer in the semiconductor industry, where she felt the pain of going from raw data to usable insights. Now at Databricks, she helps organizations make data accessible to everyone without losing the flexibility engineers need. It's a challenge she knows well, and one she's excited to explore in her session on Lakeflow Designer.

sessions.title: How to Build Agentic Pipelines with OSS Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body: Apache Spark's pipeline story has evolved dramatically— from DStreams to Spark Structured Streaming and now Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines— each generation simplified how we reason about data. But with the rise of agentic AI and vibe coding, how do we ensure our most critical data pipelines remain deterministic, testable, and production-ready? In this session, Scott Haines (Staff Developer Advocate) and Allison Wang (Staff Software Engineer, Databricks and Spark Contributor) will dive into Spark's new Declarative Pipelines API, exploring how to harness the productivity gains of agentic workflows without sacrificing the reliability your data demands. You'll leave with practical patterns for building pipelines that are both developer-friendly and production-hardened and last but not least— open source.

speakers.name: Allison Wang
speakers.bio: Allison is a software engineer at Databricks, working on Spark SQL and PySpark. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon University.

speakers.name: Scott Haines
speakers.bio:
Scott Haines is a seasoned software engineer specializing in massive distributed data systems and streaming technologies. Over the past 18 years, he’s built and scaled data infrastructure at leading companies, including Yahoo!, Twilio, Nike, and, currently stepped into a role as a Staff Developer Advocate at Databricks.

Scott was a Databricks Beacon/MVP for five years before joining Databricks, he’s the author of books on Apache Spark and Delta Lake, and makes it his mission to help organizations successfully adopt open-source.

sessions.title: How to Build and Manage the Full Agent Lifecycle
sessions.body: Taking agents into production—coordinated, measurable, and grounded in enterprise data—is where most teams hit the wall. Fragmented components, inconsistent evaluation, and brittle orchestration turn promising prototypes into projects that never ship. This hands-on session walks through the full agent lifecycle on Databricks. You'll build modular, production-ready agents using Agent Bricks, AI Functions, and Genie Code—then orchestrate them with a Supervisor Agent that dynamically routes tasks across tools and MCP servers. We'll deploy a complete agentic application on Lakebase, fully governed through Unity AI. You'll see how to measure quality, trace behavior, and build confidence before and after deployment. Through real-world examples, you'll leave with clear patterns to build, evaluate, deploy, and scale intelligent multi-agent applications on Databricks' latest agentic platform.

speakers.name: Amber Roberts
speakers.bio: Amber Roberts is a Staff Technical Marketing Manager at Databricks, specializing in Artificial Intelligence. Previously, she was AI Growth Lead at Arize AI, building Generative AI products, Senior Product Manager for AI at Splunk, and Head of AI at Insight Data Science, driving AI strategy, product innovation, and developer enablement. She holds a Masters of Science in Astrophysics and is passionate about democratizing AI and providing education on science and technology to the public.

sessions.title: How to Build Trusted CRM Enrichment with Delta Sharing and AI Agents
sessions.body: Enterprise execution relies on trusted data, yet enrichment vendors often conflict and hierarchies drift. Manual validation is slow, and blind automation poses risks. This session details a production-grade validation system built on Databricks to transform CRM chaos into governed data layer. Using Delta Sharing feeds from various providers, we built a triangulation framework to reconcile signals across parent hierarchies, Salesforce structures, and revenue estimates. Rather than accepting data blindly, we implemented an AI governance layer that: 1. Reasons across enrichment signals to propose re-parenting. 2. Validates outputs via secondary agents to eliminate hallucinations. 3. Automates approvals based on confidence thresholds or escalates for human review. Attendees will learn to design multi-agent architectures and AI guardrails that preserve trust while accelerating planning cycles—enabling autonomous, governed workflows that improve revenue visibility at scale.

speakers.name: Petar Zoric
speakers.bio: Petar Zoric is a Senior Analytics Engineer at Databricks, where his work in GTM analytics is focused on building Databricks-on-Databricks use cases with AI engineering, LLMs, scalable data systems, and data governance — through which GTM and planning teams are supported with enriched, high-quality data and AI-powered insights. The development of data products and the application of ML and generative AI are guided by creative and analytical thinking, with the goal of improving decision-making, streamlining operations, and advancing digital transformation. He holds an MSc in Data Science from the University of Belgrade.

speakers.name: Yu Chen
speakers.bio: Yu Chen is a Manager of GTM App Engineering at Databricks, where she leads data product and solutions efforts powering go-to-market strategy. Previously, she spent nearly four years at Snowflake as a Staff Data Scientist, where she built LLM-powered chatbots to simplify data access and automate sales workflows. Before that, she was a Data Scientist at BP, applying machine learning, NLP, and deep learning across energy production and safety-critical applications. Yu holds an M.S. in Applied Analytics from Columbia University and a B.E. in Geological/Geophysical Engineering from Sun Yat-sen University.

sessions.title: How to Evaluate Your Agents From First Benchmark to CI/CD
sessions.body: If your team is building agents, evaluation is the difference between a demo that works and a product you can actually rely on. But most teams don't know where to start — which metrics matter, how to build a benchmark, how to automate tests, or how to catch regressions before they reach users.In this how-to session, we walk through agent evaluation end-to-end: defining your first benchmark, choosing the right judges and metrics for your use case, automating evaluation across prompts and workflows, and building a CI/CD loop that catches regressions before they hit production. We'll share practical patterns from real production teams and show how MLflow ties it all together.You'll leave with a concrete playbook for evaluating agents from first test to continuous quality at scale — and the confidence to ship agents that keep getting better with every iteration.

speakers.name: Max Fisher
speakers.bio: Max is a Lead Solutions Architect at Databricks where he advises customers on building scalable data and AI platforms on Databricks. Max is passionate about helping customers understand how to get real value out of the investments their data teams make in building on Databricks. Max focuses heavily on how to operationalize data science and AI efforts and has deep expertise in guiding teams on how to go from experimentation to real, production outcomes with ML + AI projects.

speakers.name: Wenwen Xie
speakers.bio:
Wenwen Xie is an experienced Machine Learning and Generative AI Solutions Architect at Databricks, based in Jersey City, New Jersey. At Databricks, Wenwen specializes in the design and deployment of advanced ML systems, focusing heavily on model evaluation and validation frameworks. She is particularly passionate about Evaluation-Driven Development, advocating strongly for integrating robust model evaluation as a foundational practice in ML system design.
Prior to joining Databricks, Wenwen served briefly as a Data Scientist Lead Vice President at J.P. Morgan. Her earlier role as Senior Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer at LexisNexis significantly shaped her expertise in generative AI and natural language processing (NLP).

sessions.title: How to Fast-track Production Apps with Agentic Coding Tools
sessions.body: Coding agents like Claude Code are quickly becoming the default way developers build — but on their own, they lack the context and tool access they need to be effective in real enterprise environments. Without workspace-aware grounding, they generate plausible-looking code that doesn't actually ship.In this session, we show how the Databricks AI Dev Kit turns a general-purpose coding agent into a Databricks-native developer. By giving agents secure access to workspace context, data, and tools, they can make informed decisions and take real actions — creating assets, querying data, and updating workflows directly in your environment. We'll also demonstrate how MLflow brings observability to coding agents, so you can trace behavior, debug issues, and understand how decisions are made in production.You'll walk away with the blueprint to move from standalone coding agents to fully integrated, context-aware systems that actually get work done.

speakers.name: Austin Choi
speakers.bio:
Austin is a Delivery Solutions Architect (DSA) at Databricks who specializes in Data Science and GenAI implementation. His background in Data Science at his past roles at Deloitte, IBM and Cisco have propelled him forward in the GenAI space. As a DSA, he has helped numerous customers design creative GenAI solutions on Databricks by the platform with the latest open source technology. His passion in educating and discovery drives him to help people, no matter the problem.

In his spare time, he enjoys building PCs, swimming and playing with his two cats. As an extrovert, he organizes and builds young adult Catholic communities in the Los Angeles area while giving back where he can to the broader community.

sessions.title: How to Govern and Audit Your Coding Agent Usage with Databricks
sessions.body: As coding agents like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code become embedded in daily development workflows, enterprises face a new challenge: how to govern and audit AI-assisted code generation at scale. Without centralized visibility, organizations risk exposing sensitive data, losing track of usage, and failing to meet security and compliance requirements.In this session, we'll show how Databricks enables end-to-end governance for coding agents across the enterprise. You'll learn how to enforce fine-grained permissions, track usage and costs across teams, and capture complete audit trails of prompts, responses, and tool interactions. We'll also cover how to apply consistent policies across providers — so developers can move fast with coding agents while maintaining the control, visibility, and compliance production environments demand.You'll walk away with the patterns to unlock coding agents safely across your organization — without creating a new compliance liability.

sessions.title: How to Implement Observability to Reduce Agent Sprawl
sessions.body: As AI agents proliferate, organizations are hitting a new kind of architectural debt: agent sprawl. The real issue isn't just fragmented tooling — teams can't trace how agents make decisions, monitor usage across models and tools, or enforce consistent policies once agents reach production.This session shows how observability and control work together to scale agents responsibly. You'll see how MLflow traces every agent decision, evaluates outputs, and closes the feedback loop; how AI Gateway enforces policies and tracks usage across models and tools; and how Unity Catalog ties it all together for unified governance — across low-code builders, high-code frameworks, and MCP integrations.Through a live demo and real customer architectures, you'll leave with the patterns to debug failures, monitor cost and latency, and scale agent systems that are observable, controllable, and production-ready.

speakers.name: Alkis Polyzotis
speakers.bio: Alkis Polyzotis is a technical lead working on tools that help Databricks customers improve the quality of their data and AI assets. Prior to joining Databricks, he worked at Google in the TensorFlow Extended project and in Google's internal dataset search, and before that he held a faculty position at UC Santa Cruz.

speakers.name: Arthur Dooner
speakers.bio:
I am an SSA at Databricks specializing in Enterprise Data Science: distilling real world applications of emerging technologies in AI and ML to apply them for Enterprise scale, value, security, and quality.

My strongest specialization is in building Generative AI Enterprise Applications, but other specializations of mine include:
- Compound AI System Design
- MLOps
- Advanced ML Evaluation and Testing
- Azure Infrastructure (I was a Microsoft CSA before Databricks)
- Delta Table Optimization

sessions.title: How to Modernize Your ETL with Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
Did you ever wonder why Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) do not allow dynamic parameters or partial recalculations for specific dates? Or why for-loops are restricted in table definitions? Furthermore, how do you choose between a Streaming Table and a Materialized View?

 

These are common struggles users face when starting. While often perceived as tool limitations, these hurdles usually stem from attempting to apply imperative habits to a declarative framework.

 

In this session we will discuss real-world customer examples to demonstrate how to transition from imperative to declarative approach.Stop fighting the framework and start leveraging the declarative paradigm for more resilient data engineering.

speakers.name: Aleksandra Chashchina
speakers.bio:
Aleksandra Chashchina is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, where she partners with enterprise customers on the bleeding edge of the Databricks platform - tackling advanced use cases and the newest
capabilities before they hit the mainstream. Her focus spans Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Lakeflow Connect, and DBSQL. She is passionate about making advanced data engineering patterns
approachable for practitioners moving from legacy ETL tools to a lakehouse
architecture. Customers keep her humble by regularly stumping her with their

sessions.title: How to Run Marketing Campaigns on Databricks
sessions.body:
This session introduces how marketers – and the data teams that support them – can run agentic campaign planning, insights and execution on Databricks, where AI agents use lakehouse data and models to decide what content to send, when to send it, and to which audience. Join us to see how agentic workflows close the loop between customer data, marketing decisions, and execution.

 

In this session, you’ll learn: 

  • How to build audiences for marketing campaigns using data in Lakehouse 
  • How to connect to marketing execution channels via reverse ETL
  • How to map personalization variables and trigger one-off and micro-batch sends
  • How performance signals like opens, clicks, and conversions can flow back into lakehouse

speakers.name: Cindy Jiang
speakers.bio: Cindy is a Product Manager at Databricks, working on making UC Managed Tables simple and performant. Before joining Databricks, Cindy graduated from the M&T Program at the University of Pennsylvania with an MSE and BAS in Computer Science and a BS from Wharton.

speakers.name: Josh Braun
speakers.bio: Josh is a Staff Product Designer at Databricks focused on designing intuitive experiences for data and AI practitioners. Throughout his career, he has specialized in creating products that connect technical teams with the stakeholders they serve, making powerful data platforms easier to understand, adopt, and use.

sessions.title: How to Scale Enterprise Governance and Administration with Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
As organizations scale data and AI, governance often becomes fragmented across disparate environments, metastores, and teams. When assets are distributed, policies drift and visibility becomes limited, making it increasingly complex to manage access consistently at scale.

 

In this session, we will preview new architectural enhancements within Unity Catalog designed to bridge these infrastructure boundaries. We’ll share a first look at upcoming capabilities that move beyond traditional silos to enable a single, consolidated view of your entire data and AI estate.

 

Discover how we are building an automated control plane that allows you to design and operate a unified governance system. Learn how these advancements will help your organization eliminate operational overhead, ensure fine-grained access control, and provide a single source of truth for discovery—regardless of how your underlying infrastructure is distributed.

speakers.name: Zeashan Pappa
speakers.bio:
Zeashan is a technology executive and architect with 20+ years of expertise in enterprise software architecture, engineering, consulting, and project management.

Zeashan is a product manager at Databricks, focusing on catalog, governance, and security products.

sessions.title: How to scale governance to External Engines with Unity Catalog Open APIs
sessions.body:
Enterprises are increasingly challenged to scale data and AI initiatives across diverse tools, clouds, and teams without fragmenting governance or slowing innovation. 

 

This session explores how organizations are using Unity Catalog as a unified governance layer for enabling secure, interoperable data access across engines and open table formats such as Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg with fine-grained controls. 

 

By simplifying access management through automated, identity-based credentials and applying a single, consistent policy framework, enterprises can reduce operational complexity while maintaining strong security and compliance. In this session, we will cover Lakehouse architecture patterns with UC Open APIs, and we will also show a live demo. 

 

Attendees will learn how this approach drives governed collaboration, speeds up analytics and AI workloads, and fuels business growth in multi-engine environments.

speakers.name: Dipankar Kushari
speakers.bio:
Dipankar is a Lead Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he partners with enterprise customers to design and deliver cutting-edge data analytics and AI platforms. With deep expertise in distributed computing, he tackles complex, large-scale data challenges and translates them into scalable, production-ready solutions.
Before Databricks, Dipankar served as a Senior Solutions Architect at AWS, where he built a strong thought-leadership presence — authoring technical blogs, videos, and whitepapers — while guiding customers in architecting robust cloud analytics solutions.

sessions.title: How to Securely Access data with Lakehouse Federation Across AWS Glue, Snowflake, BigQuery, and Fabric to Innovate Faster
sessions.body:
Your data can be spread across multiple data vendors: AWS Glue, Snowflake, BigQuery, Postgres, etc. This is the session that provides you insight on how to govern, secure, and query it across different teams without having to copy data.

 

In this session we will cover Lakehouse Federation and how Unity Catalog can be the catalog of catalogs for your entire estate. We'll demo how federation works, how customers are using it at scale in production, and talk about how the Iceberg ecosystem is evolving and what you should plan ahead for next. We'll show how you can use Databricks' latest AI features like Genie on your open lakehouse and how you can upgrade your lakehouse over time to benefit from everything the platform has to offer.

speakers.name: John Spencer
speakers.bio: John is a Product Manager at Databricks, dedicated to making Unity Catalog work seamlessly with customers’ ecosystems of tools and platforms so they can easily access, govern, and use their data. Previously, he worked at Microsoft and graduated from Stanford with a BS in Computer Science.

sessions.title: How to Solve the Context Gap: Engineering Reliable AI Agents
sessions.body: The biggest hurdle to production AI isn't the model — it's the context window. What an agent sees, when, and in what format determines whether it reasons correctly or hallucinates. Most teams stitch together RAG, tools, and state management ad hoc, then struggle to evaluate whether their context decisions actually work. This session is a deep dive into context engineering on Databricks: the systematic practice of designing what agents see at every step. You'll learn how to configure RAG systems that go beyond basic retrieval, use Model Context Protocol (MCP) for secure tool and API integration, and manage long-term memory across complex agent workflows. You'll leave with a playbook for building measurement pipelines that empirically evaluate your context decisions — and the patterns to ship agents that stay reliable when users, data, and tasks evolve.

speakers.name: Michelle JanneyCoyle
speakers.bio: Michelle JanneyCoyle is an AI Forward Deployed Engineer at Databricks with a background in data science and NLP. She works with customers to build production-ready AI applications that use structured and unstructured data to support real business workflows.

speakers.name: Badr Slimani
speakers.bio: Senior AI Engineer with the Databricks AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team

sessions.title: How to Turn Every Business User Into a Decision Maker With AI/BI and Databricks One
sessions.body:
"How to Turn Every Business User Into a Decision Maker With AI/BI and Databricks One" is a practical session for leaders who want to move beyond static dashboards and operationalize data-driven decisions at scale. Youssef Mrini and Josue Bogran show how Unity Catalog Metric Views, AI/BI dashboards and AI/BI Genie, delivered through the new Databricks One experience, replace fragmented reports and spreadsheet chaos with trusted, conversational analytics.

 

See how governed KPIs create a shared semantic layer so sales, finance and operations speak the same language while still moving fast. Through live demos, follow a business user from the Databricks One homepage to a dashboard, then asking “why is this changing?” in natural language and exploring scenarios on top of trusted metrics, no SQL required.

 

Leave with a blueprint to turn report consumers into proactive decision makers and close the gap between insight and action.

speakers.name: Josue Bogran
speakers.bio:
Josue Bogran is a Databricks MVP, product advisor, and VP of Data + AI Architecture at zeb.co, a Databricks and AWS partner with 1,500+ team members.

He’s had the privilege of learning from and interviewing Databricks leaders including Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, and Reynold Xin, and has helped shape several Databricks products behind the scenes.

Josue also advises product companies such as EnrollHere.com, a fully integrated platform for carriers and agencies.

He lives in North Carolina with his wife and five children, soon to be six. When not working on data and AI, you’ll find him on a pickleball court.

To check out my videos interviews and product demos with Databricks leaders:
