2) YouTube.com/@JosueBogranChannel

speakers.name: Youssef Mrini
speakers.bio: Youssef Mrini is part of the pre-sales team in the EMEA Region at Databricks and helps customers to adopt the databricks technologies. Youssef is an ex-data engineer. He holds a degree in big Data and have been working on various areas for the last couple of years

sessions.title: How to Vibe Code Successfully: Make Your Agents Love Databricks
sessions.body:
To get the most out of your coding agents, you need to set them up for success, especially when letting them loose against a large platform like Databricks. In this talk, we will dive deep into Agent Experience (AX) for building Databricks Apps and Agent.

 

We will discuss AX as a new discipline similar to Developer Experience (DX) and review the most effective tools and best practices for successfully steering agents. We'll discuss how to set up your local development environment for building on Databricks. From agent skills and MCP to reference codebases and AppKit, we will see how these components compose together. By the end, your agents will know Databricks inside and out, allowing you to vibe code more successfully on top of the Databricks platform.

speakers.name: Andre Landgraf
speakers.bio: Andre is a passionate developer from Germany who loves building for the web. Based in the Bay Area, he is a Staff Developer Advocate at Databricks. He was previously a Senior Software Engineer at LinkedIn and holds master’s degrees in Information Systems and Computer Science. In his free time, he brings the community together through All Things Web events in San Francisco.

sessions.title: How Unified Data Can Help Secure the Future of Global Food Production
sessions.body:
Agriculture generates vast streams of information—from lab research to satellite imagery, factory sensors and farmers’ mobile apps. Each raw field, whether in a data table or on the farm, carries its own fragment of truth. The real opportunity lies in unifying these fields into connected, trustworthy insight.

 

This keynote shows how data mesh principles and Genie help teams break silos, democratize access and enable proactive decisions that lift yields and strengthen resilience. By bringing together the wisdom hidden across our digital and physical fields, we build a future where every field can help fill every plate.

speakers.name: Thomas Jung
speakers.bio: Thomas Jung is the Chief Data Officer at Syngenta Group, transforming agriculture through Data and AI. Syngenta helps millions of farmers around the world to grow safe and nutritious food, while taking care of the planet. Thomas has a strong track record of technology-powered business transformation, with a career spanning across IT consulting, M&A integration and digital R&D.

sessions.title: How Versant Media is Unlocking New Business Value in an Uncertain Media Landscape with Publisher360
sessions.body: Discover how Versant Media is building a scaled data and AI platform to power business teams across the enterprise, from subscriptions, to advertising, to content platforms and more, with a scrappy team and unprecedented time to market.

sessions.title: How We Built Agent Mode in Genie Spaces
sessions.body: Agentic analytics promises to go beyond answering questions enabling AI to investigate, reason, and synthesize insights across complex data. But building systems that do this reliably is far from simple.Genie Agent Mode introduces a new approach to conversational analytics, where AI can explore multiple hypotheses, interact with data iteratively, and generate structured explanations. Under the hood, this requires careful orchestration of planning, validation, and context management to ensure results are both accurate and trustworthy.In this session, we’ll go behind the scenes to explore how Genie Agent Mode works and what it takes to make agentic analytics production-ready:- How Genie Agent Mode plans and executes multi-step analytical workflows- How the system maintains context and evaluates intermediate results- How accuracy and reliability are enforced through validation and safeguards- Key lessons learned building agentic systems for real-world data use cases

speakers.name: Alan Lee
speakers.bio: I'm a Databricks engineer on the Applied AI team working on Genie. I was a core contributor to Genie Agent, taking it from private preview to general access.

speakers.name: Ryan Ziegler
speakers.bio: Ryan Ziegler is a software engineer on the Genie team at Databricks focused on building high-quality, helpful agentic experiences. He has most recently worked on agent monitoring and steering, token use optimization, and building new interfaces to better leverage agents.

sessions.title: Human-in-the-Loop Compliance at Global Scale: Databricks Apps + Lakebase Casework + SME Labeling
sessions.body: In this session, we share a practical pattern we call “PolicyOps” on Databricks: converting long policy documents into cited, versioned, queryable policy units, then operationalizing a human‑in‑the‑loop workflow that captures domain SME judgment as structured labels. We’ll show how to parse and structure large policy PDFs into clause-level records (including page-aware citations), how to extract decision criteria into queryable tables, and how to connect policy interpretation to real operational review.We’ll then demonstrate an SME review queue built with Databricks Apps — designed for high-signal feedback (not just thumbs up/down) — with Lakebase used to manage case workflow state (assignment, status, reviewer actions, approvals). The result is a scalable workflow that keeps humans in control of edge cases while systematically converting implicit SME knowledge into reusable labels and corrections that improve quality over time.

speakers.name: Salman Chaudhry
speakers.bio: Salman is an AI leader at Mastercard, where he architects and delivers AI systems at enterprise scale. His current focus is on agentic AI solutions that tackle complex regulatory and compliance challenges across global operations. He's driven by a core belief: the most powerful AI systems aren't the ones that replace human judgment, they're the ones that amplify it. His work sits at the intersection of applied AI/ML, large-scale system design, and real-world business impact. He's passionate about building intelligent systems that are composable, resilient, and fundamentally human-centric, designed to help people do their best thinking, not think for them.

sessions.title: Implementing Data Governance with Unity Catalog
sessions.body: This hands-on course provides a comprehensive foundation for managing governed data environments using Unity Catalog. It is designed for data engineers, platform administrators, and analytics engineers responsible for organizing, securing, and operationalizing data at scale across modern Lakehouse architectures.The course begins with an overview of Unity Catalog’s role within a cloud deployment, including how it integrates with account-level architecture and administrative responsibilities. You will explore how metastores are created and configured, how workspaces are attached, and how governance boundaries are established across environments. Through guided exercises, you will learn how data is logically and physically organized, including the use of object storage, managed and external locations, and secure access patterns for underlying storage systems.As the course progresses, you will design and implement effective data organization strategies using catalogs and schemas, translating business structures such as business units, regions, and environments into scalable naming conventions and governance models. You will apply fine-grained access control using Unity Catalog’s permission model, including ownership, management privileges, and inherited access patterns, enabling secure, least-privilege data access across teams.The course also introduces foundational interoperability concepts through Lakehouse Federation, enabling access to external data systems while maintaining centralized governance. You will explore how to bring existing data into Unity Catalog, configure secure access to external locations, and manage permissions consistently across internal and external data sources.The course concludes with practical implementation workflows, where you will create and manage catalogs, schemas, and permissions using both the UI and SQL interfaces. You will troubleshoot common configuration challenges, apply governance best practices, and establish patterns for isolating development, testing, and production environments.By the end of the course, you will be able to design, implement, and manage a secure, well-organized data governance framework using Unity Catalog, ensuring scalable access control, clear data ownership, and consistent data organization across your Lakehouse.

sessions.title: Implementing Data Governance with Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
This hands-on course equips learners with the skills to design, implement, and manage catalog structures and large-scale data organization using Unity Catalog in Databricks. Participants will learn to configure secure and scalable storage integrations, as well as implement access controls and isolation strategies for effective data governance.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces and notebooks
  • Intermediate SQL experience, including creating tables, views, and functions, and managing database object permissions
  • Understanding of Unity Catalog's hierarchical object model (metastore, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, models)
  • Basic understanding of data governance concepts, including access control, row-level security, column masking, and fine-grained access controls
  • Basic knowledge of data lineage, metadata management, and cloud computing concepts (compute, storage, identity management)

sessions.title: Inside Adobe’s Near Real-Time Cloud Spend Monitoring System
sessions.body:
Cloud costs are rising faster than budgets, yet teams often discover expensive operations only after the spend has occurred. We moved from reactive cost reporting to proactive, near real-time monitoring—reducing SQL warehouse costs by 51% and Serverless compute by 14% in less than 30 days.

 

This talk covers how we built a production-grade monitoring system managing millions in annual Databricks spend across petabyte-scale data, 94,000+ jobs, and millions of compute hours, with 15-minute monitoring cycles and zero infrastructure cost.

 

The key challenge was attribution: Databricks assigns SQL warehouse costs to warehouse creators, not query executors, obscuring who drives spend. We solved this by combining Databricks system tables—`billing.usage`, `query.history`, and `compute.warehouse_events`—to enable query-level cost attribution without added compute.

 

Attendees will learn the architecture, implementation patterns and reusable strategies to build proactive cost monitoring at any scale.

speakers.name: Rajeshwari Raghuraman
speakers.bio:
Raji Raghuraman is a Senior Data Science Engineering Manager at Adobe, where she leads the Data Engineering team in the Digital Imaging Data Science (DIDS) team responsible for analytics infrastructure supporting Photoshop, Lightroom, and Fresco. With over 20 years of experience in AI-driven analytics, data architecture, and engineering leadership, she specializes in building petabyte-scale data platforms that balance performance, cost, and compliance.

At Adobe, Raji is driving the Data Roadmap Strategy for the Digital Imaging Data Science team through thought leadership on Privacy Automation Framework, scalable architectures for their Petabyte scale data, while achieving significant cost reductions through innovative monitoring and automation.

Prior to Adobe, Raji held senior Data engineering Manager role at eBay in Risk Decision Science. She holds an M.S. in Software Systems, M.C.A., and completed MIT Professional Education in Applied Data Science.

sessions.title: Inside Nav-AI: Accenture's No-Code Agent Factory, Powered by Databricks Apps and Lakebase
sessions.body: Accenture's Nav-AI lets business users build and deploy AI agents through a visual interface — no deep technical expertise required. Every customer deployment used to be a bespoke engineering project: weeks of custom work per cloud, fragile ingestion, and no foundation for agents to improve over time.In this session, Accenture shows how Nav-AI was rebuilt on Databricks to become a true product — using Databricks Apps for one-click multi-cloud deployment, the medallion architecture for reliable customer data ingestion, Model Serving for the agent runtime, and Lakebase for persistent state and self-improvement. Expect live demos from real deployments and a concrete blueprint for turning agents from a science project into a repeatable platform.

sessions.title: Inside our Lakeflow Journey at SEGA: Scaling Streaming Analytics Across Titles
sessions.body:
At SEGA Europe, we process billions of game telemetry events daily to power real-time analytics for live ops, player experience optimisation, and business intelligence. We have rebuilt our streaming platform on Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, moving from fragile, manually managed jobs to a resilient, self-healing lakehouse architecture. This approach was battle-tested during the launch of Football Manager 2026, where scale and reliability were critical.

 

This session shares our production journey with Lakeflow—the wins, lessons, and unexpected challenges of operating at gaming scale. We’ll cover our migration from legacy streaming infrastructure, achieving sub-minute latency, and handling evolving event schemas. Topics include stream fan-out from Kinesis to Bronze, schema evolution, late and out-of-order events, data quality checks, performance tuning, and cost control. We’ll also share quantified results from FM26 and practical patterns for teams evaluating Lakeflow at scale.

speakers.name: Anastasiya Lavrenchuk
speakers.bio: A data engineer with a background in fin-tech who develops and maintains several cutting-edge data technology projects across SEGA. Databricks forms the backbone of SEGA’s data platform, which the Data team utilises to underpin a variety of streaming, machine learning and LLM use cases.

speakers.name: Sanjay Ashok
speakers.bio: Sanjay Ashok is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, acting as a technical advisor to digital-native and emerging enterprises across EMEA. He assists customers in evaluating, adopting, and scaling the Lakehouse platform for production AI and analytics workloads. With over 10 years’ experience in AI/ML, big data, and cloud architecture, he has worked across the US, India, and the UK, including at AWS, developing cloud-native data and ML solutions. At Databricks, he guides organisations from technical strategy to data-driven business transformation in gaming and fintech. His work covers GenAI applications, ML pipelines, real-time analytics, and self-serve BI dashboards. He holds an MS from the University at Buffalo.

sessions.title: Insights at Scale With Agentic AI: How AI Ready Data is Transforming Commercial Life Sciences
sessions.body:
Pharma leaders face pressure to accelerate commercialization and improve launch performance, yet many commercial analytics teams are held back by fragmented data, brittle dashboards and heavy manual insight generation. At the same time, generative AI is rapidly advancing from copilots to fully-agentic systems, creating new opportunities and risks in regulated environments.

 

In this session, Merck and ZS show how Merck is deploying Agentic AI using Databricks AI/BI Genie and Agent Bricks to build domain aware data agents on trusted, governed data products. These agents automate high-friction workflows across marketing, field effectiveness and brand performance, cutting time to insight by over 50% and enabling faster, more consistent decisions.

 

We will share Merck’s blueprint for building context-rich data products, embedding business semantics and orchestrating agent workflows that integrate with existing BI—offering a practical, scalable architecture for Agentic AI in pharma.

speakers.name: Anuya Aher
speakers.bio: Anuya Aher is a senior Data & Analytics leader with extensive experience driving enterprise data strategy, analytics transformation, and AI‑ready data ecosystems. As Director, Data Analysis, she leads initiatives that deliver scalable, trusted data and analytics products enabling faster, higher‑quality decision‑making across business functions. Anuya specializes in data‑as‑a‑product models, semantic design, and integrating structured and unstructured data to accelerate insights through automation, partnering closely with business and technology teams to turn complex needs into actionable analytics.

speakers.name: Nishesh Aggarwal
speakers.bio: Nishesh Aggarwal is a seasoned leader with over 15 years of experience driving product innovation and digital transformation within the healthcare and life sciences industries. A Wharton MBA, he specializes in building scalable Generative AI platforms and agentic architectures. Nishesh is a recognized expert in bridging the gap between complex data intelligence and enterprise-grade applications, focusing on autonomous AI systems that go beyond conversational interfaces to enable complex decision-making. At the Databricks Data + AI Summit, he shares insights on deploying production-ready, agentic AI frameworks to deliver business value at scale.

sessions.title: Integrating Lakebase Databases into Intelligent Applications
sessions.body:
This hands-on course teaches Databricks application developers how to use Lakebase as the operational database for intelligent, data-driven applications on Databricks. Learners explore how Lakebase enables applications powered by analytics, BI, and AI. Through guided exercises, the course covers Lakebase core concepts and architecture, provisioning and managing database instances, connecting from Databricks SQL, notebooks, and external clients, and applying best practices for connection management, permissions, and environment configuration. By the end of the course, developers will be able to confidently integrate Lakebase into production-ready data and AI applications, safely manage database resources, and unlock unified analytics and AI on live operational data.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces and notebooks
  • Intermediate SQL proficiency, including SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements
  • Intermediate Python programming experience, including functions, exceptions, and working with dictionaries and lists
  • Familiarity with OLTP fundamentals, including client-server relationships, ACID properties, database authentication, and concurrent access

sessions.title: Intelligent Document Processing With Lakeflow Connect and AI Parse
sessions.body:
Enterprise knowledge is often trapped in PDFs, images and office docs—out of reach for AI. This lightning talk will walk you through the end-to-end process for intelligent document processing.

 

We’ll showcase a demo of how to ingest this unstructured data securely and with governance using Lakeflow Connect—preserving permissions, metadata and lineage.

 

Then, see how to activate the data by deploying production-grade agentic workflows with Agent Bricks for functions like search, summarization and business intelligence.

 

We'll highlight customer success stories demonstrating how this process transforms fragmented documents into a governed foundation for data intelligence, enabling rapid, secure AI at scale.

speakers.name: Jason Ping
speakers.bio: Jason is a Product Manager on Lakeflow Connect, focusing on unstructured data ingestion.

sessions.title: Interoperability With Unity Catalog: Enabling Governed Data Access Across Platforms Beyond Databricks
sessions.body:
Many enterprises run their data across multiple platforms — Snowflake, BigQuery, OneLake, AWS Glue, Postgres. In 20 minutes we'll show you how Lakehouse Federation makes Unity Catalog the catalog of catalogs for your entire data estate.

 

You'll see demos on how to connect an external platform to UC, then run Genie across federated data with row-level security applied uniformly across every source.

speakers.name: Liran Bareket
speakers.bio:
With 25+ years of experience in the industry Liran has acquired expertise in everything that is data management and governance.
Liran has lead the UC adoption in Databricks since the introduction of the product.

speakers.name: Michael Saltzman
speakers.bio:
Michael Saltzman is a Senior Cloud Architect at Databricks
with deep expertise in cloud migrations, infrastructure architecture, and modern data platforms. Based in New York, he specializes in helping organizations design and scale secure, high-performance cloud environments across complex enterprise ecosystems. His background spans cloud networking, security, automation, and large-scale data infrastructure, with a strong focus on enabling organizations to modernize their analytics and AI foundations.

Michael brings a highly technical, hands-on perspective to cloud transformation initiatives, backed by advanced certifications including AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, AWS Advanced Networking Specialty, and AWS Security Specialty. He is passionate about open data architectures, platform interoperability, and helping customers operationalize modern data and AI workloads at scale.

sessions.title: Introducing Indexes for the Lakehouse
sessions.body:
Substring searches that take hours. Point lookups that scan terabytes. Pattern-matching queries that force you to maintain a separate tools alongside your lakehouse. These are problems that traditional databases solved decades ago — and that the lakehouse is now solving too.

 

In this session, we'll introduce two new indexing capabilities coming to Databricks:

  • Full-Text Search indexes for fast substring, regex, and IP-address matching with up to 20x query speedup; 
  • Standard (Secondary) indexes for needle-in-a-haystack point lookups with 30-60x speedup on non-clustered columns; 

 

We'll cover how each index type works under the hood, when to use which, and how they complement Liquid Clustering and data skipping. Then we'll show a live demo — creating indexes on real tables, running queries that previously took minutes in under seconds.

 

If you're running log analytics, SIEM workloads, UUID lookups, or any query pattern where you're scanning far more data than you need to — this session is for you.

speakers.name: Sirui Sun
speakers.bio: Sirui is a Sr. Staff Product Manager at Databricks, working on making Delta simpler and more performant. Prior to Databricks, he's spent time working on Google Cloud and at Microsoft. At the Data + AI Summit, he'd love to talk to you about your data goals and challenges!

sessions.title: Introducing Lakewatch
sessions.body:
Cyberattacks are no longer just human-operated. AI-driven threats now move at machine speed, exploiting gaps across systems while your SOC is still triaging yesterday's alerts. Traditional SIEMs weren’t built for this reality: they force painful trade-offs between data volume, retention and cost, leaving security teams flying blind with only a fraction of their telemetry in view.

 

In this session, we’ll take you inside Lakewatch, Databricks’ open, agentic SIEM built for machine-speed defense. We’ll start with the “why”: what motivated us to build something fundamentally different. Then we’ll demo how Lakewatch unifies 100% of your security, IT and business telemetry in one governed environment using open formats and Unity Catalog, with no costly duplication and no vendor lock-in. You’ll see how embedded AI agents powered by Genie Code automate threat detection and response at machine speed, and we’ll close with an exclusive peek at the roadmap and what’s coming next.

 

Whether you’re evaluating your current SIEM, dealing with runaway data costs or looking to modernize your SOC on your existing Databricks investment, this session is your practical starting point.

 

Key takeaways:

  • Why traditional SIEMs structurally fail against AI-driven threats
  • How Lakewatch unifies all your telemetry with open formats and Unity Catalog
  • How Genie agents automate detection, hunting, and response
  • A first look at the Lakewatch roadmap and what’s coming next

speakers.name: Keegan Dubbs
speakers.bio: Keegan Dubbs is a Product Manager focused on Identity Lifecycle at Databricks, where she helps shape secure and scalable user experiences. Her favorite part of the job is collecting customer feedback - she loves hearing real-world insights that directly inform the product roadmap and drive meaningful improvements. Outside of work, Keegan can often be found skiing in the mountains or daydreaming about her future golden retriever. She's passionate about building user-centric products and believes the best ideas come from listening closely to the people who use them every day.

speakers.name: Molly Limaye
speakers.bio: Molly Limaye is an Associate Product Manager on the Lakewatch team.

sessions.title: Introducing the Vibe to Value Workshop: Your Fast Track to Building Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
This is not the workshop—it’s your invitation to one. In this 20-minute lightning talk, we’ll introduce the Vibe to Value workshop: a 4-hour, hands-on experience where you install a real Databricks app and use it to learn how to build your own Databricks Apps.

 

We’ll walk through what the workshop covers, who it’s for, and why it’s different: instead of learning via slides, you learn by using an app that’s already running on Databricks, “vibe coding” your way from simple edits to a working app on top of your own data. You’ll see how the flow works end-to-end, what you’ll build, and how much you can accomplish in just one afternoon, even if you’re new to Databricks Apps.

 

You’ll leave this session with a clear understanding of the opportunity, how to sign up for the full Vibe to Value workshop, and how to coordinate with your Databricks team to bring it to your organization.

sessions.title: Introduction to Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: If you are brand new to Databricks Lakehouse and want to get a lightning tour of this intelligent data warehouse, this session is for you. Learn about the lakehouse architecture, then see how simple, streamlined interfaces are making it easier for analysts, developers, admins and business users to get their jobs done and questions answered. We’ll show how easy it is to create a warehouse, get data, transform it, build queries, create dashboards, and share with BI tools and applications. By the end of the session, you’ll be able to build a SQL warehouse in 5 minutes.

speakers.name: Justin Kolpak
speakers.bio: Justin Kolpak is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he has spent the last 3.5 years partnering with digital native and fintech customers to build scalable solutions for data engineering, data warehousing, and agentic analytics. sessions.title: Introduction to Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines: Reliable Data Pipelines Made Easy
sessions.body:
Building data pipelines often means hand-writing complex data engineering patterns like incremental processing, CDC/SCD handling, and backfills in every job.

 

Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) are the next evolution in how transformations are written in Spark by default. You declare the data you want to produce, and the platform applies proven execution semantics for you. Built on an open, declarative standard for Spark pipelines, SDP helps teams move faster on hard problems while scaling production best practices consistently.

 

In this session, you’ll see how SDP:

  • Provides a necessary foundation for agentic data pipeline development
  • Reduces the amount of custom logic required for incremental and CDC workloads
  • Makes batch and streaming pipelines easier to build, debug, and evolve over time
  • Standardizes reliability and correctness across pipelines as they scale

 

We’ll walk through concrete examples that show how declarative pipelines simplify otherwise complex data engineering patterns.

speakers.name: Zoé Durand
speakers.bio: Zoé is a Staff Product Manager on Spark Declarative Pipelines at Databricks. She holds an MBA from Stanford University, and an MS and BS in Applied mathematics from Ecole Polytechnique, France.

sessions.title: Introduction to Unified Data Engineering with Databricks Lakeflow
sessions.body:
Teams today struggle with pipeline fragility, brittle orchestration, and tool sprawl that slows delivery and increases maintenance costs. Lakeflow eliminates that friction by unifying ingestion, transformation, and orchestration on the Data Intelligence Platform, with reliability and governance built into the foundation.

 

This session shows how Databricks Lakeflow turns Spark into the most advanced execution engine for data engineering on the planet— with agentic data pipelines underpinned by managed ingestion connectors, declarative transformations, native orchestration, and intelligent incremental processing built into execution, not layered on top.

speakers.name: Ray Zhu
speakers.bio: Ray Zhu is a Director of Product Management at Databricks, where he focuses on data engineering and streaming products. He's passionate about building products that empower data practitioners of different skillsets to simplify and scale their data pipelines, enabling greater customer and business value.

sessions.title: KISS-ing Your Data+AI Platform: Rapid Multi-Cloud Migration to Databricks
sessions.body: Faced with a strategic shift toward marketplace autonomy, Adevinta transformed its global data+AI strategy by migrating from complex DIY stacks on GCP and AWS to a unified Databricks platform in under 4 ¿? months. This session, led by our Principal Architect and Product Director, provides a deep dive into how we overcame technical and organisational "old ways of working" to achieve this high-velocity transition. Beyond data engineering and data warehousing capabilities, we will focus on how we migrated our AI/ML platform to Databricks, demonstrating how a unified foundation in Unity Catalog and the Databricks AI stack has accelerated our migration and time to production, and how this foundation is now helping in our ambition to unlock even more value from data+AI across the company.

sessions.title: KRAFTON at Scale: Architecting Real-Time Game AI with MLflow & Serving
sessions.body:
This session explores KRAFTON's journey of deploying real-time AI for PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS, a title with 200M+ users. We share how a lean engineering team overcame global-scale challenges using Databricks. 1. Real-time anti-cheat MLOps: We detail the transition from an hourly batch system to a sub-minute real-time pipeline using Structured Streaming and an online feature store. By optimizing Model Serving endpoints, we drastically reduced latency and slashed costs to 1/10th, enabling just three engineers to support a massive global player base. 2. Esports win prediction: We discuss the serving strategy for Cox PH models to handle 64-player dynamics. Solutions include sequence buffering to ensure data ordering and incremental feature engineering for O(1) efficiency, delivering stable predictions with sub-200ms latency.

 

We conclude with Databricks MLOps patterns bridging the gap between research and production, alongside our roadmap for next-gen VLM-based anti-cheat.

speakers.name: Hyojun Je

At KRAFTON, he has contributed to operationalizing AI workflows and scaling analytics platforms using Databricks and modern AI technologies. Previously, he worked at PUBG Corporation, developing real-time machine learning systems for esports analytics and broadcast experiences.

sessions.title: Lakebase 101: core workflows and the Lakebase experience
sessions.body: New to Lakebase? This session walks you through the core workflows that define the Lakebase experience: provisioning a database, connecting your first application, using branching for safe development, applying point-in-time recovery, and controlling costs with autoscaling. Through live demos, you'll see how each feature maps to real-world scenarios and why running your operational database directly on the lakehouse changes what's possible for applications, analytics, and AI. No prior Lakebase experience required.

sessions.title: Lakebase and Serving Endpoints Implementation in Real-Time Pricing
sessions.body:
This breakout session presents a real-world, one of the first in Europe's FSI Industry, production implementation of Databricks Lakebase and Serving Endpoints for real-time pricing in a large-scale insurance environment. We will walk through how we implemented Databricks-native architecture for low-latency data and model access via REST APIs calls. New architecture is a replacement of external Azure PostgreSQL database and intermediate applications layers.

 

Based on experience at one of the largest insurance companies in Poland we will share how Lakebase was stress-tested on high data volumes and is being introduced to production using baby-steps approach. The session includes architecture decisions, performance observations and code-level examples.

 

Attendees will gain the practical guidance on building end-to-end, real-time and data model serving within Databricks along with a clear understanding of how Lakebase fits into architecture.

speakers.name: Klaudia Ratkowska
speakers.bio: Klaudia is a Data Engineer at ERGO Hestia, specializing in designing and managing data systems. Passionate about data and artificial intelligence, she enjoys transforming complex datasets into actionable insights and leveraging technology to drive smarter, data-driven decisions.

sessions.title: Lakeflow Connect: Cutting Enterprise Ingestion Costs by up to 90% on Databricks
sessions.body:
Enterprise CRM-to-lakehouse pipelines built on traditional third-party ingestion tools can be expensive, time-consuming to implement, and often deliver stale data batches. We replaced this with Databricks Lakeflow Connect for a Fortune 500 client — significantly reducing monthly costs, cutting setup time from weeks to hours, and achieving near-real-time CDC ingestion.

 

This talk delivers a live 7-step walkthrough: connector selection, OAuth setup, DLT pipeline config, object selection, Unity Catalog destination mapping, CDC monitoring, and production scheduling.

 

Takeaways include a cost justification framework demonstrating significant multi-year TCO savings, a migration blueprint from legacy and cloud-native ingestion tools, and governance best practices with Unity Catalog lineage.

speakers.name: Rishabh Pandey
speakers.bio: Rishabh Pandey is a Databricks MVP (2025, 2026) and data engineering professional at Celebal Technologies, leading end-to-end delivery from solution design to performance optimization and debugging complex ETL pipelines. He specializes in Delta Lake, Structured Streaming, Delta Live Tables (DLT), and Unity Catalog, with strong hands-on expertise in PySpark, Spark SQL, and cloud platforms across Azure and AWS. A Databricks Solutions Architect Champion and member of the Product and Technical Council, he holds 26 Databricks certifications and focuses on enabling scalable Lakehouse solutions, data quality, and reconciliation frameworks for global enterprises.

sessions.title: Lakeflow Designer: No-code ETL— Authored With AI, Built for Production
sessions.body:
As demand for data grows, central data teams can’t build every transformation themselves. But traditional “self-service” ETL tools often introduce new problems: logic leaves governed platforms, pipelines live in parallel runtimes, and productionization requires costly rewrites by data engineering teams.

 

Lakeflow Designer addresses this gap by giving analysts a no-code, AI-first way to do data prep on the same Lakeflow execution model used by data engineering teams. Instead of introducing a parallel toolchain, Designer produces governed, production-grade transformations that fit directly into existing data engineering workflows.

 

In this session, you’ll see how Lakeflow Designer:

  • Enables analysts to do data prep without moving data outside Databricks
  • Preserves centralized governance, quality, and lineage through Unity Catalog
  • Lets data engineers scale pipeline development by directly operationalizing designer-authored logic— without rebuilding, translating, or refactoring

sessions.title: Lakeflow Jobs: Modern Orchestration for the Data Platform
sessions.body:
Modern data platforms need more than a scheduler. They need orchestration that understands data, integrates with the platform, and scales with both engineering and AI workloads. Join this session to see how Lakeflow Jobs helps teams orchestrate pipelines, notebooks, dbt projects, SQL, and external components, natively on the Databricks Platform.

 

We will show how Lakeflow Jobs goes beyond basic scheduling with data-aware orchestration that understands the assets and systems it is coordinating. You will see how teams can trigger workflows based on data changes, build modular workflows in Python, orchestrate external systems alongside Databricks workloads, and use Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs) for a more reliable CI/CD path.

 

We will also cover how Serverless Jobs and observability features such as lineage and system tables help teams reduce operational overhead and better understand what is happening across their workflows. Finally, we will preview how agentic authoring and diagnostics can speed up building, troubleshooting, and improving production jobs, and how you can embed agents directly into your workflows.

 

Whether you are modernizing from legacy schedulers or building new workloads on the lakehouse, this session will share practical patterns, product direction, and live demos for modern orchestration on Databricks.

sessions.title: LakeFoundry: The Databricks-Native Delivery Platform for Spec-Driven Autonomous Software Building
sessions.body: Most enterprises don't struggle to write code — they struggle to consistently deliver production-grade Databricks solutions that are clearly scoped, governed, and built to last. LakeFoundry is Slalom's autonomous, agent-driven delivery platform that transforms ideas, tickets, chats, and draft requirements into a repeatable, auditable path from concept to production — entirely within Databricks.At its core, LakeFoundry operates across three planes: a Control Plane that enforces structured specification and stakeholder alignment before a single line of code is written; an Execution Plane where autonomous subagents generate, verify, and deploy production-grade code with Unity Catalog governance, policy-as-code guardrails, and replayable LLM audit trails; and a Continuous Improvement Plane where an embedded Improvement Agent analyzes MLflow traces, detects performance drift, and proposes human-reviewed PRs — keeping systems from decaying post-launch.LakeFoundry integrates natively with Slack, Jira, Teams, GitHub, and CLI — meeting teams where work already happens — while eliminating the ambiguity, context rot, and governance gaps that cause autonomous development to fail at enterprise scale.The result: spec clarity before execution, test-driven autonomous generation, and governance embedded by design — not bolted on after. For Databricks customers, LakeFoundry provides a native path to operationalize agentic software delivery on the same trusted platform that already governs their data, workloads, and environments.

sessions.title: Language-Agnostic UDF Protocol for Spark
sessions.body: User-defined functions (UDFs) are a fundamental extension mechanism in Spark, enabling users to express logic that goes beyond built-in operators. However, the current UDF execution model is not enough for the multi-language architecture in Spark Connect. Existing implementations are tightly coupled to specific runtimes (e.g., PySpark), rely on ad-hoc communication protocols, and embed language-specific logic into planning and execution.This proposal aims to introduce a language-agnostic UDF execution model for Spark. It is built around three core ideas: (1) planning UDFs based on execution shape rather than programming language, (2) a structured execution IPC protocol and (3) a declarative worker specification to decouple the Spark engine from language runtimes.To provide a clean and extensible foundation for IPC-based UDF execution across languages, this proposal aims to standardize multi-language support and establish a sustainable direction for the UDF ecosystem.

sessions.title: Large scale Member and Claims Data Platform modernization Using Databricks on AWS GovCloud
sessions.body: Johns Hopkins is undergoing a major cloud transformation, moving from a legacy SQL Server EDW to a modern, scalable data and analytics platform. sessions.title: Latest innovations in BI and AI for business users
sessions.body: Databricks is setting a new standard for BI—combining unified semantics with AI-powered agents to truly deliver on the promise of Agentic Business Intelligence.Whether through natural language with Genie, AI/BI Dashboards, or a combination of both, users can move seamlessly between conversational and visual analysis in a single, integrated experience.In this session, we’ll cover:- An end-to-end walkthrough of agentic BI on Databricks- The latest innovations and customizations capabilities to simplify access for business users- How unified semantics power consistent, trusted answers across Genie and AI/BI Dashboards- How agents, Genie, and dashboards work together to accelerate analysis- How conversational and visual workflows come together to accelerate insights and actions

sessions.title: Latest innovations in Genie Code: The Future of Agentic Data Work
sessions.body: AI coding assistants have changed how developers write code, but most stop at suggestions. Genie Code is an autonomous AI agent designed specifically for data teams. It doesn't just help you write code. It plans and executes full workflows, and it monitors your production systems in the background, triaging and fixing pipeline failures before your team even notices. In this session, we'll walk through the newest capabilities in Genie Code and how they change the way data work gets done. We'll cover: - What’s new in Genie Code - How it builds and maintains production data and AI workflows end to end, from pipeline creation to model serving observability - How Unity Catalog integration gives Genie Code the enterprise context, governance, and accuracy that general-purpose agents lack - Best practices for working with Genie Code as an autonomous partner, including Agent Skills and persistent memory

sessions.title: Learn How We Secure and Govern Lakewatch on the Databricks Trusted Lakehouse
sessions.body: Security data is among the most sensitive in the enterprise, yet many SIEM deployments lack consistent, fine-grained governance. Learn how Lakewatch leverages Unity Catalog to provide centralized governance across your entire security ecosystem. We will dive deep into the Lakewatch RBAC model, demonstrating how to manage Principals (Users, Groups, and Service Principals) across protected resources like Datasources, Detection Rules, and Notables. You’ll learn how to implement Lakewatch’s unique inherited permission model — where cases automatically inherit context from parent resources — to streamline investigations while maintaining strict "need-to-know" access. Takeaways include: implementing table, row, and column-level security for telemetry; defining Viewer, Creator, and Manager scopes at Workspace and Resource levels; practical patterns for SOC, cloud, and data teams to collaborate safely; sharing data with partners via Delta Sharing without compromising auditability or lineage.

sessions.title: Less Infrastructure, Higher Impact: Nationwide’s Serverless Transformation with Databricks
sessions.body: Simplifying infrastructure accelerates data work and drives outcomes. The future of analytics isn’t about managing clusters; it’s about empowering users with seamless, scalable compute. In this session, Nationwide and Databricks share a real-world journey from server-managed infrastructure to Databricks Serverless, covering all-purpose compute, jobs compute, and SQL warehouses. We show how serverless simplified operations, sped up development cycles, reduced cost variability, and improved the user experience. We highlight the biggest wins, explore key design decisions that shaped success, and close with practical best practices to help your organization confidently accelerate its move to serverless.

sessions.title: Let AI Work on Your Database: Safe AI-Driven Development with Database Branches
sessions.body: AI coding agents have drastically improved the way we work in so many areas of software development, but because LLMs are inherently non-deterministic, many developers are still hesitant to let AI agents touch their databases because of the risk of destructive actions. In this talk, we’ll show how to safely leverage AI in real workflows using Lakebase’s branching capabilities. With the tools and strategies we’ll discuss, you will be able to create isolated code and data environments that enable AI coding agents to build in parallel, experiment safely, and iterate faster, without risking production data. By the end of this talk, attendees will walk away with practical patterns to integrate AI into their development workflows with confidence.

sessions.title: Let Your Agent Pilot Your Fleet: Business Insights From 35,000 Feet
sessions.body:

This session shows how we made an AI assistant the primary interface for business and operational insight using Databricks Apps and how it was integrated with existing business systems and portals.

 

We walk through a real scenario: A business user opens a Databricks App, interacts with the AI agent and explores passenger usage & system performance data. The same agent can also be embedded into existing business applications, bringing consistent data access directly into daily workflows.

 

The talk focuses on outcomes and lessons learned: What Databricks simplified, where challenges appeared and what it takes to move AI agents from experiment to production for our business users.

sessions.title: lululemon: How We Modernized Our Audience Segmentation and Where It's Taking Us With Agentic AI

We came to DAIS 2025 with these problems and left with a plan: DABS, Unity Catalog, and MLflow 3.0 as the foundation for a live system.

  • DABS: parameterized pipelines that any team member can deploy in one command
  • Multi-stream architecture where each new model type inherits the same pipeline pattern
  • Unity Catalog migration seeding an enterprise feature store now scaling beyond PAVE

More recently, his focus has expanded to agentic AI in service operations, combining connected asset data, enterprise context, and AI to support context-aware field service.

speakers.name: Dora Tien
speakers.bio:
Dora leads the Supply Chain Systems & Analytics team at Xylem, where she focuses on modernizing enterprise planning technologies and advancing data maturity to enable AI readiness and autonomous decision-making.

She brings cross-industry experience across automotive, retail, and aerospace, with prior roles at Tesla, Rivian, Amazon, and General Electric. Dora specializes in product management for custom supply chain software solutions, combining deep operational expertise with a passion for building intuitive, data-driven systems.

speakers.name: Marius Hagmann
speakers.bio: Marius Hagmann is Lead Data Architect for the Data Platform at TK Elevator DTX, drawing on several years of experience delivering and scaling data solutions for large enterprises. Known for his passion for building robust, modern data platforms, he has shaped best practices, led data teams, and driven end‑to‑end architectures and key metrics that enable organizations to operate more efficiently. His work centers on transforming complex data ecosystems into scalable, value‑driven platforms that support long‑term digital growth.

speakers.name: Matthias Gohl
speakers.bio:
09/2023- today: CDO TK Elevator
2017-2022: Global Head of ZEISS Digital Innovation Partners
2014-2016: Global Head of Strategy and M+A ZEISS Group

speakers.name: Shiv Trisal
speakers.bio: Shiv is responsible for worldwide adoption of Databricks in the manufacturing, transportation & energy sectors through new solutions, partnerships >TM programs that bring differentiated value to CxO priorities. Shiv has a proven track record of leading diverse teams and delivering game-changing data & AI-led innovation across Manufacturing and Transportation and Logistics industries, with roles at EY, Strategy& and Raytheon. He regularly connects with senior executives to unfold data & AI strategies and unlock competitive advantage in their businesses. Shiv majored in Electronics Engineering from the Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology in Punjab, India and holds a MBA from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania.

sessions.title: Marketing Forum
sessions.body:
Marketing is the most AI-ready function in the enterprise: always-on, data-rich and powered by continuous experimentation. But realizing that potential requires humans, agents and applications to work together on a shared foundation of trusted, real-time context. The CMOs who define the next decade will be the ones who treat that foundation as a core marketing imperative.

 

Join marketing leaders for a deep dive into how Databricks’ unified data and AI platform is powering agentic marketing transformation. From unified Customer 360 to autonomous campaign orchestration, discover how the most ambitious marketing organizations are turning their architecture into a competitive advantage. This forum explores the imperatives reshaping the function: proving marketing impact in real time, personalizing at scale without multiplying fragmented data and moving from manual execution to outcome-driven AI workflows that adapt as channels, models and customer behavior evolve. Through candid conversations and real-world results, hear directly from marketing leaders already delivering measurable outcomes and leave with a practical playbook for building the governed data and AI foundation that makes agentic marketing trustworthy at scale.

speakers.name: chris wissing
speakers.bio: I lead our product organization, responsible for building differentiated Epsilon PeopleCloud capabilities through the lens of our clients. My team is focused on balancing short-term commitments with long-term strategic innovation, ensuring we deliver solutions that drive meaningful business growth. With over 25 years developing innovative AdTech and MarTech capabilities at Epsilon, I bring a deep experience and passion for creating products that deliver measurable impact.

speakers.name: Scott Brinker
speakers.bio: Scott Brinker, dubbed the "godfather of martech" by AdAge, has been analyzing martech and its impact on marketing for more than 18 years as an analyst for chiefmartec. He served as VP platform ecosystem at HubSpot for 8 years, building their technology partner program. Before that he was co-founder and CTO of ion interactive, a pioneering no-code platform for interactive content. He authored the best-selling book Hacking Marketing and co-authored the best-seller The New Automation Mindset.

sessions.title: MCP Security Deep Dive: How Databricks Secures Tool Access for Enterprise Users
sessions.body: As agents connect to external tools and systems, security becomes a first-order concern. Every interaction — from authentication to tool invocation — must be governed, permissioned, and fully auditable. One leaked credential or broken audit trail can break production trust overnight.In this deep dive, we'll show how to secure MCP-based integrations in production on Databricks. You'll learn how to implement authentication and authorization, manage fine-grained access to tools, and ensure every agent action is traceable end-to-end. We'll also share how Databricks applies these patterns internally — using Unity Catalog connections to securely grant MCP access to thousands of users — along with the key risks, design tradeoffs, and best practices.You'll walk away with a production-ready blueprint for protecting data and systems as agents start taking real actions on behalf of your users.

speakers.name: Samrat Ray
speakers.bio: Samrat is responsible for enterprise security for the Databricks platform including security of the serverless platform, encryption, data protection and privacy. In his previous role at Google, he has led several industry-leading products such as VPC Service Controls and Cloud SQL from concept to scale.  Samrat is a founding PM of Istio and led the vision for zero-trust security in modern production environments.

sessions.title: Media & Entertainment Industry Forum
sessions.body: AI in media: what’s hype and what’s really possible? Join us at the Media & Advertising Industry Forum to learn how industry leaders are unlocking the full potential of AI, launching production grade solutions that achieve real business outcomes. Hear from leaders across Media, Advertising, Gaming and Sports to learn how Databricks solutions are helping them drive value from maximizing advertising ROI to unlocking real time hyper personalization and superior audience experience. Discover how data and AI will continue to shape the future of audience and fan engagement, ad monetization and content production.

speakers.name: Alan Ochoa
speakers.bio: An accomplished Digital Transformation and Data Activation expert with over 15 years experience managing global strategies, marketing campaigns and digital experiences. Alan has a passion to develop digital strategies that truly enhance the consumer experience.

speakers.name: Chandos Quill
speakers.bio: Chandos has 25 years of experience building global solutions for clients across Data, Digital Advertising and Marketing Technologies. She is a proven expert in data-driven marketing by delivering revenue through leadership roles across partnerships, product management and corporate development functions. In her role as SVP, Channel and Alliances at Epsilon, Chandos is responsible for driving incremental revenue and profitability for the business by extending Epsilon products into new channels and markets as well as creating new solutions that add value to Epsilon clients.

speakers.name: Sean Muzzy
speakers.bio: Sean Muzzy is the Global President of Acxiom, where he spearheads innovative solutions and services across data, marketing operations, and technology for Omnicom. As a forward-thinking leader, Sean provides strategic expertise on critical business decisions while championing talent development throughout the company. During his 25+ year career leading marketing transformation across Financial Services, Travel, Telco, Entertainment, Pharma, and Tech/B2B Sean has built and scaled global teams that help brands turn connected data into competitive advantage.

sessions.title: Meet Bricksy - The Hyper-Personalized, Privacy-First AI Copilot for the Software-Defined Vehicle
sessions.body: As automotive industry pivots to the Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV), the challenge has shifted from collecting data to interacting with it in real-time. Drivers demand a seamless, personalized experience, while OEMs demand data sovereignty and low-latency interventions. Bricksy, a next-gen AI agent powered entirely by Databricks is an android app. We'll demonstrate a unified architecture for building voice-enabled driver companion that thinks, remembers, and protects having:1. Real-Time Nervous System: Vehicle telemetry (Engine Temp, TPMS) streams directly into Unity Catalog via Zerobus, enabling near real-time anomaly detection.2. Infinite Memory & Context: How Bricksy utilizes Vector Search and Lakebase to instantly recall car manuals, service history, and long-term driver preferences.3. AI That Comes to Your Data: How manufacturers can deploy proprietary tools and functions directly on the Lakehouse, ensuring sensitive telemetry never leaves their governance boundary.

speakers.name: Hussain Jagirdar
speakers.bio: Hussain Jagirdar is a GenAI Architect at Databricks based in Bengaluru, India, with over 7 years of experience in AI and Engineering. He builds compound AI systems that connect LLM agents to real-world hardware - most recently Bricksy, an MCP-powered AI copilot for smart vehicles. He holds a Master's degree in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur.

sessions.title: Meet Bricksy - The Hyper-Personalized, Privacy-First AI Copilot for the Software-Defined Vehicle
sessions.body: As automotive industry pivots to the Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV), the challenge has shifted from collecting data to interacting with it in real-time. Drivers demand a seamless, personalized experience, while OEMs demand data sovereignty and low-latency interventions.Bricksy, a next-gen AI agent powered entirely by Databricks is an android app. We'll demonstrate a unified architecture for building voice-enabled driver companion that thinks, remembers, and protects having:1. Real-Time Nervous System: Vehicle telemetry (Engine Temp, TPMS) streams directly into Unity Catalog via Zerobus, enabling near real-time anomaly detection.2. He builds compound AI systems that connect LLM agents to real-world hardware - most recently Bricksy, an MCP-powered AI copilot for smart vehicles. He holds a Master's degree in Computer Science from IIT Kharagpur.

sessions.title: Metric Views — What They Are, How They Work, and How to Model Them
sessions.body: Databricks has always had a strong foundation for data engineering, but one thing has been missing: a semantic layer that lives inside the platform. Metric Views finally change that.With Metric Views, measures and models are defined directly in Unity Catalog and reachable from notebooks, the SQL editor, dashboards, and Genie. Data engineers and analysts are finally working from the same definitions, no more translating DAX back into SQL to understand what a number means.In this session we will walk through what Metric Views are and what the setup looks like in practice. Then we will look at the modeling decisions, whether to build small specialized views or broader shared ones, how those choices affect reuse and consistency, and how they affect what Genie returns and how dashboards behave.New to metric views or already using them, you will leave with a clearer picture of how to approach them.

sessions.title: MGM Enterprise Data Hub: Accelerating Data Delivery With DABS CI/CD Approach
sessions.body:
MGM Resorts is unifying our data estate, leveraging Unity Catalog for centralized governance, access control and cross‑environment consistency across gaming, hospitality and partner ecosystems. We updated our framework with DABS reducing delivery time for gold tables by 67%, enabling automated deployment and validation in under 5 min, cutting deployment code by 75%.

 

We:

  • Enabled isolation and targeted lifecycle management via a multi-bundle architecture with shared utilities in a common wheel
  • Improved reliability with a GitHub Actions pipeline for sequential DEV → UAT → PROD deployments, with consistent governance across environments using Unity Catalog
  • Freed engineers to focus on business logic through centralized configuration, SCD handling, and Apache Spark™ lifecycle management

 

Key takeaways:

  • CI/CD best practices using standardized databricks.yml
  • Higher reliability and faster delivery through a bundle-based pattern
  • Metrics and lessons to drive low-risk, predictable releases across the org

speakers.name: Jennifer Young
speakers.bio: Jennifer has built her career at the intersection of data management, data engineering, governance, and business intelligence, working across industries including government, healthcare, retail, technology, and casino hospitality. She has led high‑performing data teams within large, complex organizations and currently serves as Vice President of Data at MGM Resorts International. Previously, Jennifer was a Data & AI Specialist at Microsoft, where she partnered with enterprise clients on data strategy and Azure implementation. A Las Vegas resident of over 20 years, she enjoys crafting, reading, dining out, traveling, and spending time with her four‑year‑old Boston Terrier.

sessions.title: Migrate to Lakeflow Jobs: Modernizing Data Orchestration on Databricks
sessions.body:
Still running orchestration outside Databricks? That often means more tools to manage, less context about your data, and more overhead connecting pipelines, schedules, and dependencies across systems.

 

Join this session to learn how to migrate to Lakeflow Jobs, Databricks’ native orchestrator for data and AI workloads. We will cover practical migration patterns, the tooling available to accelerate the move, and the tips, techniques, and best practices that help teams reduce risk and avoid common pitfalls.

 

You will learn:

  • Why teams are consolidating orchestration onto Databricks
  • How common migration patterns from legacy orchestrators map to Lakeflow Jobs
  • What tooling, tips, and techniques can speed up migration and simplify rollout
  • The best practices that help teams move faster with less operational overhead
  • What real customer migrations look like in practice, including key challenges, tradeoffs, and outcomes

speakers.name: Saad Ansari
speakers.bio: Saad is a product manager at Databricks working on Data Orchestration (Lakeflow Jobs). Prior to this he was CTO and co-founder at Connecterra using Artificial Intelligence to improve sustainability, productivity and animal welfare in the Dairy Industry (think Fitbit for cows!). Saad has also worked as a PM and Developer at Microsoft. He holds a masters in computer science from Stanford.

speakers.name: Greg Hansen
speakers.bio: Gregory Hansen is a Data Engineering and Governance Solutions Architect at Databricks based in Miami, FL. At Databricks, Gregory focuses on designing systems for ingesting, transforming, and governing data. He frequently contributes to open source software projects including Apache Spark, DQX, and dbldatagen.

sessions.title: Migrating from Oracle to Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: Migrating your legacy Oracle data warehouse to Databricks can accelerate your data modernization journey. In this session, learn the top strategies for completing this data migration. We will cover data type conversion, basic to complex code conversions, validation, and reconciliation best practices. Discover how to proceed with data migration by leveraging Lakeflow Connect and code migration with Lakebridge to convert complex ETL pipelines to Databricks Spark Declarative Pipelines. See before and after architectures of customers who have migrated, and learn about the benefits they realized.

speakers.name: George Komninos
speakers.bio: George Komninos is the EMEA Lead for Migrations Solutions Architecture at Databricks. He spearheads the region's migration strategy, specializing in moving complex on-premises and cloud systems to the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. George is a key contributor to the Databricks community, regularly publishing technical thought leadership and leading workshops on data warehouse modernization.  Prior to his current role, George spent several years at AWS in senior architecture and engineering leadership roles, where he pioneered accelerated delivery models for AI, analytics, and Lakehouse architectures. He holds an M.Sc. in Computer Science from the University of Edinburgh.

speakers.name: Laurent Léturgez
speakers.bio:
Laurent is working as a specialist Solutions Architect specialized in Data Warehouse Migration.
Prior to Databricks, Laurent has worked 15 years with Oracle Databases in various roles (Developer, DBA, Architect & consultant).

sessions.title: Migrating from Snowflake to Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body: Migrating your Snowflake data warehouse to Databricks can accelerate your data modernization journey. Though a cloud platform to cloud platform migration should be relatively easy, the breadth of the Databricks Platform provides flexibility and requires careful planning and execution. In this session, we present the methodologies that incorporate modernization while migrating. We explore technical approaches, automation tools, product/feature mapping, a technical demo and best practices using real-world case studies for migrating data, ELT pipelines and warehouses from Snowflake to Databricks.

speakers.name: Koundinya Srinivasarao
speakers.bio: Koundinya (“KD”) is a Solutions Architecture Leader at Databricks focused on driving adoption of Databricks SQL, working with customers on architecture definition and cloud strategy for Data, AI & Analytics. In his time at Databricks, he has led some of the largest implementations with a strong focus on governance and user adoption. Prior to Databricks, Koundinya had a varied career spanning DevOps, Cloud-Native Application Development, Observability Tooling and Networking at Pivotal/VMware, Riverbed & IBM. He earned his Computer Science Bachelor’s degree from Bangalore University and his Master's Degree from NC State University with a research focus in Optical Networks.

speakers.name: Uzi Hefetz
speakers.bio:
Uzi Hefetz leads the Global Data Warehouse Migration Practice at Databricks, helping enterprises modernize their data platforms at scale. He has over 20 years of experience in cloud migrations, professional services, and strategic partnerships, with a proven ability to turn complex technical challenges into business outcomes.

Before joining Databricks, Uzi held senior leadership roles at Google Cloud and Microsoft, where he drove cloud adoption, partner transformation, and large-scale enterprise modernization initiatives.

Uzi is passionate about leveraging technology as a business enabler and building scalable practices that foster customer success.

sessions.title: Migrating from SQL Server and Synapse to Azure Databricks
sessions.body: Learn proven best practices to modernize from SQL Server and Azure Synapse to the Databricks Lakehouse. The session will include Lakebridge's AI‑assisted migration to analyze and convert legacy SQL (T‑SQL DDL/DML, views, stored procedures) and Synapse scripts into Databricks Lakehouse and Spark‑based workloads. Adopt unified governance and privilege mapping in Unity Catalog, and follow a phased cutover: begin with Lakehouse Federation for read‑through access to SQL Server and Synapse, add CDC‑based replication, and run side‑by‑side reconciliation and query validation before switching over. Optionally leverage Lakeflow Connect for managed SQL Server ingestion under Unity Catalog governance. Finally, serve high‑performance BI at scale with SQL Serverless to deliver fast, reliable dashboards in Power BI and beyond. Learn how to de‑risk migrations, improve price/performance, and accelerate delivery.

speakers.name: Mehran Golestaneh
speakers.bio: Over 25 years of experience in data warehousing architecture and implementation across a wide range of platforms, including IBM Balanced Warehouse, Oracle Exadata, SAP HANA, Teradata, and Databricks. Previously employed by Teradata for 7 Years and 8 years of independant consulting.

speakers.name: Will Girten
speakers.bio: As a Lead SSA at Databricks and author of the Node.js connector for Delta Sharing, Will is driven by his passion for open-source technologies and creating a more connected, data-driven world. He has over a decade of experience in big data, data warehousing, and performance optimizations. Will is committed to pushing the limits of what's possible and delivering transformative results. Contributing to the Delta Sharing project is just one way he's working to make a difference.

sessions.title: Migrating to Serverless: The Databricks Journey
sessions.body: The future of the data intelligence platform is serverless, and Databricks is leading by example. We aren’t just telling customers to migrate; the Data Platform team is actively moving our own mission-critical ETL and BI workloads to Databricks Serverless SQL and Compute first. This session chronicles our internal migration journey. We will share the raw “before and after” metrics on cost, latency and engineering overhead. We will be transparent about the challenges we faced as early adopters and the specific best practices we developed to run a massive-scale, serverless-first platform that powers the business.

speakers.name: Alan Jackoway
speakers.bio: Alan is the technical lead for our internal Data Platform function at Databricks. Alan has been building data platforms at the companies that make data platforms for the last 15 years, first at Cloudera and now at Databricks. At Databricks, our internal Data Platform enables all Databricks employees to use our own product to interact with data on a daily basis. He is passionate about product feedback, and believes that when more people use data, the company can make better decisions

sessions.title: Millisecond Pricing: High-Velocity Feature Serving on the Lakebase
sessions.body:
Fragmented architectures kill pricing precision. Real-time systems require millisecond latency across millions of features without training-serving skew. We replace slow, siloed pipelines with a high-velocity pricing engine built on the Databricks Lakebase, Tecton and Fennel with Genie and Apps.

 

Technical Highlights:

  • Millisecond serving: OnlineFS provides rapid online serving for millions of features to power complex pricing models.
  • Rapid updates: Fennel enables instantaneous feature updates, allowing the online system to react to data shifts in real time.
  • Unified foundation: Databricks Lakebase provides the high-performance backbone for governed, enterprise-scale feature retrieval at scale.
  • Intelligent analytics: Databricks Genie and integrated dashboards deliver real-time visibility into pricing performance and financial risk.

 

See how to build a scalable, autonomous blueprint for real-time decisioning that bridges massive historical datasets with sub-millisecond execution.

speakers.name: Laurence Ryszka
speakers.bio: Laurence is a Senior Solutions Architect and Insurance SME at Databricks, based in London and covering the EMEA insurance and reinsurance market. He works with carriers, reinsurers and Lloyd's syndicates on modernising pricing, actuarial workflows, claims and underwriting on the Lakehouse — helping insurers scale the tools they already rely on with the power of Databricks and agentic AI, without losing their actuarial rigour. Before Databricks, Laurence spent six years at WTW, working inside the pricing and capital modelling software that much of the industry runs on. He now partners with insurers to extend that foundation into governed, real-time, AI-native operations across the policy lifecycle.

speakers.name: Rahul Pathak
speakers.bio: Rahul Pathak is a Senior Specialist Solutions Engineer and AI Subject Matter Expert at Databricks, helping organizations unlock the full value of data, machine learning, and generative AI at scale. He specializes in designing and deploying modern AI and data platform solutions that enable enterprises to accelerate innovation, improve decision-making, and deliver measurable business outcomes. With deep expertise across data engineering, machine learning, MLOps, and AI applications, Rahul partners closely with customers to build scalable, production-ready solutions on the Databricks Intelligence Platform. He is passionate about bridging business and technology, helping teams turn complex data challenges into impactful, real-world solutions.

sessions.title: Mission-Critical Inference: Powering High-Scale AI in Production
sessions.body: You've shipped your model. Now it needs to serve millions of requests a day without blinking — at the right latency, the right cost, and with zero downtime. The architecture that handled your prototype won't cut it in production, and most teams learn that the hard way.This session walks through the architecture, tuning knobs, and operational patterns that let Databricks Custom Model Serving handle the world's most demanding inference workloads. You'll see how GPU autoscaling matches capacity to traffic, how request batching drives down cost per call, how traffic splitting enables safe rollouts, and how built-in observability lets you catch regressions before users do.Bring your hardest production challenges — you'll leave with concrete patterns for running high-scale AI inference reliably, and the playbook to keep it fast, governed, and cost-efficient as demand grows.

sessions.title: Mo’ Agents Mo’ Problems: How We Simplified Lakehouse Threat Hunting as a Service at Scale
sessions.body: Security teams face an impossible ratio of millions of events, thousands of alerts, and a handful of analysts. Most hunt reactively or not at all. We built a threat hunting platform on Databricks that flips this equation. Our architecture spans the full stack: Lakeflow DLT normalizes 20+ sources into OCSF, billions of events are governed in Unity Catalog, and detection pipelines form the foundation for specialized AI agents that hunt autonomously. These agents generate hypotheses, investigate the lakehouse, enrich IOCs via MCP tools, and produce findings without prompting. The critical constraint: agents never see raw telemetry. They query pre-aggregated views, keeping billion-row datasets out of the LLM context while preserving investigative depth. You'll learn how we architected safe agent-to-lakehouse communication, orchestration patterns for autonomous hunt cycles, and detection at scale, while hearing about our service delivery at petabyte scale.

speakers.name: Mike Saxton
speakers.bio: Mike Saxton is a Senior Cybersecurity Leader at Booz Allen Hamilton where he currently supports Security Operations efforts at the intersection of defense and Artificial Intelligence (AI) efforts. As a prior Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and Deputy Program Manager to a large DoD Global Security Operations Center, Mike has established and rebuilt multiple cybersecurity programs; developed first of kind, innovative approaches to rapid detection and response of Cyber threats, and helped clients establish their cybersecurity strategy and vision. Additionally, Mike serves as a Regional Director for the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit organization that re-establishes IT communications after natural disasters.

sessions.title: Modern Data Modeling at Scale: Advanced Patterns
sessions.body: Unlock the truth behind data modeling in Databricks. This session will tackle the top 10 myths surrounding relational and dimensional data modeling. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of what Databricks Lakehouse truly supports today, including how to leverage primary and foreign keys, identity columns for surrogate keys, column-level data quality constraints and much more. This session will talk through the lens of medallion architecture, explaining how to implement data models across Bronze, Silver and Gold tables. Whether you’re migrating from a legacy warehouse or building new analytics solutions, you’ll leave equipped to fully leverage Databricks’ capabilities, and design scalable, high-performance data models for enterprise analytics.

speakers.name: Kyle Hale
speakers.bio: Kyle Hale’s journey into data and analytics began at age 8 when he created his first database to analyze baseball statistics, and hasn’t stopped yet. He’s a 20 year veteran of the data warehousing and BI space, having worn every hat from report development, modeling, and performance tuning to architecture, strategy, and governance. Having been a trusted advisor to well over 1,000 organizations big and small: Kyle has seen things.His proudest moment is being recognized by his peers at Databricks as a Data and Analytics SME - game knows game.When he’s not secretly plotting like all good BI professionals to kill Excel once and for all, he enjoys crafting synth pop soundtracks to imaginary movies, solving chess puzzles, and roaming the countryside with his wife and 4 kids in search of cool museums and awesome fried chicken. He is also an avid collector of dad jokes.

speakers.name: Shannon Barrow
speakers.bio: Shannon has spent the last 7 years at Databricks helping enterprise customers modernize their analytics platforms to maximize value from their data and drive down the total cost of ownership.  Specializing in performance for data engineering and SQL consumption, he is a leading SME in benchmarking and POC efforts across Enterprise North America.  Before joining Databricks in 2019, he was a Principal in Accenture's Innovation and Thought Leadership team.  Shannon has a Masters in Computer Science from Georgia Tech and 2 Bachelor Degrees from Florida State University.

sessions.title: Modern Data Warehousing
sessions.body:
This hands-on course is designed for data professionals who want to explore the data warehousing capabilities of Databricks. Assuming no prior knowledge of Databricks, it provides an introduction to leveraging Databricks as a modern cloud-based data warehousing solution. Learners will explore how use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to ingest, transform, govern, and analyze data efficiently. Learners will also explore Genie, an innovative Databricks feature that simplifies data exploration through natural language queries. By the end of this course, participants will be equipped with the foundational skills to implement and optimize a data warehouse using Databricks.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Basic SQL proficiency and understanding of data querying concepts
  • General knowledge of data warehousing concepts, including tables, schemas, and ETL/ELT processes
  • Some experience with BI or data visualization tools (recommended but not required)

sessions.title: Modernization Without Illusions: Migrating a Barclays Business-Critical Equities Data Warehouse to Databricks
sessions.body:
Transitioning a mission-critical data platform is rarely straightforward—especially when the legacy system already works and the environment is tightly regulated.

 

This session shares real-world lessons from moving a high-stakes post-trade data platform to a cloud-native Databricks architecture, focusing on the trade-offs that determine whether teams merely migrate or truly land well. We explore how decisions around design, execution, and platform-native patterns shape performance, cost and business SLAs from day one—and why treating migration and modernization as a binary choice often leads to poor outcomes.
