Through concrete examples, we highlight how principle-driven interventions turned initially underperforming designs into stable, scalable solutions, offering a candid look at the realities of transitioning critical data platforms without sacrificing predictability or value.

sessions.title: Modernizing Clinical Data Integration at Novo Nordisk With Lakebase and the Databricks Lakehouse
sessions.body:
Novo Nordisk transformed how vendor-sourced and vendor-facing clinical trial data is ingested, operationalized and exposed by building an API layer on the Databricks lakehouse powered by Lakebase. By replacing fragmented, self-hosted Postgres silos with Lakebase, a Postgres engine integrated with the lakehouse, we now make data available 30x faster than with legacy self-hosted Postgres.

 

This session walks through the end-to-end architecture and migration. We’ll talk about why Lakebase was chosen—horizontal scale and simplified operations—and how these capabilities reduce friction and speed onboarding. We’ll further expand on the blueprints we employed for Lakebase development, including governance and deployment patterns that can be adopted across an organization, and elaborate on the lessons learned along the way.

 

Attendees will learn how we modernized ingestion of structured and unstructured data to achieve consistent, auditable data in a regulated environment.

speakers.name: Arvid Vinther Normann
speakers.bio: Arvid Normann is Domain Architect in Architecture & Strategy at Novo Nordisk. With 20+ years in IT and 12 years at Novo Nordisk, he specializes in integration and modern platform capabilities—AI, Streaming, APIs and data platforms. Previously, he served as an SME for integration projects with some of the biggest clients in Northern Europe. Passionate about technology, Arvid is a coder at heart.

speakers.name: Henrik Lynge
speakers.bio:
Henrik Lynge is a seasoned IT leader and Sr. Director of Architecture & Strategy at Novo Nordisk (Jan 2026), with 20+ years of experience in R&D. He leads architecture across R&D, with a strong focus on GxP-compliant IT systems and data platforms. Previously, he worked with remote sens-ing, GIS and solution development across Danish Environmental Protection Agency, Hedeselskabet, and contributed through various roles at Novo Nordisk. He holds an MSc in Biol-ogy from the University of Copenhagen and executive education from CBS and Harward Business school.
He has published books, Game assets and builds solutions with Python, Vibe coding, and CI/CD, happy to read and learn on topics that he does not master yet. Labour of love - boat restore.

speakers.name: JZTS (Jonatan Selsing)
speakers.bio: Jonatan Selsing is a Principal Architect, employed at Novo Nordisk. He has a research background in astrophysics and am now a part of Global Data and AI where he operationalises and enterprise scales the most sophisticated, contemporary computational frameworks and platforms in a highly regulated industry. He works across the industry and focus on driving large projects of strategic importance that are aligned to business goals. Through the focus on the future of computers, he ensures that Novo Nordisk is ahead in the digital age.

sessions.title: Modernizing Data Governance at First Thai Bank to Prepare for an AI-First Future
sessions.body:
Founded in 1907, Siam Commercial Bank (SCB) is the first Thai bank. In September 2021, SCB embarked on a landmark transformation, restructuring into a holding company model under SCBX. This strategic shift has since driven the group's expansion to 13 core subsidiaries today, significantly increasing the complexity of managing data governance, data security, and data quality across the group.

 

Today, SCB runs its enterprise data platform on Databricks. In this session, we will highlight how SCB leverages Databricks and Unity Catalog to scale enterprise‑wide data governance and data quality. We will also demonstrate "Chat with your Metadata", leveraging Genie for enterprise-wide metadata discovery on the platform.

sessions.title: Modernizing Investment Analytics Through Data Driven Architecture
sessions.body: Transforming a 30-year-old monolithic analytics platform is as much about mindset as it is about technology. Our legacy, batch-based system—with its rigid relational model and high maintenance costs—could no longer keep up with growing data, client demands, or innovation needs. In this session, we share how we reimagined investment analytics with a cloud-native architecture modern ingestion and ETL pipelines using Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP), dimensional modeling, and a modern OLAP engine. We’ll highlight key design decisions, migration patterns, and how we preserved trusted reporting while improving data quality, transparency, and self-service. Attendees will learn practical strategies to de-risk modernization, accelerate delivery, and unlock new analytical capabilities without disrupting mission-critical operations.

speakers.name: Jacob Steiger
speakers.bio: Jacob Steiger is a Senior Vice President leading Change Management for Investment Risk & Analytical Services (IRAS) at Northern Trust (NT), based in Chicago. In this role, he leads strategic change initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness, client experience, and risk management across NT’s global analytics platform. With more than a decade of experience in digital solutions and analytics, he specializes in driving complex transformations, stakeholder engagement, and process improvement in highly regulated environments. Most recently, Jake led the modernization of the Portfolio Performance platform, implementing a data-driven operating model and technology stack that delivers near real-time analytics to support portfolio managers' investment decisions. Jacob holds an Engineering degree from Vanderbilt University.

speakers.name: Russ Houberg
speakers.bio: Russ Houberg is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he works with some of the world's largest enterprises on data engineering, AI, and lakehouse architecture. With nearly 30 years of IT experience — including time as a SharePoint Certified Master — he built his career at the intersection of data architecture and content management, co-authoring SharePoint Server 2010 Enterprise Content Management (Wrox) and leading large-scale data migrations for global enterprises. Russ draws on this unique background to show how Microsoft 365 and SharePoint can become first-class sources of institutional knowledge — fueling the democratization of Data + AI on Databricks.

sessions.title: Molecules, Merchants & Models: How Structure-First AI Makes Promotion Intelligence Trustworthy
sessions.body:
The presentation, "Molecules, Merchants & Models: How Structure-First AI Makes Promotion Intelligence Trustworthy," describes a promotion intelligence system built on the Databricks Lakehouse. Retail promotions interact through substitution, complementarity and spillover effects that merchants intuitively understand, but most tools fail to explain.

 

Our system models item and promotion relationships as reusable graph structures—Promo Molecules—learned from over 70 billion rows of transaction data. These structures explicitly surface demand shifts, including substitutes, halo effects and cannibalization. We apply Explainable AI (XAI) at the relationship level—exposing deterministic, merchant-validated signals.

 

Foundation models then reason probabilistically to answer natural-language “what-if” questions. This combined approach enables explainable, merchant-trusted promotion decisions at scale, without manual overrides or black-box predictions.

speakers.name: Karthik Iyer
speakers.bio: Karthik Iyer is Group Vice President of Intelligent Merchandising at Albertsons, with 25+ years of experience driving global transformation across retail and banking. He leads enterprise pricing and promotion intelligence, bringing together model-ready data, Explainable AI, statistical machine learning, deep learning, and agentic AI into a unified decisioning system. His work focuses on orchestrating the full AI lifecycle-from data to prediction to reasoning to action-enabling real-time decisions at scale. Previously, he pioneered CNN-based digital onboarding at NAB, widely covered in Australian media. He is pursuing doctoral research in AI focused on world models, latent representation learning, and explainability using JEPA.

sessions.title: Move Fast, Stay Secure: Enterprise AI Agent Security in Practice
sessions.body:
Agentic AI is moving from POCs to mission-critical workloads- and the attack surface is expanding fast. As LLM-driven agents reason, plan, and act across enterprise data and tools, a new class of risk emerges: the "Lethal Trifecta," where sensitive data access, untrusted inputs, and external actions converge to make prompt injection attacks exploitable end-to-end.

 

Karol Piekarski (Experian) and Nishith Sinha (Databricks) present the Databricks Agentic AI Security Framework (DASF v3), drawing on both Databricks' own AI infrastructure which handles millions of daily queries, and patterns from Fortune 100 deployments. The session walks through how the Databricks platform breaks the Lethal Trifecta at each layer: constraining what agents can access, hardening how they process inputs, and limiting what a compromised agent can actually do.

 

Finally, see how the Databricks Security team built, open-sourced, and actively uses BlackIce, a containerized AI red teaming toolkit, to shift security from a point-in-time exercise to continuous, automated validation. Leave with a practical framework for moving fast on AI without compromising governance or security.

speakers.name: Karol Piekarski
speakers.bio:
Karol Piekarski is a Lead DevOps Engineer working at Experian, where he oversees the security posture of complex enterprise systems. Joining via the acquisition of insurtech startup Gabi in 2021, Karol played a key technical role in the transition, combining startup agility with enterprise rigor.

Recognized as a Wiz MVP for his contributions to the cloud security community and an active contributor to the security frameworks, Karol holds comprehensive credentials including CCSP, CKA, and AWS Security & DevOps Professional. Recently, Karol has focused on adapting these mature DevSecOps methodologies to the emerging "wild west" of Generative AI, researching how to secure LLMs against injection and extraction attacks.

speakers.name: Nishith Sinha
speakers.bio: Nishith leads the AI Security Team at Databricks. His team is responsible for securing Databricks AI Products (Genie Code, Model Serving, Databricks One) as well as the enterprise usage of AI within Databricks. Nishith is a subject matter expert in AI Security, specializing in agents identity and security. In the last year, he has filed 10 GenAI Security patents.

sessions.title: Multi-Tenant Architecture at Scale: Fewer Workspaces, Less Admin, No Silos
sessions.body:
As analytics and AI workloads grow, most enterprises scale by adding more Databricks workspaces and infrastructure. Over time, this leads to admin overhead, duplicated standards, slow onboarding, and analytics, ML and GenAI teams operating in silos.

 

In this session, we share our lessons learned at Procter & Gamble, one of the largest Databricks workspace deployments. We show how we reversed that pattern by designing a multi-tenant Databricks architecture built to adapt to constant change and scale with minimal admin effort. Databricks is a multi-tenant platform — this session shows how to maximize it at enterprise scale.

 

Using a “hub-and-spoke” approach, we consolidated workspaces while preserving team autonomy and execution speed. Attendees will learn how to:

  • Design a multi-tenant architecture that scales without increasing admin overhead
  • Consolidate workspaces while maintaining team ownership
  • Run analytics and AI workloads on a shared platform without creating silos

speakers.name: Valeria Zhang
speakers.bio:
Valeria Zhang is a Senior Solution Architect at Procter & Gamble, where she leads enterprise data platform architecture for analytics and AI across global business domains.
She has built Databricks-based platforms serving thousands of users, consolidating distributed data environments into governed, multi-tenant architectures and standardizing batch, streaming, SQL, and machine learning workloads. Her work focuses on reducing platform sprawl, enabling scalable adoption, and improving cross-domain collaboration.

sessions.title: Navigating the Realities of AI Policy: The 2026 Data + AI Policy Intelligence Brief
sessions.body: Artificial Intelligence and how to regulate it is top of mind for companies, governments, and policymakers everywhere. Today, industry faces a “Deregulation Paradox”: While the current US Government takes executive action to dismantle AI rules, states are doubling down on their own policies and enforcement. In 2025, U.S. legislators introduced over 1200 AI-related bills, threatening a regulatory patchwork that is colliding with a federal push for preemption. To separate the signal from noise, join leading experts for a deep dive into the the policy and politics surrounding AI and data regulation at the federal, state, and international levels in the year ahead. Moderator: Alan Davidson, Databricks Head of Government Affairs

sessions.title: NBCUniversal Media Group's Journey to Databricks
sessions.body: NBCUniversal launched Peacock in 2020 with a BigQuery based reporting and analytics data stack. This provided a solid platform for the business to grow on. As data volumes and computational needs increased, in 2025 it became necessary to evaluate other technology. With an eye on data sharing, scalability and of course, cost, Databricks rose to the top of the bunch. In this talk, we will discuss the factors that led to this decision, the process of migration and the road ahead.

speakers.name: Louie Kuznia
speakers.bio: Louie Kuznia is Vice President of Data Engineering for the Media Group at NBCUniversal, where he leads data platform and engineering initiatives supporting both linear and digital media experiences. With 15 years of experience spanning data science and data engineering, he specializes in large-scale analytics platforms, reporting systems, and enabling environments for analytics and AI teams. Louie has led strategic modernization efforts, including migrations from BigQuery to Databricks. He holds a PhD, has published two research papers, and holds one patent with two additional patents pending.

sessions.title: Near Real-Time Media Analytics with Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body:
In digital-first media, analytics latency directly drives editorial, revenue and audience decisions. For global publishers, sub-second insight into content performance shapes how teams react to breaking news, tentpole events and monetisation windows. This session shares how Condé Nast — a global media company with 115+ years of publishing history — is re-architecting media analytics on Databricks, moving from a fragmented, high-latency stack to a near real-time lakehouse powered by Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Lakebase.

 

Our legacy stack delivered analytics with a 15–30 minute delay across InfluxDB, Qlik and rigid third-party tools — costing us revenue yield on trending stories, delayed subscription conversions, duplicated business logic and blind spots between top-of-funnel content and downstream drivers like commerce and MAI. The new architecture ingests directly from web collectors into Databricks. Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines unify streaming and batch, run on-the-fly aggregations and enforce consistent business logic at scale. Lakebase powers low-latency operational serving, while the lakehouse remains the system of record.

 

The result: end-to-end latency under 10 seconds, third-party black-box vendors phased out, and a single unified view across audience, subscription, affiliate and ad data. We will also explore extending this with the Databricks Genie API to bring LLM-powered text-to-query into real-time media workflows.

speakers.name: Jitendra Sharma
speakers.bio: Jitendra Sharma is a Senior Data Engineering Manager at Condé Nast, leading the development of scalable, cloud-native data platforms for global media and analytics. He specializes in modern data architectures, lakehouse platforms, and real-time processing, building declarative, modular, and AI-enabled data pipelines that drive data-driven decision-making at scale. At Condé Nast, he has advanced the lakehouse strategy on Databricks, unifying batch and streaming workloads while improving reliability, scalability, and developer productivity. He is passionate about building high-performing teams and driving innovation in data and AI.

speakers.name: arun karthik
speakers.bio:
Senior Data & Platform Engineering Leader with 20 years of experience architecting and scaling enterprise-grade data ecosystems in global organisations. Proven track record of defining and executing data product strategies that enable AI-ready, decision-centric data assets powering revenue growth exceeding $500M annually.
Deep expertise in building connected, domain-aligned data platforms across commercial, advertising, customer and enterprise domains, with hands-on experience in modern cloud-native architectures (AWS, Databricks), distributed processing frameworks & real-time data enablement. Driving platform unification, governance modernisation & cost optimisation at scale, while building high performant global engineering organisation.

sessions.title: New Foundations of Delta Lake with Kernel and Spark's Data Source V2
sessions.body: When the Delta Lake project started back in 2018, Spark had the very first version of its Data Source APIs that allowed Spark to access process data in external sources (like Cassandra, Kafka etc). These Data Source V1 (DSv1) APIs, was limited to only basic features to allow communicate the data from source to Spark leaving a LOT of the heavy lifting (stats based data filtering, advanced upsert support, etc.) for the data source implementation to figure out. Delta Lake had build all the necessary intelligence to provide users a fantastic, high-performance, intuitive experience and command support that had set the standard for last 8 years. Now Spark as a engine has caught up by building a lot more intelligence within the engine itself and is now capable of doing a lot more of heavy lifting on behalf of data sources. These are the Data Source V2 (DSv2) APIs, and in this talk we are going to explore how we updating Delta to use DSv2 to build new foundations for the next decade of Delta.

speakers.name: Rahul Potharaju
speakers.bio: Rahul is one of the Engineering Leaders at Databricks, where he leads Delta and several other storage-related efforts.

speakers.name: Tathagata Das
speakers.bio: Tathagata Das is a Staff Software Engineer at Databricks and has been one of the core developers of Apache Spark (especially Structured Streaming) and Delta Lake. He is a member of Apache Spark PMC, and a Delta Lake committer. He is also one of the authors of Learning Spark: Lighting-fast Data Analytics (2nd edition). Previously, he was a grad student in the UC Berkeley at AMPLab where he conducted research about data-center processing frameworks and networks with Scott Shenker and Ion Stoica.

sessions.title: Next-Generation Data Platform Transformation
sessions.body: The Move to Cloud initiative represents far more than a technological migration; it marks a milestone in the bank’s digital transformation journey. Delivered through collaboration across data platform, data engineering, infrastructure, architecture and centralized ingestion, it established a new foundation for data. The program migrated 16 petabytes from Cloudera and ScyllaDB environments to a modern, secure and scalable cloud architecture, increasing speed, efficiency and resilience for business growth and data-driven decisions. It also generated USD 40 million in projected cost avoidance over five years and reduced 216,000 vulnerabilities, representing 38% of the technology landscape, engaging more than 100 organizational areas. More than a project, it transformed how the bank manages and values data, positioning technology as a driver of competitiveness and future innovation.

speakers.name: Laila Kurati
speakers.bio: With more than 20 years of experience as a strategic executive in the data domain, I have extensive experience leading transformation projects in large companies such as Serasa Experian, Claro, and Banco Santander.

sessions.title: No Code ETL with Lakeflow Designer
sessions.body: Lakeflow Designer is Databricks' AI-native, no-code experience for building data preparation and transformation workflows directly in the lakehouse. Built into the platform and governed by Unity Catalog, it allows analysts and business users to create reliable pipelines without leaving Databricks or managing separate tools.In this session, we will explore what Lakeflow Designer is, how it fits into the Databricks ecosystem, and how to get started using natural language with Genie Code to build workflows with little to no coding experience. We will cover data ingestion, built-in and custom operators, output options, and how visual workflows translate into production-ready code that can be versioned with Git, exported to notebooks, and added to larger enterprise pipelines.

sessions.title: Normalising Chaos: Atlassian’s OCSF Security Lakehouse on Databricks
sessions.body:
Atlassian’s security data lake, built on Delta Lake and standardized to the OCSF schema, powers 500+ production threat detection signals and enables fast, cost‑efficient investigations on open lakehouse architecture.

 

We’ll share hard‑won practices: adopting OCSF to unify schemas of relevant security logs and accelerate development, a ruthless, value‑vs‑cost log prioritization rubric and Databricks optimizations that unlocked capabilities like “conversational incident response” and live ML threat detections.

 

Learn how Atlassian achieved:

  • 80% ingestion cost reduction moving to file notification loader
  • Scheduled jobs running queries in seconds from minutes
  • Day‑long searches accelerated from minutes to seconds with Z‑ORDER and OPTIMIZE
  • We’ll cover PySpark patterns, and collaboration spaces, reusable libraries and notebooks that make IR handoffs repeatable. Walk away able to design OCSF‑first schemas, implement cost‑aware ingestion, and operationalize ML detections on an open lakehouse

sessions.title: O(n*m) Architecture in Open Source. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?
sessions.body:
There's a quiet crisis going on in open source right now — whenever an open table format wants to build a new feature or integration, there's an exponentially more amount of work to do to incorporate it. A project that's increasingly harder to contribute to is the death of innovation.

 

Kernel sets out to solve this problem by rewriting the source of truth. When other projects adopt Kernel, they no longer need to do any additional development for new features — they just appear. Join us for a deep dive into how we turned this project on its head, to solve not just these problems, but future problems we anticipate in open source.

 

What started out as a contribution to Delta, could change the way that open table formats fundamentally integrate everywhere.

 

Join Robert Pack, open-source contributor for Delta, Iceberg, Arrow and all round Rust enthusiast, and Holly Smith, tech communicator, who bullied Robert into this talk.

speakers.name: Holly Smith
speakers.bio: Holly Smith is a developer advocate and multi-award-winning Data and AI expert and tech educator with over a decade of experience working at the cutting edge of Data and AI in various capacities. One of the first employees at Databricks, she is a renowned public speaker and teacher. She is well known for her YouTube series on AI + data engineering.

speakers.name: Robert Pack
speakers.bio: Robert has extensive experience in designing and implementing Data & AI platforms within large multinational organizations. Through this work he has been an avid contributor to the open lakehouse ecosystem - specifically Delta Lake. Now at Databricks, his focus is entirely facilitating and contributing to the open source ecosystem for building lakehouse architectures.

sessions.title: Observability for the AI Era: Governing Data, Cost, and Risk with Governance Hub
sessions.body:
As data and AI estates scale, account-wide observability becomes critical to maintaining control, trust, and efficiency. In this session, we’ll introduce the Governance Hub, your unified center for governance and observability in Databricks.

 

You’ll learn how to monitor changes across your environment, identify risks, and take action across data and cost governance from a single interface, with expanding support for areas like performance and AI governance. We’ll also show how built-in recommendations help you surface and resolve issues, and how system tables support programmatic governance and automation workflows.

speakers.name: Kristen Wilder
speakers.bio: I'm a product manager on the Unity Catalog team who specializes in discovery and governance experiences. I love here in San Francisco and love hiking, skiing, and reading during my free time!

speakers.name: Michael Postiglione
speakers.bio: Michael is a Product Manager at Databricks and works on observability within the Data Intelligence Platform. He holds a BSE in Electrical & Computer Engineering and Biomedical Engineering from Duke University and earned an MBA from the University of Chicago. Previously, he worked at AWS and focused on building data infrastructure for digital marketing.

sessions.title: Observability's Agentic Moment: Operating AI in Production with Genie Code
sessions.body: Shipping AI products is easy. Trusting and operationalizing them at production scale is the hard part. Operational observability is now having its agentic moment. Join us to see how Databricks is reinventing operational observability for the agentic era — a unified, production-scale telemetry layer powered by Genie Code, our AI assistant, spanning every AI offering on the platform: Model Serving, AI Search, AI Gateway, Agent Bricks and Apps. Genie Code doesn't just alert you that something's wrong — it delivers instant root-cause analysis, pinpoints fixes for new error patterns and runs agentic operations on demand. Walk away knowing how to keep your application running smoothly in production — and how to get to the bottom of any issue in seconds when it doesn't.

sessions.title: Oil and Gas: Powering the Future with Data-Driven Energy Intelligence
sessions.body: Explore how two of the world's leading oil and gas companies are harnessing the power of data and AI to transform exploration, production, and sustainability operations. TotalEnergies and Repsol share how they are leveraging the Databricks to unlock insights from massive datasets, optimize asset performance, and accelerate their transitions toward cleaner energy futures.

speakers.name: Nicolas Ranchet
speakers.job_title: Head of HSE data strategy & analytics

speakers.name: Oussama Acheche
speakers.bio: Data and digital transformation enthusiast

speakers.name: daniel escuder
speakers.bio: CDAO with more than 20 years of experience, currently at Repsol, leads the corporate data strategy, the transformation towards intelligent data models, information governance and the incorporation of advanced analytics and AI capabilities within the D&A platform to generate business value and accelerate digital transformation. In his current role, he promotes scalable data models, FinOps, robust governance practices, and a focus on the strategic use of data as a key asset for decision-making. In addition, he combines his current work with teaching in various Big Data Analytics & Data Science programmes at institutions and business schools (such as IE and The Valley Digital Business School).

sessions.title: OLTP on the Object Store: Reimagining Postgres with the Lakebase Architecture
sessions.body:
Traditional databases force architects into a familiar set of tradeoffs: scale compute and you pay for storage you don't need, add read replicas for analytical queries and you introduce replication lag, separate your OLTP and OLAP systems and you're managing data movement and consistency across boundaries. These aren't bugs in the design; they're consequences of tightly coupled storage and compute.

 

Lakebase decouples storage from compute and runs Postgres natively on object storage. In this session, you'll learn what that architecture looks like, why it changes the tradeoff calculus, and what it makes possible: analytical queries running directly on operational data without read replicas, compute that scales to zero when idle, and transactional workloads sitting alongside lakehouse analytics on the same underlying data.

 

We'll map the architecture to concrete use cases, including real-time applications and AI workloads that need fresh operational data, and hybrid workloads that previously required two separate systems. You'll leave with a clear mental model of how Lakebase works and where it fits in your stack.

sessions.title: One Platform to Replace Them All: Our Databricks Migration
sessions.body:
Fonterra is replacing 12,000+ reports with AI-driven, self-service analytics powered by Databricks AI/BI and Genie.

 

After moving from Oracle and Fabric to a unified Databricks platform, the Ingredients and Trading team shifted from static reporting to governed, natural language access to data. The team now supports 1,300+ data products and has deployed 25+ Genie Spaces, driving rapid adoption and measurable business impact.

 

You’ll hear how Metric Views and AI/BI Dashboards are becoming the standard, and how Fonterra is extending Genie into multi-agent workflows—connecting Genie Spaces with Knowledge Agents for leadership reporting—as they scale AI-powered analytics to 20,000+ users.

speakers.name: Curt Roehricht
speakers.bio: Passionate about turning data into real-world impact, I lead teams and initiatives that transform ideas into outcomes. I focus on building high-performing teams, driving innovation, and making data a core driver of business success—with a hands-on approach and a strong bias for action.

speakers.name: Divya Perumal
speakers.bio: As a Senior Data Engineer with nine years of hands-on experience, I specialize in architecting and optimizing scalable data platforms that power business transformation. My work spans leading large-scale on-premise to cloud migrations, where I've championed reimagined, cloud-native solutions over simple lift-and-shift approaches. I'm passionate about elevating data quality and building robust observability into every layer of the data stack, ensuring reliable, actionable insights at scale. I’m currently leading a big project in Fonterra which is focussed on migrating a legacy system called ‘MAS’ which uses tools like SQL and SSIS to a modern data platform built completely on Databricks.

sessions.title: One Stack for Retail AI: From Transactional Planning to Agentic Intelligence on Databricks
sessions.body:
Retail AI platforms are no longer just analytics or ML systems — they must power real-time planning, massive-scale AI and intelligent decisioning on a single foundation. In this session, we share how our retail AI SaaS product is built entirely on Databricks’ unified platform.

 

What we do uniquely on Databricks:

  • We run classic AI (forecasting, optimization) and GenAI + agentic workflows together in a single Databricks stack, eliminating fragmentation between ML pipelines, planning logic and intelligent decision automation.
  • Our hyperlocal forecasting USP (unique model per SKU–Store via ensemble selection) is possible only because Databricks enables massive distributed ML at low cost, scaling to millions of combinations without infrastructure sprawl.
  • Hierarchical forecasting across store > city > region > national levels, combined with genetic optimization for inventory and replenishment, runs at production scale using Apache Spark™’s distributed compute and optimized execution engine.

speakers.name: Amit Rohatgi
speakers.bio: Amit Rohatgi leads Product Management at Algonomy, with deep expertise in composable CDP architecture, mult-channel marketing, and real-time personalisation. He works closely with enterprise retail customers across the US, UK, and APAC to solve the hardest data-to-decision problems in modern retail — translating complex architecture patterns into practical frameworks that marketing and technology teams can act on together.

sessions.title: Open Streaming Meets Governed Lakehouse: Running Apache Flink With Unity Catalog–Managed Delta Tables
sessions.body: As organizations adopt open streaming engines like Apache Flink alongside centralized governance platforms, interoperability becomes critical. This talk explores how the Flink Delta Connector bridges Flink’s real-time processing model with Delta Lake tables managed by Unity Catalog. We’ll explain how the connector preserves Delta’s ACID guarantees, integrates with UC-managed metadata, and respects centralized governance when writes originate from external Flink clusters. Through architectural deep dives and practical examples, we show how teams can build end-to-end streaming pipelines that combine Flink’s scalability with Databricks’ unified governance and lakehouse architecture.

sessions.title: Open Table Formats for Dummies
sessions.body:
With the enormous amount of discussion about open storage formats between nerds and even not-nerds, it can be hard to keep track of who’s doing what and how this actually makes any impact on day to day data projects.

Let's take a closer look at the three big projects in this space; Delta, Hudi and Iceberg. They’re all trying to solve for similar data problems and have tackled the various challenges in different ways. This talk with start with the very basics of how we got here, what the history is before diving deep into the underlying tech, their roadmaps, and their impacts on the data landscape as a whole.

speakers.name: Holly Smith
speakers.bio: Holly Smith is a developer advocate and multi-award-winning Data and AI expert and tech educator with over a decade of experience working at the cutting edge of Data and AI in various capacities. One of the first employees at Databricks, she is a renowned public speaker and teacher. She is well known for her YouTube series on AI + data engineering.

sessions.title: OpenAI + Hertz Global + Databricks: Turning Customer Feedback into Business Impact
sessions.body:
Generative AI is moving from proof-of-concept to production at scale, but the path from lab to customer-facing workload remains unclear for many enterprises.

 

In this joint session, we'll explore the common use cases that leading enterprises are adopting. OpenAI will share insights from across their customer bases on model selection, serving infrastructure, latency and cost optimization.

 

Then Hertz Global will walk through their production implementation: how they operationalized GPT-powered NPS survey summarization across thousands of daily surveys for storefront managers, and deployed Whisper for real-time call transcription to accelerate high-value lead conversion. You'll see how their Databricks Apps consume and present summarized insights, even delivering automated audio briefings to branch managers.

 

This session will equip you with the use case patterns, architectural blueprints, and real-world lessons that separate successful deployments from stalled pilots.

sessions.title: Operating Databricks at Enterprise Scale: 60–70% MTTR Reduction Through SQL & AI Functions
sessions.body:
As Databricks scales enterprise-wide, IT Operations teams face mounting challenges: controlling analytics costs, maintaining reliability and supporting business-critical workloads. A global semiconductor manufacturer leveraged Databricks SQL and AI functions to transform operations at scale—turning cost control and incident response into repeatable, automated workflows.

 

Databricks SQL and AI functions create an autonomous optimization engine, Unity Catalog ensures enterprise governance and production-safe validation guarantees zero SLA risk.

 

Databricks SQL provides the analytical foundation, enabling deep workload analysis through query metadata, execution plans and table statistics. AI functions layer intelligent reasoning on top, automatically generating optimized SQL, reconstructing data lineage and validating code transformations—all within the platform. These are leveraged to address five key problems and the operations team could save a significant time and achieve cost savings.

sessions.title: Operational Analytics at Speed: The Engine behind the Lakehouse
sessions.body: Operational analytics demands fast, predictable performance. Traditional engines often struggle to deliver speed at scale. In this session, we discuss how the engine behind Databricks Lakehouse powers operational analytics and future workloads. Join this session to understand how the Lakehouse enables faster, lower-cost analytics.

speakers.name: Himanshu Raja
speakers.bio: Himanshu Raja is a Directory of Product at Databricks working on DBSQL, Query engine, and table formats.

speakers.name: Matt Holzapfel
speakers.bio: Matt Holzapfel is a Product Adoption leader at Databricks where he helps customers adopt emerging product capabilities. Prior to Databricks, he was the Chief Product Officer at Tamr. Matt earned an MBA from Harvard Business School and a bachelor's degree in engineering from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

sessions.title: Operationalizing Fine-Grained Data Security With ABAC at Enterprise Scale
sessions.body:
As Amgen’s analytics platform scaled across teams and data domains, enforcing fine-grained data access through direct user and group entitlements became difficult to operate, govern and audit. Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) enabled a shift to policy-driven access based on business attributes, delivering consistent enforcement, improved scalability and reduced operational overhead across the platform.

 

This session details how ABAC emerged as the next step in Amgen’s data security architecture. We will cover early challenges with third-party access control tools, our migration to Databricks Unity Catalog, and the progressive adoption of dynamic views, row-level filtering and column-level masking. These capabilities laid the groundwork for scalable, attribute-driven access control.

 

Attendees will learn the key architectural choices, implementation of tradeoffs and governance results behind deploying ABAC on Databricks at Amgen.

speakers.name: Jaison Dominic
speakers.bio: Jaison Dominic is a Data & Analytics Strategy leader with a passion for driving innovation and unlocking the value of data. He excels in leading enterprise data platform strategies that fuel business growth, streamline operations, and enhance customer experience. With deep expertise in advanced analytics and emerging technologies, Jaison delivers actionable insights that enable impactful decision-making. He is committed to driving organizational success through data-driven excellence and transformation.

speakers.name: Jinesh Kunjumon
speakers.bio: Technology enthusiast with a passion for problem solving and a proven track record in designing, developing, and deploying scalable data warehouse and analytics solutions across industries. Experienced in modernizing legacy systems, building data lakehouses, and leading cloud migration initiatives. Adept at architecting secure, high-performance big data platforms and driving innovation through platform capabilities. Skilled in AWS, Databricks, Snowflake, Python, Java, and Scala. Known for leading cross-functional teams, handling petabyte-scale data, and delivering value through strategic technology adoption and robust engineering frameworks.

sessions.title: Optimize Lakehouse Cost and Performance With Intelligent Storage and Liquid Clustering
sessions.body:
Optimizing cost and performance in the lakehouse starts with how your data is stored and organized. In this session, we’ll show how Intelligent Storage and Liquid Clustering work together to automatically optimize data layout for your workloads. You’ll get a quick refresher on Liquid Clustering, then dive into what’s new, including Automatic Liquid Clustering on Unity Catalog managed tables, adaptive layouts that handle evolving query patterns, and metadata-driven optimizations that reduce unnecessary data scans.

 

More importantly, we’ll cover best practices for when and how to rely on automation versus manual tuning. Learn how to choose the right table types, avoid common pitfalls, and take advantage of co-clustered joins and layout-aware optimizations to accelerate queries at scale. Whether you’re managing terabytes or petabytes, walk away with practical guidance to reduce costs and improve performance without constant intervention.

speakers.name: Jeffrey Gong
speakers.bio: Product Manager at Databricks on the Lakehouse Storage and Predictive Optimization team

speakers.name: Rahul Mahadev
speakers.bio: Databricks Engineer working on Delta Lake since 2019

sessions.title: Optimizing AI/BI Dashboard performance: Best practices for speed and scale
sessions.body: Slow queries, long load times, and inconsistent responsiveness don't just frustrate users — they limit adoption and erode trust in your data. In this session, we'll teach you how to apply the right design patterns and leverage the latest AI/BI Dashboard capabilities — including automatic materialization to deliver consistently fast, interactive performance at scale. You'll walk away knowing how to: - Design datasets and queries for fast, interactive dashboard performance - Leverage caching, query optimization, and warehouse configuration effectively - Use automatic materialization for the right queries to maximize performance gains - Identify and fix common performance pitfalls

speakers.name: Daniel Streit
speakers.bio: Daniel is a Staff Software Engineer at Databricks.

sessions.title: Performance Tuning the Data Platform at Databricks
sessions.body: Even on the world's fastest data platform, inefficient code can bring pipelines to a crawl. In this technical deep dive, the Data Platform team shares the specific optimization techniques we use to tune our heaviest, most complex internal workloads. From optimizing file sizing and Z-ordering to leveraging predictive I/O and materialized views, we will share the "power user" tips and tricks that we use to shave hours off our runtimes. If you want to know how the experts tune Databricks for maximum performance, this is the session to attend.

speakers.name: Bruce Wong
speakers.bio: Bruce leads our internal Data Platform function at Databricks.   We build, own and operate our enterprise lakehouse for Databricks where all employees and all teams inside use Data and AI to solve problems and guide our decisions.  Previously Bruce held technical leadership roles at Netflix, Twilio and StitchFix where he gained deep experience building planet scale systems in a cloud-native environment.  Bruce also formed the Chaos Engineering team and led the initiative at Netflix to achieve ultimate resilience.  Bruce has also shares his experience and insights serving on product advisory boards previously for DataDog, PagerDuty, currently for DataBricks.

sessions.title: Petabytes in Plain Sight: Extending Databricks to the On-Prem Data You Already Have
sessions.body: Every enterprise building a lakehouse hits the same wall: the most valuable data lives on-premises. You can mask it. Tokenize it. Replicate a fraction. But data bound by HIPAA, GDPR, or sovereignty mandates cannot leave at all. Either way, Databricks never sees the full picture.Until now.MinIO and Databricks have solved this by embedding open sharing protocols directly into the data foundation. When your data foundation natively speaks open sharing protocols, data movement becomes unnecessary. Databricks queries on-prem tables directly, in place with full governance retained by the data owner.MinIO CTO Ugur Tigli shows how customer demand drove MinIO and Databricks to run analytics on full-fidelity production data on-prem through open protocols like Delta Sharing and the Apache Iceberg™ REST API. He covers what happens to your security posture when pipelines disappear, what it means when you unlock petabytes to become first-class Databricks assets.

sessions.title: Phar Lakehouse: The Evolution of Our Data Market
sessions.body:
As organizations migrate to the lakehouse architecture, they often struggle with the fragmented management of physical storage, authentication, and logical governance layers. This session introduces "Phar Lakehouse," a robust data product designed to standardize and automate the deployment of Databricks Unity Catalog across complex enterprise environments.

 

We will explore how the Phar Data Platform team leveraged infrastructure as code (Terraform) to transform disjointed infrastructure tasks into a unified “black box” process. By providing a standardized storage foundation based on the Medallion Architecture, Phar Lakehouse enables squads to deploy tailored schemas—including specialized Utilities and PII-secure layers—without manual overhead.

speakers.name: Leandro Szikora
speakers.bio: Driven by a love for data systems and the impact of smart, scalable architecture. Outside of optimizing cloud infrastructures, my workflow is powered by the argentinian traditional mate and the constant supervision of my two cat assistants, who ensure my workday stays as productive (and well-feline) as possible

sessions.title: Physical AI in Supply Chains: How Real-Time Intelligence Maximizes Visibility and Reduces Loss
sessions.body: Supply chain leaders lack real-time visibility into the location and condition of goods across complex, distributed networks — driving shrink, inefficiencies, and missed revenue.Physical AI introduces a new paradigm by continuously capturing real-world data from physical assets, enabling a live, accurate view of operations. The Wiliot Physical AI platform, powered by Databricks, processes this data at scale to deliver real-time intelligence and automated decision-making.Organizations are achieving up to 12x ROI by improving inventory accuracy, reducing loss, and unlocking end-to-end visibility. Leading retailers like Walmart are using this approach to transform how they monitor and optimize product flow.Attend this session to learn how to operationalize Physical AI in your supply chain and achieve continuous, scan-free, real-time visibility — so you can respond instantly, reduce waste, and drive ROI from day one.

speakers.name: Amir Khoshniyati
speakers.bio: Amir leads Strategy, Channel, & Marketing for Wiliot. Prior, he was the Executive Vice President and General Manager of Identiv IoT. He also served as the Head of NFC Business at Avery Dennison following the successful acquisition of Smartrac in March of 2020. He is a leading stakeholder for IoT, BLE, and NFC technology globally, and previously served on the NFC Forum Board, which defines standards, processes, and leads the adoption of the technology in this IoT era. Amir was recognized for the design of four value-add solutions that are key modules within the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Product Stack. He has a strong passion for assisting youth in the Southern California community and frequently gives back through his organization, Gentlemen of Orange County.

sessions.title: Pilot to Platform: How NAB Deployed Databricks Genie at Scale Across the Bank
sessions.body:
While initial generative AI adoption is simple, operating it at scale demands strong governance, clear controls, and coordinated rollout across teams. In this session, NAB shares how it implemented Databricks Genie as a first‑class engineering capability, from early prototypes to bank‑wide adoption.

 

We will walk through the key decisions and patterns that made Genie genuinely useful for technical teams: how it integrates with existing SDLC and data workflows, how NAB approached onboarding and change management, and examples of high-value use cases and how their benefits were measured.

 

Attendees will leave with a practical blueprint for scaling Databricks Genie in their own organisations, rollout phases, adoption playbooks and lessons learned on what to avoid.

 

Whether you are just experimenting with Genie or planning an enterprise rollout, this session will help you turn a promising pilot into a reliable, governed platform for AI‑assisted development.

sessions.title: Pipeline to Production in Minutes: How a Leading P&C Insurer Achieved End-to-End DevOps on Databricks
sessions.body:
P&C insurance data platforms must deliver analytics rapidly while meeting stringent governance and regulatory requirements. Although Databricks is widely adopted as the analytics backbone, many P&C organizations continue to struggle with inconsistent deployments, manual promotions and fragmented DevOps practices.

 

This lightning talk demonstrates how a P&C organization implemented true end-to-end DevOps on Databricks using Asset Bundles, Databricks Apps and GitHub Actions.

 

Learn how a Git-driven, declarative deployment model uses Asset Bundles to package notebooks, workflows and DLT pipelines with environment-aware configuration, enabling consistent promotion across multiple environments, while GitHub Actions orchestrates CI/CD pipelines for validation, automated deployment and auditability.

 

The session highlights how Databricks Apps are integrated into the same pipeline to operationalize analytics use cases as secure, production-ready data product governed by Unity Catalog.

speakers.name: Harshit Mishra
speakers.bio:
Harshit Mishra
Principal Data Engineer
Nationwide Insurance – P&C Data Organization

15+ years of experience working across diverse data projects and technologies.
6+ years of expertise with Databricks, focusing on building data pipelines, managing Databricks infrastructure and implementing standards and best practices.
Currently serving as a Principal Data Engineer, leading the Data Enablement Team in the Nationwide P&C Data Organization.
Passionate about driving data modernization, efficiency, and delivering business value through innovative data solutions.

sessions.title: Pitch Data to Player Insights: How the Cleveland Guardians Use AI and Real-Time Analytics at Scale
sessions.body: The Cleveland Guardians run a real-time data and AI platform that ingests live game feeds, scores every pitch with neural network models, and delivers AI-powered scouting insights to analysts through natural language tools.Behind the scenes, this system supports high-stakes, in-game decisions. Built on Databricks, it combines streaming ingestion, ETL pipelines, model serving, and live dashboards. The challenge was not just building it, but deploying it across dev, QA, and production without slowing innovation.In this session, we will share how we standardized and scaled the platform using Databricks Asset Bundles. By consolidating assets into a version-controlled monorepo, we created a unified deployment framework for modular jobs, shared clusters, coordinated builds, and post-deployment orchestration.You will leave with a practical blueprint for operationalizing a modern data and generative AI platform, plus candid lessons on what worked and what we would refine.

sessions.title: Powering bespoke experiences with Genie: APIs, integrations, and embedded AI agents
sessions.body: Genie delivers trusted conversational analytics—and now it can reach your users wherever your they work.With Genie, users can now talk to their data directly from the tools they already use: Teams, Slack, Confluence, or custom web apps. Whether you’re using our native Copilot Studio/Foundry integrations or building with the Genie Conversation APIs/SDK, Genie can now bring natural-language analytics into everyday workflows.In this session, we’ll show how to build and deploy Genie-powered experiences across your organization:- Build custom conversational apps using Genie Conversation APIs and MCP- Leverage native integrations with Teams and Slack, and extend into Microsoft Power Platform and Copilot Studio- Design AI agents that operate seamlessly within real business workflows- Apply best practices for secure, scalable, and governed integrations

speakers.name: Ambarish Dongaonkar
speakers.bio:
Ambarish Dongaonkar is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he partners with organizations to build robust, scalable data architectures on the Lakehouse platform. An expert in modern data paradigms, Ambarish specializes in Data Governance, and the integration of embedded AI agents.
He is a frequent speaker at industry events, including the Data + AI Summit, AI Days and regional User Groups, where he shares best practices on leveraging Databricks Genie APIs to bring natural-language analytics into everyday workflows. Additionally, Ambarish is an active contributor to the data engineering community, co-authoring thought leadership on Lakehouse presentation layers and architectural best practices.

sessions.title: Powering KPMG Audit’s AI Future with Databricks
sessions.body: What does it take to turn a complex audit estate into an AI‑ready lakehouse in months, enabling auditors to move faster without losing trust? KPMG migrated nearly 400 SQL Server scripts into Databricks SQL in three months using lakehouse patterns, Lakebridge, and AI‑assisted refactoring — cutting manual effort while maintaining audit‑grade governance, lineage and performance. This session unpacks the blueprint: unified governance on Delta, SQL Serverless to handle extreme peak‑season demand and secure cross‑entity data access built for regulated environments. A focused enablement program onboarded 200+ users rapidly, embedding modern engineering practices and an AI‑first mindset. Finally, we’ll explore how this platform now powers AI/BI Genie and Lakeflow Designer, putting governed natural‑language and low‑code analytics directly into the hands of citizen analysts and front‑line auditors.

speakers.name: Simon Kershaw
speakers.job_title: Partner - CTO Run and Build UK Audit

sessions.title: Prada Group Serves High-Quality Business Metrics with Lakebase
sessions.body: Prada Group's advanced analytics and KPI calculations had evolved across multiple disconnected systems, each serving different teams and use cases. This fragmentation made it difficult to maintain consistent definitions, reuse existing logic, and deliver a single trusted view of performance across the business. As data volumes and reporting demands increased, the organization needed a way to reliably manage and compute thousands of KPIs across regions, product categories, and time periods while still providing fast, decision-ready insights. To address this, Prada Group implemented a unified analytics architecture supported by Lakebase as its central data foundation. Lakebase consolidated previously siloed data into a single governed and scalable environment, enabling high-volume storage, efficient querying, and low-latency KPI computation. On top of this foundation, a standardized KPI model and microservices-based APIs provided consistent, easily accessible analytics across departments and systems, transforming fragmented reporting into a trusted, enterprise-wide capability for data-driven decision making.

speakers.name: Andrea Carmè
speakers.bio: Andrea Carmè is a Senior Manager at ICONSULTING with over 15 years of experience in data platforms, analytics, and AI-driven transformation. He is a Databricks Solution Architect Champion, specializing in designing and governing enterprise-scale Lakehouse architectures on Databricks. Andrea works closely with organizations in Fashion & Luxury and Consumer industries, helping them turn data into trusted, scalable, and AI-ready assets. Andrea is a frequent speaker at Databricks events and an active contributor to the Databricks community.

speakers.name: Michele Piunti
speakers.bio: Michele is a global executive in data, AI, and digital transformation, recognized for leading enterprise-wide innovation and advanced analytics initiatives. As Data Platform manager at Prada Group, he leads strategic transformation programs and is the principal architect of the Group’s global enterprise Data Lakehouse. He has also held leadership positions at Prada Group, Boston Consulting Group, Reply Group driving business transformation through AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics across consumer retail, fashion, and luxury. He holds a European PhD in Computer Science and an MSc in Artificial Intelligence and Software Engineering, and has authored over 70 publications in AI and computer science venues.

sessions.title: Precision and Progress: An Industry Manufacturing Executive Session
sessions.body: Manufacturing excellence demands both precision in execution and progress in thinking. This exciting session, featuring industry leaders from Cummins and Corning, examines the practices and innovations driving competitive manufacturing operations and what it takes to lead them.

speakers.name: Denis Kamotsky
speakers.bio:
Over 25 years of professional experience in software architecture, design, development, and support. Specializing in E-Commerce, Manufacturing, Information Retrieval, and Machine Learning applications.

Arrived in e-commerce from the background in computational linguistics research. As a Principal Engineer at macys*com, designed, and built Keyword Search and Product Discovery platforms. Implemented original engineering solutions covered by multiple U.S. patents.

Now working in Corning as a Principal Software Engineer, Advanced Analytics. Helping researchers, data scientists, and technologists build and scale cloud-enabled machine learning pipelines. Promoting modern software development practices in the world of advanced analytics.

sessions.title: Precision Targeting at Scale: How GM & Acxiom Turn Customer Intelligence into Measurable Outcomes
sessions.body: GM has leveraged their robust data foundations and modeling expertise to drive measurable marketing outcomes. Leveraging the Databricks platform and Acxiom product offerings, GM has built an intelligence layer across the customer lifecycle, applying identity resolution, propensity modeling, and audience optimization to power smarter, faster decisioning across channels.By operationalizing these capabilities at scale, GM is sharpening audience targeting, increasing marketing effectiveness, and accelerating time-to-activation across its brand portfolio. This session explores how GM and Acxiom are translating data infrastructure investments into real, quantifiable impact, and what it takes to make intelligence-driven marketing a repeatable, scalable practice.

speakers.name: Jennifer McCluskey
speakers.bio: Jennifer McCluskey is a marketing data strategist who has spent her career creating systems, teams, and solutions that deliver lasting value. At General Motors, she leads technical enablement within Marketing Applied Sciences (MAS), where they are advancing AI, data, and activation capabilities in service of the marketing organization. Her team supports precision targeting and their in-house identity-driven audience activation model, while expanding capabilities in AI-powered experimentation and clean room measurement, enabling faster, more precise decision-making across the brand portfolio.

sessions.title: Predictable Migrations: Scaling Lakebase Adoption With Provider-Agnostic Readiness Tools
sessions.body:
Successful migration from managed OLTP services to Lakebase depends on one factor: identifying architectural nuances before the transition begins. Instead of a “move-and-fix” approach, teams need a rigorous, automated way to audit environments and quantify technical debt. This session introduces a unified readiness assessment framework designed to evaluate any managed OLTP workload for Lakebase compatibility.

 

We will explore how an automated engine interrogates database metadata to audit schemas, extensions, and configuration limits. By analyzing version disparities and provider-specific constraints, the tool generates a high-fidelity compatibility roadmap. This approach allows architects to identify blockers early, estimate refactoring with precision and build a high-integrity execution plan. Attendees will learn to standardize pre-migration checks, transforming a high-stakes transition into a predictable, well-orchestrated architectural upgrade.

speakers.name: Fatine Boujnouni
speakers.bio: Fatine Boujnouni is a Senior Specialist Solutions Engineer at Databricks based in Paris, with strong expertise in data warehouse migrations and business intelligence. She helps organizations modernize legacy data platforms, design scalable analytics and AI solutions, and bridge technical and business teams to deliver practical business outcomes.

speakers.name: Savannah Longoria
speakers.bio: Savannah Longoria is a Senior Developer Advocate at Databricks. She's spent her career in the database world, from SingleStore to PlanetScale to Neon (now part of Databricks). She started out as a Solutions Architect helping customers design schemas and optimize queries, and now spends her time building tools and writing content to make Neon and Lakebase easier to work with. Based in Seattle, WA, Savannah cares about making complex database concepts approachable and meeting developers where they are.

sessions.title: Press Start: From Gaming to Real-Time Analytics with Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
What if classic video games could teach you new tricks — and what if community gameplay data could power automation?

 

Join Andrew Sitz (Databricks MVP) and Scott Haines (Staff Developer Advocate) as they build a live gaming environment on Databricks. We'll load a Game from Unity Catalog Volumes, host interactive gameplay through Databricks Apps, and capture every input and state change as streaming data. Using Lakebase and Delta Lake, we persist player sessions, track progress, and serve real-time leaderboards with low latency and full ACID guarantees. From there, we explore how aggregate play data reveals community patterns — surfacing strategies and insights players might never find alone.

 

Finally, we show how recorded gameplay can train simple automation strategies, closing the loop from observation to action. Come for the nostalgia, stay for the data engineering.

speakers.name: Scott Haines
speakers.bio:
Scott Haines is a seasoned software engineer specializing in massive distributed data systems and streaming technologies. Over the past 18 years, he’s built and scaled data infrastructure at leading companies, including Yahoo!, Twilio, Nike, and, currently stepped into a role as a Staff Developer Advocate at Databricks.

Scott was a Databricks Beacon/MVP for five years before joining Databricks, he’s the author of books on Apache Spark and Delta Lake, and makes it his mission to help organizations successfully adopt open-source.

sessions.title: Privacy-Centric Identity Resolution for Analytics and Activation
sessions.body:
Identity resolution sits at the core of modern data and AI. As signals disappear and privacy constraints tighten, the ability to unify fragmented customer records across partners directly impacts data quality, analytics accuracy, and model performance. In this session, we show how Databricks Clean Rooms enable organizations to build a trusted view of customer data by resolving identities across datasets without exposing raw PII.

 

Join us for a technical deep dive with LiveRamp as we demonstrate how a durable identity backbone supports accurate, privacy-safe matching across organizations. You will learn how to standardize fragmented data into interoperable models, improve match rates, and unlock higher-fidelity analytics through governed collaboration using Clean Rooms.

 

We will also cover practical implementation patterns, including enforcing privacy controls and scaling compliant collaboration across multiple partners. The result is a foundation for identity-first analytics that improves your marketing outcomes while maintaining strong privacy standards.

speakers.name: Nikhil Gaekwad
speakers.bio: Nikhil leads product management for the Data & AI Ecosystem at Databricks, where he focuses on products that help customers and partners securely build, share, and collaborate across the lakehouse. His work spans Databricks Clean Rooms, partner ecosystem experiences, and emerging AI governance initiatives.

sessions.title: Proactive Cyber Defense with Global Cyber Threat Intelligence, Scaled Analytics and AI Acceleration
sessions.body: In 2025, the Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) provider ecosystem produced over 1.9 trillion data points delivered in over 100,000 data feeds that describe threat actors, their tactics, techniques & procedures (TTPs) and related indicators of compromise.  To leverage this global CTI for proactive defense against these attacks, all the data must be consumed, analyzed and operationalized in real-time - any delays create exploitable gaps that can lead to infiltration, data theft, extortion and malicious outcomes.  This session will provide insights into the challenges and successes in the designing of a scalable intelligence analytics and operations platform that streams global CTI from its sources into Databricks to enable human and autonomous classification, triaging and deployment of actionable threat indicators and context within minutes of ingestion.

speakers.name: Dave Ahn
speakers.bio: Dave is a technology leader and innovator with a distinguished track record in cybersecurity and healthcare informatics.  He holds numerous patents in these fields, many of which have been successfully commercialized through groundbreaking startups.  At his current endeavor, Centripetal, Dave focuses on proactive ways of leveraging intelligence and analytics to transform cybersecurity defenses, accelerate security operations and advance threat research.

sessions.title: Production Lakebase Patterns: OAuth Token Lifecycle, Async Pooling, and Caching for Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
Lakebase gives you PostgreSQL on Databricks, but production applications need patterns the documentation doesn't cover. From deploying a conversation persistence layer for an energy sector knowledge assistant, we share battle-tested solutions: Proactive OAuth token refresh that recreates connection pools before credentials expire, async connection pooling with psycopg3 sized for Databricks Apps concurrency, LRU caching with TTL for high-frequency thread lookups, and upsert patterns with conflict resolution for concurrent agent writes. Every pattern is production code running on Databricks Apps today.

 

This lightning talk is for developers who've tried Lakebase in a notebook and want to know what it takes to run it in a real application with real users.

speakers.name: Irvin Umaña
speakers.bio: I am currently a Lead Scale Solutions Engineer at Databricks, where over the past three years I have helped customers architect, deploy, and operationalize ML and Gen AI solutions in production environments. My work spans scalable AI system design, enterprise implementation, and modern data architectures leveraging technologies such as Lakebase (Databricks Postgres), translating advanced analytical methods into real-world applications. I am also an M.Sc. candidate in Electrical Engineering at the University of Costa Rica, where my research focuses on reconstruction algorithms for the LHCb experiment at CERN.

sessions.title: Production Patterns for Multi-Tenant AI: Scaling to 800 Banks on Databricks
sessions.body: Serving 800 German banks on one AI platform required solving a fundamental multi-tenant challenge: maintaining strict data isolation while scaling to hundreds of QPS under banking regulations. We present two innovations:1. Metadata-driven capacity management: Delta tables track index capacity per endpoint in real-time. When thresholds are reached, the system provisions new Vector Search endpoints and rebalances indexes. This eliminates manual scaling interventions and provides a reusable pattern for any platform hitting infrastructure limits at scale.2. Hierarchical retrieval with RAPTOR: Plain Agents retrieve flat chunks. We implement recursive clustering and summarization to build tree structures, enabling retrieval across abstraction levels, from granular details to high-level themes. This approach significantly improves answer quality for complex financial documents.Takeaways: federated vector search patterns, metadata-driven auto-scaling architecture, RAPTOR implementation

speakers.name: Simon Schmitz
speakers.bio:
Simon is a Senior Data Scientist and AI Engineer at Atruvia, the digitalization and IT partner for Germany’s cooperative banking network. He works on GenoGPT, a GenAI-powered platform for banks. With 10 years of experience in AI and data engineering, including 7 years focused on natural language processing and conversational systems, he specializes in building scalable AI systems for the banking and insurance sectors.
Simon is passionate about bridging the gap between AI innovation and software engineering best practices to build reliable, production-ready AI systems at scale.

sessions.title: Provisioning for the Agentic Era: How Databricks Built a Self-Serve Infrastructure Vending Machine
sessions.body:
As Databricks' go-to-market organization grew past 7,000 people — and AI agents became first-class consumers of platform resources alongside human engineers — our field team ran into a familiar problem: shared demo environments couldn't keep up. Too many users needed admin-level access, platform limits became real constraints, and it was hard to see who was using what, whether that "who" was a person or an agent.

 

In this session, we'll share how we addressed that by building the Field Engineering Vending Machine (FEVM), a Databricks App that gives every engineer — and every agent — just-in-time, isolated, and governed environments on demand. Instead of filing tickets or juggling shared workspaces, engineers describe what they're trying to do — build a demo, run a hackathon, reproduce an issue, spin up an agentic workflow — and FEVM delivers a fit-for-purpose environment in minutes, then cleans it up automatically when it's no longer needed.

 

We'll show how this "vending machine" model has improved speed, control, and cost visibility for thousands of users and countless agent runs, and why building it as a Databricks App has become a blueprint for how we dogfood the platform internally — for the agentic era and beyond.

sessions.title: Public Sector Industry Forum
sessions.body: Join public sector leaders at this year’s forum to hear firsthand how organizations are modernizing the way they operate, moving from fragmented siloed systems to connected data platforms that enable real collaboration across organizational boundaries. Through candid conversations and real-world results, this forum will explore how the public sector is embracing the speed and innovation of commercial technology to finally deliver on the promise of data-driven mission outcomes.

speakers.name: Marcie Kahbody
speakers.job_title: Deputy Secretary and AIO, California State Transportation Agency & CIO, Caltrans
speakers.bio:
Marcie Kahbody is the Deputy Secretary of Technology, Agency Information Officer (AIO) for the California State Transportation Agency and the Chief Information Officer (CIO) for Caltrans. Marcie leads collaboration across California transportation entities to increase innovation and successful IT delivery. Marcie is responsible for developing policies and procedures to govern business processes, security protocols, operational programs, and IT resources.
Marcie has held IT positions within the State of California for over 32 years, including the role of AIO at CalSTA since 2015. Prior to she worked at the Department of Health Care Services, Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation, and Department of Technology, and Department of General Services.
Marcie earned a bachelor’s degree in computer science from CSU Sacramento. In 2023, Marcie received the esteemed ‘Women Who Mean Business Award’ from the Sacramento Business Journal.

speakers.name: Prathibha Prabakaran
speakers.bio:
Everyone wants AI. Few know how to run it.
I am an enterprise technology and data leader focused on turning AI from ambition into execution. Working at the intersection of platform strategy, data architecture, and operating models, I help organizations move beyond pilots to systems that scale. Their work spans modern data platforms, event-driven architectures, and governance frameworks that balance speed with trust. Known for cutting through hype, I bring a practical lens to how enterprises actually build, orchestrate, and operationalize AI - where complexity is the norm and execution is the differentiator.

speakers.name: Ryan Mosley
speakers.company: Cal Department of Health Care Services

speakers.name: Venu Boppana
speakers.bio: Venu Boppana is a Strategy and Innovation leader in the Office of Business Informatics (OBI) in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), FDA.  The Office of Business Informatics (OBI) supports CDER’s regulatory decision-making by identifying, implementing, and managing CDER-wide informatic systems to meet business needs. Since joining the FDA in 2013, Mr. Boppana has led several critical strategic programs by introducing AI/ML/Gen AI to support mission critical business initiatives including Drug Supply Chain, COVID IT projects, CDEROne Enterprise Data Analytics Program. He has over 20-years’ experience in leading and architecting Augmented Analytics, Enterprise Architecture, Cloud Infrastructure and Applications Development.

sessions.title: Read-Time CDF in Delta Lake
sessions.body:
Traditionally, enabling Change Data Feed (CDF) in Delta Lake incurs a "write tax"—increasing storage costs and latency to materialize changes during ingestion.

 

In this session, we introduce Read-Time CDF, a new architecture that unlocks zero-overhead writes by deferring change computation to query time. By leveraging the new unified CDC interface in Spark Data Source V2 and Delta’s Row Tracking, users can now query row-level changes without ever explicitly enabling delta.enableChangeFeed.

speakers.name: Gengliang Wang
speakers.bio:
Gengliang Wang, a committed Apache Spark PMC Member and Committer, actively works on important Spark projects including ANSI SQL mode, TIMESTAMP_NTZ data type, and data sources. His contributions extend to enhancing the SQL compiler and UI.

In addition, he's engaged in a project using large language models to streamline Spark application development. His work underscores a dedication to improving and making Apache Spark more user-friendly.

sessions.title: Real-Time Analytics on Live Postgres Data
sessions.body: Teams want to run analytics on fresh transactional data without building fragile ETL pipelines or maintaining fleets of read replicas. Lakebase addresses this by separating Postgres storage from compute. In this session, you'll see how the lakebase architecture takes this one step further, for powering low-latency operational analytics for use cases including fraud detection, real-time dashboards, all without duplicating data or slowing down production systems.

speakers.name: Ippokratis Pandis
speakers.bio: Ippokratis Pandis is a Distinguished Engineer at Databricks with a background in database systems. He spent over a decade helping shape Amazon Analytics as VP/Distinguished Engineer at AWS, and before that, he worked at Cloudera and IBM Almaden Research Center. He holds a Ph.D. from Carnegie Mellon University on multicore transaction processing and has contributed to both industry and academic communities around large-scale data management. He is currently the President of HPTS and served as General Chair of SIGMOD 2023.

speakers.name: Jonathan Katz
speakers.bio: Jonathan Katz is a Sr. Staff Product Manager at Databricks on the Lakebase Team. He's on the Core Team of the open source PostgreSQL project.

sessions.title: Real-Time Context Engineering for AI With Databricks
sessions.body:
Just like we don’t put crude oil in a car, we refine it into gasoline. AI can’t run on raw data either. It needs continuous, refined context. Serving fresh context is the missing architectural layer for reliable AI.

 

In this session, learn how Confluent Intelligence and Databricks turn operational data into low-latency context for AI agents and applications. See how Confluent’s fully managed streaming platform feeds trusted data into the Databricks lakehouse for Agent Bricks and AI/BI.

 

We’ll demo real-time architectures for anomaly detection, product personalization, and AI-powered data enrichment, showing how to keep ML models and LLMs grounded in the live state of your business, not stale batch snapshots.

 

You’ll leave with practical, streaming-native patterns to move from brittle pipelines and demos to production-grade AI on Databricks while reducing TCO.

speakers.name: Sean Falconer
speakers.bio:
Dr. Sean Falconer is Confluent’s AI Entrepreneur in Residence, driving AI strategy and thought leadership. Sean has built and launched products that have impacted millions. As the founder of Proven.com, he led engineering, product development, and go-to-market strategies, successfully guiding the company to acquisition. At Google, Sean worked on enhancing developer experience and advancing conversational AI technologies.

He holds a Postdoc in Bioinformatics at Stanford University, where he collaborated with the World Health Organization to modernize the International Classification of Diseases.

He has published extensively on topics ranging from AI to quantum computing, reflecting his diverse expertise and contributions to the field.

sessions.title: Real-Time ML Features for Payment Fraud: Architecture Patterns at Scale
sessions.body:
Checkout.com is a leading global digital payments provider, processing over $300 billion in e-commerce volume annually. Our fraud models depend on fresh features, but batch pipelines limited how quickly we could detect new fraud patterns. In this session, we’ll show how we built real-time feature pipelines using Spark Structured Streaming on Databricks, reducing feature computation to a few seconds and unlocking an eight-figure revenue opportunity.

 

We’ll cover our technical approach, including custom stateful aggregations with transformWithStateInPandas, event-time watermarking for late payments, and TTL-based state management for deduplication. We’ll also discuss cost optimization at billion-event scale, and consistency between online and offline features.

 

By incorporating real-time features into our fraud models, we achieved a 2% increase in PR-AUC, translating into millions in prevented fraud losses - offering a practical blueprint for real-time machine learning at scale.

speakers.name: Dinis Peixoto
speakers.bio: Dinis Peixoto is a Staff Machine Learning Engineer at Checkout.com, where he architects high-scale distributed systems that power global payment intelligence.
