He specializes in the end-to-end lifecycle of machine learning systems, designing resilient architectures for real-time feature engineering at billion-event scale with high-throughput, and low-latency model serving.

speakers.name: Matt Slack
speakers.bio:
Matt Slack is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, specialising in helping customers solve their data engineering and geospatial challenges, and building out their modern data platforms. He has a strong background in low latency streaming pipelines at scale, creating innovative solutions with Databricks and other technologies.

Previously he has led on the build and architecture of multiple cloud data platforms across a range of industries, including Finance, Transportation and E-commerce. Matt has a Bachelor's in Computer Science from the University of York.

sessions.title: Redact at the Speed of AI: De‑identifying PII in the Lakehouse with ai_query
sessions.body: Teams need to unlock data responsibly. This lightning talk shows how to use AI Functions—specifically ai_query—to automatically redact PII across both structured tables and unstructured documents in Databricks.We'll walk through how it works for tabular data, then show how the same pattern extends to free-text fields like clinical notes. We'll briefly touch on batching for throughput and checking output quality. A brief live demo runs against realistic unstructured healthcare notes, de-identifying patient information so analysts and ML teams can experiment without risk. You'll leave with reusable queries, sample prompts for both structured and unstructured redaction, and a practical starting point to operationalize PII redaction in your Lakehouse.

sessions.title: Redefining Detection Engineering With Interactive AI Agents in the SOC
sessions.body:
AI is transforming how Security Operations Centers (SOCs) operate, with tools that augment detection engineers and analysts to combat threats. We show how one SOC at a major hedge fund adopted AI to enhance detection engineering, accelerating creation, and minimizing response time.

 

By integrating the Mosaic AI Agent Framework with Databricks Notebooks & Apps, this SOC provided detection engineers an AI assistant within their existing workflow.

 

This agent accelerates detection baselining, anomaly detection, and filtering false positives while giving engineers control over final logic, ensuring human expertise remains central. The modular architecture enables adding capabilities like MITRE ATT&CK mapping, threat intelligence enrichment, and custom patterns without rewriting core logic.

 

We demonstrate this assistant and how Databricks AI tools, including Genie and MLflow Evaluation, contribute to faster development, increased efficiency, and shortened response times to emerging threats.

speakers.name: Chandhana Padmanabhan
speakers.bio: Field Engineer / Specialist Solutions Architect (AI/ML/Cybersecurity)

speakers.name: Riley Nastase
speakers.bio:
Riley Nastase is an AI/ML Engineer at Rearc, where he builds production AI, ML, and analytics systems for high-stakes data problems. He is especially interested in AI that supports decision-making in domains that demand human expertise in the loop.

With a background spanning data science and engineering delivery, Riley focuses on practical systems that are grounded in reliable data, evaluated rigorously, and designed to help experts move faster. He has strong opinions about hallucinations and false confidence, and believes that the best systems keep human discernment and accountability at the center.

sessions.title: Reimagining SIEM: SAP ECS’s Journey to an Open Security Lakehouse
sessions.body:
SAP Enterprise Cloud Services (ECS) is rethinking the traditional SIEM model by building a Security Data Platform with Lakewatch and Anvilogic shifting to an open, AI-ready foundation for cybersecurity.

 

We’ll walk through how ECS designed and operationalized the platform to replace SIEM-centric workflows with a lakehouse approach that lowers total cost and time to respond using agentic AI. We will discuss the full architecture—routing with Cribl and Kafka, ingestion into Lakewatch, detection engineering in Anvilogic, incident response and reporting. We will close out with agentic AI use cases on the roadmap that are now enabled through the open lakehouse approach.

speakers.name: Alan Mazankiewicz
speakers.bio: Alan is Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks in Germany. At Databricks he works with various cybersecurity customers and partners. He regularly speaks publicly about the intersection of cybersecurity, data and AI.

speakers.name: Ian Tetlow
speakers.bio: Ian Tetlow is a Senior Technical Leader within SAP SE’s ECS Defensive Architecture team, where he leads the technical direction of GuardTower, a centralized Databricks-based security data lake focused on large-scale cyber defence and observability. With more than 25 years of experience in data engineering and over 15 years delivering Big Data and cloud-native solutions, Ian has designed and led enterprise-scale platforms across cybersecurity, real-time streaming, analytics, and cloud transformation initiatives. His background spans SAP, Deutsche Bank, BT Cyber Defence, and the UK Office for National Statistics, with deep expertise in Databricks, Hadoop ecosystems, ETL, cloud architecture, and security-focused data platforms.

sessions.title: Reinventing Operational Scale through Agentic Underwriting
sessions.body: CFC as a Lloyd's of London leading Cyber speciality insurer, is globally scaling our business by amplifying every Underwriter. For this we've created the "Agentic Underwriter" in production to augment critical steps in the underwriting journey. By combining Databricks' delta lake architecture with modern LLMOps processes and open source frameworks like LangGraph we've rapidly created agents capable of creating fully fledged quotes. The agent is able to intelligently navigate our systems & the complexities of the speciality lines insurance process to deliver ready made quotes for our underwriters to confirm or adjust via a HITL process. The result is our underwriters have trusted quotes ready in 5 minutes vs 24 hours - a 99% time decrease. Equated to cost, we have quotes ready for £0.50 vs £5 - a 90% cost decrease. Our customers are feeling the impact with quotes arriving faster and prices more competitive. In this way, we have created the industry's first true agentic underwriter.

sessions.title: Reliance Jio  Customer Churn Radar and next best action
sessions.body: Reliance Jio’s home business (JioFiber + JioAirFiber) operates at a very large scale and is a leader in India’s home broadband market, with both fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) and 5G fixed‑wireless (FWA) connectivity users totalling ~30 million.In India’s broadband market, Jio accounts for roughly half of total broadband subscribers, with over 500 million wireless broadband (mobile included), giving it the largest overall broadband share.

speakers.name: Raghuram Velega
speakers.job_title: Vice President- Group Head Data Platform

sessions.title: Replace your Legacy SIEM with Lakewatch: Build Your Own Custom Apps with Lakehouse & Lakebase
sessions.body:
Many legacy SIEMs charge on ingestion, lock data behind proprietary formats, and limit AI customization. Databricks Lakewatch changes that. As the Open Security Lakehouse, Lakewatch lands 100% of your telemetry in open formats on Delta Lake — and because the data is open, security teams can pull any signal into custom apps built natively on Databricks.

 

This session walks through a production SecOps platform on Lakewatch, ingesting 13TB/day across 22 sources at up to 80% lower cost. OCSF-normalized SDP pipelines deliver sub-15-minute detection with 94% MITRE ATT&CK coverage. A React + FastAPI app on Databricks Apps, backed by Lakebase, shows the art of the possible — AI threat hunting with Claude and custom analyst workflows no prebuilt SIEM could surface.

speakers.name: Anand Rao
speakers.bio: As a Solutions Architect at Databricks, I support public sector clients in addressing their Data and AI challenges by leveraging Databricks' robust platform. By emphasizing collaboration and understanding client needs, I help deliver tailored solutions that enable organizations to meet and exceed their strategic goals. My work focuses on integrating Data and AI technologies to drive innovation and transformative outcomes.

speakers.name: Surya Sai Turaga
speakers.bio: My name is Surya! In the past I have played the role of a Field Engineering Leader and evangelist in the Advanced Analytics Space, I come with strong conceptual hands-on experience in Agentic AI, Cloud (AWS+Azure+GCP), Big Data and Data Warehousing environments. I worked as a developer and implemented FSLDMs on Teradata. I am passionate about turning ideas as Agentic AI automation systems. I enjoy developing high-performance teams, mentoring data enthusiasts and working in cross-functional environments.

sessions.title: Replacing Legacy Data Dumps with Governed Delta Sharing: A Real-World Provider and Consumer Story
sessions.body: Many data-sharing implementations begin with full database exports dropped into object storage, leaving consumers to navigate raw CDC logs, weak governance, and fragile manual processes.This session shares how Kraken and Meridian replaced that model with a governed, cross-cloud Delta Sharing architecture on Databricks. Kraken moved from sharing parquet files and CDC logs to publishing curated, modelled Delta tables through Databricks-managed cross-cloud Delta Sharing. Structured datasets, controlled permissions, and Infrastructure-as-Code governance enable repeatable, auditable deployment.Meridian receives Delta Shares directly into Databricks without building bespoke ingestion pipelines. More than 300 tables were available almost immediately, delivered at a 60-minute cadence. Shares surface as read-only sources via Unity Catalog, with DAB- and DLT-driven promotion into integrated layers.The result: reduced operational risk, lower TCO, and faster access to trusted data.

speakers.name: Youcef Kadri
speakers.bio: will send later

sessions.title: Retail and Consumer Goods: The Shelf Starts with Sharing— Retailers and CPGs Unlock Growth Through Data Collaboration
sessions.body:
Supply chain volatility is the new normal, and the old playbook of siloed forecasting, batch EDI, and reactive logistics can't keep up. The next frontier of CPG-retail performance isn't just efficiency; it's collaboration.

 

Leading companies are replacing linear supply chains with intelligent networks that sense and respond in real time, unifying retailer POS, demand signals, and inventory data to power AI models that continuously optimize forecasting, replenishment, and risk detection. And they're doing it on a single, governed platform where shared data fuels not just dashboards and insights, but AI agents that act autonomously— triggering replenishment, reallocating inventory, and adjusting plans the moment conditions change.

 

In this session, hear directly from the retailers and CPGs making this shift.

 

Learn how open data sharing, AI-powered demand sensing, and joint planning on Databricks are turning adversarial transactions into growth partnerships, and why the companies that collaborate on data today will own the shelf tomorrow.

speakers.name: Karan Sinha
speakers.bio: Karan is a seasoned product leader with stints at Walmart and Sabre

sessions.title: Rethinking Database Cost with Lakebase Autoscaling
sessions.body: Traditional databases charge you whether you use them or not. Lakebase's serverless autoscaling changes that, scaling compute up to match traffic spikes and down to zero when idle so you only pay for what you actually use. In this lightning talk, you'll see how autoscaling works in practice and what the cost implications look like across workloads from development environments to production applications.

sessions.title: Revolutionizing Construction Intelligence: Scaling Procore Analytics With Delta Sharing & AI
sessions.body: Procore serves as the backbone for global construction data. Historically, providing seamless access to large-scale analytics meant complex ETL pipelines and high egress costs. This session explores how Procore Analytics pivoted to a “zero-copy” architecture using Databricks Delta Sharing. We will detail our cloud connector solution, showcasing how we securely share petabyte-scale data via Unity Catalog. We’ll highlight a global enterprise that leveraged this architecture to break down internal silos. By combining Procore capital project data with diverse enterprise datasets, they unlocked high-value use cases with data primed for AI and agent execution. Attendees will learn how the open Delta Sharing protocol enables frictionless “Bring Your Own Warehouse” capabilities, reducing TCO and latency. We’ll share technical lessons on optimizing cross-cloud performance and building an AI-ready foundation for the world’s most complex industry.

sessions.title: Rewind, Replay, Recover: Building Operational Resilience at NAB With Spark Declarative Pipelines
sessions.body: Discover how National Australia Bank (NAB) scales production streaming with Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP), using Streaming Tables and Materialized Views to enable rewind and replay — restoring pipelines to a consistent state, applying fixes safely and reprocessing only affected data. Explore how this approach reduces brittle manual interventions and avoids full refreshes by leaning on declarative semantics, governed data products, and robust checkpoint/versioning patterns and helps proactively prevent bad data from reaching downstream systems and ensures that data demographics can be safely restored to their previous usable state in the Lakehouse. Walk away with actionable designs, checklists and success criteria for resilient, cost‑efficient streaming at enterprise scale in regulated environments. Outcomes include faster recovery, lower operational effort and cost, improved reliability and correctness and sustained performance as concurrency grows.

speakers.name: Dheeraj Puli
speakers.bio: Dheeraj Puli is Head of Data Reliability Engineering at National Australia Bank (NAB), where he leads teams responsible for building resilient, future‑ready data platforms and improving how more than 500 engineers deliver and operate data at scale. With over 18 years’ experience across data engineering, architecture, delivery and consulting, he has designed and run automation‑focused data environments on platforms including Teradata, big data systems, Databricks and Snowflake in senior roles at NAB and previously Commonwealth Bank, Teradata and IBM Global Services. Dheeraj is known for his passion for automation, data quality and data‑driven solutions, using DevOps practices and reliability engineering to solve complex business problems

speakers.name: Partha Sarathi Sahoo
speakers.bio:
Partha Sarathi Sahoo is a Senior Delivery Solution Architect at Databricks, where he works with enterprise customers across Australia and New Zealand to design, implement, and operationalize data and AI platforms on the Databricks Lakehouse. With over 20 years' experience spanning data engineering, big data architecture, analytics, and cloud platforms, he has built and scaled data solutions across the aviation, cloud services, and financial sectors industries in roles at Barclays, Emirates Airline, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and now Databricks.

Partha is passionate about operational resilience, data reliability, and helping organisations move from legacy platforms to modern Lakehouse architectures that deliver real business value.

sessions.title: Right Features, Right Time: Modernizing Real-Time Fraud Feature Serving on Databricks
sessions.body: Fraud does not wait for batch. To block funds from moving, Coinbase models need the right features at the right time—fresh, consistent, and served with predictable low latency.This session explains Coinbase’s Databricks-based feature platform for real-time fraud ML: Real-Time Mode on Structured Streaming; declarative Feature APIs + CI/CD (features as code); AI/agent-assisted migration and feature creation; and Lakebase feature serving targeting p99 <50ms with autoscaling and workload isolation.Early testing reduced typical streaming feature freshness from ~770ms to ~100–200ms (3.8–7.7×) and suggests potential for >90% streaming infra cost reduction and up to >95% p99 freshness improvement. Moving self-built batch feature sets to a managed feature store is also driving an estimated ~25–35% productivity gain by retiring bespoke pipelines and shrinking the on-call surface. Attendees leave with a reference architecture + migration playbook across latency, reliability, and TCO.

sessions.title: Running LLaMA at Scale: Production Inference on Databricks Model Serving
sessions.body: Serving LLMs at consumer scale stresses everything: throughput, latency, correctness and cost. At Superhuman—formerly Grammarly—we built a production system that serves a fine‑tuned LLaMA‑3B model for grammatical error correction to millions of monthly users on Databricks Model Serving. This talk shares what we validated and how: direct‑ingress patterns for high RPS, load testing toward 100K+ QPS targets, multi‑region failover and cold‑start mitigation, and observability. We’ll cover validation checks—A/B tests, golden sets—plus the cost model we used to compare against our internal vLLM-based stack, including levers like dynamic batching, autoscaling and speculative decoding. Expect concrete configs, dashboards and a candid readout of wins, incidents and unit‑economics tradeoffs that informed our ramp from pilot to majority traffic.

speakers.name: Christoph Stuber
speakers.bio: Christoph is a Machine Learning Engineer at Superhuman, where he focuses on production model inference optimization for NLP systems. He studied computer science at TU Berlin and has worked across industries on data and ML engineering projects spanning computer vision, logistics, and natural language processing. He's passionate about making ML models fast, reliable, and cost-effective at scale.

speakers.name: Mykhailo Troianovskyi
speakers.bio: Myke Troianovskyi is a Machine Learning Software Engineer at Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), where he scales production ML services serving tens of millions of users and partners with Databricks on ML inference. He built and drove company-wide adoption of an in-house ML serving framework that enabled rapid ML adoption and scaled to support user growth. Over 14 years in the industry, Myke has worked across back-end engineering, infrastructure, observability, and MLOps for companies ranging from enterprise consultancies to consumer-scale products.

sessions.title: Safe Skies: Automating Trust at Scale With AI-Generated Contracts at Boeing
sessions.body:
In aviation, "bad data" is an operational risk. For large enterprises with hundreds of data products, manual stewardship stifles innovation. To ensure "safe skies," we transformed governance and quality into engineering disciplines.

 

This session explores our "Governance as Code" architecture using DQX and Ontos on Unity Catalog. We demonstrate using GenAI to bootstrap trust, scanning raw data to auto-generate Open Data Contract Standards (ODCSq). We then show how DQX acts as the enforcer, compiling contracts into pipelines that quarantine violations and alert on drift.

 

AI-assisted contracts: Using LLMs to profile data and draft rigorous ODCS contracts, cutting onboarding time.

 

Automated quality: Deploying DQX to enforce row-level quality, quarantine bad data and trigger drift alerts.

 

Semantics-first: Using Ontos to map technical assets to business meaning for a discoverable data marketplace.

 

Join us to learn how we replaced bureaucracy with automation and engineering rigor.

speakers.name: Alan Reese
speakers.bio: Alan Reese is a Resident Solutions Architect at Databricks. Over the past year he's been embedded with Boeing's data and architecture teams, co-developing the quality and governance pattern in this session — ODCS contracts, DQX enforcement, and Unity Catalog wired into CI/CD — and has led workshops on it at Boeing and across the Databricks community. He also supports multi-quarter energy engagements and has architected end-to-end agentic GenAI solutions with Agent Bricks, Agent Framework, and Genie. Before Databricks, Alan spent a decade as a data leader, most recently Principal Data Architect at Cotton Holdings, where he built the team and greenfield lakehouse that became the company's first modern data platform.

speakers.name: Michael Hewitt
speakers.bio: As a Technical Leader and Data & AI Architect at Boeing Vancouver, I bring nearly 20 years of industry experience with six years focused on Databricks, data, and AI. Three years ago I led the roll-out and build-out of Boeing’s first Data Mesh on Databricks, centering governance on Unity Catalog to standardize metadata, lineage, access controls, and policy automation. I helped established reusable data-product patterns that reduced time-to-production, introduced MLOps and model governance and mentored cross-functional teams to scale adoption. I now focus on Governance-as-Code for a discoverable data marketplace and accelerating safe, production-grade data and AI across the enterprise. Honored to speak at the Databricks & AI Summit.

sessions.title: SAP and Databricks: Unlock the Full Potential of Databricks on Your SAP Data
sessions.body: The SAP BDC Connector on the Databricks Platform enables, for the first time, the unification of core SAP ERP, supply-chain, and financial data with operational and IoT telemetry in a single lakehouse, unlocking predictive maintenance, supply-chain optimization, and AI-driven insights that were previously out of reach. In this session, we also discuss new innovations in SAP BDC Connector and how customers are leveraging it. Then, you'll hear from CAF (Construcciones y Auxiliar de Ferrocarriles), a global leader in rail and bus manufacturing. CAF became one of the first adopters of SAP BDC, bridging rich IoT telemetry streaming from trains across three continents with the SAP modules that run their business. Don't miss this session if you are an SAP and Databricks customer, learn the use cases and lessons learned from bridging these two worlds.

speakers.name: Jon Petralanda
speakers.job_title: Head of Data & AI Centre of Excellence
speakers.bio:
Jon Petralanda Urien is a Data & AI specialist in the industrial sector. He currently serves as Head of Data & AI Centre of Excellence at CAF, where he leads the development of the company’s Data and AI platform and key strategic Data & AI initiatives.
He holds an engineering background in telecommunications, complemented by studies in industrial management, business management, and big data.
Throughout his career, he has worked with organizations such as the United Nations, IDOM, and public institutions, contributing to projects in sustainability, smart cities, and advanced analytics.
His profile combines strong technical leadership with strategic vision to drive digitalization in complex industrial environments.

sessions.title: Scale Trust, Not Headcount: AI-Powered Semantic Engineering at Southern Glazer’s Wine & Spirits
sessions.body:
Trust in business decisions erode when reports, AI Agents, and operational systems provide different values for the same KPIs. The solution is a unified semantic fabric in which KPIs are managed as versioned, testable, and reusable assets—like software—implemented entirely within Databricks without added tooling overhead.

 

Organizations no longer need hordes of data and semantic engineers, manually coding pipelines and maintaining definitions. With AI agents automating data transformations, semantic alignment, and business rule updates, organizations can reduce manual engineering effort, accelerate delivery, and lower operating costs while improving data trust.

 

This session showcases how Southern Glazer's Wine & Spirits is implementing an AI-augmented approach to build their Metrics Bank and Semantic Layer in Databricks. You'll discover real-world results: reduced manual engineering effort, accelerated time-to-insight, and scaled decision-making capabilities across the enterprise.

sessions.title: Scaling a Multi-Agent App Platform with Databricks @ SKULD
sessions.body: How we designed, scaled, and shipped a multi‑agent AI app platform for Skuld—built 100% natively on Databricks—and the unified App + AI + Data patterns that made it possible. Maritime insurance claims depend on shifting legal facts, mixed‑format case files, and strict audit requirements, and standard chunking plus top‑k filtering lost provenance and broke under load. At Skuld, we built a multi‑agent app on Databricks: Lakeflow Jobs runs parsing and enrichment pipelines, Model Serving powers synchronous agent calls, Databricks Apps handles secure user workflows, and Unity Catalog governs access end to end. The talk dives into our evidence‑first retrieval pattern, where documents become source‑linked fact cards, conflicting facts stay visible for review, and agents return exact citations instead of opaque answers. Attendees leave with a hosting decision framework and benchmark data on parsing throughput, queues, token cost, rate limits, and latency.

speakers.name: Domonkos Pal
speakers.bio: Domonkos Pal is Head of Digital Products at Hiflylabs, where he helps enterprises design and build data and AI applications on Databricks for clients across Europe and the US. His work centers on Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Genie, agents and the broader app ecosystem — particularly how to make AI applications scalable, secure, and maintainable in production, with a strong focus on DevEx and agentic  engineering workflows. As the world's first Databricks Apps MVP (2025–2026), Domonkos returns to the Data + AI Summit stage in 2026.

speakers.name: Miran Hadziomerovic
speakers.bio:
Miran is the Senior Executive and AI Lead at Skuld, the marine P&I insurer, where he runs AI across three fronts: product delivery, enterprise governance, and building AI competence across the organisation. He focuses on moving AI past pilots - shipping systems that claims handlers and underwriters actually use, with trust, auditability, and access controls designed in from the start. Alongside the build work, he puts the governance frameworks and learning programmes in place so the rest of the business can adopt AI responsibly.

Before Skuld, Miran spent years as a Senior IT Consultant across AI, ML, DevOps, infrastructure, and data/software engineering, leading cross-functional teams on complex projects for clients across industries.

sessions.title: Scaling Agentic AI and Enterprise Data Mesh With Databricks Lakebase
sessions.body:
Zillow is evolving from a search platform into an AI-native "Super App." To move agentic AI from prototype to production, we solved a critical challenge: providing agents with a reliable, high-performance sense of state.

 

Persistent memory is central to this shift. By integrating Databricks Lakebase, we’ve bridged the gap between the data lake and the millisecond latency real-time agents require. This allows our AI to maintain long-term, vectorized context—enabling agents to remember, learn and act with precision.

 

As Lakebase adoption grows, it is catalyzing enterprise-wide innovation. By powering real-time segmentation and communications, it reduces architectural friction and accelerates our Data Mesh strategy, paving the way for Zillow’s next generation of real-time data.

sessions.title: Scaling Agentic Execution at ARM to Deliver Measurable ROI
sessions.body: Most enterprises struggle to move AI from experimentation to enterprise-grade deployments because agents lack a grounded, real-world understanding of how their business actually runs. Without this "operational reality," AI agents remain unreliable at scale, creating a trust gap that prevents true autonomous execution and measurable efficiency. Together, Celonis and Databricks provide the foundation to transform operations and make them AI-first from the ground up. We provide AI agents with the business logic needed to reason about the past and predict the future, bridging the gap between raw data and autonomous action.Join us to learn how ARM is industrializing AI, moving beyond isolated pilots to an environment where people, agents, and systems work together with unprecedented accuracy. By connecting business processes, ARM is orchestrating global operations with measurable productivity gains and a clear path to long-term ROI.

speakers.name: Harsha  Dronamraju
speakers.bio: As VP of Product Management for Celonis AI (CeloAI), Harsha leads the product strategy and roadmap for a fantastic cross-functional organization of PMs, engineers, and designers. Celonis' mission is to build the "Process Context" layer—the foundational map of how a business actually operates—to power high-precision agents in the enterprise.

sessions.title: Scaling AI Agents at Mercedes-Benz: Unified AI Governance in a Multi-Cloud Enterprise Ecosystem
sessions.body:
Managing AI at the scale of Mercedes-Benz requires more than just models—it requires a unified AI ecosystem. With thousands of practitioners across global business units, the challenge was providing a single point of entry for AI capabilities while maintaining strict governance across multi-cloud and multi-model environments. In this session, we go under the hood of the Mercedes-Benz.

 

AI Ecosystem. We will detail the technical architecture that integrates Databricks Agent Framework, Model Serving, and AI Gateway to create a governed interoperability for AI agents. We’ll discuss the "how-to" of:

  • Centralizing discovery: Building an internal marketplace for foundation models and reusable agents
  • Unified governance: Integrating Mercedes-Benz AI Marketplace into Databricks AI Gateway
  • Operationalizing agents: Deploying and publishing AI agents for self-service at Mercedes-Benz

 

Attendees will leave with a technical blueprint for building an interoperable enterprise AI agent platform.

speakers.name: Markus Heubach
speakers.bio: Markus is Product Manager for the AI Ecosystem at Mercedes‑Benz. He leads multiple product teams building a cloud‑agnostic AI ecosystem across the enterprise. In his role, he shapes the strategic direction of AI initiatives and drives their execution in complex, cross‑functional environments. Markus brings extensive experience from large‑scale AI and data programs.

speakers.name: Sai Yang
speakers.bio: Sai Yang is a Solutions Architect for the Automotive Manufacturing sector at Databricks. With 6 years of experience in the data & AI domain, Sai has strong expertise in Data Science, Machine Learning, AI, and Data Governance. At Databricks, he has led multiple large-scale platform migration projects and AI use cases for global leading automotive companies. These initiatives enabled the organizations to build and implement scalable analytics and AI solutions with unified governance on Databricks, helping them become the industry leaders in data and AI. Before joining Databricks, Sai worked in technology consulting, where he designed, developed, and deployed reliable machine learning systems in production for Fortune Global 500 companies.

sessions.title: Scaling App Development Beyond the Data Team
sessions.body: The next wave of enterprise app development isn't coming from IT or data engineering alone — it's coming from everyone. Business users are building apps and agents. Analysts are shipping tools their teams actually use. And admins are left figuring out how to govern an explosion of applications they didn't deploy and can't fully see.In this session, we'll cover where enterprise app development is headed, what it means for the teams responsible for keeping things secure and cost-effective, and how Databricks Apps is evolving to give builders the freedom they need and admins the control they require. Tune in for the Apps roadmap, vision, and a look at what's coming soon.

sessions.title: Scaling at Scale: The Journey of RAIP and Genie Code at Repsol
sessions.body:
Since launching its digital transformation program in 2018, Repsol has developed RAIP, Repsol Artificial Intelligence Products, a framework that encapsulates years of analytical expertise and supports hundreds of production-grade AI models across the organization. Within RAIP, solutions such as REPSENS for time series forecasting have been validated in demanding industrial environments.

 

With the rise of generative AI, rather than treating it as a separate paradigm, we focus on integrating generative capabilities with proven AI assets to maximize impact. In this session, we present ho Genie Code builds on RAIP to automate advanced workflows such as time series forecasting. We also compare this approach with foundation models such as TimeGPT and Chronos, and discuss how this agentic paradigm extends to pricing and optimization use cases. It augments existing AI models while preserving governance, reliability, and operational control and democratizes access to RAIP across business units.

speakers.name: Victor Vaquero Soto
speakers.bio:
Víctor Vaquero Soto is a Senior Data Scientist specializing in advanced analytics, time series forecasting, and scalable data solutions. At Repsol, he develops forecasting libraries for low-code platforms, enabling rapid deployment of predictive models across industrial and energy systems.

He holds a Ph.D. in Physics, focused on nuclear and particle physics, where he applied Big Data techniques to large experimental datasets. His background combines research and industry experience to turn complex data into actionable insights.

Passionate about AI and data engineering, he builds tools that bridge research and real-world applications, and explores how generative AI can make advanced solutions more accessible.

sessions.title: Scaling Custom LLMs with vLLM and Databricks Model Serving: Fast, Flexible, and Production-Ready
sessions.body:
Databricks Model Serving supports deployments ranging from classical ML models on custom-CPU workloads to foundation models with dedicated provisioned throughput endpoints. But what about the use-cases that need any of the 1000s of other open-source or fine-tuned LLMs? Deploying them efficiently can be challenging.

This breakout session explores deploying LLMs on custom-GPU endpoints with vLLM. In it, we’ll examine:

  • Serverless GPU Compute: How it simplifies the deployment process, saving hours on configuration work alone.
  • vLLM + GPU workloads: How they work in tandem on the platform to deliver high-throughput inference with scalable infrastructure.
  • Implementation: A step-by-step code walkthrough for packaging models, configuring vLLM runtime, and deployment!

Serving LLMs on GPUs doesn’t have to be scary. Learn more about how Databricks enables you to deploy even your most demanding model serving workloads!

speakers.name: Colton Peltier
speakers.bio: I am a Staff Data Scientist at Databricks in Professional Services helping customers develop and deploy cutting-edge ML solutions.

speakers.name: Mohamad Aboufoul
speakers.bio:
Mohamad is an AI FDE who has worked on a breadth of projects over the years, spanning computer vision, classical machine learning, language models, and agentic AI. His work has largely focused on production use cases, helping stakeholders gain value from data science.

Mohamad holds a master's in computer science from North Carolina State University and currently works at Databricks, implementing GenAI and classical data science projects for customers in various industries spanning media, retail, healthcare, and biotech, among others.

sessions.title: Scaling Cybersecurity Analytics Without Scaling Costs
sessions.body:
Cybersecurity teams often struggle with the cost and scale of analyzing massive telemetry. JetBlue solved this by building a security-first analytics platform on the Databricks lakehouse.

 

By leveraging Delta Lake, Auto Loader, and Databricks SQL, JetBlue ingests high-cardinality data into low-cost cloud storage, applying compute only when necessary. This enables long-term retention and flexible analysis that legacy tools find prohibitively expensive.

 

Using Databricks SQL, they developed a fastly-focused security layer to:

  • Detect anomalies and bot abuse
  • Measure CAPTCHA effectiveness
  • Analyze attack trends by IP, geography, and path
  • Support real-time and historical investigations
  • Decoupling storage from compute resulted in faster investigations, better visibility, and significant savings. Attendees will learn how to use Databricks to scale detection and investigation workflows cost-effectively.

sessions.title: Scaling Data and AI Trust: How Credicorp Built a Cross-Institution Data Product Marketplace
sessions.body:
As financial groups scale across regions and subsidiaries, the challenge is no longer collecting data; it’s governing, sharing and trusting it at an enterprise level. Eduardo Torres, CDO at Credicorp and Alvaro Villanueva, Credicorp’s Data Marketplace Product Owner, will share their team’s journey to building a data product marketplace that spans financial institutions and countries using Databricks Unity Catalog.

 

Torres & Villanueva will share how they built a reliability layer at the foundation of their data product marketplace with data and AI observability, enabling multiple subsidiaries to publish and discover trusted data products without costly duplication or security risk. They will dive into the team’s approach to key challenges, including operating models, incentives and change management when subsidiaries are also competitors. Attendees will learn how trusted data across a data product marketplace unlocks a unified customer view, and real business impact at enterprise scale.

sessions.title: Scaling Databricks Genie 10x at GSK Global Supply Chain: Building a Production AI/BI Factory
sessions.body:
Most organizations don't struggle to prototype conversational AI—they struggle to get it reliably into production at scale. At GSK's Global Supply Chain, operating across 37 GMP-regulated manufacturing sites with thousands of daily decisions, we built an AI/BI factory designed to move Databricks Genie from early experimentation to enterprise-grade production—serving analysts, planners and decision-makers across a complex, regulated environment.

 

This talk explores the journey from pilot to platform: how we scaled Genie 10x by treating it not as a standalone tool, but as a production system embedded in a broader agent operating model—one that fuses technology, process, governance and organizational ways of working into a repeatable delivery engine.

 

What we’ll cover:

  • Genie Spaces lessons learned and best practices
  • Enterprise observability dashboard for Genie
  • CI/CD migration and deployment automation for DevOps
  • Semantic caching for Genie

speakers.name: Virginie Marelli
speakers.bio:
Virginie Marelli, Principal Generative Engineer –GSK

From a banking traineeship, Virginie discovered a passion for data science during the Jupyter notebook era. She then mastered Python and Spark (when it was still running on Hadoop). Joining a small data and AI startup as a machine learning engineer, she grew with the company and the wider adoption of AI, becoming tech lead and then head of innovation, delivering AI solutions to real-world problems, in the cloud. Now at GSK, she's working at the forefront of generative and agentic AI.

sessions.title: Scaling Energy Deal Evaluation With Databricks Lakebase
sessions.body:
Quantum Capital Group screens hundreds of energy investment opportunities each year, supported by more than 1.5 billion records across public, premium and proprietary datasets. While its Databricks Lakehouse already provided a scalable and governed foundation, the next challenge was enabling teams and downstream tools to work more efficiently from the same trusted data as deal volume and complexity increased.

 

In this session, Quantum shares how it extended its Lakehouse with Databricks Lakebase to introduce relational structure and familiarity without sacrificing openness or scale. Attendees will learn how Lakebase integrates with Delta Lake, Unity Catalog and Lakeflow to support governed, materialized datasets that teams can access using SQL, geospatial tools and existing analytics platforms.

 

The talk focuses on how relational access and governance helped Quantum scale human-led diligence across engineering and investment teams, evaluate complex deals with greater confidence.

speakers.name: Ian Brown
speakers.bio: Ian is the Head of Digital Engineering at Quantum Captial Group. Prior to joining Quantum, he served as the Vice President of Product Development for Xecta where he managed all aspects of software development, product cybersecurity, and cloud infrastructure. Previously, Ian has served as a Senior Technical Director at Baker Hughes, leading commercial software products and IOT hardware developments, and with Standard and Poor’s as a Global Director managing a multi-million-dollar digital portfolio. Ian began his career in energy and finance with Halliburton in the U.K. where he held various software engineering and product management positions. Ian holds a B.S. in Computer Science and an M.B.A. from Robert Gordon University (Scotland)

sessions.title: Scaling Executive-Ready Insight With Databricks AI Query on AI/BI
sessions.body: Creating executive-ready metric summaries is harder than it looks. Leaders expect insights that are accurate, consistent, action-oriented, and concise, yet many organizations still rely on manual reporting — driving high effort, slow turnaround, and inconsistent interpretation. In this session, we share a real-world example of sales strategy and analytics teams automating daily pipeline summaries using Databricks AI Query within an AI/BI dashboard. Each summary previously took ~30 minutes per territory—an estimated 36,000 manual hours annually. By standardizing business logic, strengthening the Databricks data foundation, and applying AI selectively, we scaled executive-ready insights to hundreds of leaders. The key lesson: 80% of impact comes from clear strategy logic and trusted data — AI delivers the final 20% by generating consistent natural-language summaries at scale. Attendees will learn a practical model to encode executive expectations, govern AI outputs, and reduce time to insight.

speakers.name: Kimberly Zee
speakers.bio: Kimberly Zee is a Business Intelligence Manager on the GTM Strategy & Operations team at Databricks, based in the Seattle office. She focuses on enabling data-driven go-to-market decisions and reporting, partnering closely with GTM and analytics leaders to improve visibility into performance and drive operational excellence.

sessions.title: Scaling for MHHS: Octopus Energy’s 50x Cost-Efficient Margin Data Engineering
sessions.body: As the global energy system moves to intermittent renewables, the challenge for data engineering is providing a clear signal to consumers for when the energy is at cheapest and cleanest. This talk is for data engineers and leaders navigating the UK’s Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement (MHHS) transition. Facing a 48x surge in data volume for 8M+ customers, Octopus Energy re-engineered its margin systems to bridge the gap between monthly billing and half-hourly settlement.The Results:Data Efficiency: 98.8% reduction in rows processed (from 25B to 300M).Cost Savings: 50x cost reduction per settlement date, avoiding $1M in annual infrastructure increases.Velocity: Improved data freshness from weekly to daily.By decoupling the pipeline into grain-specific modules and applying Spark and Incremental optimisations, we transformed a regulatory hurdle into a scalable engine for margin visibility. Aligning your data architecture with the business logic enables a sustainable energy future.

speakers.name: Ben Wood
speakers.bio: Ben Wood is a Data Engineer at Octopus Energy, currently working in the Gross Margin team. He specialises in GB electricity settlements and Spark optimisation. He leverages his industry knowledge to deliver critical business insights, and frequently shares his Spark technical expertise through internal talks.

speakers.name: Saad Ali
speakers.bio: Saad Ali is a data leader and platform builder who translates first-principles energy knowledge into systems that scale. Currently at Octopus Energy, he leads the team building margin data systems that underpin multi-billion pound retail revenue. Twice a first technical hire, he previously built a full energy supply platform from zero, enabling the business to scale 300x.

sessions.title: Scaling Geospatial Analytics at S&P Global Energy: From Billions of Points to AI-Powered Map Agents with Databricks
sessions.body:
At S&P Global Energy, we transformed our geospatial analytics architecture to handle billions of records with query results in seconds — removing the need for separate geospatial databases and reducing costs using our Oil & Gas well production data.

 

Architecture evolution:

  • Unified single-source-of-truth on Delta Lake without redundant geospatial systems
  • Databricks Spatial SQL with native spatial types enabling performant queries
  • Databricks SQL Serverless delivering on-demand H3 aggregations

 

Interactive Databricks app demo for large-well datasets.

 

What’s next – AI geospatial agent (work in progress):

  • Natural language map interactions powered by Agent Bricks
  • Genie-driven text-to-SQL for dynamic map layer creation
  • 50+ analytical tools like chart generation from spatial queries

 

Attendees will learn practical patterns for scaling geospatial workloads, leveraging Spatial SQL with native spatial types, H3 indexing, and see how AI agents are reshaping spatial analytics workflows.

speakers.name: Hubert Boguski
speakers.bio: Software Engineer specializing in AI and Geospatial. Love learning the new technologies. Avid runner and Formula 1 fan.

speakers.name: Michael Johns
speakers.bio: Michael is one of the founding members of the Geospatial SME group at Databricks where he has worked with a variety of spatial data and frameworks, offered thought leadership for current geospatial direction, authored content, and spoken at numerous Databricks-sponsored events. As Geospatial Specialist Leader, he is responsible for enabling and developing a team of strong subject matter experts (SMEs). He also represents field interests with product management, marketing, and engineering to package high-quality geospatial features and field-delivered assets for our customers and partners.

sessions.title: Scaling Governed AI Beyond PoCs: A Public Sector Agent Architecture With Lakebase and AgentBricks
sessions.body:
Many AI pilots succeed, but productionisation remains difficult in regulated environments where governance, auditability and state management are required. This session is grounded in Skills SA’s Organisational Self-Assessment (OSA) process, a compliance-driven workflow combining structured operational metadata and unstructured free-text submissions. Around 200 assessments are reviewed annually, requiring significant assessor effort (~1,800 hours)

 

We present a multi-agent architecture built on Databricks Lakebase and AgentBricks. A single Databricks App invokes specialised agents via AgentBricks. OSA data is stored in Delta tables, with Lakebase providing operational state management and governance. Agent prompts and scoring rules are versioned as governed data, and AI/BI Genie is used for natural-language queries over operational metadata.

 

Attendees will learn practical patterns for running production AI systems in regulated environments.

speakers.name: Claudia Kralik
speakers.bio:

With over a decade of experience, Claudia works at the intersection of business and technology, with a strong interest in agentic AI, low-code frameworks, and scalable delivery models.

She regularly shares practical insights on productionising AI and driving adoption in complex environments, helping organisations translate AI potential into real-world value.

sessions.title: Scaling Human Connection with Real-Time AI Conversation Monitoring
sessions.body: With over 300 million messages exchanged since 2013 and more than a decade of expertise, Crisis Text Line is now leading the implementation of LLMs in the mental health nonprofit space. We will discuss a set of conversation monitoring capabilities built on the Databricks ecosystem that provide unprecedented observability into live, high-stakes conversations. These models surface risk signals, quality metrics, and contextual insights. We will demo how these capabilities enable co-pilot-like support that helps crisis responders and clinical supervisors focus on what they do best—supporting people in need.

sessions.title: Scaling Micro-Offers With Hybrid AI
sessions.body:
This work proposes a pipeline for responsible investment offer personalization in Brazilian Open Finance, integrating data governance, segmentation (K-Means), propensity modeling (Random Forest) and an ethical filtering layer via LLM-based digital twins. Applied to 427,929 Caixa Econômica Federal customers, the model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.57. Digital twin validation reduced the high-propensity pool from 213,764 to 6,543 eligibles, applying suitability rules and generating auditable justifications to mitigate overcontact.

 

Distributive analysis indicated a concentration of offers among higher-income profiles. In a pilot within the My Wallet app, the approach yielded a 21.0% positive intention rate, surpassing the 3–5% generic average. Results suggest that combining Open Finance, ML and GenAI enhances assertiveness and algorithmic governance, highlighting the need for formal fairness metrics and large-scale causal experiments.

speakers.name: Andre Victor Ruiz Pedroso
speakers.bio:

Beyond his professional work, André also has a background in mechatronics and software development, which gives him a hands-on perspective when designing robust systems. He is interested in the intersection of AI, automation, and human behavior, particularly how intelligent systems can reshape services and everyday interactions.

Her main mission is to support customers on their Data and AI journey, helping them grow and innovate with Databricks.

sessions.title: Scaling Paediatric Cancer Analytics with Databricks: The Zero Childhood Cancer Data Lakehouse
sessions.body: CCIA currently manages more than two petabytes of cancer patient data from over 2800 patients participating in the Zero Childhood Cancer Program (ZERO), a world-leading precision medicine program for children and young people with cancer that is built upon the Databricks Lakehouse. Databricks has fundamentally transformed precision medicine research and clinical workflows at ZERO. Previously, variant data was stored across thousands of text files, making comprehensive searches across the entire cohort intractable. Scientists were limited to analyzing predefined gene panels, severely constraining hypothesis-driven research. With Databricks, we can now search across all 14+ billion variants from our entire patient cohort simultaneously, allowing researchers to test novel hypotheses and rapidly identify patients with related variants across any genomic region, a capability that was previously impossible, and represents a key capability in helping CCIA scale from 2800 to over 4000 patients

sessions.title: Scaling Responsible AI and Powering Product Innovation in Banking and Payments
sessions.body: Discover how leading banks and payments companies are powering a new era of hyper-growth and automated efficiency. Learn how Databricks customers turned their data into an enterprise backbone that is scaling responsible AI, powering product innovation, and unlocking natural language query, removing the analytics bottleneck to enable faster, more strategic decision making.

speakers.name: Bruno Paronetti
speakers.bio: Bruno Paronetti is Global Head of Finance Transformation at Santander Payments Solutions, where he works at the intersection of finance, data, technology, and payments. With more than 17 years of experience across fintech, proptech, and technology, he has held finance leadership roles at Santander, Booking Holdings, and Tesla. With a background in actuarial science and finance, Bruno has led finance transformation, regulated financial services, payment platforms, and large-scale automation initiatives. He focuses on building data-driven finance capabilities that help turn finance into a strategic growth function powered by scalable systems and AI-enabled decision-making.

speakers.job_title: CFO and Head of Strategy, Payments

speakers.name: Joel Castaneda
speakers.bio: Joel Castaneda is Chief Risk Officer at Vantage Bank, a $5B commercial bank headquartered in Texas. Joel enables responsible innovation through forward-looking risk frameworks that keep pace with emerging technology, including the Hazel Network, a bank lead tokenized deposit and payments initiative on blockchain rails—keeping Vantage Prepared for What's Possible™. He started at the OCC in 2007 examining community banks, held risk and operations roles at a Texas bank, and served as a Director within USAA's Enterprise Risk Office.

sessions.title: Scaling Trustworthy AI: Takeda’s Self-Service AI Foundation on Databricks
sessions.body: Takeda and ZS share a bold vision for the future of enterprise AI—one where innovation scales through a secure, self-service AI foundation with governance built in by design. In this session, Takeda and ZS share how they are building a unified AI foundation on Databricks, enabling teams to develop, deploy and operate AI confidently in a highly regulated environment. We will walk through Takeda’s AI foundation architecture—built on the Databricks Mosaic AI framework and leveraging managed model serving endpoints and enterprise wide vectorization patterns—while also demonstrating how automated, compliant project provisioning and Takeda-specific responsible AI guardrails enable secure, scalable delivery of AI-driven applications. Attendees will learn how Takeda’s self-service AI foundation accelerates experimentation, improves reuse and reduces operational friction while strengthening trust, audit readiness and enterprise-wide adoption of AI.

speakers.name: Dileep Shankar
speakers.bio: Leading Data & AI transformation—turning complex data into intelligent, business-ready decisions. Passionate about building scalable AI systems, agentic workflows, and real-world GenAI solutions that move beyond hype to measurable impact. Bridging engineering, strategy, and storytelling to help organizations unlock the true value of AI.

speakers.name: Hardeepsingh Saluja
speakers.bio: Hardeepsingh Saluja is an Enterprise Architect at ZS Associates with experience helping organizations design and scale enterprise platforms, data and digital capabilities, and modern technology foundations that drive business transformation. He works across architecture, engineering and strategy to enable secure, scalable and high-impact solutions in complex enterprise environments. His expertise spans cloud platforms, data and analytics, enterprise integration, platform modernization and AI, with a focus on building solutions that are practical, trusted and aligned to business outcomes. He is particularly passionate about creating foundations that improve speed, reuse, governance and long-term scalability across the enterprise.

sessions.title: Secure by Default, Connected Everywhere: What’s New in Databricks Platform Security
sessions.body:
Databricks is shipping a wave of platform security, networking and compliance capabilities that make enterprise-grade protection the default — not an afterthought. In this session, we cover the highlights including Private Network Gateway for managed, secure connectivity to your data sources, context-based ingress policies that bring adaptive network controls to Genie, apps, AI/BI, and agentic workloads and cloudless compute with a cross-cloud backbone that simplifies networking across environments.

 

We’ll also showcase automatic identity management (AIM), which automates identity provisioning and enforces least-privilege at scale. On the compliance side, we’ll announce a new Azure GovCloud environment, expanded AWS GovCloud capabilities and new certifications (ISMAP, HITRUST, FedRAMP High). Plus, secure cross-workspace access, serverless egress logs, account frontend private link, CMK for UC Catalogs and more. Come see how Databricks is making security a platform advantage.

speakers.name: Jason Wu
speakers.bio: Jason Wu is a product and engineering leader specializing in enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure, currently heading Platform and Security products at Databricks. Prior to Databricks, he led the Google Cloud Storage portfolio, overseeing the product and strategy for GCS, high performance AI Storage, and Google wide internal Storage infrastructure. Throughout his career, Jason has focused on building and scaling foundational AI and cloud technologies, holding various leadership roles at Microsoft, Alibaba Cloud, and Huawei Cloud.

speakers.name: Samrat Ray
speakers.bio: Samrat is responsible for enterprise security for the Databricks platform including security of the serverless platform, encryption, data protection and privacy. In his previous role at Google, he has led several industry-leading products such as VPC Service Controls and Cloud SQL from concept to scale.  Samrat is a founding PM of Istio and led the vision for zero-trust security in modern production environments.

sessions.title: Secure External Data Access with Connections, Secrets, and Functions in Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
Modern data platforms are rarely islands; they exist in a sprawling ecosystem of external databases, APIs, and third-party services. However, managing the "connective tissue"—JDBC drivers, secret rotation, and custom logic—often creates security silos and governance gaps.

 

In this session, we will hands-on demonstrate how the next generation of Unity Catalog Connections, Secrets and Functions work in concert to centralize external data access, eliminate hardcoded credentials, and deploy governed UDFs across any compute type. 

 

Attendees will learn how to build a "zero-trust" data architecture that simplifies the user experience while providing full lineage and auditability from the source to the final insight.

speakers.name: Jakob Mund
speakers.bio: Jakob is part of the product team at Databricks working closely with the engineering teams on secure and extensible compute in Unity Catalog and across the Lakehouse. Favorite topics include Python UDFs, DBSQL extensibility and Unity catalog clusters. Prior to Databricks, Jakob worked at Tableau's data platform build on the Hyper extract engine.

speakers.name: Vladislav Mantic-Lugo
speakers.bio: Vladislav Mantic-Lugo is a Product Manager at Databricks, focused on developer experience and connectivity across the lakehouse. His work centers on enabling data engineers and scientists to build, debug, and run applications from their preferred tools through innovations like Databricks Connect and IDE integrations.

sessions.title: Securing Agentic AI on Databricks: From Experimentation to Enterprise Grade Systems
sessions.body:
Agentic AI systems—where LLM-powered agents plan, reason, and act across data and tools—are rapidly moving from proof-of-concept to mission-critical production. However, this shift introduces a new security surface: autonomous decision-making, dynamic tool use, and data access at scale. How do you innovate without compromising security, governance, or compliance? 

In this session, we explore how to build secure, enterprise-ready agentic systems on Databricks. Designed for practitioners and architects, we break down the unique risks of agentic workflows and map them to concrete controls. We will introduce the Databricks Agentic AI Security Framework developed with top researchers from OWASP, NIST, and Fortune 100 companies. 

Key Takeaways:

  • Reference architectures for deploying secure agentic AI at scale.
  • A framework to operationalize and explain your security posture to cyber teams.
  • Actionable tools, including a worksheet and live demo, to test your deployments and MCP security.

speakers.name: Arun Pamulapati
speakers.bio: Arun is a core member of Databricks' Field security practice and has 25 years of experience in building data products, including over a decade of experience in building AI products. Arun led and co-created the Security Analysis Tool (SAT) and SSPM for Databricks, he is coauthor of Databricks, and AI Security Framework (DASF). Arun has a bachelor’s in computer science, holds Cloud security and AI/ML industry certifications, and contributes to HITRUST and FAIR Institute AI workgroups.

speakers.name: Samrat Ray
speakers.bio: Samrat is responsible for enterprise security for the Databricks platform including security of the serverless platform, encryption, data protection and privacy. In his previous role at Google, he has led several industry-leading products such as VPC Service Controls and Cloud SQL from concept to scale.  Samrat is a founding PM of Istio and led the vision for zero-trust security in modern production environments.

sessions.title: Securing the Databricks Lakehouse — a Multi-Layered Defense Against Outside and Inside Threats
sessions.body: As organizations transition mission-critical workloads to the Databricks Lakehouse Platform on AWS, the traditional “castle-and-moat” security model is no longer sufficient. This presentation outlines a comprehensive, defense-in-depth strategy designed to protect data assets from both external adversaries and internal risks. By synthesizing identity federation, network hardening and dynamic governance, organizations can achieve a “Zero Trust” posture that scales with their data growth.

speakers.name: Daniel Goldszmit
speakers.bio: Data Architect at Natura with over 25 years of experience in the tech industry. I specialize in building scalable Lakehouse architectures. Beyond architecting complex cloud ecosystems, my greatest joy is spending quality time with my wife and daughter."

sessions.title: Securing the Grid: Modernizing E&U Security Operations with Lakewatch (AI-Native SIEM)
sessions.body:
Energy & Utilities (E&U) face a perfect storm: surging OT/ICS ransomware, strict NERC CIP/TSA regulations, and an explosion of IT/OT telemetry. Traditional SIEMs, hampered by ingest-based pricing and data silos, can no longer keep pace. Enter Lakewatch: Databricks’ open, AI-native SIEM, built natively on the Lakehouse.

 

This session provides insights from Energy Queensland's journey of navigating the challenges of traditional SIEM and the impact a security lakehouse on Databricks can deliver. We'll discuss how Databricks Lakewatch, the lakehouse-native SIEM, eliminates "ingest taxes" and unifies IT, cloud, and OT logs through OCSF-aligned schemas; how SQL-based detection engineering and agentic threat hunting open up petabytes of historical data in seconds; and how an open, decoupled storage and compute architecture delivers the visibility, long-term retention, and AI-readiness critical infrastructure operators need to increase their situational awareness.

speakers.name: Dylan Mills
speakers.bio: Dylan is a cybersecurity engineer at Rearc with over 7 years of experience in SOC engineering, incident response, cloud security, vulnerability management, and more. Over the last 2 years he has been working with Databricks to develop cyber content and capabilities within the open security lakehouse ecosystem.

speakers.name: Rakesh Cherukuri
speakers.bio: Rakesh Cherukuri is a Solutions Architect at Databricks based in Australia, where he partners with enterprise customers to solve their most complex business challenges using data and AI.

speakers.name: Shane Atherton
speakers.bio: Shane is an Account Executive at Databricks, where he partners with Queensland's largest energy organisations to help solve their biggest challenges.  He's most passionate about the positive impact leading with data can have on better and faster decision making.

sessions.title: Security at Anthropic: Building D&R for an AI-Native Company
sessions.body: As AI systems become critical infrastructure, security teams face a new challenge: how do you defend an AI-native company at the speed and scale that modern threats demand? In this session, Jackie Bow, Technical Lead of Threat Detection Engineering at Anthropic, shares how her team thinks about building detection and response capabilities purpose-built for an AI company including the architectural decisions, tradeoffs, and lessons learned along the way.Jackie will offer a practitioner's perspective on what it takes to operate a security function inside one of the world's leading AI labs, including incorporating agentic workflows alongside more traditional D&R tooling.In the final segment, a Databricks product leader will connect these themes to Lakewatch, Databricks' new open, agentic SIEM and explore how the Security Lakehouse architecture is designed to help security teams modernize detection and response at enterprise scale.

speakers.name: Jackie Bow

Cybersecurity engineer with 15+ years experience, primarily in threat detection and response, also as an early-stage security hire building out programs and working to establish teams in Product Security, Infrastructure Security and Detection and Response. Interested in the intersection of mental health and security, and building security programs and processes that not only work, but scale and thrive. Flexible, passionate, polymath. Experienced in the challenges of growing security teams and balancing risk with encouraging engineering excellence.

speakers.name: Keegan Dubbs
speakers.bio: Keegan Dubbs is a Product Manager focused on Identity Lifecycle at Databricks, where she helps shape secure and scalable user experiences. Her favorite part of the job is collecting customer feedback - she loves hearing real-world insights that directly inform the product roadmap and drive meaningful improvements. Outside of work, Keegan can often be found skiing in the mountains or daydreaming about her future golden retriever. She's passionate about building user-centric products and believes the best ideas come from listening closely to the people who use them every day.

sessions.title: Self-Healing Product Catalogs: Drift-Aware Computer Vision for Retail & CPG on Databricks
sessions.body: Product catalogs are living things — new packaging, regional variants, seasonal SKUs are always cycling through — and every change impacts the model's accuracy. Neurolabs runs image recognition across 20,000+ SKUs in 28 markets, generating millions of shelf crops every month. Most are routine; only a handful contain the signal that makes the next model better — a new pack variant, a misclassified flavour, a confused competitor. We've moved that selection loop onto Databricks. Inference results land in Delta, every crop is scored for training value, and Unity Catalog governs which crops feed the next model and surfaces catalog-health metrics back to the CPG brands that own the SKUs. The result: a product catalog that heals itself, and a computer vision model that gets sharper with every shelf photo.

sessions.title: Semantic Modeling Best Practices for BI and AI
sessions.body: AI is making self-service data real, but it creates a new challenge: ensuring humans and AI interpret data the same way. When logic is fragmented across tools, inconsistencies emerge, trust erodes, and AI insights become unreliable.Databricks addresses this with a unified approach to semantics across BI and AI. UC Business Semantics provide governed definitions, AI/BI Dashboards add local semantics, and the Genie Knowledge Store adds domain context to improve how AI answers. Together, these layers enable consistent BI and accurate AI. We’ll cover best practices for designing and operationalizing semantics across Unity Catalog, dashboards, and Genie:- Define and manage UC Business Semantics for governed metrics and dimensions- Use Dashboard Semantic Models and Metric Views for report logic- Use Genie Knowledge Store to improve AI accuracy with domain context and SQL- Combine central semantics and local curation across BI and AI- Avoid common pitfalls in semantic modeling

speakers.name: Chris Eubank
speakers.bio: At Databricks, Chris focuses on enabling business users to unlock insights through expressive and fast interactive dashboards. Previously, he drove efforts in data modeling at Tableau.

sessions.title: Serverless at Bank Scale: NAB's Complete Workload Migration to Serverless at Enterprise Scale
sessions.body: Explore how National Australia Bank (NAB) adopted Databricks Serverless across notebooks, jobs, declarative pipelines, SQL Warehouses and Model Serving—delivering platform reliability, cost efficiency and performance without compromising security or governance. Hear NAB’s blueprint: phased migration, workload prioritization and cross‑team operationalization. Learn the essentials—Unity Catalog for fine‑grained governance, plus Private Link and Secure Egress Gateway for private connectivity—and hard‑won lessons from uplifting Spark to declarative pipelines (DLT/LDP), moving SQL to serverless warehouses, and operationalizing model serving with observability and guardrails. Walk away with actionable patterns, checklists and success criteria for regulated environments. Outcomes include broad serverless adoption, faster MLOps cycles, better SQL performance, lower ingestion cost and sustained query scale—a pragmatic path to bank‑grade serverless at enterprise scale.

speakers.name: Allan Cuthbertson
speakers.job_title: Head of Platform Engineering and Design
speakers.bio:
Allan is a data professional with over 20 years' experience across a number of sectors(Banking, Telecoms, Trading and Advertising ) in the UK, USA and now Australia.

He has worked in and led teams across the data lifecycle - architecture and design, ingestion, transformation, visualisation, science, and platform operations.

His broad experience helps him deliver assets that are usable, reliable, and integrated into businesses that solve real customer problems. What’s the point of having a Data Lakehouse if no one is going to use it?

At NAB, Allan is a Distinguished Engineer focussed on embedding the banks Databricks Lakehouse environment and decommissioning heritage platforms.

speakers.name: Tom McMeekin
speakers.bio: Tom McMeekin is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he partners with some of Australia’s largest enterprises to design and scale modern data and AI platforms. With a background spanning cloud architecture, analytics, and cybersecurity, Tom specialises in helping organisations unlock value from their data through secure, cost-effective, and governed solutions. Prior to Databricks, he held senior roles at AWS and brings over a decade of experience in enterprise technology strategy. Tom is a regular speaker and contributor on topics such as serverless data platforms, AI governance, and the future of analytics in regulated industries.

sessions.title: Serverless Compute for Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines: Latest Launches and What's Next
sessions.body: Serverless Compute for Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines has reached a turning point. What started as a convenience for ad-hoc and smaller workloads now runs petabyte-scale production and mission-critical SLAs at some of the largest Databricks customers. With Standard mode for Jobs and Pipelines, serverless is cost-competitive with well-tuned classic compute while removing the operational burden of cluster sizing, autoscaling, and runtime upgrades.This session shares concrete lessons from customers running serverless at serious scale, covers the most recent launches across runtime, performance, and cost controls, and previews what is coming next in workload compatibility and governance.If you have been waiting for serverless to be ready for your hardest and largest workloads, this is the session to recalibrate.

speakers.name: Roland Fäustlin
speakers.bio:
Roland is a Product Manager at Databricks, focusing on the orchestration of data and AI workloads with Databricks Workflows and fully managed serverless compute since April 2021.

He has over 13 years of experience in technology, including roles at Google and as a team leader at McKinsey’s Business Technology Office in Europe and Latin America.

He holds a PhD in plasma physics, a master’s degree in laboratory astrophysics from The University of Texas at Austin, and a minor in computer science.

sessions.title: Serverless Scala on Databricks: Running Apache Spark™ JARs Without Managing Clusters
sessions.body:
Scala remains a critical language for some of the largest and most performance-sensitive Apache Spark™ workloads. But running Scala pipelines shouldn’t require managing clusters, dependencies and runtime configuration by hand.

 

This lightning talk introduces Serverless JARs on Databricks, now in Public Preview and heading to GA. We’ll show how teams run existing Scala Spark applications on serverless compute, what changes operationally and what stays the same.

 

This lightning talk will cover:

  • When serverless execution makes sense for Scala Spark workloads
  • Best practices for packaging and running Scala JARs
  • Common migration pitfalls and how to avoid them

 

The goal is to help Scala teams move to serverless execution without rewriting code or giving up performance and control.

speakers.name: Prashanth Babu Velanati Venkata
speakers.bio: Prashanth is a Principal Product Specialist at Databricks with 15 years of experience in Big Data and 10 years prior as a Java architect. A Spark user since 2014, he joined Databricks in 2018 and works closely with both Product Management and Field Engineering. He has played a key role in shaping and driving adoption of Databricks Workflows and Serverless Workflows, enabling enterprises to simplify orchestration and scale data pipelines efficiently. Prashanth partners with customers to define Lakehouse best practices and accelerate the build, productionisation and deployment of robust data engineering solutions at scale. He is also the co-author of Delta Lake: The Definitive Guide and an active contributor to the data engineering community.

sessions.title: SharePoint to Lakehouse with Lakeflow Connect — Top 5 Powerful GenAI Patterns
sessions.body:
Many organizations have rich SharePoint data but struggle to use it at scale for intelligence, reporting, and automation. In this demo-heavy session, we demonstrate how to leverage valuable SharePoint content as a first-class data source for data intelligence and analytics by ingesting it into your lakehouse.

 

Using the new Lakeflow Connect SharePoint connector, we will demonstrate incremental, governed pipelines (via Unity Catalog) that ingest both structured data (Excel, CSV, lists) and unstructured content (PDFs, Office files, images). Data lands as streaming tables enriched with SharePoint metadata to power downstream analytics, search, and AI. 

We will walk through five low-lift, high-impact patterns: driving an AI-powered BI dashboard from Excel and list data, summarizing and analyzing PDF reports, querying PowerPoint decks via natural language in a secure Genie Room, OCR’ing scanned images for text extraction, and consolidating many CSV reports into a single streaming table.

speakers.name: Russ Houberg
speakers.bio: Russ Houberg is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks, where he works with some of the world's largest enterprises on data engineering, AI, and lakehouse architecture. With nearly 30 years of IT experience — including time as a SharePoint Certified Master — he built his career at the intersection of data architecture and content management, co-authoring SharePoint Server 2010 Enterprise Content Management (Wrox) and leading large-scale data migrations for global enterprises. Russ draws on this unique background to show how Microsoft 365 and SharePoint can become first-class sources of institutional knowledge — fueling the democratization of Data + AI on Databricks.

sessions.title: Sneak Peek: How We Use Databricks Apps to Power Field Demos at Scale
sessions.body:
How does Databricks keep thousands of field engineers on-message, with the right demo ready for every customer conversation? The answer: we run our demo program on Databricks Apps. In this session, you’ll get a behind-the-scenes look at how we use Apps to catalog, search, and launch hundreds of demos across products and industries.

 

We’ll walk through the FE Demo Catalog, a Databricks App backed by Lakebase that acts as the single source of truth for demos—complete with AI search, links to live environments, recordings, decks, and scripts—so any seller or architect can quickly find “the one right demo” for their meeting. We’ll also show how our Demo Builder flows let field teams submit and update demos in a structured way, keeping quality high without central bottlenecks.

 

If you’ve ever wondered how to scale demo excellence inside your own company, this “Databricks on Databricks” story will give you a concrete pattern for using Databricks Apps to run demo catalogs and demo tools at scale.

sessions.title: Spark DSV2: Growing Up Fast
sessions.body: Spark’s DataSource V2 integration has taken a major step forward, beginning with the addition of a procedure catalog and row identifier support to enable richer table management and row-level operations across modern data sources. Building on this foundation, recent updates improve MERGE INTO with safer schema evolution and enhance partition filtering for more efficient query planning and execution. DML summaries now provide clearer visibility into write behavior, while key cache fixes resolve long-standing correctness issues in Spark execution. DataSource V2 has also been extended with first-class SQL features such as table constraints, complex default values, and generated columns, laying the groundwork for more advanced table semantics. We’ll also look ahead to deeper Change Data Feed (CDF) integration in Spark to support robust incremental processing, highlighting what’s available today and what’s coming next as Spark continues to close the gap with traditional warehouse systems.

speakers.name: Szehon Ho
speakers.bio: Szehon Ho is a software engineer at Databricks working on Apache Spark.  Previously, he was working on Apache Iceberg at Apple, and is an Apache Iceberg PMC.  Prior to that, he was working on Apache Hive at Cloudera and Criteo, and is an Apache Hive PMC.

sessions.title: Spatial Simplified With Databricks SQL Where-House: Patterns, Performance and Applications
sessions.body: Spatial data has always been important and working with it has always been complex. Until now. In this session we'll discuss simplified approaches for working with spatial data, highlighting new performance benchmarks that demonstrate how Databricks Spatial SQL scales spatial workloads, and what this means for real-world use cases. You'll also hear about customer stories and key partner integrations that shape how leading organizations are maximizing the value from location-based data.
