sessions.body: Discover how Salesforce uses Slack and Slackbot to drive efficiency at scale. This session explores how teams across IT, sales, and beyond leverage automation and workflows to reduce ticket volume, accelerate resolution times, and streamline operations. Learn how Salesforce deploys Slack agents for routine requests, builds custom solutions for everyday work, and develops processes that deliver measurable productivity gains while strengthening internal alignment.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Salesforce | Tableau & Databricks: Demystifying the Open Semantic Interchange (OSI)
sessions.body: Explore how Tableau and the Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) provide the essential metadata layer that ensures your metrics remain consistent and trusted for both humans and agents. You will learn how our current analytics integration and future roadmap for semantic interoperability allow agents to work seamlessly inside the systems that run your business.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Salesforce | Turn Databricks Data into Action with Trusted Context from Salesforce Data 360
sessions.body: Your data platform is powerful, but data alone doesn’t drive outcomes. To operationalize AI and deliver real-time customer experiences, teams need trusted context: governed data, business logic, and unified customer intelligence. In this session, discover how Salesforce Data 360 connects directly to your Databricks lakehouse to activate data without moving or duplicating it. Using Zero Copy access, you can unify customer profiles, power real-time personalization, and ground Agentforce agents in trusted enterprise data so they act accurately at scale. We’ll explore three practical use cases: building unified profiles from lakehouse data, enabling AI agents with governed context, and activating data across sales, service, and marketing channels. Zero Copy is the foundation. Trusted context is what drives action. Leave with a clear blueprint to maximize the value of your Databricks investment.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: SAP | SAP and Databricks Turn SAP Data Into AI-Driven Business Outcomes
sessions.body: Enterprise AI often stalls due to fragmented data foundations. This session shows how SAP Business Data Cloud and Databricks delivers a unified, governed data fabric for AI that reduces data movement, data delays and silos. Learn how to combine SAP’s business context with Databricks lakehouse data to enable analytics and AI at scale. Through real-world use cases like cash flow forecasting, tariff impact analysis and supply chain risk modeling, see how you can accelerate AI and drive measurable outcomes.

speakers.name: Rams Srinivasan
speakers.bio:
Ramaswamy Srinivasan (Rams) is a senior technology and data transformation leader with over 25 years of experience across Information Technology, Telecommunications, Consulting, and Executive Management. He currently serves as Global Head of Strategic Solution Advisory at SAP, where he leads a global team focused on Data and AI, helping organizations unlock value from enterprise data at scale.
In his role, Rams works closely with customers and partners on complex Data, AI and analytics initiatives—positioning modern data platforms to enable advanced analytics, real-time insights, and AI-driven use cases. His team plays a key role in translating customer challenges and field learnings into product innovation and roadmap evolution.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: SELECT | Taming Databricks Costs: SELECT's Proven Framework from 250+ Customers
sessions.body: Databricks is one of the most cost-effective data platforms on the market. After working with over 250 companies on cloud data platform cost optimization, we've refined a 6-part framework — visibility, attribution, controls, alerts, insights, and automations — that optimizes cost management on Databricks. In this talk, we'll walk through each area with practical examples — from calculating fully loaded workload costs and attributing spend to teams, to building guardrails and automations that continuously optimize your environment. We'll also share hard-won lessons on why decentralizing cost ownership is the only approach that scales and how to build a culture of cost awareness across your organization.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Sigma | How Sigma Makes Databricks AI Safe and Scalable for Every Business User
sessions.body: Databricks is rapidly advancing its AI capabilities—from Genie Spaces to LLM-powered analytics. But for most organizations, making that innovation accessible to everyday business users in a way that’s intuitive, governed, and scalable remains the real challenge. Sigma activates Databricks AI to build intelligent, user-facing workflows that accelerate productivity. Learn how teams use natural language querying, assistants, and agents to analyze data, automate decisions, and take action directly on live Databricks data. Through real-world examples, discover how organizations are operationalizing AI and turning investment into measurable business outcomes.

speakers.name: Zalak Trivedi
speakers.bio:
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Zalak Trivedi leads product direction for AI and Enterprise Platform at Sigma, driving innovation to ensure customers can deliver high-performance agentic analytics for their organizations and within their own applications. He champions Sigma's product for companies to offer data insights in their native ecosystem and promotes these benefits through conferences, whitepapers, blogs, and media appearances.

SIGMA CAREER:
Zalak joined Sigma in April 2022 and leads the AI & Enterprise Platform charters

ROOTS:
Zalak brings experience across the tech industry, having held roles at OvationCXM, Oracle, and Acquire. He holds an MBA from UC Davis and a Bachelor's in Engineering from BITS Pilani.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Sigma | How Unilever Optimizes Supply Chain Inventory with Sigma and Databricks
sessions.body: Unilever’s supply chain team spends hours each day identifying inventory gaps across retailers and distribution centers. By combining disparate datasets, Unilever built a supply chain analytics application using Sigma on Databricks. The solution enables data-driven supply chain decisions with on demand self-service analytics at speed. This centralized “command center” gives teams a daily view of opportunities, reduces manual analysis by up to half a day, and helps balance inventory across locations.

speakers.name: Phillip Nelson
speakers.bio: Phil Nelson is a Commercial & Customer Analytics Manager at Unilever, where he helps transform retail and supply chain data into actionable business insights. With over 15 years of experience in the CPG industry, Phil uses data and BI tools to create solutions for retailer and business teams, helping them meet their goals. He is passionate about enabling data-led, informed, and impactful decision-making across the business.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Sigma | Reinventing Healthcare Finance: How HSS Built XRAY on Databricks with Sigma
sessions.body: When a new CFO set out to deliver more reliable, enterprise-wide data, Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) modernized its approach—consolidating fractured financial and operational systems on Databricks and cutting report turnaround from 30 days to 24 hours. HSS implemented the Databricks lakehouse to bridge several disparate systems to finally connect the dots to tell a full financial story from operational driver to bottom-line result. This was achieved by redesigning the operating model: a cross functional data product team was formed with one singular vision to transform the organization's approach to financial reporting. This structure connects financial expertise, frontline context, data engineering, and analytics. The result is XRAY—a governed, real-time financial visibility solution powered by Sigma that enables cross-functional data conversations and empowers the entire organization to actively find insights at scale.

speakers.name: Richard Lee
speakers.bio: Working in the intersection of Product + Data; passionate about healthcare, learning, golf, and pintxos.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Slalom | From Legacy Drag to AI Value: A Framework for Databricks AI Success
sessions.body: Enterprise AI success is not just about models or platform selection. It depends on prioritizing the right work for AI, proving measurable business value, enabling the organization to adopt new ways of working, and reducing the drag of legacy systems. In this session, Slalom shares a practical framework for scaling AI on Databricks using accelerators mapped to each part of that equation. We will show how VelocitiIQ helps modernize legacy data platforms, how Lakefoundry turns ideas into executable Databricks solution plans, how the AI Value Platform builds confidence through ROI modeling and prioritization, and why organizational enablement is essential for moving from pilots to production. Attendees will leave with a simple, actionable model for connecting modernization, value realization, and AI adoption at scale.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Snorkel AI | The Art & Science of Benchmarking Agents
sessions.body: Our ability to measure AI has been outpaced by our ability to develop it, and this eval gap is one of the most important problems in AI. We need more enduring benchmarks to close this gap, and consequently advance entire new vectors of capabilities for the field. In this talk, I'll share our learnings evaluating agents, drawing from experience working with nearly all global frontier labs and leading academics. We'll discuss the science (i.e., mechanics that make benchmarks rigorous and effective) and art (i.e., intangibles driving ambitious and enduring benchmarks) of building great benchmarks. I'll close by sharing some of the learnings from Open Benchmarks Grants— a $3M initiative in partnership with Hugging Face, Together AI, Prime Intellect, Factory, and others.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Snowplow | The Missing Layer Between Your Lakehouse and Genie: Customer Context with Snowplow
sessions.body: Genie lets anyone ask data questions in plain English. But ask about customer intent, real-time behavior, or why conversions dropped, and most teams don’t have the data to work with. In this session, we'll show how Snowplow delivers a validated customer context layer directly into your lakehouse, i.e., every digital interaction, human and AI agent alike, governed through Unity Catalog. Pre-built semantic models plug into Genie's knowledge store so business users self-serve behavioral insights without the data team. No custom engineering. No modeling from scratch. We'll also unpack the flywheel: every interaction generates richer data, which sharpens Genie answers and agent decisions. Walk away with a practical architecture for turning Genie into the customer intelligence layer your teams actually trust.

speakers.name: Jonathan Malloy
speakers.bio: Jon Malloy is a Data Strategist at Snowplow where he is responsible for helping customers get the most value from their pipeline and derive meaningful insights. Prior to join Snowplow, Jon spent 4 years as a Technical Analyst in the US health care communications industry and 4 years as a Data Scientist in the US health care communications / finance industry. He holds as Master of Science in Business Analytics from Bentley University and resides in Boston, MA.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Solace | From Lakehouse to Event House: Making Databricks Act on Data in Real Time
sessions.body: Pairing Databricks with Solace's Event Mesh creates an Event House — a platform that moves data continuously and intelligently everywhere it needs to go. Solace replaces batch ETL with real-time, bi-directional streaming. Intelligent routing delivers data to AI agents, edge systems, and business domains simultaneously — no bottlenecks, no point-to-point integrations. Solace's Event Mesh spans AWS, Azure, GCP, on-premises, and edge natively — keeping data governed and discoverable across your estate. Walk away with a concrete architecture and a repeatable pattern your team can deploy in weeks.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Stardog | Implementing Agentic AI on Databricks with an Ontology-Driven Semantic Layer
sessions.body: Building reliable AI agents on Databricks requires more than pipelines and models—it demands a semantic foundation that encodes business meaning and context. In this session, we’ll show how to implement an ontology-powered semantic layer that integrates with Delta Lake and Unity Catalog to ground LLM-based agents. You’ll learn how to bootstrap ontologies, enable real-time semantic queries, and go beyond traditional RAG approaches. We’ll walk through patterns for evaluating agent performance against natural language queries across use cases like supply chain, drug discovery, and compliance. Leave with a practical architecture for deploying explainable, production-ready agentic AI on Databricks.

sessions.title: Sponsored By: Tealium | Unifying Data and Action: WGU, Databricks, and Tealium Driving Real-Time Insights at Scale
sessions.body: Organizations today face a critical challenge — not just collecting data, but activating it in real-time to drive meaningful outcomes. Using WGU as a practical example, we’ll examine how the WGU, Tealium, and Databricks integration supports personalized student experiences, improves engagement, and enhances operational efficiency. This session explores how Tealium, Western Governors University (WGU), and Databricks can work together to create a modern, scalable data ecosystem. Tealium enables real-time data collection and audience orchestration, while Databricks provides a unified platform for data, AI, and analytics. Attendees will gain insight into architectural patterns, integration strategies, and real-world use cases that demonstrate how streaming data and AI-driven insights can be operationalized across the enterprise to deliver measurable impact.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Tech Mahindra Limited | From Data to Decisions - How We Gave Our AI a Business Brain
sessions.body: A practitioner session showing how grounding agentic AI in an ontology layer changed what was possible. Not a theory talk, a walk through of what broke first, why RAG wasn't enough, how existing Power BI logic became the foundation, and what the agents can actually do now. Real numbers, real workflows, real lessons. A session with a joint customer for architects and business leaders who are past the hype and need to know what good looks like.

speakers.name: Saurabh Jha
speakers.bio: Saurabh Jha is a seasoned business professional and digital & analytics evangelist with over two decades of experience. A passionate technocrat, he has built and scaled businesses from concept to high‑growth portfolios by leveraging innovative and emerging technologies. As Senior Vice President and Global Head of the Data & Analytics (D&A) Practice at Tech Mahindra, Saurabh is driving enterprise transformation across data, cloud and AI. His solutions and frameworks have earned recognition from leading analysts and customers worldwide. Previously, he held leadership roles at KPMG, Oracle and Mphasis, leading several large‑scale digital transformation initiatives.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Tenarai| AI-Accelerated Real Time Supply Chain Operations on Databricks
sessions.body: Enterprises are reimagining supply chains by consolidating fragmented data into a unified Lakehouse, enabling real-time decisions, AI-driven forecasting, and end-to-end visibility from factory to last mile. In this session, we will showcase how we innovated with AI to accelerate migration, modernization, and transformation of supply chain operations for global customers. This solution addressed critical business challenges like demand volatility, misaligned inventory, shipment risks, and decision latency due to fragmented systems and batch-era architectures that significantly impact cost and performance of operations. Our real time and event-based solution is powered by Structured Streaming, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Agent Bricks and AI/BI Genie architecture to drive ~20+% faster operations, ~$15M+ cost savings, and ~60% reduction in manual effort leading to resilient supply chain operations at scale.

speakers.name: Sriraj Srinivasan
speakers.job_title: Senior Vice President | Data and AI Head

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Tiger Analytics | From Data Potential to Business Value: Scaling Commercial & Consumer Products at PepsiCo
sessions.body: "Data platforms create potential; Data products create value.” At PepsiCo, the Enterprise Data Foundation (EDF) anchors enterprise-wide data access, but real business impact comes from what gets built on top of it. In this session, Petr Gazaryan (PepsiCo) and Parag Shah (Tiger Analytics) share the strategic approach behind designing, scaling and operating a global portfolio of commercial and consumer data products. These span revenue management, store effectiveness, media mix modeling, and personalization, deployed across 25+ markets globally. The talk centers on critical decisions that matter at scale: architecting reusable data products across markets, managing downstream complexity on a shared platform, and designing for operational sustainability rather than one-off delivery. Attendees will leave with a strategic framework for moving beyond platform investments to a mature, scalable data product operating model, with lessons from one of the world’s largest CPG organizations

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Tredence | PepsiCo’s Enterprise Data Foundation Journey for Agentic AI Readiness
sessions.body: At PepsiCo, operating across 190+ countries, 6 sectors, and 1,500+ applications, data has long been fragmented across siloed, sector-specific lakes. As PepsiCo is preparing for the era of Agentic AI, the priority has shifted from simply managing data to making it truly enterprise-ready, through a global, unified data platform. In this session, discover how PepsiCo, in partnership with Tredence, is building a an Enterprise Data Foundation platform using Unity Catalog and a unified data lake to establish a single, trusted source of truth across all sectors. From breaking silos to standardizing governance at scale, Amlan will share the real challenges encountered along the way and how PepsiCo is addressing them to become truly ready for GenAI and Agentic AI. The session will also offer a glimpse into the use cases PepsiCo is unlocking in parallel to building this data foundation, to drive faster, smarter, and more connected decision-making across the enterprise.

speakers.name: Majaz Mohammed
speakers.bio: Leads the CPG Business for Tredence, working with 8 out of the top 10 CPG companies, powering Data and AI strategies. Known for delivering business impact focused AI in Supply chain, Manufacturing, Marketing and Consumer Insights, and Commercial excellence like RGM, and In Market Execution.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Weil | Goldmines and Minefields: Building AI Systems for High-Stakes Work
sessions.body: Most organizations treat AI as a tooling upgrade. Weil treated it as a systems architecture problem — and rebuilt how legal work gets done. This session is for builders — executives, engineers, and product leaders — deploying AI where data is messy, stakes are high, and trust is non-negotiable. We’ll cover: • Structuring complex data (contracts, policies) for LLMs • A modular, multi-step “reasoning” architecture • Designing for privacy, security, and auditability • Rebuilding workflows into AI-native pipelines Professional services is both a goldmine (high-value, repeatable work) and a minefield (sensitive data, real liability). We’ll share what we’ve built — and what it means for deploying AI in real-world, high-stakes environments.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: West Monroe | Operational Intelligence at the Point of Decision with Clonal and Databricks
sessions.body: Organizations are investing in Databricks for analytics and AI, but struggle to turn insights into real-time action across CRM, service, and frontline workflows. This session introduces Clonal, an operational intelligence platform that activates Databricks data at the point of decision. Clonal creates a live operational model by unifying data from core systems and Databricks, processes events in milliseconds, and orchestrates actions across systems. While Databricks powers data engineering, analytics, and AI, Clonal translates those outputs into context-aware applications embedded directly into workflows. Together, they form a complementary architecture: Databricks as the system of intelligence, Clonal as the system of action. Attendees will learn how to close the gap between having great data and using it in every interaction—enabling real-time, consistent, and scalable execution powered by AI.

speakers.name: Jeremy Bruck
speakers.bio:
Jeremy Bruck is a Partner at West Monroe, a global business and technology consulting firm, where he helps private equity firms and their portfolio companies unlock measurable value from data, analytics, and AI. He focuses on bridging the gap between emerging technologies and real business impact—turning data and AI investments into revenue growth, margin expansion, and operational efficiency.

With deep expertise in data strategy and digital transformation, Jeremy advises executive teams, boards, CIOs, and CFOs on how to prioritize and scale initiatives that deliver tangible results. His work centers on moving organizations beyond experimentation to build durable capabilities grounded in strong data foundations, modern architectures, and clear operating models.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Wisdom AI | Why Data Analysts are the Future of AI: The Rise of AI Context Engineers
sessions.body: AI analytics projects struggle to scale beyond demos because AI understands code but lacks critical business context—details like defining churn or explaining anomalies. Without this knowledge, AI produces wrong answers. The essential context is held by data analysts, who are currently underutilized. In this session, Kapil Chhabra introduces the AI Context Engineer, a vital new role merging analytics, data engineering, governance, and business strategy. Learn why this role is critical for building trusted AI on modern lakehouse platforms like Databricks. You will learn: why AI analytics projects fail; the four layers of context AI requires; how analysts become AI Context Engineers; and how governance improves trust in AI outputs. Success belongs to the companies that operationalize context.

speakers.name: Kapil Chhabra
speakers.bio:
Kapil Chhabra is the Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer of WisdomAI, where he leads product vision and innovation for the company’s enterprise analytics platform. He brings more than 20 years of experience building category-defining products across data, analytics, cloud, and AI.

Prior to WisdomAI, Kapil held leadership roles at Rubrik, where he led product organizations during its growth to $400M+ ARR. As Senior Director of Product Management, he oversaw initiatives across enterprise data protection and SaaS. He also led new database products scaling to $50M ARR in under three years.

Before Rubrik, Kapil was a Senior Product Manager at AWS, launching major services like Amazon Kinesis Analytics. Earlier, he spent a decade at Akamai Technologies building award-winning analytics and media products.

Kapil is also an active angel investor and advisor in the AI and cloud infrastructure space.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: You.com | Building AI Search Infrastructure for the Agentic Era
sessions.body:
AI agents need to go beyond simple lookups. They need to search deeply, synthesize across hundreds of sources and verify facts across multi-step reasoning chains. But building a deep search system that's accurate, fast and reliable at scale is a fundamentally different problem than traditional software systems. Saahil Jain, CTO of You.com, shares how the team built the Research API — ranked #1 on DeepSearchQA with 83.67% accuracy and 93.16% F1 — and what they learned along the way. The talk covers:

  • Why a robust but simple harness paired with high-quality search tools outperforms complex agent orchestration
  • The architectural choices behind pushing the accuracy-latency frontier across benchmarks from SimpleQA to DeepSearchQA
  • Why single-run eval numbers are misleading for agents, with practical techniques for measuring what actually matters.

 

Built for builders on platforms like Databricks who want to add deep search to their agentic workflows.

speakers.name: Saahil Jain
speakers.bio: Saahil Jain is the CTO of You.com. He started at You.com in December 2020 as a Founding Engineer and most recently served as the Head of AI. Before You.com, Saahil was a graduate researcher in the Stanford Machine Learning Group under Professor Andrew Ng, where he researched topics related to deep learning and natural language processing (NLP) in resource-constrained domains like healthcare. His research work has been published in machine learning conferences such as EMNLP, NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, and ACM-CHIL among others.

sessions.title: Sponsored by: Ziggiz | The Security Lakehouse You've Already Decided to Build — Here's How to Actually Do It
sessions.body: You don't need to be sold on the security data lakehouse. You already know it's the answer to the cost, scale, and performance problems that have plagued SIEMs for years. The hard part is getting there. Data collection at scale, lake management, and semantic modeling are each difficult problems on their own. Solving all three in production is where most security lakehouse projects stall. In this session we'll show exactly how ziggiz accelerates the journey — live on Databricks. See how ziggiz handles high-volume security data collection, manages the Delta Lake layer without manual schema wrangling, and delivers a detection-ready semantic model out of the box. No months-long data engineering project required. If your team has committed to the lakehouse path and wants to see what production-ready looks like on Databricks, this 15 minutes is for you.

speakers.name: Ben Newton
speakers.bio: Benjamin Eliot Newton is what happens when you combine a developer, a legal mind, and an extrovert — a combination so statistically improbable it probably deserves its own research grant. He's spent over a decade building large and complex cloud systems in various areas - even convincing some financial teams to migrate away from Excel. He's currently a Founding Engineer at ziggiz: building a modern Cybersecurity focused data platform on Databricks to save customers the pain he has already experienced.

sessions.title: SQL Is Still Your Superpower: Building Production Ready Data Pipelines Using Only SQL
sessions.body:
SQL didn’t get weaker, data platforms got better.

 

In this session, we demonstrate how modern data engineering on Databricks can be delivered end-to-end using SQL alone on the Lakehouse, without dependency on Python or external frameworks, including SQL AI functions and Geospatial Functions. Designed for organisations with strong BI/SQL foundations, this session shows how to transition to production-grade data engineering with minimal upskilling.

 

We showcase how pipelines are built using Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines via the Pipeline Editor, with ingestion, transformation, and data quality rules all defined declaratively in SQL. This demonstrates how SQL moves beyond querying into full pipeline engineering.

 

Governance is implemented by design using Unity Catalog, providing fine-grained permissions, lineage, and auditability across the entire pipeline. We also showcase AI/BI Genie, configured using SQL-only approaches (metrics, dimensions, instructions, and evaluation queries), enabling natural language access to trusted data.

 

This session reframes SQL as a first-class engineering language on the Lakehouse, capable of handling streaming, transformation, data quality, governance, and AI consumption, while unlocking existing talent and accelerating adoption without increasing complexity.

sessions.title: SQL Programming and Procedural Logic
sessions.body:
In this hands-on course, you will explore core SQL programming and procedural logic skills within Databricks, focusing on how to build modular, maintainable, and production-ready analytics workflows. You’ll start by learning about key SQL constructs—such as Common Table Expressions, temporary views, and User Defined Functions—that make your SQL development cleaner and more reusable. The course then guides you through advanced SQL scripting techniques using compound statements, variables, control flow, conditionals, loops, and robust error handling to create structured and flexible SQL processes. Finally, you’ll discover how to orchestrate and modernize complex workflows with Lakeflow Jobs and migration strategies, transforming legacy tasks into modular, automated pipelines that leverage the full capabilities of the Databricks platform.

Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026. 

Prerequisites

  • Familiarity with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, including workspaces, SQL warehouses, and notebooks
  • Experience with Databricks Lakehouse architecture, including Delta Lake and Unity Catalog
  • Intermediate SQL experience, including stored procedures, dynamic queries, and data analysis in relational databases
  • Familiarity with data pipeline orchestration and workflow management
  • Working knowledge of data warehousing concepts, including ETL, schema design, data modeling, and BI reporting

sessions.title: SQM: From Fragmented Data Silos to Real-Time ML Operations with Delta Sharing
sessions.body:
SQM set out to increase production efficiency by improving how raw materials are converted into finished product. But, it faced a classic data engineering challenge: critical operational data was trapped in silos (plant historians, lab systems, simulation tools) with no scalable way to unify it with enterprise data in Databricks. Operating decisions relied on operator experience rather than predictive models, leading to excess raw material use and inconsistent output.

 

Instead of building custom ETL pipelines to move data across systems, SQM leveraged Delta Sharing to create a governed, real-time data backbone. AVEVA’s cloud-based industrial intelligence platform, CONNECT, seamlessly shared data with Databricks on Azure using zero-copy and no data movement. This enabled operational data to be unified and refined into consistent minute-level views, and used to develop machine learning and optimization models.

sessions.title: Startup Forum
sessions.body: Hear from VC leaders, startup founders and early-stage customers building on Databricks around what they are seeing in the market and how they are scaling their early-stage companies on Databricks. This event is a must-see for VCs, founders and those interested in the early-stage company ecosystem.

speakers.name: Josh Lillie
speakers.bio: Josh helps lead the Startups GTM business at Databricks where he works with early stage companies to adopt Databricks. Separately, Josh is an investor and GTM advisor in numerous early stage startups.

speakers.name: Luyuan Fang
speakers.bio: Dr. Luyuan Fang is CEO and Founder of Curative AI, building AI-native solutions to transform healthcare revenue cycle management and clinical operations. The company reached cash-flow positivity in its first year without external funding. Previously, Luyuan was Chief AI Officer at Change Healthcare (acquired by Optum for $13.5B), leading AI at scale across the largest healthcare administrative network in the US, processing ~50% of US claims. She was also Chief AI and Data Officer at Prescryptive Health, landing AI in a network of 50,000+ pharmacies; and Founder of Expedia AI Labs, supporting all 14 Expedia Brands. Earlier, she held leadership roles at Microsoft Azure, Cisco, eBay, and AT&T. She holds a PH.D. in AI and 10 US patents.

speakers.name: Phil Mizrahi
speakers.bio: Phil Mizrahi is CEO and co-founder of Linkup, search infrastructure for AI agents and autonomous systems. Linkup indexes the web at the level of atoms of information, the granularity AI agents actually need. Backed by Gradient, Linkup powers real-time web search and deep research for teams building production AI. Previously, Phil built Amundsen, the open-source search engine at Lyft.

sessions.title: Stateful Apps for Thousands of Users: Horizontal Scaling, Session Affinity, and Sharding in Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
Databricks Apps make it easy to stand up a powerful internal app, but most teams don’t have a clear mental model for what happens when usage jumps from a handful of users to hundreds or thousands. In this advanced, under-the-hood session, we’ll walk through how Databricks Apps can remain stateful at scale: horizontal scaling across multiple app instances, session affinity to keep user context and in-memory state attached to the right replica, and sharding to distribute traffic and load safely across your fleet.

 

By the end, you’ll have a practical architecture playbook and checklist you can apply to take an existing Databricks App—from LLM agents to analytics UIs—and harden it for real production scale without giving up the fast developer experience you already enjoy.

sessions.title: Stop Arguing About Numbers: How Zalando Scales Governance With Unity Catalog and Metric Views
sessions.body:
At Zalando’s scale—serving over 50M European customers via a decentralized microservices architecture—data governance quickly turns into a "Data Swamp." Domain teams shipped fast, but without a unified semantic layer, "Net Revenue" on a marketing dashboard rarely matched the finance report. We faced a familiar dilemma: centralize and create bottlenecks, or stay decentralized and lose trust in our numbers.

 

This session will focus on our implementation of Unity Catalog, scaled across an organization with over 1,000 data engineers. This setup fosters team autonomy, enabling rapid data creation. We will also detail the governance mechanisms we've put in place to facilitate data sharing while maintaining minimal compliance risk.

 

We’ll then go deep into how we use metric views to move business logic out of siloed BI tools and directly into the lakehouse. This metric-as-code approach ensures that whether users query via notebooks, dashboards or AI agents, they get the same trusted answer.

speakers.name: Fabian Halkivaha
speakers.bio: Long Time veteran in the Data + AI space at Zalando who built the first "Big Data" pipelines back in 2013 when Hadoop was still a buzz word. Nowadays, mostly focusing on Analytical tooling and semantic governance topics.

speakers.name: Mukrram Ur Rahman
speakers.bio: Mukrram is a Principal Software Engineer at Zalando Data Foundation and is passionate about building scalable, governed, and business-friendly data platforms. He works at the intersection of data engineering, governance, and AI-driven analytics, helping organizations make trusted data more accessible while maintaining strong control and reliability. His experience spans platform architecture, data standardization, governance frameworks, and AI-driven innovation, with a consistent focus on turning technical complexity into business value. In his free time, he enjoys solving problems and actively explores AI, both as a technology and as a tool for creating practical, high-impact solutions.

sessions.title: Stop Guessing, Start Scoring: LLM Extraction Evaluation on Databricks
sessions.body: Speakers: Michelle JanneyCoyle (Databricks), Darshana Nair (CLA)Robust evaluation is key to building reliable LLM-based systems. Together with CliftonLarsonAllen (CLA), a leading accounting and professional services firm, we developed a Databricks-native evaluation solution. This system centralizes metrics, ground truth, and expert feedback to enable repeatable offline evaluation for their SOC extraction workflow.In this talk, we deconstruct our implementation, highlighting how we use managed MLflow, custom scorers, and a Databricks App with Lakebase to capture SME feedback and structured ground truth. During this talk you will learn how this framework makes quality measurable and provides clear signal for future improvements. Key TakeawaysAutomating evaluation using Databricks tools.Using Databricks Apps to bridge the gap between Data Science and domain experts.Lessons from evaluating complex semantic extraction and structured JSON outputs.

speakers.name: Darshana Nair
speakers.bio: Darshana Nair is a Data Scientist Director at CLA, where she leads the development of AI-driven solutions focused on intelligent automation, document intelligence, and data extraction. She specializes in agentic workflows, AI validation techniques and agent orchestration to streamline complex workflows, improve accuracy, and accelerate decision-making across enterprise operations.

speakers.name: Michelle JanneyCoyle
speakers.bio: Michelle JanneyCoyle is an AI Forward Deployed Engineer at Databricks with a background in data science and NLP. She works with customers to build production-ready AI applications that use structured and unstructured data to support real business workflows.

sessions.title: Stream into the Future: Mastering Stream processing for All Workloads
sessions.body:
The data world isn't slowing down—it’s streaming faster than ever. And if you're still thinking batch-first, it's time to flip the script.

 

Join us for an overview of new features in Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming. Learn how it is enabling AI workloads for Cursor, machine learning workflows in Coinbase, and complex real-time requirements of MakeMyTrip.

 

If you are an advanced user, this session is for you: we will showcase advanced features like real-time mode, transform with state, and streaming from hybrid sources. If you like simplicity, this session is also for you: you will discover how Spark Declarative Pipelines’s constructs can simplify stream processing.

speakers.name: Indrajit Roy
speakers.bio: Indrajit is passionate about making data processing simple and easy to use for everyone. At Databricks, he leads the teams the power Spark Structured Streaming and make materialized views magical. Indrajit used to lead the peta-byte scale and revenue critical Napa datawarehouse at Google. Indrajit started his career as a researcher at HP Labs, sprinkling machine learning over columnar store databases.

sessions.title: Streaming at Scale With Real-Time Mode: Sub-Second Train Telemetry Across the Netherlands
sessions.body:
In this talk, we showcase how NS (Dutch Railways) built an end-to-end Databricks solution that processes train telemetry in real time, enabling live detection of carriage failures and improving overall reliability. The platform handles more than 100 billion data points per day with sub-second end-to-end latency.

 

The session features a live demo of real train telemetry, giving the audience a direct, in‑room experience of real time.

 

We explain how the solution was engineered using the new Real-Time Mode for Spark Structured Streaming. The entire stack is built in PySpark and SQL, so no microservices, no separate streaming framework, just Databricks.

 

Throughout the session, we connect to other high velocity domains with cases like real time parcel rerouting, live airport baggage tracking and real-time signals feeding analytics and AI. Attendees leave with practical insights into bringing real time data into the modern data stack without the complexity of traditional streaming systems.

speakers.name: Anant Pingle
speakers.bio: Anant is a Sr. Specialist Solutions Engineer at Databricks, where he focuses on data engineering and warehousing. With a passion for streaming data, he helps organizations build robust, real-time data architectures. Before joining Databricks, he worked as a data engineer in the retail and insurance industries.

speakers.name: Wout de Ruiter
speakers.bio: Wout is a Data Architect at Capgemini with a strong focus on real time analytics. For almost three years, he has been working closely with Dutch Railways (NS), where his most recent project focuses on processing and analyzing live train telemetry at massive scale with an end-to-end Databricks solution. Wout enjoys working across the entire spectrum, from crafting data connectors to designing and delivering complete, production ready use cases. His approach centers on building durable platforms and reusable patterns that organizations can operate and evolve independently, turning real time data into a strategic, internal capability.

sessions.title: Streaming Data for Operational Apps: Building the Bridge From Analytics to Serving
sessions.body: Real‑time operational applications need instant query responses, but analytical platforms optimize for throughput over latency. Running separate operational and analytical databases leads to duplicate infrastructure, complex sync logic and data consistency issues. We needed sub‑second dashboards for factory operators to track machine performance in real time, while also enabling historical analysis and ML on the same data. Our previous platform stored only four days of raw data and lacked proper engineering practices. We built a streaming architecture on Databricks that serves operational queries via Lakebase Postgres and analytical workloads via Delta Lake from a single pipeline, eliminating the dual‑database problem. This session covers the architecture, our custom streaming sink, validation of the new platform alongside the legacy system, early mistakes and patterns for complex state logic, exactly‑once delivery, and measurable production outcomes.

speakers.name: Dmitry Ratushnyak
speakers.bio: Dmitry Ratushnyak is Global Data Engineering & Platform Lead at Lipton Teas and Infusions, where he drives the company’s data and AI platform strategy. With a background spanning Unilever and financial services, he specializes in building scalable data platforms and enabling real-world business impact through data. Dmitry focuses on turning complex architectures into practical, high-value solutions, helping organizations unlock insights and accelerate their data journey with modern technologies like Databricks.

sessions.title: Streaming NASA Data with Lakeflow and Agent Bricks: A Data Engineer's Guide to Databricks AI
sessions.body:
This Data + AI Summit session walks you through a streaming application that analyzes live NASA space data using Lakeflow and Agent Bricks.

 

Lakeflow is the foundation layer of every AI application. I explain how Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) ingests from one of the very few public Kafka topics that exist and how it works in symbiosis with Agent Bricks to turn real-time NASA circulars about cosmic events into an AI-powered knowledge base with Databricks Apps UI.

 

The AI stack covers AI Gateway, guardrails, Vector Search, agent evaluation, and MLflow tracing, all from a data engineer's perspective.

 

The second part focuses on Time to Value. I used several Databricks AI tools: Genie Code, Claude Code, the AI Dev Kit, and others. Each capable of taking you from zero to a working application in days rather than months. I share the trade-offs and best practices learned.

 

Grab the full application from GitHub afterward — and play with data from exploding supernovas.

sessions.title: Streaming the Game: Scaling Real-Time Intelligence at DraftKings With Kafka, Databricks & Sigma
sessions.body:
DraftKings set out to build a real-time analytics capability before the use cases were fully defined. Rather than waiting for perfect requirements, we invested in the streaming foundation first — allowing meaningful use cases to emerge from the platform itself.

 

We assembled an initial solution to deliver second-level visibility into transactions, active users, and revenue. As stakeholders gained live insight, new needs surfaced — including real-time liability tracking and deeper financial monitoring — many not originally envisioned.

 

As adoption expanded, we evolved the architecture to Kafka, Databricks Spark Declarative Pipelines and Real-Time Mode, as well as Sigma to improve scalability, flexibility, and governance. In this session, we will review the architectural evolution, key streaming design decisions, and how we blend real-time, historical, and forecast data into a financial intelligence system.

 

Attendees will leave with practical lessons for designing streaming-first systems when requirements are evolving.

speakers.name: Monika Hristova
speakers.bio: Monika Hristova is a Lead Software Architect at DraftKings with 18 years of experience designing complex, large-scale systems. Over the past decade, she has specialized in distributed, real-time data architectures using Apache Flink, Spark, and Databricks. She leads fraud detection and streaming initiatives, focusing on scalability, resilience, and performance. Her background spans multiple industries, where she delivered data platforms and ML pipelines. She is passionate about scalable system design and enjoys mountain biking, trail running, and reading.

speakers.name: Vinod Paidakula
speakers.bio: I’m a data leader with 17 years of experience across data and analytics, currently leading Data Product Management and QA at DraftKings. I’m passionate about bringing product thinking into data—building scalable platforms centered around reusable capabilities and self-serve access. More recently, I’ve been driving GenAI adoption to transform how data teams operate and deliver. Outside of work, I’m an avid pickleball player.

sessions.title: Streaming to Lakehouse: How Launchmetrics Simplified Pipelines, Built Data Trust and Adopted Genie
sessions.body:
At Launchmetrics, a leader in Brand Performance for fashion, luxury and beauty, our AWS real-time streaming architecture delivered low latency but created growing complexity, data inconsistencies and rising infrastructure costs.

 

We shifted to a batch-first Databricks Lakehouse built on Delta Lake, using medallion architecture and Unity Catalog for governance. The impact exceeded expectations: fewer pipelines, predictable costs, safe historical recomputation, and stronger data reliability—restoring trust across product, commercial and leadership teams.

 

Most importantly, this foundation enabled company-wide adoption of AI/BI Genie. Today, non-technical stakeholders query the lakehouse in natural language, reducing dependency on the data team and accelerating decisions.

 

In this session, we’ll share how we evaluated real-time vs. batch trade-offs, executed the migration safely and designed a “Genie-ready” lakehouse that delivers measurable business value.

speakers.name: Pau Montero Pares
speakers.bio:
Pau Montero Parés is a technology executive with more than 20 years of experience in technology leadership, digital transformation, and team management. He currently serves as Chief Technology Officer at Launchmetrics, where he leads the company’s technology strategy, product innovation, and engineering organization.

Prior to Launchmetrics, Pau worked as Development and Systems Manager at iMente Global, building strong expertise in technical operations and R&D. He holds a background in computer engineering and a master’s degree in policy and marketing, combining strategic vision with deep technical knowledge.

He is passionate about building high-performing teams, driving innovation, and scaling modern cloud-based and AI-powered platforms that support global growth.

sessions.title: Supercharging Genie Performance With Metric Views
sessions.body: Databricks Genie allows users to talk to their data, but its answers are only as good as the semantic layer beneath it. The Data Platform team shares how we are "supercharging" our internal Genie deployment by feeding it highly structured Metric Views. We will discuss the art of curating data specifically for GenAI consumption, ensuring that natural language queries yield accurate, trustworthy SQL generation. If you want to deploy AI/BI that actually works, you need to see how we structure our data for it.

speakers.name: Krishna Bhupatiraju
speakers.bio: Krishna Bhupatiraju is an engineering leader with nearly two decades of experience building scalable data platforms at top tech companies. He currently leads Data Platform Engineering at Databricks, where he oversees multiple global teams focused on data frameworks, ingestion, governance, and developer experience. Previously, Krishna drove experimentation infrastructure at Airbnb and led data engineering teams at Amazon. His work has empowered data-driven decision-making at scale, and he’s passionate about developing high-impact platforms and growing strong engineering cultures.

sessions.title: Tech Industry Forum | Sponsored by Entrada
sessions.body:
As the first wave of AI experimentation matures, leaders are facing a new bottleneck: the “Architectural Tax” of fragmented stacks. To move beyond universal foundation models and build production-grade AI applications, an interoperable foundation is essential. This foundation must unify governance, data and model choice to power high-frequency data and governed intelligence from a single location.

 

This 90-minute Tech Industry Forum joins leaders from the top AI innovators to bridge the gap between AI ambition and operational reality. We will move past the hype to address the foundational challenges that now define market leadership: eliminating the latency between data and application, slashing the overhead of massive compute costs and establishing the governance frameworks required to scale intelligent systems with confidence. This session is designed for leaders who must act now to transition from experimental AI into a high-velocity, production-scale operation.

 

After the session, connect with your peers during the exclusive Industry Forum Happy Hour. Reserve your seat today!

speakers.name: Daniel Cane
speakers.bio:
Daniel Cane is the co-CEO and co-founder of ModMed, a Florida-based health tech company transforming specialty healthcare. A Cornell graduate and co-founder of Blackboard Inc., Dan helped take Blackboard public and has since been recognized as a Top 50 Healthcare Technology CEO (2022–2024), EY Entrepreneur of the Year, and South Florida Ultimate CEO.
He serves on several boards, launched The Cane Institute for Advanced Technologies, and
established the Cane Entrepreneurship Scholars program at Cornell University. Passionate about innovation, Dan champions AI, telehealth, and structured data to improve healthcare outcomes and transparency.
Dan lives in Boca Raton, Florida, with his wife and three children.

speakers.name: Jason Reid
speakers.bio: Jason Reid is a Director of Product Management at Databricks and co-founder of Tabular. He's currently working on enhancing data compatibility and interoperability between lakehouse formats.

speakers.name: Michael Flynn
speakers.company: Rivian And VW Group Technology, LLC

speakers.name: Sheridan McDonald
speakers.bio:
Sheridan McDonald is VP & GM of Digital Natives at Databricks, where he helps leading tech and AI companies use data and AI to scale faster, operate smarter, and drive business impact. He leads one of Databricks’ fastest-growing businesses, partnering across sales, product, engineering, and marketing to accelerate growth and expand AI adoption across digital native and SaaS companies.

Sheridan joined Databricks in 2018 and has held leadership roles across Azure Databricks and Digital Natives. He brings more than 19 years of sales and leadership experience building high-performing teams and helping customers translate the Databricks Lakehouse and AI platform into business growth.

sessions.title: Tech Industry Session: How AI is Redefining the Way Apps are Built
sessions.body:
The traditional blueprint for building applications is more than 20 years old and optimized for a fragmented, ETL-heavy architectures of the early cloud era. The rise of agentic AI has broken this model, forcing us to reimagine how we — or perhaps agents — will build applications for the next 20 years. Today's AI native applications are increasingly written by agents, require easy access to real-time context and AI generated insights from other agents that legacy cloud platforms cannot provide without an expensive "Architectural Tax."

 

Join Akhil Gupta and engineering leaders from the leading tech companies as they discuss the shift from legacy stacks to an interoperable foundation. We’ll explore the "Lakebase" paradigm, where Lakebase, Databricks Apps and Agent Bricks provide the modern way to build AI-native applications. This session will move beyond the "vibe check," offering a candid look at how to eliminate silos and ship governed, production-grade AI applications at scale.

 

Key topics include:

  • Identifying and eliminating the "Architectural Tax" imposed by legacy cloud silos.
  • Understanding why AI-native applications require an interoperable app foundation: Lakebase.
  • How do you provide easy access to AI to these applications with Agent Bricks and Databricks Apps
  • Learn how a unified governance layer for both your data and AI helps you move from experimental prototypes to production agents faster.

speakers.name: Jaya Upadhyay
speakers.bio: Jaya Upadhyay is Senior Director of Enterprise Data Platform at Zillow, where she is enabling Zillow's data to be AI-ready for consumer experiences and internal teams. She leads the company's data mesh transformation across a portfolio spanning API and MCP orchestration, real-time streaming, analytics and ML platforms, and end-to-end data governance. With nearly two decades of data engineering and data platform leadership across Boats Group, Expedia Group, and Groupon, she has built petabyte-scale platforms, customer data ecosystems, and the high-performing teams behind them.

sessions.title: Tech Industry Session: The High-Velocity Platform for Customer Apps
sessions.body: The hidden cost and engineering friction of maintaining fragmented infrastructure for customer-facing features slows your product velocity. As high-frequency data and intelligence become the core of the user experience, the traditional strategy of managing siloed operational and analytical stacks has shifted from a technical inconvenience to a strategic liability. For organizations that must ship faster while controlling infrastructure overhead, the path forward is a fundamental move toward consolidation. This tech industry session moves past the theory to provide a proven blueprint for architecting experiences built directly on a unified foundation. We will explore the shift from “integrated” to “built-on” and detail how to consolidate specialized databases, eliminate brittle data pipelines and use the lakehouse and Lakebase architectures to power user experiences at a fraction of the traditional engineering cost.

speakers.name: Bruce Wong
speakers.bio: Bruce leads our internal Data Platform function at Databricks.   We build, own and operate our enterprise lakehouse for Databricks where all employees and all teams inside use Data and AI to solve problems and guide our decisions.  Previously Bruce held technical leadership roles at Netflix, Twilio and StitchFix where he gained deep experience building planet scale systems in a cloud-native environment.  Bruce also formed the Chaos Engineering team and led the initiative at Netflix to achieve ultimate resilience.  Bruce has also shares his experience and insights serving on product advisory boards previously for DataDog, PagerDuty, currently for DataBricks.

sessions.title: Technical Deep Dive: Architecting Production-Ready Data & AI Apps
sessions.body:
Organizations are moving beyond simple dashboards to interactive, secure Data & AI applications built directly where their data lives. This session provides a technical deep dive into Databricks Apps, exploring how to transform complex AI logic into production-ready business tools.

 

We will cover the essential architectural choices for developers, including a comparison of Pythonic frameworks like Streamlit and Gradio versus full-stack JS/TS implementations. The discussion will focus on the end-to-end development lifecycle, teaching you how to master authentication via Service Principals and On-Behalf-Of (OBO) tokens, and how to implement robust production workflows using Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs). Additionally, we will share best practices for optimizing performance and scalability—such as using async operations—and ensuring enterprise-grade observability through diagnostic logging and audit trails

speakers.name: Ivan Trusov
speakers.bio: Ivan Trusov is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks. His main focus specialties are Unity Catalog, Platform Automation, Serverless Security and Databricks Apps.

sessions.title: Telecommunications Industry Forum
sessions.body: Join us this year at the Telecommunications Industry Forum. Industry leaders from around the globe will share how data and AI are allowing them to unlock key business outcomes like enhanced customer experience, true autonomous networks, and fraud prediction and prevention. Discover how Databricks is empowering operators to overcome legacy silos, accelerate innovation with Agentic AI, and turn massive data volumes into measurable growth and operational excellence.

sessions.title: The 52x Multiplier: How Zepto Mastered AI Agent Evaluation at Scale
sessions.body:
In quick commerce, delivery windows are measured in minutes, making AI reliability existential. At Zepto, scaling to 80,000 daily autonomous support tickets demanded more than “vibe-based” testing—it required treating evaluation as core infrastructure. This session unveils the comprehensive dual-loop framework (powered by MLFlow 3.0 and DSPy) that transforms operational risk into a competitive advantage.

 

We achieved a verified 52X ROI on evaluation infrastructure, slashing support costs by 65% while boosting CSAT by 20.5%. By shifting from reactive fixes to real-time tracing, we compressed issue detection from 3 hours to 5 minutes and reduced social media escalations by 74%. We will deconstruct the technical blueprint for establishing “Evaluation as Infrastructure”—covering LLM-as-a-Judge calibration, strategic sampling, and automated feedback loops—enabling teams to deploy complex, multimodal AI agents with absolute confidence and control.

speakers.name: Deepak Dhankani
speakers.bio: Deepak Dhankani is a Data Science leader at Zepto, India's fastest growing quick commerce platform, where he heads a multidisciplinary team spanning Ads, Customer Delight, Fraud, and Pricing. With hands-on technical depth and strategic leadership, he drives end-to-end data science initiatives from building ad systems, Bayesian fraud detection models and agentic AI customer support systems to designing multi-agent frameworks.

speakers.name: Gireesh Sreedhar K P
speakers.bio: Gireesh Sreedhar is an AI Systems Architect and Transformation Leader with 23+ years in technology and a decade building and scaling Data + AI systems for global enterprises. At Databricks, He partners with technology leaders and Engineer teams to turn ambitious AI strategy into production‑grade, agentic AI on the Lakehouse, with a sharp focus on MLflow‑driven MLOps and rigorous evaluation at million‑plus interaction scale. He has delivered enterprise AI agents that slash processing from hours to minutes, cut costs by up to 85%, and achieve 5–8x faster resolutions with double‑digit CSAT uplift in complex, highly regulated environments.

sessions.title: The Agent Supervisor: Reinventing Industrial Document Workflows with AI
sessions.body: Industrial enterprises sit on decades of unstructured knowledge locked in engineering drawings, work orders, and maintenance logs. Join this session to see how leading manufacturers, energy producers, and transportation operators are using multi-agent supervisor architectures on Databricks to extract, validate, and reason over complex technical documents - cutting review cycles, improving compliance, and turning institutional knowledge into a competitive edge.

speakers.name: Karthik Josyula
speakers.bio: Tailored Data and Analytics industry Leader focusing on Data AI and GenAI technology strategy, change management, execution and value delivery. Spearheaded delivery of impactful AI capabilities in Supply Chain, Customer Experience and GTM domains.

speakers.name: mitchell Calvert
speakers.bio: Mitchell Calvert is a Senior Supply Chain Systems Manager at Kohler, where he leads AI, analytics, and digital transformation initiatives across global operations. He architects and deploys enterprise-scale solutions leveraging Databricks, SAP, and Microsoft’s Power Platform to optimize planning, procurement, and manufacturing.  Known for bridging business strategy with advanced analytics, he helps organizations unlock scalable value from AI in complex supply chain environments.

sessions.title: The Agentic Lakehouse: Optiver’s AI Data Stack
sessions.body:
AI-driven usage has accelerated sharply in recent months. A significant portion of our users now delegate Databricks work to agents rather than interacting with the platform directly. This shift increases the importance of the foundations beneath.

 

This session introduces Optiver's Lakehouse AI Stack: a set of MCP servers, skills, and deployment tooling designed to provide agents with the context Databricks does not expose by default. We walk through a representative user journey, highlight where agents fall short today, and describe how each component addresses a specific gap.

speakers.name: Calvin Yiu
speakers.bio: Calvin Yiu sits between Optiver's lakehouse and the people who use it. As a software engineer on the Lakehouse Team, he's spent two and a half years building the tooling that turns infrastructure into something engineers, researchers, traders, and increasingly their agents can actually work with.

sessions.title: The Agentic Stack: A Founder Conversation on the Open Infrastructure Powering AI Agents
sessions.body:
The next great platform shift isn't a model. It's the infrastructure that turns models into autonomous action. Just as cloud produced a layered stack of open technologies, the agentic era is producing its own, defined right now, in the open.

 

This panel brings together the founders building each layer: how agents are constructed, how they collaborate as teams, how context is processed and made agent-ready, and how they're governed at scale. Together, they'll discuss what the "Linux moment" for agents looks like and what it means when the most consequential software in an enterprise writes itself.

 

The big questions:

  • Where does the open platform stack land in next 2-3 years - a thriving ecosystem or a consolidated stack?
  • What happens when agents become the primary consumers of infrastructure, not humans?
  • When does multi-agent coordination actually outperform a single well-built agent and when is it just complexity for complexity's sake?
  • Who owns accountability when an open-source agent takes an autonomous action on production data?
  • How do agents process context differently than humans? What are the implications on how context must be processed and exposed through tool interfaces?

speakers.name: Jerry Liu
speakers.bio: Jerry is the co-founder/CEO of LlamaIndex, the most accurate and secure platform to automate document workflows with AI agents. Before this, he led ML monitoring at Robust Intelligence, did self-driving AI research at Uber ATG, and worked on recommendation systems at Quora.

sessions.title: The Alpha Advantage: Building the Intelligent Capital Markets Firm with Databricks
sessions.body: Markets look calm, but underneath, there is a rapid reshuffling of outcomes driven by technology, capital intensity, and AI. In this environment, the edge isn’t models— it’s proprietary data and the ability to operationalize it.With Databricks, firms like Franklin Templeton and LSEG are automating workflows, scaling AI, and turning data into a durable competitive advantage.

speakers.name: Adam Towne
speakers.bio: Adam Towne is a Director of Product at LSEG, where he leads Lipper, the firm's fund analytics business, and owns data distribution across Analytics. With over a decade building data and analytics products in financial services, he focuses on serving sophisticated institutional users — quants, portfolio managers, and analysts who treat data as critical infrastructure. His current work spans cloud delivery, enterprise data licensing, and applying AI to fund research workflows. His product philosophy centers on designing for power users — what he calls "optimizing for the 1,000th use, not the first." He holds a degree in engineering from Cornell University.

speakers.name: Andrea DeSosa
speakers.bio:
Andrea DeSosa is the Global Capital Markets GTM Lead at Databricks, driving strategy and executive engagement across investment banks, asset managers, exchanges, and data providers. She partners with C-suite stakeholders to modernize front-office workflows and accelerate AI adoption across financial services.

Previously, Andrea spent 15+ years at Bloomberg in enterprise sales and product management, most recently leading fixed income AI initiatives focused on natural-language workflows and discoverability. Her background spans enterprise data platforms, large revenue books, and trading workflow modernization in fixed income markets. She brings deep capital markets expertise and a pragmatic approach to complex, regulated environments.

speakers.name: Mark Nigro
speakers.bio:
Mark Nigro is the Head of Portfolio Research at Franklin Templeton, where he leads research efforts focused on evaluating investment managers, markets, and portfolio opportunities across asset classes. His work centers on creating unique, large-scale structured data sets and using AI to improve how investment insights are communicated and applied, turning market complexity into clear, actionable outcomes for investors.
Mark has spent his 20-year career in asset management working with complex investment data across research, portfolio construction, fixed income, alternatives, and institutional and advisor-facing roles.
Mark is a CFA and CAIA Charterholder and holds a B.S. in Finance from Canisius University.

speakers.name: Paul Signorelli
speakers.bio:
As a Solutions Architect at Databricks, I leverage my expertise in software development and data system architecture to design and implement scalable and secure solutions for our customers. With a long history of experience in the tech industry, I have a proven track record of delivering high-quality results.

Through my career I have honed my skills in software development, system architecture, and software design and I am passionate about creating innovative solutions that meet the needs of diverse stakeholders and drive business growth.

sessions.title: The Data Gap in Women's Football & How FIFPro and Databricks Are Helping to Close It
sessions.body:
As the FIFA World Cup kicks off in the USA days before this summit, billions will follow the men's game, but women footballers still fight for visibility and basic protections. FIFPro, representing 65,000+ professional footballers, is using data to change that.

 

For over a decade, FIFPro has surveyed women footballers worldwide on working conditions, welfare and employment rights. But that data lived on laptops in fragmented spreadsheets with critical insights locked away.

 

In this session, Blend shares how we built a data platform on Databricks to power evidence-based advocacy. We'll cover designing a medallion architecture for messy survey data spanning multiple tournament cycles, configuring AI/BI Genie so non-technical researchers can query data in natural language, and building Power BI dashboards that surface cross-confederation trends.

 

When women's football data sits on laptops, it's easy to overlook. In a lakehouse, it's impossible to ignore.

sessions.title: The Databricks Big Book of AgentOps: The New DevOps Principles for AI Agents
sessions.body: The journey from traditional machine learning models to AI systems demands a new, specialized set of operational practices. This talk traces the evolution of core DevOps principles from the decade of MLOps to the Agents era, where we must plan for deploying and maintaining autonomous, multi-step AI agents that can reason, plan, and take actions in the real world using external tools.The talk will show how classic DevOps tenets like continuous deployment must be radically re-engineered to tackle core AgentOps challenges. Authors of The Databricks Big Book of Agent Ops will cover:Ensuring Maturity of Operational Controls: How critical operational controls must evolve to support multi-agent architectures.Distributed Tracing and Observability: Transforming single-step I/O logs into traces essential for debugging and explaining agent behavior.Governed Deployment and Rollback: Establishing AgentOps CI/CD pipelines that treat configurations (prompts, tools, routing logic) as code

speakers.name: Jeanne Choo
speakers.bio: Jeanne Choo is the APJ ML Lead at Databricks. She started as AI Engineer #1 at AI Singapore, building their consulting arm, apprenticeship program and technical stack from scratch. Jeanne was then AI Lead at Bank of Singapore. Her best projects have been APAC-specific, for example, Japanese Search Query Understanding, Speech Recognition models for Singlish, and building NLP models and corpuses for Indonesian. Each of these projects faced similar MLOps challenges; to be at Databricks solving these issues is very exciting for Jeanne.

speakers.name: Kyra Wulffert
speakers.bio: Kyra Wulffert is an AI Specialist Architect at Databricks with a background spanning production ML, AI strategy, and agentic systems. She specialises in agentic architectures, evaluation frameworks, and production pipelines, having previously led data science teams shipping NLP, recommendation, and predictive systems. She has spoken at PyData London, ODSC Europe, and WiDS Stanford.

sessions.title: The Databridge Platform: Connecting Data Silos Seamlessly With Databricks
sessions.body:
We introduce the Databridge Platform, a solution developed by Rakuten Group, Inc. to address the significant data management challenges inherent in their vast global ecosystem. Rakuten faces issues such as data and infrastructure silos, complex data access procedures and data duplication.

 

Built on the Databricks ecosystem, the Databridge Platform leverages technologies like Unity Catalog, Data Access Management Service (DAMS) and AI/BI Genie. Its architecture prioritizes a single workspace for ease of setup while retaining flexibility for dedicated tenant workspaces. The platform's strategic roadmap includes a proof of concept by March 2026, a production release by June 2026, and a long-term goal of achieving 100% connected data warehouse federation by 2028, ultimately unlocking enhanced AI capabilities and driving cross-business growth through improved data utilization.

speakers.name: Prakash Balraj
speakers.bio: Engineering Manager at Rakuten, sits at the intersection of data infrastructure and business transformation. With over 13 years of experience, I have architected scalable pipelines that turn raw data into key insights for Rakuten’s diverse business units. I am currently spearheading Rakuten’s unified data solution, optimizing the end-to-end workflow from discovery to analysis. I am dedicated to building the foundational infrastructure required to scale Data and AI initiatives across the global organization.

sessions.title: The Enterprise Guide to Agentic AI Risk: Security, Governance, and the Cross-Functional Playbook
sessions.body: When AI systems shift from analyzing to acting, the threat model changes fundamentally. Most enterprises are not ready. Agentic AI amplifies both the speed of innovation and the magnitude of risk, creating new attack surfaces and governance gaps that no single team can close alone. The organizations getting this right are not treating agentic security as a CISO problem. They are building cross-functional response models that unite security, data, legal, and technology leadership around a shared risk framework. In this session, Databricks CISO Omar Khawaja introduces the lethal trifecta of agentic risk, the three converging conditions that create enterprise-scale exposure and the organizational playbook for neutralizing it. You'll walk away with a prioritized set of actions your enterprise can begin implementing in the next 30 days, and a model for the cross-functional partnerships that make agentic AI governable at scale.

sessions.title: The Evolution of Prompting: From Artisan Craft to Algorithmic Optimization
sessions.body: LLMs unlocked advanced capabilities for users of all technical abilities precisely because of their natural language interface. Building enterprise solutions involved prompt engineering - a process of trial and error. This talk explores how automated prompt optimization represents a paradigm shift in how we build high quality, maintainable enterprise solutions with LLMs. We'll examine the core limitations of hand-crafted prompting, then dive into how prompt optimizers solve these problems. The session will cover the current state of the art in prompt optimization, including the latest algorithms such as GEPA. We'll demonstrate measurable performance gains that prompt optimizers achieve over manual engineering - often discovering counterintuitive prompts that humans would never write but dramatically outperform our best handcrafted attempts. You'll leave understanding how prompt optimizers work and why they are essential for building high quality, maintainable GenAI solutions.

speakers.name: Hanna Moazam
speakers.bio: Hanna is a Solutions Architect at Databricks, based in London. While she specializes in data science and ML, she enjoys solving all kinds of complex problems with data. She is a strong proponent of and contributor to the open source community, developing open source solutions for governance and GenAI. Prior to Databricks, she was a Data & AI CSA at Microsoft. Hanna has a degree in Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon University.

sessions.title: The Friday Afternoon Incident - Branching Beyond Code
sessions.body: Git branching revolutionized code development—but databases remain bottlenecks.Shared dev databases force sequential work, causing conflicts and blocking deployments.This live demo shows database branching with Lakebase Autoscaling using a fraud detection system (Databricks Apps + Lakebase).Watch multiple developers work in parallel on merchant risk scoring—each with isolated database branches.We demonstrate:(1) Shared database problems(2) Parallel development with branch isolation(3) Production hotfix without blocking feature work(4) Conflict-free merges(5) Autoscaling cost savings.Technical highlights: live schema migrations, branch-aware apps, automated conflict detection, database CI/CD.Takeaways: eliminate database bottlenecks, test safely against production schemas and data, deploy without blocking teams, reduce infrastructure costs.Technologies: Lakebase Autoscaling, Databricks Apps, Unity Catalog, Databricks Asset Bundles.

speakers.name: Ben Hazan
speakers.bio: Ben Hazan is a Sr. Solutions Engineer at Databricks specializing in data platform architecture and Lakehouse analytics. He helps organizations modernize their data infrastructure, using Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and MLflow — spanning data engineering, ML/GenAI workflows, and governance. Ben regularly presents at customer summits and leads hands-on workshops on ETL, MLOps/LLMOps, and cost optimization. Based in Israel, he brings a practical, developer-centric approach to solving complex data challenges.

speakers.name: Guy Livni
speakers.bio: Guy Livni is an enterprise Solutions Architect with extensive experience in data platform architecture and data-driven business solutions. He specializes in helping organizations modernize their data infrastructure and scale their analytical capabilities. Guy has worked with diverse organizations across various industries to design and implement robust, future-proof data solutions. He is deeply passionate about developer productivity and frequently presents on topics ranging from data engineering best practices to AI-powered applications.

sessions.title: The Full Databricks App Experience
sessions.body: What does a real Databricks App look like in production? In this session, we walk through an internal tool we use every day: an agentic Lakeflow generation system built entirely on the Databricks platform. Starting from raw Unity Catalog tables, the app uses foundational models orchestrated in a LangGraph loop to profile data, design pipelines, validate transformations, and generate fully deployable Lakeflow artefacts from Silver through to Gold.We’ll show how application state, specifications, and user preferences are managed in Lakebase, enabling a seamless, iterative build experience inside Databricks. Forget the quick toy POC Apps you've been seeing. This is a practical blueprint for building intelligent, stateful data applications natively on the Lakehouse.

speakers.name: Simon Whiteley
speakers.bio: Simon is the CTO of Advancing Analytics, a world-leading, forward-thinking Databricks consultancy, where he turns complex technology innovations into practical organisational guidance. With a career spent architecting data systems and shaping strategy, he brings a rare mix of deep technical expertise and big-picture vision. On stage and online, Simon shares insights on AI, Engineering and Analytics with clarity and energy making the future of tech both accessible and exciting. A trusted voice in the Databricks space and a prolific YouTuber, he’s driven by a passion for building solutions that are as impactful as they are intelligent, always keeping people, purpose, and progress at the core.

sessions.title: The Future Grid: Utilities Leaders on Data & AI
sessions.body: Discover how forward-thinking utilities are reimagining grid management, customer experience, and renewable integration through advanced analytics and AI. EDP and Eversource discuss how they are using the Databricks to turn complex operational data into actionable intelligence by improving reliability, reducing costs, and driving the clean energy transition at scale.

speakers.name: Nelson Pinho
speakers.bio:
Nelson Pinho is Global Head of Digital & AI at EDP, where he leads the group’s digital strategy, data platform architecture and AI transformation across business units. Over his career at EDP, he has progressed from roles in technology and digital innovation into global leadership, driving large‑scale cloud, data and AI programs that support the company’s energy‑transition strategy.

He is recognized externally as a leading data and AI executive, has contributed to international initiatives such as World Economic Forum work on AI in industry, and invests in his executive development through programs like INSEAD’s Advanced Management Programme.
Before that Nelson was an executive at Microsoft

sessions.title: The Future Is Self-Serve: Lessons Learned on Democratized Data and AI Agents at OpenAI
sessions.body:
