OpenAI isn’t just building breakthrough AI—it’s reinventing how teams work, grow, and scale in an AI-first world.

 

In this session, hear directly from Jeff Canada, Marketing Operations Lead about how OpenAI is transforming its organization to support rapid and sustained growth.

 

He’ll share how OpenAI built a trusted system of record on Databricks and how composable technologies built on Databricks, such as Hightouch, enable accurate, self-serve access to data and AI across the business.

 

You’ll walk away with practical lessons on modern data foundations, democratized access across teams, and AI-powered operations—but more importantly, you’ll get inspired by how OpenAI empowers every team member to move faster and make better decisions in an AI-driven future.

sessions.title: The Future of Cross-Company Collaboration on Databricks
sessions.body:
For years, cross-company collaboration meant sharing files, tables, and dashboards. That era is ending. In this session, we explore the next era of collaboration — one where organizations share intelligence, not just data.

 

Databricks is reimagining what it means to work across organizational boundaries. Instead of exchanging static assets, partners and customers will interact through AI-native experiences — governed, secure, and designed for a world where every company runs on agents. We'll paint the picture of a new ecosystem of tools and services that turns every data relationship into something dynamic, conversational, and instantly valuable.

 

If you believe the future of B2B is agentic, this session will show you where it's all heading. You'll leave with a new mental model for what collaboration looks like when AI is the interface.

sessions.title: The Intelligent Healthcare System: How AI Is Redefining Care Delivery to Coverage
sessions.body:
The next wave of healthcare transformation won't be driven by data alone, it will be driven by AI that can reason, act and operate across the full continuum of care. In this session, we explore how leading healthcare organizations are moving beyond dashboards and static models to deploy agentic AI workflows built on Databricks — where Genie enables clinical and operational teams to query complex data in plain language, and Mosaic AI orchestrates multi-step agents that surface insights at the point of decision.

 

You'll hear from thought leaders including Centene around "The Gifts of the MAGI: Delivering Secure, Repeatable, and Explainable AI". For enterprises in regulated industries, scaling agentic AI requires more than policy, it demands runtime governance. Centene, in partnership with Databricks and Slalom, built MAGI (Machine Agentic Governed Intelligence), a production framework that delivers three essential gifts: Security that enforces compliance and protects PHI by default, Repeatability through a governed "paved road" for consistent AI development, and Explainability via immutable audit trails for every AI decision. They'll demonstrate how MAGI's composable architecture uses automated evaluation, centralized monitoring, and feedback loops to accelerate safe AI adoption at scale. This approach has given Centene the consistency and confidence to grow its AI portfolio across its enterprise. You'll leave with practical patterns for building your own runtime governance for agentic AI on Databricks.

speakers.name: Barrett Foat
speakers.bio: Barrett C. Foat is a senior AI and machine learning leader responsible for leading large-scale enterprise AI initiatives within Centene’s Data & Analytics organization. He currently oversees the development, deployment, and governance of machine learning and AI capabilities that support business decisioning and healthcare outcomes across the enterprise. He is recognized for aligning AI innovation with business strategy, enabling measurable ROI, and operationalizing AI at scale through disciplined engineering, MLOps, and governance practices.

speakers.name: Guneeti Sharma
speakers.bio: Guneeti Sharma is a Senior Principal in AI at Slalom, leading enterprise Agentic AI strategy and delivery for healthcare organizations. She specializes in building large-scale AI platforms on Databricks that operationalize LLMs, multi-agent systems, and AI governance in regulated environments. Her work focuses on transforming care delivery and payer operations through intelligent workflow orchestration, responsible AI, and scalable enterprise adoption. She is recognized for bridging AI innovation with execution—helping organizations move from experimentation to production-grade AI systems that drive measurable business and healthcare outcomes.

speakers.name: Mark Tabor
speakers.bio: As a Senior Manager at Centene, Mark Tabor leads Enterprise Data Science & AI Platforms. He specializes in building robust MLOps frameworks that operationalize Data Science at scale within complex enterprise environments. Mark combines technical depth with a passion for science and technology to deliver future-ready, intelligence-driven solutions in the healthcare space.

sessions.title: The Lakehouse Behind a Modern CDP
sessions.body: Building a CDP isn’t just a UI and APIs—it’s a data platform problem at scale. This talk shows how Warner Bros. Discovery built the Databricks-powered “back of house” for Mosaic, supporting audience segmentation and activation across millions of subscribers. We’ll walk through the data plane that converts high-volume first-party events (client SDK + server events) into governed Delta tables using Spark Structured Streaming, then runs incremental batch pipelines to produce custom attributes and curated event views for segmentation across identity grains. We’ll also cover the audience evaluation engine: drag-and-drop audience definitions are stored as rule trees, compiled into Spark plans and evaluated at scale to generate deterministic audience outputs for downstream delivery. Key production patterns include table modeling, join/partition strategies, observability and separation between the metadata plane (API-driven config) and the Databricks execution plane.

speakers.name: Apratim Tiwari
speakers.bio: Apratim is an Software Engineering manager building high-throughput backend systems for marketing platforms—APIs, orchestration, and low-latency services that turn data into better campaigns.

sessions.title: The Modern Databricks Notebook: Tips, AI workflows, and Best Practices for Every Practitioner
sessions.body: Databricks Notebooks are the heartbeat of data and AI work, but most practitioners only scratch the surface of what they can do. Whether you are writing your first cell or building production-grade pipelines, this session is a practical guide to getting more out of the modern notebook experience.Topics include:- Core authoring productivity: side-by-side editing, tab groups, TOC and minimap, and smarter cell management- Running and exploring data with result table profiling, filter-to-SQL, and targeted SQL execution- AI in your notebook with AI functions for SQL and Python, plus Genie Code for agentic development- Engineering best practices with the notebook debugger, unit testing, and Serverless session restore- A live end-to-end workflow that brings everything together

speakers.name: Samantha Banchik
speakers.bio: Samantha Banchik is a Product Manager at Databricks, focusing on authoring with the Databricks Assistant. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science from the University of California, Berkeley. Samantha brings a strong background in software engineering and product management, with previous roles in developer tooling, cloud security, and autonomous vehicles.

sessions.title: The New CISO Mandate: Navigating the Speed vs. Risk Dilemma of Deploying Agentic SOC Tools
sessions.body: In the race to outpace automated threats, AI is no longer optional, it is the primary defense. However, deploying AI within the Security Operations Center (SOC) requires more than just new tools; it requires a new framework of governance to ensure those tools are safe, unbiased, and effective.Join Databricks Field CISO Omar Khawaja and a panel of security experts as they explore the intersection of AI governance and real-world SOC operations. We will dive into the practicalities of:Operationalizing Safety: How to deploy AI-driven detection and response without introducing new enterprise risks.The Velocity Gain: Leveraging AI to radically compress vulnerability lifecycles and patching windows.Guardrails for Autonomy: Implementing the essential governance "kill switches" and oversight needed when moving toward an Agentic SIEM.This session provides a practical roadmap for security leaders trying to navigate the "Speed vs Risk" dilemma of deploying modern AI technology.

sessions.title: The New Genie: From Data Q&A to Enterprise Agent
sessions.body: In this session, we'll introduce the new Genie, a unified, multi-agent AI that doesn't just answer questions about your data, it acts on it. We'll show how Genie connects enterprise knowledge stores and unstructured content to deliver richer insights, how it orchestrates across Genie Spaces and custom agents to complete complex work, and how it can take governed actions on your behalf, including automating recurring tasks and skills. Attendees will leave understanding why Genie is not just a data Q&A chatbot, but an enterprise AI that connects your people, your data, and your systems—and gets work done.

speakers.name: Elise Georis
speakers.bio: Elise Georis is on the product team at Databricks, focused on Genie: an enterprise AI that connects your people, data, and systems to help you get work done. Previously, she oversaw product for Lakeflow Connect.

sessions.title: The Open Handshake: Scaling Multi-Cloud Delivery via Delta Sharing and Iceberg
sessions.body:
Client demand is shifting. They don’t want our data; they want it in their platform. We solved the “Vendor Lock-in” crisis by building an Open Data Passport. This session deconstructs how we leveraged Delta Sharing and Apache Iceberg UniForm to deliver high-scale healthcare products to clients without moving a single byte of raw data. We’ll share the engineering “scars” of managing cross-cloud permissions and how we turned an interoperability headache into a competitive product advantage for our global ecosystem.

 

Demo: A live cross-platform “handshake” between a Databricks source and a non-Databricks consumer with zero ETL.

 

Takeaways:

  • Architecting zero-copy delivery via Delta Sharing
  • Managing multi-platform governance
  • Building vendor-agnostic data products

speakers.name: Ravi Purohit
speakers.bio: Ravi is a builder at heart who finds his "zen" at the intersection of deep engineering and product craft. Currently leading high-scale Data Platforms at McKesson, he has spent 15+ years architecting global ecosystems serving 1Bn+ users across e-commerce, fintech, and healthcare spanning both B2C and B2B domains. Ravi specializes in the "un-breakable" stuff - mission-critical migrations, high-performance infrastructure and state of the art user experience. A seasoned speaker, he’s best known for sharing "scars from the trenches" and proving that even the most daunting technical challenges can be reshaped into elegant, scalable user experiences.

speakers.name: vinaya thimmappa
speakers.bio: Vinaya is a seasoned engineering leader currently serving as Director of Engineering at McKesson Compile India, where he drives technical strategy and builds high-performance software teams. With over two decades of experience across technology and product organizations, Vinaya has led engineering efforts at companies spanning startups and large enterprises. He writes and speaks about software engineering practices, agile frameworks, and tech leadership, and enjoys sharing insights on observability, coding philosophy, and team culture. Vinaya holds advanced business and technical credentials and is passionate about mentoring engineers and shaping scalable systems

sessions.title: The Open Security Lakehouse: Building Agentic Cyber Defense with Lakewatch
sessions.body:
Legacy SIEMs are drowning security teams in alerts but starving them of insight. As threats grow more complex and attackers operate at machine speed, cybersecurity must be treated as a data and AI problem at scale.

 

In this session, we'll walk through a Cybersecurity Intelligence Platform powered by Lakewatch, Databricks' open, agentic SIEM. We'll show how to streamline security data ingestion and automated cloud log collection, then rapidly normalize it into the OCSF standard to cut time-to-value.

 

From there, we'll explore large-scale analytics, behavioural ML, and Detection-as-Code workflows that bring software engineering rigor to detection and response. The highlight is Agentic Threat Hunting with Lakewatch: AI agents that reason over security signals alongside business and application data, leveraging internal knowledge to add critical context, reduce false positives, and automate complex triage.

 

Join us to see how modern SOCs can move beyond the traditional SIEM toward true security intelligence with Lakewatch and the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform.

speakers.name: Alysson Souza
speakers.bio: Alysson Souza is a Product Specialist at Databricks, focused on helping data and cybersecurity teams across the Asia-Pacific region design and deploy Lakehouse architectures for security analytics, threat detection, and operational resilience.

sessions.title: The Right Model for the Job: A Practical Framework for AI
sessions.body: Not every problem needs the biggest model — and not every model works out of the box. With frontier models, small open models, and fine-tuning all on the table, the hardest question isn't "can we do AI?" It's "which model is actually right for this?"In this session, we walk through how to match models to use cases across real enterprise workloads. You'll see when a frontier model earns its cost, when a small open model wins on latency, and when fine-tuning turns a generic model into a specialist that knows your business. We'll put the tradeoffs in action — quality, cost, latency, control — using concrete examples across customer support, document processing, and analytics.You'll leave with a repeatable framework for choosing, customizing, and deploying the right model on Databricks every time — and the patterns to keep those decisions sharp as new models land.

speakers.name: Nuno Castro
speakers.bio: Nuno is a Director of AI Forward Deployed Engineering at Databricks, leading a specialized team that builds and productionizes first-of-its-kind AI applications. With 20 years of AI/ML experience - 12 in commercial leadership -he excels at moving AI from experimentation to live production. Previously, he was Sr. Manager of Applied Science at AWS, delivering 150+ GenAI and Agentic AI projects. His background includes 8 years at Expedia Group directing global data science for Search and Personalization, and fighting fraud at Feedzai. Nuno holds a PhD in CS/ML and began his career in R&D at Nokia-Siemens.

speakers.name: Viktoria Semaan
speakers.bio: Viktoria Semaan is Principal Technical Evangelist at Databricks, where she helps Fortune 500 enterprises adopt and scale AI. With 15+ years of experience as a solutions architect and technical leader, she has advised global enterprises on building production-grade AI and cloud architectures across industries including financial services, manufacturing, and SaaS. At Databricks, she focuses on enterprise AI adoption, agentic systems, and the practical patterns that move AI projects from prototype to production. Previously, she was at AWS, supporting global strategic partners. She holds an MBA from UCLA Anderson and an MS in Information Systems and Technology.

sessions.title: The Talent Engineering Playbook: How Yanolja Built a High-Performance Data Culture
sessions.body:
A modern data platform is just the foundation; success depends on the teams steering it. For Yanolja, Korea’s leading travel-tech unicorn, scaling innovation required a systematic talent strategy to match rapid technical growth.

 

This session offers an inside look at enterprise-scale talent evolution. We deconstruct an "assess-and-architect" methodology, using data-driven diagnostics to bridge skill gaps. A key pillar was establishing an enterprise-wide data capability framework. This created a shared language for skills and maturity — acting as a cultural catalyst that aligns leadership, engineering and business teams.

 

Partnering with Databricks, Yanolja redefined how human capital accelerates platform ROI. Discover how structural enablement became a tangible value driver. Learn how technical fluency correlates with platform returns and how leadership can pivot from managing systems to architecting a resilient, data-first culture.

speakers.name: YOUNGHO SONG
speakers.bio:
Youngho Song is the Data Engineering Lead at Yanolja Next, the technology
subsidiary of Yanolja, South Korea's leading travel-tech company. With more
than ten years of experience building large-scale data platforms, he leads
the group's data platform on Databricks, focused on connecting data across
the company's affiliates and establishing federated data governance.

His current focus is turning cross-affiliate data from siloed raw assets
into a trustworthy, discoverable resource that any business unit can build
on.

speakers.name: Youngjin Kim
speakers.bio:
Youngjin Kim is a prominent technology executive currently serving as the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of NOL Universe, the Consumer Platform Division of Yanolja, South Korea's leading travel-tech unicorn
. In this role, he spearheads the company's global data vision and the practical application of artificial intelligence across its leisure and travel platforms

sessions.title: The Titans of Trust: Powering the Open Security Ecosystem
sessions.body: As organizations transition from cloud-native to AI-native, the traditional boundaries of security have vanished. To defend at scale, security operations must be as interconnected as the systems they protect. Join industry leaders from Wiz, Palo Alto Networks, and CrowdStrike for a strategic dialogue on the convergence of data intelligence, AI, and collective defense.The discussion will dive into how visibility now spans from the infrastructure layer to the core of the AI model. We will explore how the Open Security Ecosystem creates a unified fabric for developing and deploying AI agents safely—allowing teams to neutralize complex attack paths that siloed tools miss.This session offers a rare look at how industry leaders are partnering to ensure that the velocity of AI innovation is matched by the resilience of its defense.

speakers.name: Jiong Liu
speakers.bio: Jiong Liu leads the product marketing team for Wiz and is responsible for product GTM strategy and cross-functional execution. She loves working closely with customers to securely accelerate their cloud and AI journeys. Before that, Jiong led the GTM strategy and product marketing team for Okta's customer identity products and Business Value practice. Jiong holds bachelor’s degrees in Economics and Interdisciplinary Studies from the University of California, Berkeley, and an MBA from the University of Pennsylvania, Wharton School.

sessions.title: The Trust Gap: Why Enterprise AI Fails Beyond the Prototype
sessions.body: AI has crossed a tipping point—what once lived in prototypes is now expected to power real business decisions. But as organizations push AI into production, a critical gap is emerging: what works in experimentation often fails under enterprise demands for trust, reliability, and accountability.In this talk, Uri Knorovich explores why today’s AI systems struggle to deliver consistent, trustworthy outcomes. While models have advanced rapidly, the external data layer they rely on remains fragmented, stale, and difficult to verify—leading to inaccurate outputs, rising costs, and limited confidence in production AI.Drawing on real-world examples across AI and enterprise infrastructure, Uri will examine why reasoning alone is insufficient without reliable, real-time data, the risks of black-box retrieval systems, and what enterprises must build to bridge the gap between AI experimentation and production-ready systems.

sessions.title: The Upcoming Apache Spark™ 4.2: The Next Chapter in Unified Analytics
sessions.body:
AI workloads demand real-time feature pipelines, multimodal data support, and seamless AI-assisted development. Apache Spark™ 4.2 brings these capabilities into the engine, unifying batch and streaming while optimizing them at the planner level.

 

Metric views provide a first-class semantic layer to define measures once and ensure consistent results. Catalog-managed flows make incremental and streaming queries lifecycle-aware catalog objects. A language-agnostic UDF protocol enables portable user logic across Python and emerging Spark Connect languages. Enhanced LLM discoverability and local performance improvements, including Arrow-backed caching and shuffle-free execution, make development faster and more interactive.

 

Apache Spark™ 4.2 evolves into a governed, incremental, and AI-native platform built for the demands of the AI age.

speakers.name: DB Tsai
speakers.bio: DB Tsai is an engineering leader at the Databricks Spark team. He is an Apache Spark Project Management Committee (PMC) Member and Committer, and he enjoys building teams with great cultures focusing on large scale distributed data infrastructure. Before his transition to a leadership role, he implemented several algorithms including Linear Regression and Binary/Multinomial Logistic Regression with Elastici-Net (L1/L2) regularization using LBFGS/OWL-QN optimizers in Apache Spark project.

speakers.name: Xiao Li
speakers.bio: Xiao Li is an Engineering Director at Databricks, an Apache Spark Committer, and a PMC member. He has a deep interest in Spark and database engines. Previously, he was an IBM Master Inventor and an expert in asynchronous database replication and consistency verification. Xiao earned his Ph.D. from the University of Florida in 2011.

sessions.title: The Write Way: Building Bi-Directional Data Pipelines in the Lakehouse
sessions.body:
Ever wondered how to bridge the gap between analytical data and operational workflows without breaking your lakehouse architecture? What if business users could edit data directly in a web app while maintaining a single source of truth? Traditional lakehouses excel at analytics but struggle with user-driven updates, often creating silos or complex workarounds.

 

There’s a better way—in this session we’ll cover a full writeback loop where lakehouse (Unity Catalog) syncs to PostgreSQL (Lakebase) for operational speed, a Databricks app offers an intuitive editing interface and Lakeflow jobs sync changes back every 5 minutes.

 

The lakehouse stays the source of truth while users get flexibility. We’ll explore scenarios including form-based data entry, table editing and data quality workflows, all built with Dash and Databricks Asset Bundles. By the end, you'll have a clear blueprint for building bi-directional data flows that empower users without sacrificing governance or reliability.

speakers.name: Falek Miah
speakers.bio:
Databricks Champion and Microsoft & Databricks certified consultant with over 15 years of experience in data, analytics, and Azure.

Specialises in designing and delivering end-to-end data platforms using Azure, Databricks, and the Power Platform, with a strong focus on automation, DevOps, and scalable analytics. Works closely with engineers and stakeholders to turn complex data problems into practical solutions.

An active member of the data community who enjoys sharing real-world lessons through talks, blogs and mentoring. Outside work, enjoys running, swimming, football, and learning new technologies.

sessions.title: Thinking Fast & Slow: How Databricks Built High-Speed and Deep Research Agents
sessions.body:
In today's competitive agentic search landscape, two operating modes are mission-critical. The first is a low-latency, low-cost mode for consumer-facing scale. It must meet strict tail-latency budgets for real-time, high-throughput use cases at minimal per-query cost, without sacrificing quality.

 

The second is a compute-intensive deep research mode enabling expert-level analysis—from financial due diligence and technology mapping to clinical review and manufacturing diagnostics. The system must plan multi-step retrieval, triangulate sources, and synthesize coherent answers.

 

Using our Instructed Retriever and Aroll frameworks, we built a unified agentic harness supporting both modes in a single architecture. Our system sits at the Pareto frontier of cost, speed, and quality. Instant mode delivers single-digit second latency maintaining accuracy, while Thinking mode achieves SoTA-level performance across enterprise domains.

sessions.title: Tips and Tricks for Postgres Observability at Scale
sessions.body: Running Postgres in production gets harder as your application grows — logs pile up, metrics live in one tool, schema changes live in another, and when something breaks, you are stuck stitching it all together under pressure. This session shares practical tips and tricks for getting ahead of common Postgres operational challenges — we will cover how to spot configuration issues before they hit production, how to unblock application updates when schema changes go sideways, and how to quickly connect application failures back to the database changes that caused them. Along the way, we will show how bringing Postgres operational data together with modern AI tooling can take a lot of the manual work out of diagnostics — so you spend less time hunting for root causes and more time shipping. Whether you are running a handful of Postgres instances or managing them at scale, you will leave with concrete techniques you can apply to your own environment.

sessions.title: Train and Fine-Tune AI Models Without Managing GPUs
sessions.body: "Training and fine-tuning AI models shouldn’t require becoming a GPU infrastructure expert. As enterprises scale AI beyond prototypes, managing clusters and distributed compute has become a major bottleneck.In this session, we’ll introduce AI Runtime, a new serverless GPU training experience on Databricks that provides on-demand NVIDIA A10 and H100 GPUs directly on Lakehouse data. You’ll see how teams can train and fine-tune LLMs, recommendation systems, forecasting models, and computer vision workloads without managing infrastructure.We’ll cover how AI Runtime combines optimized GPU compute and distributed training with native support for frameworks like PyTorch and Hugging Face, alongside MLflow, Unity Catalog, and Lakeflow to unify the full AI lifecycle.You’ll learn how to reduce infrastructure overhead, accelerate iteration cycles, and standardize end-to-end AI workflows from experimentation to production."

speakers.name: Brian Law
speakers.bio: Brian Law is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks with a specific focus on Machine Learning and Advanced Analytics. Previously, he was a Solutions Engineer at Cloudera and worked in industry as a Data Scientist on various use cases from Timeseries Forecasting through to NLP and Computer Vision

sessions.title: Transforming Data into Delivery: PostNL’s BDC Journey
sessions.body: PostNL is transforming how it uses data to drive operational efficiency, innovation, and better customer experiences across its logistics network. In this session, PostNL shares its journey with BDC, highlighting how a unified data platform enables faster insights, stronger collaboration between teams, and scalable AI initiatives. Learn how PostNL is building a future-ready data foundation that supports decision-making at the speed of delivery and unlocks new business value.

sessions.title: Transforming Governance Into a Scalable Data & AI Capability in the Data Mesh Era
sessions.body:
As enterprises scale AI and data products across domains, traditional governance models fail to keep pace. Historical approaches to data ownership no longer flex to meet data product demands. Domain autonomy creates inconsistency. AI amplifies risk. This presentation presents a scalable operating model that integrates data literacy, enterprise governance, governance engineering and domain enablement into a single cohesive approach built on the modern data platform. Using a federated data mesh architecture powered by Databricks, this modern approach to data ownership transforms governance from documentation and oversight into a programmable, platform-embedded enterprise capability.

 

The result:

  • Faster domain onboarding
  • Reduced regulatory risk
  • Automated policy enforcement
  • Measurable AI readiness

speakers.name: Sherri Adame
speakers.bio: Sherri is a dynamic data governance leader with a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale strategies that drive compliance, reduce costs, and accelerate data delivery. Currently in GM, Sherri is leading enterprise data governance transformation embedding data governance into engineering with proactive processes.  She worked in healthcare at Cigna, where they launched a metadata strategy cataloging over 25,000 attributes & implemented a reference data framework saving over $1M in 6 months. Sherri has lead development of personalized customer experiences for 100M+ users while meeting Health Data Interoperability standards. Sherri brings a pragmatic, results-driven approach to data strategy and governance.

sessions.title: Translating Nubank’s Data Lake Access Control Model Into Databricks Unity Catalog
sessions.body: Nubank implemented consistent, fine-grained access control across its multi-platform data environment by translating its internal data lake access control model into Databricks Unity Catalog permissions. This model uses centrally managed "Permission Groups" (based on geography, data domains and column sensitivity) to govern access to over 300K tables for 5K+ users, enforcing control at the table and column level. The presentation will detail the architectural implementation, the programmatic translation process using Unity Catalog APIs, and the application of read-time masking for sensitive columns. It will address practical challenges in modeling fine-grained permissions and operating at scale, providing attendees with a reusable architectural pattern and concrete lessons for designing scalable, enterprise-grade access control on Databricks.

speakers.name: Nikita Deshmukh
speakers.bio: I am a Staff Software Engineer on the Data Platform team, where I design and evolve the access control and governance architecture for the company’s Databricks-based analytics platform and AWS data lake. My work focuses on extending the Data Lake access control model for read and write permissions, enforcing column-level security and PII masking, and ensuring data subject rights deletion and broader data protection requirements are correctly implemented on the lake. I am particularly interested in pragmatic architectures that keep sensitive data safe without blocking real workloads. At the Data + AI Summit, i'll share hard-won lessons from building privacy-aware, access-controlled data lake platforms in a fast-moving fintech environment.

sessions.title: Travel & Hospitality: The Making of the Modern Hospitality Experience— Humans, Data, and the Age of Anticipation
sessions.body:
The best hospitality has always been about anticipation— knowing what a guest needs before they ask. AI is now making that possible at scale, but only when it's built on unified, governed data. With customer information still fragmented across legacy systems and siloed tools, most brands can't recognize the same traveler across channels, let alone act on real-time context. The brands pulling ahead are the ones turning data into a moat and AI into a co-pilot for every guest-facing and operational moment.

 

Hear from leading travel and hospitality brands on how they're doing exactly that with Databricks. You’ll leave with practical architectures for transforming fragmented data into anticipatory, human-centered experiences.

speakers.name: Charma Parker
speakers.bio: With over a decade of dynamic experience in the marketing industry, Charma Parker is a seasoned expert in crafting and executing high-impact email and mobile marketing strategies. She has driven innovative campaigns for leading brands across diverse sectors, including retail companies like Carter's & OshKosh B'Gosh and Home Depot, sports and entertainment organizations such as the Atlanta Hawks & State Farm Arena, and quick-service restaurant leader, Chick-fil-A. Charma brings a wealth of practical insights and a proven track record of engaging audiences and delivering measurable results.

speakers.name: Charuta Sathe
speakers.bio: As a Data Engineering Manager at United Airlines, I bring over 15 years of global experience modernizing data across the aviation industry. Following a decade in digital technology in the Middle East, I now focus on building the data products that elevate United's passenger experience and empower our frontline teams. As a passionate traveler and first-time speaker, I can't wait to connect with the data community.

speakers.name: Dan MacDonnell
speakers.job_title: Sr. Lead Tech Product Owner - MarTech
speakers.bio: A senior product and MarTech leader with a track record of driving enterprise-scale customer experience transformation. As a Senior Technical Lead Product Owner at Chick-fil-A Inc., Dan leads Customer360 and marketing technology capabilities unifying customer data to enable personalization, performance measurement, and scalable decisioning across all customer touch points. A robust background that spans Wall Street (Lehman), sports media (ESPN, NBA, NCAA) and enterprise innovation (Nationwide), equips Dan with a unique ability to align data, technology, and business strategy to deliver measurable customer experiences.

sessions.title: Tuesday Keynote
sessions.body: See the latest innovations from Databricks, live demos and unscripted conversations with the leaders shaping enterprise AI.

speakers.name: Ali Ghodsi
speakers.bio: Ali is the CEO and co–founder of Databricks, responsible for the growth and international​ ​expansion of the company. He previously served as the VP of Engineering and Product​ ​Management before taking the role of CEO in January 2016. In addition to his work at Databricks, Ali serves as an adjunct professor at UC Berkeley and is on the board at UC Berkeley’s RiseLab. Ali was one of the creators of open source project, Apache Spark, and ideas from his academic research in the areas of resource management and scheduling and data caching have been applied to Apache Mesos​ ​and Apache Hadoop.​ ​​Ali​ ​received his MBA from Mid-Sweden University in 2003 and PhD from KTH/Royal Institute of Technology in Sweden​ in 2006​ in the area of​ ​Distributed Computing.

speakers.name: Greg Brockman
speakers.bio: Greg Brockman is the Co-Founder and President of OpenAI, a research and deployment company whose mission is to ensure artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

sessions.title: Turning Data into Better Banking: How NAB Uses Databricks and Genie to Deliver Customer Value
sessions.body: At NAB, better banking starts with seeing our customers clearly. Fragmented data environments had long made it difficult to build a focussed, timely view of customer needs, slowing decision‑making and limiting the value we could return to customers. In this session, we’ll share how NAB is using Databricks to bring customer data together into a unified, trusted platform and how Genie is making those insights accessible across the bank. By enriching transactional data and making it accessible in reusable, product‑ready datasets, our teams can spot customer needs faster, design more relevant experiences, and respond with greater consistency across channels.You’ll hear how this shift is helping NAB move from isolated insights to shared customer signals, supporting everything from day‑to‑day service improvements to more personalised products and smarter risk decisions. Join us to explore how a modern data platform is enabling NAB to deliver simpler, more responsive banking, and what this approach could mean for the future of customer‑centred financial services.

sessions.title: Turning Data Requests Into Self-Service: Building an AI-Powered Analytics Product Users Love
sessions.body:
Ticketmaster's operations team was drowning in data requests. Every "how many fans showed up to buy tickets last week?" question cost engineering hours. We were spending over 8 weeks/year being human query engines. We needed to give users the power to answer their own questions.We built OMT Wizard: a conversational analytics tool that lets non-technical users ask questions in plain English and get instant answers. Powered by Databricks Genie, it launched to 500+ users and achieved high stickiness. The users who try it keep coming back.

 

This session shares product lessons from building AI-powered internal tools — how we identified the right problem to solve, designed for trust and transparency, trained the AI on business logic, measured real adoption and turned skeptics into champions. You'll learn what worked — suggested questions, showing your work — what didn't — hiding complexity — and how to build AI products that solve real problems instead of looking for problems to solve.

speakers.name: Brian Muehlenkamp
speakers.bio: Brian Muehlenkamp is a Product Manager at Ticketmaster, where he leads the Onsale Management Technology platform serving 400+ operators through high-demand onsales. He works AI-native — using and evaluating new tools continuously and letting that practice reshape how he discovers, designs, and ships. Energized by the craft of product management and motivated by a futurist view of where the discipline is headed, Brian has delivered a portfolio of cutting-edge, high-impact products that have moved the business forward.

sessions.title: UC Managed Tables: What's New and How to Decide, Adopt, and Scale
sessions.body:
UC managed tables built on Delta and Iceberg table formats deliver faster query performance, lower storage costs, and automatic optimizations out of the box — and they've improved significantly in the last year. This session covers what's new, what UC managed tables unlock, and what you need to know to make an informed decision.

 

We'll walk through the latest capabilities now available on UC managed tables. Highlights include Catalog Commits that enable writes from external engines and multi-statement transactions, Managed Disaster Recovery, Automatic Upgrades, Auto-TTL, Auto Indexing, Automatic Liquid Clustering and Predictive Optimization which can increase query speeds by 20x and reduce storage costs by 50%.

 

From there, we'll address the questions we hear most and share best practices. How can I easily convert to managed tables if I access my external tables today by path? How can I segregate my data? How can I access these tables externally? You'll leave with a clear understanding of what UC managed tables offer today, what's changed, and a framework for deciding when and how to adopt them.

speakers.name: Elizabeth Bowman
speakers.bio: Elizabeth Bowman is a Product Manager at Databricks, where she leads initiatives in data governance and platform architecture, focusing on Unity Catalog and managed tables. With a background in mechanical engineering and early career experience in surgical robotics, Elizabeth brings a systems-oriented perspective to solving complex data problems. Prior to joining Databricks, she built enterprise AI applications at C3.AI. Elizabeth holds an MS/MBA in engineering and business, and is passionate about making sophisticated data platforms easier to use. At Databricks, her work on Unity Catalog managed tables helps customers reduce storage costs and improve query performance—bringing tangible efficiency gains to customers' data architectures.

speakers.name: Naga Raju Bhanoori
speakers.bio: Naga Raju Bhanoori is a Staff Software Engineer at Databricks. He works on Predictive Optimization and enhancing the out-of-the-box performance of Managed Tables.

sessions.title: Ultra Low Latency Streaming for Real-Time Feature Engineering
sessions.body: Feature freshness is critical for fraud-detection, ad tech, real-time recommendations, dynamic pricing, etc. Historically, ML engineers have had to maintain two separate systems for feature engineering, leveraging Spark and Spark Structure Streaming for batch/near real-time features, while building bespoke pipelines when they needed sub-second feature freshness. In this session, we'll learn about Real-Time Mode in Apache Spark Structured Streaming, the engine behind the Databricks Feature Store, and how companies like DraftKings are using it to power real-time features with millisecond-level freshness. You'll learn how to pair Real-Time Mode with Lakebase to build a state-of-the-art online feature store and leave with a practical blueprint for a unified feature engineering platform that eliminates logic spread across different systems and shifts the focus from infrastructure orchestration to semantic feature modeling.

speakers.name: Abhay Bothra
speakers.bio: Abhay leads real-time streaming and feature engineering at Databricks. Prior to joining Databricks, he was the founder and CTO of Fennel AI and has spent almost 15 years building systems at scale.

speakers.name: Jerry Peng
speakers.bio: Jerry Peng is currently an Staff Software Engineer at Databricks extensively working Apache Spark Structured Streaming. Before joining Databricks, he was a Principal Software Engineer at Splunk working on streaming and messaging projects especially with Apache Pulsar and Apache Flink. Jerry is a committer and PMC member of Apache Pulsar, Apache Storm, and Apache Heron projects. Before Splunk, he worked at Streamlio (acquired by Splunk), Citadel, and Yahoo on distributed systems and stream processing. Jerry has been working in the area of distributed systems and stream processing since his days in grad school at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.

sessions.title: Under the Hood: Scalable Ingestion Strategies for Databases, Applications, and File Sources
sessions.body:
Data engineers spend far too much time maintaining fragile scripts for a fragmented landscape of databases, applications, and file sources. In this technical session, we’ll explore how Lakeflow Connect allows you to build robust pipelines without the operational burden of DIY infrastructure.

 

We’ll dive into:

  • Database ingestion: A look under the hood at efficient CDC for sources like Oracle, MySQL, and Postgres, alongside query-based ingestion for sources like Teradata, Redshift, and Synapse.
  • Application and file ingestion: What’s new—and happening behind the scenes—across our newest connectors for customer 360, employee 360, financial analytics, and more.
  • Cost and performance optimization: Technical best practices for networking, security, and minimizing impact on source systems—plus how to use new features to slash TCO and boost performance.

 

We’ll wrap up with how to create your own application and database connectors. Stop managing infrastructure and start delivering data.

speakers.name: Peter Pogorski
speakers.bio: Peter is a Staff Product Manager, focused on data ingestion.

speakers.name: Sonia Bendre
speakers.bio: Sonia is an Associate Product Manager for Lakeflow Connect.

sessions.title: Underwriting the Future: How Leading Insurers Turn Proprietary Data into Competitive Advantage with Databricks
sessions.body:
Insurers today are caught between rising claims complexity, evolving risks, and policyholders who expect more— faster. The carriers pulling ahead aren't just building better models. They're winning on data: who owns it, who can access it, and how quickly they can act on it.

 

In this session, you'll see how leading insurers use Databricks to break down data silos, operationalize AI at scale, and put natural language insights directly in the hands of underwriters, claims teams, and distributors— turning data strategy into smarter risk selection, faster settlements, and profitable growth that compounds.

speakers.name: Elizabeth Barth-Thacker
speakers.bio: Dr. Elizabeth Barth-Thacker is Vice President and Head of Enterprise Data & Analytics at American Modern Insurance Group, part of Munich Re. She leads enterprise data strategy, AI and data governance, analytics enablement, and cloud data transformation initiatives across the organization. Since joining American Modern in 2021, she has helped modernize the company’s data ecosystem and scale AI-ready analytics capabilities that drive faster, smarter business decisions. Elizabeth brings executive leadership experience across insurance, healthcare, operations, technology, and analytics, with a focus on enterprise transformation and data-driven leadership. She holds a Doctorate, and graduate degrees in AI, Business, Technology & Cybersecurity.

sessions.title: Unified Governance for Enterprise Analytics and AI
sessions.body:
We implemented a unified governance architecture for enterprise analytics leveraging Databricks Unity Catalog as the authoritative control plane. The platform designed with a configuration-driven, dynamic attribute-based access control (ABAC) model with fully enforced row-level security (RLS) and column-level security (CLS) ensuring precise, policy-driven data access across the organization — including hierarchical visibility for cost owners and business leaders aligned to their reporting structures. This design prevents governance drift, reduces operational complexity, centralizes policy management, and enables secure self-service analytics across domains. Governance policies extend natively to AI/BI dashboards and Databricks Genie, ensuring consistent, compliant data access without duplicating or redefining security frameworks.

 

Impact

  • Eliminated decentralized access control models across 40+ dashboards.
  • Enabled secure self-service analytics for 300+ users across 20+ teams.

speakers.name: Anand Tirthgirikar
speakers.bio: Anand Tirthgirikar is a Staff Engineer at InMobi, where he leads large-scale data platform and governance initiatives powering enterprise analytics and AI workloads. He has driven multiple platform modernization efforts across open lakehouse architectures, data governance, cost optimization, observability, and self-serve analytics. Anand works at the intersection of distributed systems, metadata platforms, query engines, and AI-enabled data experiences, with a strong focus on building scalable and developer-friendly platforms. He is passionate about solving complex data infrastructure challenges and enabling organizations to build governed, efficient, and future-ready data ecosystems.

sessions.title: Unified SRE Observability: How Workday Democratizes Multi-Platform Insights With Databricks AI/BI Genie
sessions.body: As Workday’s infrastructure scaled across multi-cloud environments, the Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams faced a common hurdle: fragmented data silos. Monitoring reliability across Databricks, Snowflake, ServiceNow and FiveTran required pivoting between tools, leading to delayed insights and manual reporting toil. To solve this, Workday built a unified cross-platform KPI dashboard on Databricks, centralizing telemetry into a single pane of glass for platform adoption, job performance and ITSM health. This session explores the architecture behind this “one-stop shop” — leveraging third-party integrations for seamless ingestion and the power of Databricks AI/BI Genie. By embedding conversational AI into the SRE workflow, Workday enables stakeholders to “talk to their data” — getting instant, natural-language answers without SQL. Learn how this shift from static charts to AI-driven insights has accelerated incident response, improved governance and freed SREs to focus on engineering

speakers.name: Aniruddha Vishnupurikar
speakers.bio: Aniruddha Vishnupurikar is a seasoned technical leader with over 20 years of experience in data and software engineering. He currently serves as the Director of AI Platforms and SRE at Workday, where he oversees the AI Platforms and Operations while utilizing AI/ML technologies to drive operational success. Throughout his career, Aniruddha has specialized in designing and managing massive-scale cloud ecosystems and data frameworks. His previous engineering leadership roles include directing large-scale infrastructure at ThoughtSpot , managing workflow orchestration systems and metrics at Twitter , and developing core petabyte-scale data warehousing infrastructure at Amazon.

sessions.title: Unify Your Data + AI Ecosystem via Databricks Marketplace
sessions.body: The average enterprise depends on dozens of third-party data and AI providers. Yet discovering, evaluating, and operationalizing those products remains fragmented, slow, and siloed. In this lightning talk, we'll explore how Databricks Marketplace is becoming the central hub for organizations to discover, access, and manage third-party data, apps, and AI models. Whether you're a data leader looking to streamline your vendor ecosystem or a provider looking to grow your reach, this session covers the vision and roadmap.You'll learn:How Marketplace simplifies discovery and access to third-party data and AI productsStrategies for reducing procurement friction and accelerating time to valueHow providers can expand distribution by meeting customers where they work

sessions.title: Unifying Upstream Intelligence with Generative AI
sessions.body: PetroWizard & IntelliSense utilizes an agent-based generative AI architecture on Databricks to address PETRONAS's challenge of fragmented, largely unstructured upstream data (90% unstructured, across OSDU, PI, SQL, etc.). Engineers previously spent 3–5 days locating data. This solution, featuring a Central Orchestrator and four specialized agents (Subsurface, Surface, Sensor, Model Router), enables cross-domain reasoning and model-agnostic, governed data intelligence. Outcomes include reducing data discovery time to 30–45 seconds, achieving 90%+ query accuracy, high user satisfaction (4/5 across 3,000+ users) and full audit traceability, fundamentally transforming upstream decision-making.

speakers.name: Prashant Singh
speakers.bio: Prashant Singh is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks with 10+ years of experience in Data & AI. He specializes in Lakehouse architecture, AI-driven applications, and enterprise data strategy, working with organizations across Southeast Asia to build scalable and impactful data platforms.

sessions.title: Unity AI Gateway: How to Govern Multi-AI Access Across Your Company
sessions.body: As coding agents like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code become embedded in daily development workflows, enterprises face a new challenge: how to govern and audit AI-assisted code generation at scale. Without centralized visibility, organizations risk exposing sensitive data, losing track of usage, and failing to meet security and compliance requirements.In this session, we'll show how Databricks enables end-to-end governance for coding agents across the enterprise. You'll learn how to enforce fine-grained permissions, track usage and costs across teams, and capture complete audit trails of prompts, responses, and tool interactions. We'll also cover how to apply consistent policies across providers — so developers can move fast with coding agents while maintaining the control, visibility, and compliance production environments demand.You'll walk away with the patterns to unlock coding agents safely across your organization — without creating a new compliance liability.

speakers.name: Ahmed Bilal
speakers.bio: Bilal is a product manager on the Mosaic AI team at Databricks, where he leads efforts to scale real-time and batch model serving for both traditional ML and GenAI workloads. Prior to Databricks, he worked at GitHub and Microsoft, building developer tools. Bilal holds an MS and an MBA from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

sessions.title: Unity Catalog 101: Unified Governance for data, AI and applications
sessions.body:
As organizations build AI-powered applications and autonomous agents, governance becomes more complex. Data, models and tools must be discovered, understood and securely accessed across teams, platforms and engines, yet governance is often fragmented across catalogs, security systems and AI tooling.

 

Unity Catalog is the unified governance solution for all AI agents, applications and data on the Databricks Platform. It enables organizations to discover trusted data with shared business context, apply consistent governance policies across data and AI assets and automate governance workflows using built-in intelligence, all while governing open data formats and assets across clouds and platforms.

 

In this introductory session, we’ll walk through how Unity Catalog works and how it enables three foundational capabilities: discovery with business context, unified AI governance and AI-powered automation. You’ll learn how organizations use Unity Catalog to simplify governance, reduce data and AI sprawl and build trusted AI systems on an open and governed data foundation.

speakers.name: Murt Neemuchwala
speakers.bio: Murt is a product manager on the Unity Catalog team at Databricks. At the Data + AI Summit, he'd love to talk with you about data and AI governance!

sessions.title: Unity Catalog: Advanced Field-Proven Patterns from the Experts
sessions.body: Join us for a real-world exploration of Databricks Unity Catalog designed for data leaders scaling their platforms. We will tackle the challenge of governance at scale, demonstrating how to balance centralized management with decentralized, domain-driven operating models. Learn field-tested strategies for catalog organization that establish structured guardrails. These patterns will allow your teams to innovate rapidly without traditional bottlenecks. We will also cover how to accelerate metadata curation to empower true data discovery and a frictionless self-service experience. Leave with flexible best practices for cross-boundary collaboration, secure data sharing, and AI readiness that adapt to your organization's unique architectural needs.

speakers.name: Jyotsna Bharadwaj
speakers.bio:
I am a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks . I Help Architect and Build Innovative Data and AI solutions for Enterprise Customers
Prior:
25+ years in the software industry
Have successfully spearheaded numerous complex global IT programs
Nokia , Ericsson , Wipro , Tata Consultancy Services

Education:
Masters in CS (Machine Learning), Georgia Institute of Technology
Bachelors in Electrical Engineering

speakers.name: Pamela Pettit
speakers.bio: Pamela is a Senior Solution Architect at Databricks.

sessions.title: Unlock business value with Databricks leveraging GenAI, ML and Genie
sessions.body: Great Southern Bank (GSB) has successfully migrated from SAS to Databricks—unlocking higher model accuracy, faster insights, and the ability to democratise data at scale using Genie and AI/BI. Importantly, GSB achieved this with a much smaller team than the major banks, demonstrating practical expertise and delivery experience that other organisations can learn from. To date, GSB has migrated and integrated 85% of its enterprise data onto the Databricks platform and is on track to shut down its legacy warehouse by 2026. Databricks AI capabilities are already delivering material value across traditional ML and gen AI use cases— e.g. a home-loan churn model was built by a single employee in three months and matched the accuracy of a 3rd party model. On top of the enterprise data foundation, Genie Spaces now enable business users to self-serve insights faster and with improved accuracy. GSB is also accelerating value creation in areas such as complaints analysis and sentiment using GenAI.

speakers.name: Matt Cammack
speakers.job_title: Head of Customer Technology Data and AI

sessions.title: Unlock radical speed-to-market with agentic execution powered by Celonis Process Intelligence
sessions.body: Companies struggle to keep pace with shifting consumer demand and strict regulatory mandates because their go-to-market process is bogged down by isolated processes, disparate data, and limited visibility. This lack of transparency across R&D, sourcing, manufacturing, sales, and distribution leads to missed seasonal windows and penalties, putting millions in revenue at risk. The Celonis Process Intelligence Graph acts as a "Living Digital Twin" to fuel Databricks AI Agents, providing the company-specific context they need to operate autonomously and orchestrate the end-to-end product development and launch journey. By agentifying the go-to-market process, organizations are replacing fragmented manual coordination with autonomous execution to achieve radical speed-to-market without sacrificing quality or compliance. A global consumer leader leveraged Celonis to accelerate time-to-market by 17 weeks, save 2,000 hours in manual work per year, and reduce the risk of revenue loss by $50M.

sessions.title: Unlocking Antibody Space With Databricks Vector Search
sessions.body: Antibodies form the bedrock of human health, and the body’s ability to create what is estimated to be a quintillion unique variants creates an impressive scaling issue for their study. Molecules derived from antibodies are now the fastest growing therapeutic category, and our understanding of how to design and modify antibodies requires solutions that scale. Databricks Vector Search provides an engineered solution for scaling up similarity search to 1 billion embeddings per endpoint, and by embedding antibody sequences with the protein language model AMPLIFY we will describe how this system might be used with the Observed Antibody Space dataset. The potential throughput of this system, at ~30 queries returned per second, would demonstrate state-of-the-art search. Using this scalable approach, we would then be positioned to explore advantages that this embedded representation affords for metadata lookup and statistical analysis.

speakers.name: Peter Hawkins
speakers.bio: Peter Hawkins, PhD, is a Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks, focusing on applying machine learning at scale to accelerate drug discovery in the life sciences. He began his academic career researching ultrafast quantum optics before becoming deeply interested in machine learning and its application to biology. He spent four years as a Principal Scientist at Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, where he led a small research team focussing on machine learning models for immune receptors. He earned his MSci (2012) and PhD (2016) from Imperial College London, performed postdoctoral research at the University of Marburg and led an ML research group at Regeneron Pharmaceuticals before joining Databricks in 2024.

speakers.name: Robert Vernon
speakers.bio: Robert Vernon, PhD, has a career focus on the study of protein sequence to function relationships including protein design, structure prediction, and the protein folding problem. He completed his PhD under David Baker at the University of Washington, did his post-doctoral work on intrinsically disordered proteins under Julie Forman-Kay at the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto, and is currently the Director of Therapeutic Protein Design at Amgen.

sessions.title: Unlocking Cross-Engine Governance With Scan APIs
sessions.body:
While companies have embraced the data lakehouse architecture and benefits it provides, maintaining data governance has become a much more complicated story.

 

Many companies today implement cumbersome workarounds, such as processing and maintaining multiple copies of datasets, duplicating access policies in different systems, or worse bypassing access controls altogether.

 

In this talk, we'll explore some of the current problems with data governance and the data lakehouse architecture and how Scan APIs can address some of those challenges.

sessions.title: Unlocking Video Data at Scale: VLM Batch Inference with Ray on Databricks
sessions.body: Organisations sit on vast video archives (surveillance, manufacturing, inspections), yet lack scalable methods to extract insights. This session presents a production-ready architecture for distributed video analytics using Vision Language Models (VLMs) on Databricks.We'll walk through a three-stage accelerator: (1) video ingestion into Unity Catalog Volumes, (2) VLM registration with MLflow for reproducibility, and (3) distributed batch inference using Ray and VLLM with Qwen2.5-VL-32B. You'll see how Ray orchestrates GPU-accelerated inference across video datasets and how to extract structured entities from VLM outputs using Databricks AI Functions.Attendees will leave with:A reusable pattern for multi-modal video intelligence at scaleWorking code integrating Ray, VLLM, and Unity CatalogPrompt engineering techniques for video inputsCost and performance considerations for VLM workloadsWhether your use case is retail, manufacturing, or public safety—this pattern applies.

speakers.name: Samantha Wise
speakers.bio: Samantha Wise is a Senior Specialist Solutions Engineer in AI/ML at Databricks, where she helps regulated enterprises take advanced AI from prototype to production, including vision-language batch inference, agentic systems, and forecasting at scale. With an MSc in Mathematics from the University of Bristol, she began her career as a data scientist at an asset management firm, contributing to the Coronavirus Research Taskforce, before moving into Generative AI at a marketing-tech startup. Samantha is passionate about leveraging data and AI to solve real-world problems that matter and about coaching the next generation of practitioners along the way.

sessions.title: Using AI to Migrate Semantic Models and Dashboards to Databricks Metric Views and AI/BI
sessions.body:
At HP, we are working to integrate more of our business intelligence and analytics directly into the Databricks platform. To minimize impacts on analytics teams and their partners across organizations, we needed a way to automate and accelerate migrations of legacy semantic models and dashboards into Databricks.

 

We developed a scalable AI based approach to parse existing BI artifacts, translate semantic models into Metric Views, convert existing visualizations into Databricks Dashboards and validate the results. This presentation shares lessons learned across multiple migrations, including both our key challenges and successes.

speakers.name: jeff.mabeck jeff.mabeck
speakers.bio: Jeff Mabeck is principal analytics architect at HP Inc., focused on large scale analytics platform strategy, data architecture, and modernization. His work spans data lake and BI platform convergence, standardization of analytics and governance patterns, and the design of scalable, privacy-aware data products and BI solutions. He collaborates closely with engineering, product, and privacy stakeholders to translate complex data into actionable insights that inform decision making and improve customer experiences.

speakers.name: Utkarsh Siddu
speakers.bio:
A Principal Architect with over 11 years of experience advancing AI/ML from research to large-scale production, he has built and scaled intelligent systems across printing, additive manufacturing, and enterprise data platforms. His journey spans deep learning–based computer vision, real-time quality inspection systems, and distributed model training, to leading GenAI strategy, LLM Agents & agent frameworks, and knowledge platforms in production environments.
He owns multi-quarter AI roadmaps and reference architectures, driving governance, reliability, and cost-performance rigor while building strong executive alignment. A multi-time summit presenter, patent holder, and recipient of the HP Amaze Award (top 1%), he is recognized for transforming complex AI innovation into secure, observable, and measurable business impact.

sessions.title: Using Genie to Speed Traditional Machine Learning Tasks
sessions.body: Machine learning on Databricks is becoming accessible to every role — from business analysts who have never written code to seasoned data scientists building production pipelines. This session introduces two complementary capabilities that democratize both the consumption and authoring of ML workloads.Genie for ML brings predictions directly to non-technical users. The agent understands user intent, recognizes when a question calls for ML — forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, regression — and delegates to optimized SQL ML functions behind the scenes. No Python, no notebooks, no training. Genie Code for ML targets the other side: technical users building those workflows, acting as an expert ML copilot that guides even junior data scientists through complex end-to-end ML journeys.Walk away with the patterns to make ML accessible across your organization — without sacrificing the depth experts need.

sessions.title: Vendor Sprawl to Lakeflow: Scaling a Governed, Multi-Tenant Platform in Financial Services
sessions.body: Highly regulated organizations struggle to balance data democratization with governance, operational overhead, and tool sprawl. In this session, we share how we scaled a Databricks-centered platform using a governed multi-tenant model that separates interactive self-service analytics from production-grade data services. We outline the architecture and operating patterns that enabled growth—governance, tenancy, and automated deployments—and how we implemented Lakeflow, including Lakeflow Connect, to standardize ingestion and consolidate third-party tools into Databricks-native services. Attendees will gain practical strategies to define workload boundaries, enable repeatable low-risk deployments, operationalize ingestion as a product, and execute phased consolidation with measurable outcomes.

sessions.title: Versionless and Environments for Notebooks, Jobs, Pipelines: Safe DBR Upgrades and Cached Packages
sessions.body: On classic compute, upgrading a DBR version and stitching together cluster libraries, init scripts, and Spark configs consumes a meaningful share of a platform team's time, and every upgrade risks breaking production pipelines. Serverless eliminates both with versionless runtime and Databricks' Environment model.This session covers the two pieces that make versionless trustworthy at enterprise scale. Lakehouse Replay continuously replays a representative sample of real production workloads to validate Databricks Runtime changes before they ship, catching regressions with zero customer effort. Environments deliver a unified, portable dependency strategy with faster startup, tighter governance, and clearer observability for Notebooks, Jobs, and Pipelines.Attendees leave with a clear picture of how versionless and environments fit together and how to plan their move off manual DBR upgrades.

speakers.name: Justin Breese
speakers.bio:
Justin is a Staff Product Manager at Databricks. He primarily focuses on their serverless products - versionless runtime, dependency management (environments), and containers.

When not thinking about execution engines, you can find him staying busy with soccer, hiking, brewing beer, roasting coffee, and older cars.

Justin lives in Topanga, CA with his wife, son, and daughter.

sessions.title: Vibe Coding on Databricks
sessions.body:
This hands-on course introduces Databricks Apps, a feature that empowers developers to build and deploy secure data and AI applications directly on the Databricks platform. It is designed for data scientists, data engineers, and developers who want to rapidly create and deliver applications that make data insights accessible to non-technical users across their organizations.

The course begins with an overview of the core components, architecture, and constraints of Databricks Apps, along with common use cases and how they compare to traditional web app deployment. You will deploy a simple app using built-in templates, then iteratively enhance it—both through structured development workflows and emerging “vibe coding” techniques—to quickly prototype and refine functionality. You will build and deploy a data-driven application that integrates with key platform features, including SQL warehouses and AI model serving endpoints. You will also learn how to develop and manage apps using both UI-based workflows and a local IDE, applying best practices for configuration, authentication, and environment management.

The course concludes with a focus on enterprise readiness, including observability, error handling, security architecture, and governance, where you will implement logging, troubleshoot real-world issues, and apply best practices for permissions, auditing, and secure application design.Note: Hands-on training courses will be updated to reflect the newest product and feature announcements from Data + AI Summit in June 2026.

sessions.title: Vibe Investigating with Lakewatch and Genie
sessions.body: For decades, security investigations have required equal parts query-language incantations, instinct, and raw persistence. Lakewatch and Genie use AI to change the game, allowing analysts to investigate by simply asking questions in natural language, extracting patterns, pivoting, and getting results fast. In this session, we'll demonstrate "vibe investigating" using Genie against real-world security datasets. We'll uncover multi-stage attacks including prompt injection, credential theft, C2 beaconing, lateral movement, and a few more surprises! We'll show the full investigation arc — establishing baselines, detecting anomalies, pivoting across data sources, and building attack timelines. No query languages — just questions, answers, and a faster path to results. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for using Lakewatch Genie, crafting effective investigation prompts and supercharging their security investigations.

sessions.title: Vibe Your Data Model, Supercharge Your Genie
sessions.body: Nobody loves data modeling. It takes weeks, requires dozens of meetings, and by the time you ship a schema the business has already changed. But skip the model and your Genie Spaces pay the price: wasted tokens on join definitions, ambiguous metrics, and answers you can't trust. In this session we show you how to break out of that trap. We introduce Vibe Data Modeling, where AI agents generate complete, validated business data models from a plain English description of your organization and iterate on them in minutes, not months. Then we connect the dots to Genie: a solid data model paired with Metric Views eliminates the token tax, letting Genie focus on understanding your questions instead of navigating your schema. The result is a Genie that is cheaper, faster, and dramatically more accurate. We will walk through a real customer engagement that produced a 679-table enterprise model across 21 domains in days and show how it feeds directly into Genie Spaces that actually deliver.

speakers.name: Cary Moore
speakers.bio: Cary Moore is a Senior Solutions Architect with Databricks and supports federal healthcare customers like the VA, DHA and CMS.  Cary has spent his career implementing Data Warehouses using both traditional ETL and On Prem relational databases as well as several now in the cloud.  Cary assisted the Department of Veterans affairs successfully implement their Lakehouse using Azure Databricks and Delta.

speakers.name: Roberto Bruno Martins
speakers.bio: Roberto Bruno Martins is a Senior Solutions Architect at Databricks with 30+ years in data, spanning engineering, analytics, architecture, and AI. He advises enterprises on modern data and AI platforms, with a focus on governance, Lakehouse architectures, ML/GenAI adoption, and translating technology into measurable business outcomes. Roberto is known for pragmatic approaches to complex problems, balancing technical depth with organizational realities. His interests include data governance, semantic layers, enterprise AI, and how organizations adapt operating models, products, and decision making in the age of AI.

sessions.title: Virtual Delta Tables: Building a Multimodal Lakehouse
sessions.body:
Managing multimodal inference is one of the defining challenges facing AI teams. LLMs now consider documents, images, and videos, producing higher quality results and reducing time wasted with data prep. The lakehouse architecture solves part of the problem but many teams are struggling to incorporate an increasing variety of data into their workflow. Rather than ingesting, re-encoding, or modifying massive troves of existing data, multimodal teams are looking to work with original artifacts.

 

This talk introduces Virtual Delta Tables and the associated open source code designed for multimodal inference. Virtual Delta Tables incorporate original data from different sources into a singular logical structure for ease of use by data scientists and ML engineers. By offering a Delta Lake interface the entire ecosystem from Databricks to DuckDB can be used in multimodal work. We'll highlight just how far you can push the lakehouse architecture in the rapidly changing AI data landscape!

speakers.name: Tyler Croy
speakers.bio: At Scribd Tyler created the delta-rs project and has presented a number of times on Scribd's large scale data and ML workloads combining Rust, Delta Lake, and the Databricks platform. He has written extensively on using Delta Lake from Python and Rust, joining the talented authors of the award-winning #1 best selling book "Delta Lake: The Definitive Guide", by contributing Chapter 6.  Tyler is also a Databricks MVP and a generally tall guy.

sessions.title: Weaving Data Into the Financial Fabric: How Nasdaq Uses Databricks to Power the Innovation Economy
sessions.body:
Nasdaq is the trusted fabric of the world’s financial system, and data is at the heart of everything we do. Learn how we’re using Databricks to drive insights, support decision-making and deliver industry-leading financial solutions. Using Delta Lake’s open formats and Unity Catalog, we’ve consolidated disparate data stores into a unified corporate data lakehouse to create a single source of truth for enterprise data. We’ll demo how we’re using AgentBricks and Databricks Apps to democratize access to data while maintaining oversight and governance.

 

You’ll also discover how our Capital Access Platforms division has built its core data platform on Databricks. With exchange and index data, alternative datasets and institutional data for more than 110,000 public and private‑market strategies and funds covering over $90 trillion in institutional assets, the platform enables rapid product development, creates value from our data assets and forms the foundation of our AI strategy.

speakers.name: Angie ruan
speakers.bio:
Angie Ruan is the Divisional CTO for Nasdaq Capital Access Platforms. She is responsible for overseeing the division’s technology strategy, including engineering across Listings, Index, Data, Analytics, Investor Relations, and Governance Solutions. She rejoined Nasdaq after serving as SVP at Chime. Prior to Chime, Angie was SVP of Global Technology at Nasdaq, overseeing key Market Technology engineering.
Angie has a strong track record of leading business transformations across American Express, PayPal, and eBay. She holds four technical patents, a Master of Science in Computer Science from UC Santa Barbara, and studied undergraduate in Computer Science at Tsinghua University of China.

sessions.title: Wednesday Keynote
sessions.body: Be first to witness the latest breakthroughs from Databricks and share the success of innovative data and AI companies.

sessions.title: Welcome Reception
sessions.body: Join us at our Welcome Reception at the Expo to socialize with your fellow data professionals while enjoying food and drinks.

sessions.title: What is Databricks Apps?
sessions.body: Databricks Apps is the fastest way to build, deploy, and govern production-grade applications directly on the Databricks Platform. In this foundational session, we’ll explore how Databricks Apps allows you to transform your data and AI/ML models into interactive, custom applications that your entire enterprise can use. Whether you are building AI-powered agents, real-time dashboards, or internal tools for business process automation, discover how we’ve simplified application development on Databricks.

sessions.title: What Worked, What Didn’t: Virgin Atlantic’s Flight to Trusted Generative BI
sessions.body:
As decision-making at Virgin Atlantic sped up, our BI stack creaked. Leaders wanted answers in hours and questions increasingly cut across commercial, operational, and customer data. Like many teams, we turned to GenBI to close that gap.

 

Our first attempt didn’t go well. Answers arrived faster, but confidence dropped. Without shared metric definitions, visible lineage, or governance designed in from the start, ambiguity scaled faster than trust. “Is this right?” became the default question again.

 

In this session, we share how we rebuilt GenBI on trusted foundations using Databricks. We’ll show how Unity Catalog and UC Metrics Views anchor AI answers to signed-off metrics, how Databricks Genie enables users to interrogate and explain results, and why explainability became part of the user experience.

 

Attendees will leave with practical lessons for moving to decision-grade GenBI, drawn from real production use cases and delivered as a visual, story-led case study.

speakers.name: Tom Barber
speakers.bio: With over 13 years of experience in data & analytics within the aviation industry working for two of the UK's most well-known airlines, Tom has led the development of data products, data platforms, analytics environments and evolved the airline's data governance and its data culture. Tom's latest focus has been in the world of Customer Analytics and the platforms that fuel them to unlock value for both the airline and the experience of its customers. Tom is lives on the South Coast of the UK and loves jumping on (and out of) planes in his spare time, he is also a DJ in his spare time!

sessions.title: What’s New for FinOps on Databricks
sessions.body:
As your Databricks adoption scales, FinOps teams need full visibility that connects performance, usage, and spend, and tools that turn insight into action.

 

In this session, we’ll show how to operationalize FinOps on Databricks . You’ll see how to enrich workloads with tags, explore cost and performance through dashboards and Genie, and implement proactive alerting across compute types. We’ll also unveil new FinOps-focused features & tools that your team will want to be aware of.

speakers.name: Sadhana Bala
speakers.bio: Sadhana is a Product Manager at Databricks, focused on cost observability & management across the platform. She holds a Bachelors in Applied Mathematics from Brown University, and a MBA from Harvard.

speakers.name: Youssef Mrini
speakers.bio: Youssef Mrini is part of the pre-sales team in the EMEA Region at Databricks and helps customers to adopt the databricks technologies. Youssef is an ex-data engineer. He holds a degree in big Data and have been working on various areas for the last couple of years
