sessions.title: What’s New in Apache Spark™ 4.1?
sessions.body: Explore the exciting new features of Apache Spark 4.1 with major new capabilities for both data engineering and analytics workflows. We introduce Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) to let users define what their data pipelines should accomplish while Spark orchestrates execution, dependencies, parallelism and retries, an official Real-Time Mode in Structured Streaming for sub-second, continuous low-latency processing, and extensive improvements to the PySpark ecosystem with Arrow-native UDFs/UDTFs, Python Data Source filter pushdown, and better Python worker logging. The release also brings Spark Connect enhancements including GA support for Spark ML on the Python client and increased stability for large workloads, and expands SQL support with GA SQL Scripting, the VARIANT type with shredding optimizations, support for recursive CTEs, and new approximate data sketch functions. Spark 4.1 prioritizes higher-level abstractions, real-time performance, richer Python support, and more.

speakers.name: Daniel Tenedorio
speakers.bio: Daniel Tenedorio is a senior staff software engineer at Databricks, working on Spark Core and Spark SQL. He interacts with the Apache Spark™ open-source community to develop and review query processing features. Daniel has a breadth of experience in database systems development from building and launching features underpinning multiple major production services over time.

speakers.name: Wenchen Fan
speakers.bio: Wenchen Fan is a software engineer at Databricks, working on Spark Core and Spark SQL. He mainly focuses on the Apache Spark open-source community, leading the discussion and reviews of many features/fixes in Spark. He is a Spark committer and a Spark PMC member.

sessions.title: What's New in Databricks Apps
sessions.body: Databricks Apps has moved from “great for prototypes” to an enterprise app hosting platform you can trust for real mission critical applications and this session is your fast tour of what’s new. We’ll cover major improvements to the developer experience, upgrades that make each individual app more production-ready and reliable. and new admin and governance capabilities that let you group, govern, and operate thousands of apps across your organization. If you’re building or planning to build on Databricks Apps, this is the roadmap of how the platform is evolving to support you—from first app to fleets of them.

sessions.title: What’s New in Unity Catalog With Live Demos!
sessions.body:
Unity Catalog is evolving fast! Join the product team for a demo-packed dive into the latest capabilities shipping now and what’s on the horizon for data governance.

 

We’ll unveil powerful new features across access control, data lineage, AI governance, observability, discovery and many more!

 

Walk away with a complete understanding of what Unity Catalog can do for your organization today — and what advancements are coming next!

speakers.name: Lianne Zelsman
speakers.bio: Lianne is a Sr. Product Manager on the Unity Catalog team at Databricks.

speakers.name: Paul Roome
speakers.bio: Paul is a Staff Product Manager at Databricks responsible for building out Unity Catalog.

sessions.title: When 75% of Your Builders Aren't Engineers: Enterprise Vibe Coding Meets Databricks
sessions.body: The Replit × Databricks integration was built on a bet: that non-technical business users, not just developers, should be able to build production data apps on enterprise data. That bet is paying off. 75% of users building with our integration are non-technical, and they're shipping governed apps that deploy directly into Databricks with full Unity Catalog permissions, data masking, and platform-team observability. This session covers what happens when you put vibe coding tools in the hands of LOB and data teams at Fortune 500 companies. We'll discuss the architecture that makes this possible, the trust model that convinced security teams to say yes (apps deploy to .databricks.com), and the adoption we are seeing in leading companies using AI tools with a data foundation set in Databricks.

sessions.title: When Anyone Can Build Anything: The New AI-Native Stack
sessions.body:
The act of building, whether software, knowledge systems or workflows, is being fundamentally democratized. Natural language is becoming the new interface between human intent and outcome. Natural language is becoming the new programming language. Ideas are becoming applications in minutes, not months. This panel brings together the founders of AI-native tools that are collapsing the distance between human intent and running software. Together, they'll explore a near-future where dramatically more people can ship products, and where the primary bottleneck shifts from technical skill to creative vision.

The big questions:

  • What happens when the cost of building software drops by orders of magnitude?
  • Are we heading toward a world with far more software, fewer traditional developers or both?
  • When AI agents can build, test, and deploy autonomously, how does engineering culture evolve?
  • What's still hard and what will remain uniquely human in the development process?
  • Where do AI agents break down and are we moving fast enough to find out before it matters

Join the founders reshaping the most fundamental act in technology for a candid look at where this lands in the next 2–3 years.

sessions.title: When Redis Isn’t the Answer: Serving Lakehouse Data at Scale
sessions.body: As our feature and operational use cases grew, maintaining separate Redis/DynamoDB stacks alongside the data lake added latency, skew and ops burden. At Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), we adopted Lakebase to serve low‑latency data directly from Databricks, simplifying our architecture while meeting strict SLAs. This session details our setup and results: how we modelled entities and keys, tuned Lakebase capacity and read replicas for high QPS and enforced freshness with Change Data Feed–driven syncs. We’ll show code and configs for provisioning online stores, publishing tables, and querying endpoints, plus before/after latency and maintenance metrics. Attendees will leave with reference patterns to consolidate online serving on Lakebase without sacrificing performance.

speakers.name: Michael Kobelev
speakers.bio: Michael Kobelev is a Software Engineer at ML Infrastructure team at Superhuman, focused on making ML data fast and reliable at scale. He spent three years at Grammarly building the data systems behind features like personalized emails, and recently led the effort to replace Feast with Lakebase. Before ML infrastructure, he built backend systems for the payments team. Based in Berlin.

sessions.title: Where AI Governance Is Headed: Best Practices for Unifying Data, Models and Agents
sessions.body:
AI is shifting from single models to multi-agent systems, and governance must evolve with it. Traditional approaches break down when agents dynamically access data, tools, APIs and multiple AI models across platforms.

 

In this session, Databricks and Thoughtworks introduce a unified approach to AI governance built on a data-centric foundation. Learn how to extend governance from data to models, agents and tools using Unity Catalog, consistent identity-based controls and end-to-end observability.

 

We’ll explore where AI governance is headed, including multi-AI governance with Unity AI Gateway, open and interoperable controls across frameworks and real-time monitoring to detect risk and manage cost.

 

Thoughtworks will share architectural principles for building governed agentic systems at scale. Walk away with a clear path to move fast with AI without losing control.

speakers.name: Shayan Mohanty
speakers.bio: As Chief Data and AI Officer at Thoughtworks, Shayan Mohanty spearheads the global strategy for delivering production-ready AI atscale. A veteran of the AI space, he was previously the co-founder and CEO of Watchful (acquired by Thoughtworks) and led the critical stream processing infrastructure for ad metrics at Facebook. With a career spanning from research at Los Alamos National Laboratory to the front lines of AI startups, Shayan specializes in moving beyond the proof of concept to build AI systems that are interpretable, controllable, and impactful.

sessions.title: Who Goes There? Enterprise Auth and Identity Management on Databricks Apps
sessions.body:
For an application to move from a prototype to a core business asset, it must meet the highest standards of enterprise security and compliance. This session explores the advanced security architecture of Databricks Apps, demonstrating how it inherits and extends the robust governance of the Data Intelligence Platform.

 

We will move beyond basic access to explore sophisticated identity management patterns, including On-Behalf-Of (OBO) authentication for user-scoped actions and secure compute resource delegation. You will also learn how the platform is hardening the application lifecycle with features like automated secret rotation and dedicated network namespaces to ensure total isolation. Whether you are handling sensitive PII or building internal tools for thousands of users, this session provides the blueprint for building apps that are secure by design, fully audited, and ready for the most regulated environments.

speakers.name: Wenxin Liu
speakers.bio: Wenxin Liu is a Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect at Databricks with more than 10 years of experience across cloud infrastructure, security, and platform engineering. They specialize in helping teams design secure, scalable architectures and translate emerging platform capabilities into practical patterns for builders. At Databricks, Wenxin focuses on Databricks Apps, enterprise identity, observability, and secure connectivity, helping customers and internal teams build and operate data and AI applications with confidence at scale.

sessions.title: Why Caresource Chose Databricks AI/BI Over Traditional BI for Regulatory Reporting
sessions.body:
CareSource initially planned to migrate hundreds of state-mandated SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) reports to Power BI Paginated Reports. However, with a mature Databricks platform already in place, that approach would have required added data movement, duplicated governance logic, and new licensing costs.

 

CareSource and West Monroe share how a Databricks AI/BI pilot reshaped the strategy. By keeping regulatory reporting in Databricks, CareSource eliminated downstream exports, improved reliability, and reduced runtimes from hours to minutes. We’ll review the scalable architecture, including a custom extract framework that generates state-specific files and automates secure SFTP delivery, plus a business-friendly interface that drove adoption among non-technical users. Attendees will gain practical guidance on building governed regulatory pipelines and knowing when AI/BI is a strong alternative to traditional BI tools.

speakers.name: Cam Cross
speakers.bio: Cam Cross is a Technical & AI Subject Matter Specialist at West Monroe. He builds Databricks-native data, analytics, and AI solutions for healthcare and government payers. Cam partners with executives and engineers to stand up data platforms, ship governed reporting, and put AI to work inside Databricks. His focus: helping regulated healthcare orgs modernize their data capability, and get more out of their Databricks investment with AI-native solutions.

speakers.name: Roger Turner
speakers.bio: Roger Turner is a senior data and technology leader at CareSource with a proven record of driving business outcomes through modern data and analytics capabilities. As Sr. Director of Data Operations, he brings extensive expertise in enterprise data platforms, regulatory and operational reporting, and large‑scale data modernization within highly regulated healthcare environments. He is an industry leader aligning technical execution with business strategy, delivering reliable, well‑governed data solutions that support payer operations while improving performance, cost efficiency, and overall data quality.

sessions.title: Why It's Time to Take AI/BI Seriously
sessions.body:
I'm a Power BI developer by trade, and for years I've refused to engage with other data visualization platforms. Every time I did, I just found it was lacking capabilities or had serious deficiencies compared to Power BI. Then 2025 hit and Databricks invested heavily in improving AI/BI, metric views and Genie. Now, AI/BI is ready to be a legitimate challenger in the Data Visualisation space.

 

In this talk I will show you how you can use AI/BI, metric views and Genie to get the most out of your data. We will start from basics, building a metric view, using it to build a dashboard and then setting up a Genie space. I'll then walk you through my top tips on how you can get the most out of each of them. We'll talk about the types of work where AI/BI thrives and discuss where I see it going in its pursuit of being the next big data visualization platform.

 

AI/BI is here and it's ready to be taken seriously.

speakers.name: Ashley Warren
speakers.bio:
Ash is a Senior Analytics Consultant at Advancing Analytics, a data and AI consultancy and Databricks Gold Partner. Ash focuses on analytics engineering and data visualisation, helping our enterprise customers get value out of their data

In the past, I've led data teams at small and large organisations, helping unlock the power of data through storytelling that's underpinned by strong foundations. I started out my data career as a Power BI report developer, though in the last couple of years I find myself spending more of my time building in Databricks.

Ash can regularly be found speaking at user groups, conferences and events, sharing what he's learnt back with the community.

sessions.title: Why Vector Stores Are Not Enough: Using Lakebase as a Durable Memory Layer for Autonomous Agents
sessions.body:
We are told that Vector Databases are the 'Memory' for AI Agents. But they give you a probabilistic similarity score. In enterprise workflows, 'probably' isn't good enough. Agents need deterministic, transactional state.

 

We will use Lakebase as a memory layer for agents, enabling them to remember actions, lock resources, and handle concurrency.

 

We will build a 'Stateful Worker' agent live with:

  • The 'Two-Phase Commit' Prompt: Forcing an LLM to lock a row in Lakebase before calling an external API, preventing hallucinated actions.
  • Time Travel for Agents: Leveraging Lakebase Branching to create isolated 'simulation' environments where agents can test destructive actions (e.g., 'Delete User') in a sandbox before committing to production.
  • Hybrid Recall: A pattern combining Vector Search for knowledge with Lakebase for state, proving you need both to build reliable agents.

 

Attendees will leave with a reusable architecture to build high-performing and autonomous agents in production.

speakers.name: Jenny Sun
speakers.bio: Jenny is a software engineer on the Databricks Agent Platform team based in San Francisco. She graduated from Princeton University with a B.S.E in Computer Science. At Databricks, she works on various agent initiatives, with a focus on making it easier for developers and customers to build reliable, stateful AI agents on Databricks.

speakers.name: Nam Nguyen
speakers.bio: Nam Nguyen is a Senior Solutions Engineer, and he is part of the field engineering team based in Paris, France. He has 7+ years of experience in data engineering working for big tech companies in France. At Databricks, Nam helps entreprise to navigate the technologies decision and accelerate the adoption cycle. Nam holds several Databricks and AWS certifications in data engineering and generative AI.

sessions.title: Women in Data + AI
sessions.body: Join us for a dynamic panel on Wednesday, June 17 at YBCA Forum + East Garden, featuring senior women leaders in data and AI as they share reflections on their inspiring career journeys and how they're navigating the next wave of technological transformation. The conversation will offer both practical insights and personal reflections followed by a networking reception designed to connect and further build this global community.

speakers.name: Caroline Peika
speakers.bio: Caroline Peika is a Data & AI executive with 15+ years of experience building and scaling machine learning, analytics, and AI capabilities across healthcare, gaming, telecom, travel, and retail. Passionate about AI since the start of her career, she has spent over a decade turning emerging technologies into real-world business and human impact. Caroline specializes in enterprise AI transformation, modern data platforms, experimentation, and bringing machine learning from research to production at scale. She currently leads data and AI initiatives in pediatric healthcare, helping shape the future of responsible and generative AI in complex, highly regulated environments.

speakers.name: Jaya Upadhyay
speakers.bio: Jaya Upadhyay is Senior Director of Enterprise Data Platform at Zillow, where she is enabling Zillow's data to be AI-ready for consumer experiences and internal teams. She leads the company's data mesh transformation across a portfolio spanning API and MCP orchestration, real-time streaming, analytics and ML platforms, and end-to-end data governance. With nearly two decades of data engineering and data platform leadership across Boats Group, Expedia Group, and Groupon, she has built petabyte-scale platforms, customer data ecosystems, and the high-performing teams behind them.

speakers.name: Kristy Mayer-Mejia
speakers.bio:
Kristy Mayer-Mejia is the Global Head of Data Transformation at Kraken, where she works with utilities to operationalize data in complex, regulated energy systems - turning analytics into effective, customer-centric operations and scalable clean energy innovation.

She has built and led data organizations across clean energy and fintech, including at Arcadia, Opower, Kiva, and DoE. Her work spans data platforms, product, and policy, to help organizations move from insight to execution at scale.

sessions.title: Women in Data and AI Reception
sessions.body: Join us for a dynamic panel on Wednesday, June 17 at YBCA Forum + East Garden, featuring senior women leaders in data and AI as they share reflections on their inspiring career journeys and how they’re navigating the next wave of technological transformation. The conversation will offer both practical insights and personal reflections — followed by a networking reception designed to connect and further build this global community.

speakers.name: Robin Sutara
speakers.bio:
From repairing Apache helicopters near the Korean DMZ to the corporate battlefield, Robin has demonstrated success in navigating the high stress, and sometimes combative, complexities of data-led transformations. She has consulted with hundreds of organizations on data strategy, data culture, organizational design, and operational efficiency.

Robin has had an eclectic career in technical and business functions with more than two decades in tech companies, including Microsoft and Databricks. She has been recognized as a Top 20 Women in Data and Tech, DataIQ 100 Most Influential People in Data, and Tech leader of the Year.

sessions.title: You Built That with Databricks Apps?! A Customer Showcase of What’s Possible
sessions.body:
You’ve seen Databricks Apps used for simple dashboards and internal tools—but that’s just the starting line. In this breakout, we’ll showcase some of the most creative, high-impact apps real customers have built on Databricks, from agentic workflows and decision copilots to line-of-business apps that entire organizations now run on every day.

 

We’ll walk through a curated set of customer stories, each answering three questions: What problem were they stuck on? What did they build on Databricks Apps? What changed in their business as a result? Along the way, you’ll see patterns for building AI assistants on top of your lakehouse, rich operational UIs that write back to Lakebase, governance-aware “self-service” data apps for business users, and more.

 

If you’ve been thinking of Apps as “just a nicer way to host a notebook or dashboard,” this session is designed to flip that mental model. You’ll leave with concrete ideas, architectures, and inspiration to say, “Wait—we could build our version of that.

sessions.title: Your AI Strategy is Only as Good as Your People Strategy
sessions.body: As AI moves from experimentation to enterprise impact, success depends on workforce readiness, not just technology. Market leaders have upskilled over 50% of their employees and are redesigning workflows around AI, while 60% of organizations still struggle to generate value from their investments. In this session, Robin Sutara and Melanie Botha explore how to build an AI-enabled workforce by aligning culture, people, process and enablement with your data strategy. You'll learn how to assess your data and AI maturity, close critical skills gaps at scale through structured learning programs, and integrate AI agents into teams in ways that elevate human talent. Drawing on customer proof points and the Databricks data and AI maturity framework, this session provides a practical roadmap for treating upskilling as a core investment—so every project becomes a data and AI project and every employee contributes to AI-driven outcomes.

speakers.name: Melanie Botha
speakers.bio:
Melanie leverages 25+ years of experience to guide organizations in building data-driven cultures and scale initiatives. A trusted advisor to C-suite executives, she believes technological transformation requires organizational and cultural evolution. Her team empowers customers, partners, and internal stakeholders to maximize their data and AI potential.

Previously, at AWS ANZ, she led programs that skilled over 200,000 individuals, including pioneering GenAI training for non-technical audiences.

At Microsoft South Africa, she managed Consumer Channels Group and Marketing and Operations. Earlier roles spanned across Europe and Africa. Melanie is a qualified Art Therapist supporting individuals to overcome mental health challenges.

speakers.name: Robin Sutara
speakers.bio:
From repairing Apache helicopters near the Korean DMZ to the corporate battlefield, Robin has demonstrated success in navigating the high stress, and sometimes combative, complexities of data-led transformations. She has consulted with hundreds of organizations on data strategy, data culture, organizational design, and operational efficiency.

Robin has had an eclectic career in technical and business functions with more than two decades in tech companies, including Microsoft and Databricks. She has been recognized as a Top 20 Women in Data and Tech, DataIQ 100 Most Influential People in Data, and Tech leader of the Year.

sessions.title: Your guide to fine-grained access control: Permissions, ABAC, and RBAC in Unity Catalog
sessions.body:
Fine-grained access control in Unity Catalog isn’t a set of disconnected features; it’s a unified framework. Understanding how permissions, RBAC and ABAC work together is key to governing data and AI at scale.

 

In this session, we’ll break down each approach and when to use it. Learn how granular permissions enforce least privilege, how RBAC creates clear isolation boundaries and how ABAC uses governed tags to apply row filters, column masks and policy logic across entire catalogs automatically.

 

We’ll walk through this as a progression — from dynamic views and table-level controls to scalable, tag-driven policies — so you know how to evolve your approach as your data estate grows. We’ll also cover performance considerations, how to avoid conflicts when combining methods and real-world patterns for production environments.

 

Finally, we’ll preview what’s next, including extending fine-grained governance to AI assets and unstructured data, along with new visibility and impact analysis capabilities in Unity Catalog.

 

Walk away with practical guidance to design, scale and future-proof access control.

speakers.name: Adriana Ispas
speakers.bio: Adriana Ispas is a Sr. Staff Product Manager at Databricks working on the Databricks Runtime and Unity Catalog. She holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from ETH Zurich.

speakers.name: Arush Mehrotra
speakers.bio: Arush Mehrotra is a Product Manager at Databricks, where he works on advancing scalable, fine-grained access control through attribute-based access control (ABAC) and Unity Catalog compute. He earned his degree in Computer Science from the University of Pennsylvania.

sessions.title: Your Guide to Open Table Formats — Delta, Iceberg, Best Practices, and What’s Next!
sessions.body:
Open table formats had a breakthrough year—and now the focus shifts to how to use them effectively.

 

In this session, we’ll break down what’s new across Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, including an early look at Delta 5.0 and the Iceberg v4 Adaptive Metadata Tree, which brings the two formats closer together at the metadata layer for high-performance, multi-engine workloads.

 

More importantly, we’ll share best practices for working across formats today. Learn how teams are using the Unified Delta Kernel (now GA, written in Rust) across Spark, Flink, and DuckDB, and how Catalog-Managed Commits enable safer multi-engine writes, stronger governance, and multi-table transactions. We’ll also cover Auto CDF for building efficient incremental pipelines.

 

Finally, we’ll highlight innovations for AI workloads, including the FILE data type and VARIANT shredding.

 

Walk away with practical guidance to build, optimize, and future-proof your open data architecture.

speakers.name: Benjamin Mathew
speakers.bio: Ben is a product manager at Databricks, focused on making data and AI accessible to new markets and users. He helps drive product management for the SAP-Databricks partnership and Databricks "SaaS".

speakers.name: Scott Sandre
speakers.bio: Scott Sandre is a Sr Software Engineer at Databricks on the Delta Ecosystem team, where he leads the design of catalog-managed Delta tables and drives the catalog integration support in Delta Kernel.  Based in San Francisco, Scott is passionate about open-source technologies and building performance-intensive systems.

sessions.title: Zero-Copy Federated Energy Analytics: ADME + Databricks in Action
sessions.body: Oil and gas companies have standardized on Azure Data Manager for Energy (ADME) as their subsurface system of record, but running analytics and AI on that data has meant copying massive OSDU datasets into downstream platforms, breaking governance and slowing every workflow that follows. In this jointly developed Microsoft and Databricks session, we introduce the ADME connector for Azure Databricks: a zero‑copy, federated path that brings Databricks compute directly to OSDU data, with native Unity Catalog governance and serverless scale. The connector is on track to land as an official Lakeflow Community Connector, giving Databricks customers a governed, supported path into ADME out of the box.We walk through the architecture, show the connector in action against live ADME, and share how operators across the industry are accelerating subsurface analytics while keeping ADME as the single source of truth.

speakers.name: Andy Corran
speakers.bio: Andy Corran is a Principal Product Manager in Azure Databricks, part of Microsoft’s Azure Core AI organization. He focuses on building and scaling enterprise data and AI platforms on Azure Databricks, defining cloud‑native features, driving Azure integrations, and ensuring platform reliability with engineering teams, customers, and partners across Azure.

sessions.title: ZeroETL Was Just the Start: Operational Databases belong in the Medallion Architecture
sessions.body: The medallion architecture dictates how we typically think about data, but that framework has historically been limited to the data lifecycle strictly within the Lakehouse. Lakebase takes this a step further by expanding the architectural blueprint to redefine how data enters your Bronze layer and how it is consumed from Gold. Rather than extracting and moving data across system boundaries, your operational database natively acts as the Bronze foundation to immediately feed downstream analytics. On the other end, Lakebase closes the loop by directly serving those refined Gold datasets to production applications with operational low latency, eliminating the need to export data out of your ecosystem.

speakers.name: Pranav Aurora
speakers.bio: Pranav is a Product Manager leading the integration of Lakebase across the broader Databricks Platform, including Unity Catalog and the Lakehouse. Prior to his current role, he was a co-founder of Mooncake Labs, a startup dedicated to bridging the gap between Postgres and the Lakehouse ecosystem.
